<sub>`D:/00mk/steel project/training/Training/workmen's_diary/2026-08-25(teach mk).md` · partial-fix-reported-as-complete</sub>

#### 🟡 MEDIUM · 2026-08-25 · Near-miss: the first fix considered for the F2 false positives would have silently deleted real footings

**What happened.** When the F2 template fired 3 false footings on a beam plan, the first instinct was to raise the matching threshold. That would have suppressed the false hits — and simultaneously dropped genuine F2 footings out of the real footing plan, turning a visible wrong-positive into an invisible missing-positive.

**Root cause.** Threshold tuning is the reflexive knob in template matching, and it operates globally: it cannot distinguish 'this shape appears where it shouldn't' from 'this shape is faint'. The real distinction was contextual (footing plans contain no beams), not numeric.

**Impact.** Caught before implementation — cost nothing. Had it shipped, footing recall would have quietly fallen from 12/12 while the visible false-positive count went to zero, i.e. the scoreboard would have improved while the tool got worse.

**Fix.** fixed by design choice: rejected the threshold change and added a domain rule instead — any footing whose centre falls inside a detected beam band is discarded (provably safe, since real footing plans detect 0 beam bands)

**→ Rule.** A global knob cannot fix a contextual error; it only trades a loud failure for a quiet one. When the wrong answer is wrong *because of where it is*, the fix is a rule about place, not a number.

<sub>`D:/00mk/steel project/training/Training/workmen's_diary/2026-08-25(teach mk).md` · near-miss-wrong-fix</sub>

#### 🟡 MEDIUM · 2026-08-25 · "Just increase B" assumed model size is a free dial; the family is already at its open-weight ceiling

**What happened.** The suggestion to fine-tune a bigger Qwen was researched: open-weight Qwen3.6 has exactly two sizes (27B dense and 35B-A3B MoE, already in use). The only larger option in the line is Qwen3.6-Max-Preview, which is closed-weight and API-only. The next genuinely bigger open VLM (Qwen3-VL-235B-A22B) needs ~513GB VRAM for inference alone and ~770GB for LoRA fine-tuning — an 8-GPU multi-node rental, not "rent one bigger card".

**Root cause.** Treating parameter count as a continuously adjustable setting, without checking what sizes actually ship as open weights or what hardware each step implies.

**Impact.** Would have committed budget and schedule to a path that requires a different order of magnitude of hardware and multi-GPU distributed training the team has never done.

**Fix.** Researched and reported the family ceiling, the closed-weight status of the only larger option, and the concrete VRAM/GPU-count cost of the next real step, framed as an explicit budget decision rather than a config tweak.

**→ Rule.** Before proposing a bigger model, enumerate the actual released open-weight sizes and price the hardware for each. "Bigger" is a hardware and pipeline decision, not a hyperparameter.

<sub>`D:/00mk/steel project/training/Training/workmen's_diary/2026-08-25.md` · wrong-assumption</sub>

#### 🟡 MEDIUM · 2026-08-25 · Translating the whole prompt to English scores ~8% worse than a native prompt — a trap the dictionary idea could have walked into

**What happened.** Researching the professor's Thai→English dictionary idea surfaced a counter-finding: translating the entire prompt into English can score about 8% lower than a native-language prompt, because translation loses context the native phrasing carried. The safe version is targeted term-glossary insertion (DIP, arXiv 2411.01141), not a wholesale translation pass.

**Root cause.** The intuitive reading of "add English to help an English-centric model" scales to "translate everything", which is the version the literature shows is harmful.

**Impact.** None yet — caught during research before anything was built. Building the wholesale version would have cost a tuning round and degraded accuracy.

**Fix.** Recorded the counter-finding alongside the technique, and flagged that the professor must first clarify which problem the glossary is meant to solve before any glossary file is written.

**→ Rule.** When adopting a technique from a meeting suggestion, search for its published failure mode as well as its success case, and pin down which specific problem it is supposed to solve before writing any of it.

<sub>`D:/00mk/steel project/training/Training/workmen's_diary/2026-08-25.md` · wrong-assumption</sub>

#### 🟡 MEDIUM · 2026-08-25 · First hypothesis wrong: F1 vs F2 footings differ in shape, not scale — multi-scale matching missed all F1s

**What happened.** Multi-scale template matching was expected to handle footing variation across houses. On the second house tested (บ้าน 12), F2 turned out to be a tall rectangle with 2 pile crosses — a different symbol entirely, not a resized F1 — and multi-scale alone still found only 6 of 12 footings, missing every F1.

**Root cause.** Assumed the appearance difference between footing types was a scale difference, without inspecting the actual symbols side by side first.

**Impact.** Half the footings missed on the very second house tested. This is exactly the scale/appearance-variance limitation the morning's research had flagged (SkeySpot: template matching needs a template per variant) showing up immediately in practice.

**Fix.** Replaced single-template multi-scale with a template bank (`tpl_footing*.png` glob), all candidates merged before one NMS pass. Recorded the wrong first hypothesis in the teaching document as a reasoning exercise.

**→ Rule.** Before choosing an invariance strategy (scale, rotation), look at the actual variants side by side. If they are different symbols, no amount of scaling will find them — you need a template per variant, exactly as the literature says.

<sub>`D:/00mk/steel project/training/Training/workmen's_diary/2026-08-25.md` · wrong-hypothesis</sub>

#### 🟡 MEDIUM · 2026-08-25 · F2 tall-rect footing template false-fired on beam plans

**What happened.** The F2 template (a tall rectangle) matched vertical beams passing through column boxes, producing 3 false footing detections on บ้าน12 หน้า22, a beam plan with no footings at all.

**Root cause.** The template captures a generic geometric shape that recurs in a different structural context; template matching has no semantic notion of what page it is looking at.

**Impact.** False footing counts on beam-plan pages, which would corrupt any downstream count or cross-check built on the tool.

**Fix.** Drop any footing detection whose center falls inside a detected beam band — provably safe because real foundation plans detect 0 beams.

**→ Rule.** A shape-based detector needs a context filter, not just a higher threshold. Use a mutually-exclusive signal from the same page (here: beams and footings never coexist) to reject cross-context false positives.

<sub>`D:/00mk/steel project/training/Training/workmen's_diary/2026-08-25.md` · false-positive</sub>

#### 🟡 MEDIUM · 2026-08-25 · Multi-scale matching on a tiny 28x34 column template inflated detections 14 → 21 with noise

**What happened.** Applying multi-scale matching to the small column template (28×34 px) on บ้าน17 raised detections from a correct 14 to 21, the extra 7 being noise. Reverted to single-scale for columns.

**Root cause.** A very small template carries little distinguishing structure; scaling it further reduces the information per match and lets background texture cross the threshold.

**Impact.** Would have produced a 50% over-count on column detection had it not been checked against a known-good page.

**Fix.** Column matching reverted to single-scale only, with the reason recorded.

**→ Rule.** Do not apply the same invariance strategy uniformly across templates. Small templates have too little signal for multi-scale — always validate a strategy change against a page with a known correct count before keeping it.

<sub>`D:/00mk/steel project/training/Training/workmen's_diary/2026-08-25.md` · false-positive</sub>

#### 🟡 MEDIUM · 2026-08-25 · tpl_footing9 was too generic — leaked junk on other houses while scoring poorly on its own

**What happened.** The square-plus-cross template from บ้าน 30 scored only 5/9 on its own house with scores dropping 1.0→0.76, while emitting junk at 0.72–0.73 on other houses — its junk scores overlap its real scores.

**Root cause.** The symbol is too geometrically generic (a square with a cross) to be distinctive across drawing offices; adding it traded a real gain on one house for noise across the whole set.

**Impact.** Would have inflated coverage numbers with false positives. Removing it honestly returned house 30 to "under-detected" status.

**Fix.** Removed from the bank (moved to `rejected_` in staging), accepting house 30 as honestly under-covered rather than falsely covered.

**→ Rule.** Judge a new template by its worst effect across all houses, not its best effect on the one it came from. Prefer an honest gap over a template whose junk scores overlap its real scores.

<sub>`D:/00mk/steel project/training/Training/workmen's_diary/2026-08-25.md` · false-positive</sub>

#### 🟡 MEDIUM · 2026-08-25 · Molmo-72B's HuggingFace-listed 293GB was fp32, not bf16 — nearly double the real weight size

**What happened.** Molmo-72B's repo size on HuggingFace reads 293GB, which would have ruled it out on hardware grounds. Checking the file layout (83 safetensors at ~3.51GB each, 73B × 4 bytes ≈ 292GB) showed it is fp32; the real bf16 size is about 147GB.

**Root cause.** Assuming a HuggingFace repo's listed total size reflects bf16 weights, without checking the dtype implied by parameter count versus byte count.

**Impact.** A viable candidate would have been eliminated on a doubled size figure. Generalizes to every model in the comparison.

**Fix.** Verified real bf16 weight sizes via the HF API with `?blobs=true` for every candidate, and recorded the dtype-check rule.

**→ Rule.** Before using a model repo's listed size, divide bytes by parameter count to infer the dtype. A repo published in fp32 will read roughly 2x its real bf16 footprint.

**What happened.** The search filter was "100–200B, not Qwen". **Fix.** Checked every candidate's `config.json` backbone directly; both InternVL entries excluded from the "not Qwen" answer.

**→ Rule.** Verify model lineage from the config's declared backbone, never from the brand name. A VLM's vision tower and its LLM often come from different organizations.

#### 🟡 MEDIUM · 2026-08-25 · A research pass assumed the training run was 4-bit QLoRA when LOAD_IN_4BIT was already False (bf16)

**What happened.** One research pass built its VRAM and candidate reasoning on the assumption that training was 4-bit QLoRA. Checking `train_t03.py` showed `LOAD_IN_4BIT = False` — the run is bf16 LoRA.

**Root cause.** An assumption about the current setup was carried into analysis without reading the actual configuration file.

**Impact.** Any VRAM or cost conclusion from that pass would have been off by the difference between 4-bit and bf16 weights (roughly 4x on the weights term, which is 74 of 87.5 GB).

**Fix.** Corrected against the real config; the VRAM decomposition was rebuilt from the true bf16 numbers.

**→ Rule.** Read the actual config file before reasoning about resource usage. Assumptions about your own setup are the easiest thing to verify and the most expensive thing to get wrong.

#### 🟡 MEDIUM · 2026-08-25 · Pattern recognition validated on only 2 houses from the same drawing series

**What happened.** The tool was verified on บ้าน17 and บ้าน12 only, both from the same BMA "แบบบ้านยิ้ม" series. Other series and other drawing offices are untested, and 07บ้าน_ใหญ่_2ชั้น_01 has no plan_footing/plan_beam ground truth to compare against.

**Root cause.** Validation used whichever houses had ground truth available, which happen to share a drawing office and therefore share symbol conventions — so the test set does not exercise the cross-office variance the method is most fragile to.

**Impact.** The tool's reported accuracy is only valid within one drawing series. Later harvest measurement across 44 houses confirmed the concern: only 23 correct / 19 under / 2 over.

**Fix.** Recorded as an explicit limit; cross-series testing left in the pending list. The later harvest sweep across 44 houses gave the honest cross-series number.

**→ Rule.** When your test set shares a common source, you are measuring within-source accuracy, not accuracy. State the source-diversity of the test set alongside every accuracy figure.

<sub>`D:/00mk/steel project/training/Training/workmen's_diary/2026-08-25.md` · insufficient-validation</sub>

#### 🟡 MEDIUM · 2026-08-25 · Two houses over-detect footings roughly 2x — likely a cross-series template matching an inset

**What happened.** After the honest two-sided measurement, houses 08 (25 detected vs 12 true) and 18 (26 vs 12) over-detect at roughly double. The suspected cause is a template from a different drawing series matching an inset detail.

**Root cause.** A template harvested from one drawing series matches a visually similar but semantically different element in another series — the same cross-series appearance-variance problem that has recurred all day.

**Impact.** Two houses report roughly 2x their true footing count; any downstream count cross-check on them would be wrong in the direction that looks like the model missing nothing.

**Fix.** Not fixed — recorded as pending work with the working hypothesis stated.

**→ Rule.** Over-detection is as much a failure as under-detection and is easier to overlook because it looks like coverage. Always measure both directions and chase the over-detecting cases with the same energy as the misses.

<sub>`D:/00mk/steel project/training/Training/workmen's_diary/2026-08-25.md` · false-positive</sub>

#### 🟡 MEDIUM · 2026-08-26 · Self-harvest can only recover element types already in the template bank — its real ceiling, found by measurement

**What happened.** After the threshold fix, self-harvest recovered exactly the missing footings on two houses, but on house 10 the remaining 16 missed elements were a different type entirely and correctly yielded +0.

**Root cause.** Self-harvest promotes new templates by matching against the existing bank; a type with zero templates has nothing to match against, so the loop cannot bootstrap itself into a new class.

**Impact.** Self-harvest cannot close the coverage gap on its own — the columns/beams/slab gaps that show up two days later still need hand-cropped seed templates. Any plan that treated self-harvest as the coverage strategy was over-optimistic.

**Fix.** measured and recorded as the real ceiling; hand-cropping seeds remained the path

**→ Rule.** A bootstrapping loop's ceiling is the classes it already has one seed for. Measure per-class recovery, not aggregate recovery, or the aggregate number hides that a whole class recovered nothing.

<sub>`D:/00mk/steel project/training/Training/workmen's_diary/2026-08-26.md` · wrong-assumption</sub>

#### 🟡 MEDIUM · 2026-08-29 · The blanket punctuation-stripping rule would have collapsed the stirrup abbreviation ป. into ป and collided it with ประตู (door)

**What happened.** While removing `.` `_` `*` `#` etc. from all prompts, the glossary entry `ป.` → stirrup had to be exempted: stripping the dot makes it indistinguishable from the prefix of ประตู.

**Root cause.** A mechanical character-removal rule applied across Thai text, where the period is load-bearing as an abbreviation marker rather than decoration.

**Impact.** Caught before the rule was applied — otherwise the glossary would have taught the model to map door labels to stirrups, a wrong-field mapping that would surface as unexplained rebar errors much later.

**Fix.** exempted `ป.` (and ว.ส.ท., §0.5 decimals, ST.n/WC.n) from the stripping rule, with the reason recorded

**→ Rule.** A blanket character rule over Thai text needs an exemption list built by grepping real usage first. The dangerous cases are the ones where stripping still produces a valid-looking token.

<sub>`D:/00mk/steel project/training/Training/workmen's_diary/2026-08-30.md` · assumption-verification</sub>

#### 🟡 MEDIUM · 2026-08-30 · Asserted 'LoRA weights can't be averaged together' — PEFT has `add_weighted_adapter`, and this case was ideal for it

**What happened.** Claude flatly stated that LoRA adapters cannot be weight-averaged. Makham pushed back. PEFT in fact provides `add_weighted_adapter` supporting linear (Model Soup), TIES, DARE, svd and cat — and this case was especially favourable: same base model, same rank, and identical seed 3407 across folds meaning the same LoRA A init, i.e. the same-basin condition soup requires.

**Root cause.** Second unchecked negative claim of the same day — a capability assertion made from memory rather than from the library's documentation/source.

**Impact.** Would have discarded a viable and cheap plan (the 4-fold soup that became Purson's actual shipped weights). Cost credibility and required Makham to catch it.

**Fix.** Corrected, apologised, and recorded as an explicit lesson in the diary; the soup plan was then adopted as the real Purson deliverable.

**→ Rule.** Every negative capability claim must be backed by a checked source before it is spoken. Two unchecked negatives in one day is a pattern, not an accident — treat 'X can't do Y' as a research task, never a recall task.

<sub>`D:/00mk/steel project/training/Training/workmen's_diary/2026-08-30.md` · assumption-verification</sub>

#### 🟡 MEDIUM · 2026-08-31 · Assumed ปร.4 material-list pages were stacked top/bottom; they are actually side by side rotated 90 degrees

**What happened.** The first assumption about the two-sheet material_list layout was top/bottom. Real inspection showed the sheets sit side by side, always rotated 90 degrees, with the lower-numbered sheet on the right.

**Root cause.** An assumption was formed from a mental model rather than from opening the actual pages.

**Impact.** Would have produced systematically mislabelled sheet ordering across 89 pages had it not been checked.

**Fix.** Confirmed against two real examples from two different houses (one visually, one where the source file already carried an explicit warning), then applied the rule at confidence 0.85 rather than 1.0 because only two pages were eyeballed.

**→ Rule.** Verify any layout assumption against at least two independent real examples from different sources before batch-applying it, and record the confidence honestly to reflect how many were actually checked.

**What happened.** Confidence was stated about something not actually verified (e.g. an external tool's syntax) without first checking it.

**Root cause.** Defaulted to sounding confident instead of stating the real, lower confidence level and proposing a verification step.

**Impact.** Risk of acting on an unverified claim as if it were confirmed fact.

**Fix.** Adopted a standing rule: never state confidence that hasn't been verified — state the real confidence level and propose a verification step instead of guessing silently.

<sub>`d:/00mk/steel project/training/Training/No_touch_box/docs/rule_of_tune.md` · false-confidence</sub>

#### 🟡 MEDIUM ·  · A cited rule was acted on in the same message instead of stopping to wait for the user's answer

**What happened.** A rule requiring the user's confirmation was cited, but then acted upon in the same message instead of genuinely stopping and waiting for the user's answer.

**Root cause.** Citing a rule was treated as equivalent to having satisfied it, without the actual behavioral step of pausing for a real answer.

**Impact.** The confirmation step was rendered meaningless — a rule 'followed' in name only, since the action proceeded regardless of what the user might have said.

**Fix.** Adopted a standing rule: citing a rule that requires an answer must be followed by an actual stop-and-wait, never cited-then-immediately-acted-on in the same message.

**→ Rule.** Citing a rule must be followed by an actual stop-and-wait for the user's answer — not cited-then-immediately-acted-on in the same message.

<sub>`d:/00mk/steel project/training/Training/No_touch_box/docs/rule_of_tune.md` · confirmation-gate-bypass</sub>

#### ⚪ LOW · 2026-07-06 · Label Studio <Style> className support is only documented for View/Choices, not Text — nearly applied unverified

**What happened.** Research into Label Studio docs found a `<Style>` tag for reusable CSS classes via className, but no documentation confirming it works directly on Text elements — only on View and Choices. className was therefore used only on View wrappers while Text/TextArea kept inline `style=`, which was already proven to work in the existing label-studio-structural.xml.

**Root cause.** Documentation gaps in the tool: a feature is documented for some element types with no statement about the others, so applying it broadly is an unverified assumption.

**Impact.** Avoided. Had className been applied to Text elements, styling would likely have silently not applied and the layout fixes would have appeared to fail for an unrelated reason.

**Fix.** Restricted className to View wrappers (row/card/stickycol); Text/TextArea continued using inline style=, matching a configuration already proven to work.

**→ Rule.** When a tool's docs confirm a feature for some element types and are silent on others, treat the silence as 'unsupported' and fall back to the configuration already proven to work in this repo — do not extrapolate from partial documentation.

<sub>`D:/00mk/steel project/training/Training/workmen's_diary/2026-07-06.md` · unverified-assumption</sub>

#### ⚪ LOW · 2026-07-10 · The backup was auto-flagged as failed because robocopy exit code 1 means success

**What happened.** Two robocopy background jobs backing up 4.5 GB (Constistant 2.5 GB, Training 2.0 GB) to E:\constitant\20260710\ were auto-flagged as failed by the system on exit code 1. Reading the logs showed FAILED=0 on both — robocopy's exit code 1 means 'success, files copied'.

**Root cause.** A generic non-zero-exit-means-failure rule was applied to a tool with non-standard exit-code semantics.

**Impact.** A backup of the entire project briefly appeared to have failed; only reading the actual logs settled it.

**Fix.** Checked the robocopy logs directly, confirmed FAILED=0 for both jobs and 100% success.

**→ Rule.** Check a tool's exit-code semantics before trusting a red/green verdict — for robocopy specifically, anything under 8 is success, and the log's FAILED count is the real answer.

<sub>`D:/00mk/steel project/training/Training/workmen's_diary/2026-07-10.md` · tooling/false-positive</sub>

#### ⚪ LOW · 2026-08-25 · Duplicate column detection at grid (B,2) — 13 boxes for 12 real columns

**What happened.** บ้าน12 หน้า20 produced 13 column boxes against 12 true columns, one of them a doubled box at grid position (B,2). บ้าน17 หน้า15 shows 19 columns which were not individually verified and may contain further doubles.

**Root cause.** The greedy NMS suppression radius is not tight enough for two overlapping matches on the same symbol at slightly different offsets.

**Impact.** Small over-counts in column detection, which would corrupt any recall cross-check built on the tool.

**Fix.** Not fixed — recorded as a known minor issue in the pending list.

**→ Rule.** Report detector counts against a hand-verified truth for every validation page, not just the headline page. An unverified count is not evidence, and small systematic over-counts hide inside "about right" numbers.

<sub>`D:/00mk/steel project/training/Training/workmen's_diary/2026-08-25.md` · false-positive</sub>

#### ⚪ LOW · 2026-08-26 · Molmo-72B's real bf16 footprint is ~147GB, not what '72B' implies — the model-size column and the GPU you must rent are different numbers

**What happened.** The catalogue's size column carries a parenthetical for Molmo: '72B (bf16 จริง ~147GB)'. Every other row lists parameter count alone, so a shortlist sized on the label alone would under-provision the rental for this candidate by more than 2×.

**Root cause.** Parameter count was used as the screening axis because it is the number vendors advertise; actual weight bytes at the precision you intend to run were only checked for one model and only recorded as an aside.

**Impact.** Caught before any rental — the model was screened out for lacking a verified LoRA framework, not for size. But the shortlist's size column is not a rentable-hardware column, and nothing in the doc says so.

**Fix.** Recorded as a parenthetical on that one row. The other rows still list parameter count only.

**→ Rule.** Screen candidates on bytes at the precision you will actually run, not on the marketing parameter count — and note it in every row, not just the one where someone happened to check.

<sub>`D:/00mk/steel project/training/Training/workmen's_diary/แคตตาล็อก_AI_ทางเลือก_2026-08-26.md` · planning-assumption</sub>

#### ⚪ LOW · 2026-08-26 · Plan assumed grid master carried pixel coordinates — it only has pos_m

**What happened.** The CV hint design assumed grid master entries could be converted to approximate pixel positions (g≈) for the hint text. Grid master only stores `pos_m` (metres), no pixel data at all, so the plan had to be rewritten to use ordinal row position instead.

**Root cause.** The hint design was written against an assumed schema rather than by reading the actual grid master file. The schema was never checked before designing on top of it.

**Impact.** Design rework mid-implementation; the hint mechanism ended up weaker (ordinal rows rather than pixel proximity).

**Fix.** Rewrote the hint to use ordinal row ordering instead of pixel estimates.

**→ Rule.** Open the actual data file before designing anything that consumes it. Five seconds of reading beats an afternoon of rework built on an assumed field.

<sub>`D:/00mk/steel project/training/Training/workmen's_diary/2026-08-26.md` · wrong-assumption</sub>

**What happened.** Houses 01 and 02 draw their column icon smaller than 28px, below the size the harvest tooling assumed, so no candidate was produced until the crop was deliberately widened to include surrounding context.

**Impact.** Two houses silently contributed zero column templates, holding back the column coverage number until someone dug in specifically.

<sub>`D:/00mk/steel project/training/Training/workmen's_diary/2026-08-28.md` · wrong-assumption</sub>

---

## T02 — Silent Failures & Swallowed Errors

*Code or pipelines that failed, skipped, or produced wrong values without any visible error.*

**22 entries** · 7 critical · 8 high

#### 🔴 CRITICAL · 2026-07-05 · Background agent stalled twice, was killed mid-task, and pages 41-47 of the spread-footing BOQ were never extracted at all

**What happened.** Agent 4 was dispatched for pages 38-47 (spread-footing BOQ). It stopped itself mid-task twice and had to be resumed via SendMessage twice, completed only pages 38, 39, 40, and was then killed by Makham while it was on page 41. Pages 41-47 were never extracted — not in round t1, and not in round t2 either (t2's scope was limited to pages 1-37).

**Root cause.** A long-running agent on a homogeneous, high-page-count task self-terminated repeatedly with no automatic resume, and there was no work-unit checkpointing that would let another worker pick up cleanly at page 41. The remaining gap then fell out of scope for the next round because t2 was scoped by page range rather than by 'what is still missing'.

**Impact.** 7 pages of BOQ ground truth permanently missing from the dataset for house 01 across two full extraction rounds. Carried as an open pending item on 2026-07-05, still open at end of 2026-07-06, and it left an orphan scratch file behind.

**Fix.** Not fixed. Listed as pending item #5 at end of 2026-07-06: 'Pages 41-47 (spread-footing BOQ) still not extracted in either round.'

**→ Rule.** Give long agent runs small explicit work units and a resume marker per unit, and never scope a follow-up round by page range — scope it by the diff against what is actually complete, so a known gap cannot silently fall outside the next round's boundaries.

<sub>`D:/00mk/steel project/training/Training/workmen's_diary/2026-07-05.md` · agent-failure / incomplete-work</sub>

#### 🔴 CRITICAL · 2026-07-28 · Bug 2: the collator's default resize='min' silently fell back to 512px — a 25x resolution loss — while VRAM deceptively looked comfortable

**What happened.** The vision collator defaults to resize='min', which reads the model's image_size key. Qwen3-VL has no image_size key at all, so the collator silently falls back to 512px — a 25x loss of resolution against what was intended. VRAM usage looked comfortable, which reads as a healthy run rather than a broken one.

**Root cause.** A library default that degrades silently when a lookup key is absent, combined with the fact that the only observable symptom (low VRAM) resembles success. Nothing asserted the actual resolution reaching the model.

**Impact.** Would have trained the model on images 25x coarser than intended, with every dashboard indicator looking fine. This same bug, undetected on the t01 side, later invalidated the entire A/B comparison.

**Fix.** Forced resize='max' explicitly, plus an assertion checking the resolution of the first batch.

**→ Rule.** Never rely on a library default that resolves via an optional key. Assert the actual effective value on the first batch — and treat unexpectedly low resource usage as a red flag, not reassurance.

<sub>`D:/00mk/steel project/training/Training/workmen's_diary/2026-07-28.md` · library-default/silent-failure</sub>

#### 🔴 CRITICAL · 2026-08-25 · The one guard against the project's most expensive bug was 4x too lenient and would have waved it through

**What happened.** train_t03.py's first assert is commented "ตัวอย่างแรก (ภาพเดียว)" and does `_tok = (grid[:,1]*grid[:,2]).sum() // 4` then `assert _tok > 1000`. But `train_ds[0]` in the op04 dataset has 4 images and `.sum()` totals across all of them while the threshold is per-image. Simulation confirmed t01's exact failure level (266 tokens/image) × 4 images = 1,064 > 1,000, so the assert passes.

**Root cause.** The guard was written when the first example had exactly one image, and the dataset shape later changed to multi-image examples without the guard being revisited. The assert's own comment still documented the old assumption.

**Impact.** The single guard that exists to prevent a repeat of t01 (silently training at 266 tokens/image, the most expensive bug in the project's history) was inert. A t01-class disaster would have run to completion undetected, burning a full GPU rental.

**Fix.** Divide by `_gt.shape[0]` so the threshold is genuinely per-image, print the configured cap alongside the measured value, and add a non-fatal warning when the measured value falls more than 25% below the cap. `ast.parse` clean; both branches simulated.

**→ Rule.** A guard written for one data shape silently rots when the data shape changes. Periodically re-prove your guards by simulating the exact failure they were written to catch — if you cannot make the assert fire, it is not protecting you.

<sub>`D:/00mk/steel project/training/Training/workmen's_diary/2026-08-25.md` · guard-rot</sub>

#### 🔴 CRITICAL · 2026-08-25 · t01 silently trained at the library default 512px / ~266 tokens per image and tanked accuracy

**What happened.** Referenced in this session as the project's benchmark disaster: t01's MAX_PIXELS was never set explicitly, so the processor defaulted to 512px (~266 visual tokens/image) instead of the intended budget, and accuracy collapsed. Recorded as rule_of_tune #12.

**Root cause.** A load-bearing training hyperparameter was left to a library default rather than being explicitly set and asserted, and nothing printed the effective value at run start.

**Impact.** An entire fine-tuning round (GPU rental plus wall-clock time) produced degraded results and had to be diagnosed after the fact — the most expensive bug in the project's history.

**Fix.** MAX_PIXELS is now set explicitly in train_t03.py and guarded by an assert (which itself needed fixing this session — see the 4x-too-lenient guard).

**→ Rule.** Set every accuracy-critical hyperparameter explicitly, print the effective value at startup, and assert it. A library default you did not choose is a silent config bug waiting for its first expensive run.

<sub>`D:/00mk/steel project/training/Training/workmen's_diary/2026-08-25.md` · silent-default</sub>

#### 🔴 CRITICAL · 2026-08-29 · pass 0 mislabelled roof structure pages in 8 of 11 houses, silently deleting all roof beams from the BOQ

**What happened.** The pass 0 page-classification stage assigned the wrong label to roof-structure sheets in 8 out of 11 houses. Because pass 1 routes images into folders based on pass 0's answer, those pages fell out of the whole conveyor and every roof beam vanished from the resulting BOQ.

**Root cause.** pass 0 is a single point of failure with no downstream cross-check: a misclassified page is not flagged, it simply never appears again. Nothing reconciles 'pages in' against 'pages consumed' or checks that expected element types are present in the output.

**Impact.** Roof beams entirely missing from the bill of quantities for 8 houses — a silent quantity shortfall in the shipped output, not a visible error.

**Fix.** Documented as the most dangerous stage of the conveyor in pass0/README.md; the classification target was changed to answer with the destination subtask (plan_beam, section, …) rather than a pattern, so pass 1 knows exactly where each image belongs.

**→ Rule.** Any routing/classification stage that can drop data must have a reconciliation check downstream: count pages in versus pages consumed, and assert that expected element categories are non-empty. A misroute must raise an alarm, never just produce a smaller result.

<sub>`D:/00mk/steel project/training/Training/workmen's_diary/สอน_t04_Purson_2026-08-29.md` · data-pipeline</sub>

#### 🔴 CRITICAL · 2026-08-30 · Web importer recognised only spec pattern names (`plan`/`gridline`) that appear in ZERO real files — import silently produced 0 elements

**What happened.** Simulating a real user uploading house 01 through the web revealed that `raw-extraction-adapter.js` only knew the pattern names `'plan'` and `'gridline'` from the written spec, while the entire real library of 50 houses uses `beam_plan` (85), `footing_plan` (60), `etc_plan` (199), `roof_frame_plan` (46) = 390 files, plus `grid_master` (42 files). Files named `plan`/`gridline` numbered 0. Pressing the import button on real data returned 0 elements and no grid, silently.

**Root cause.** The adapter was written against the spec document instead of against the real data, and the repo's test fixtures used the spec's invented names — so every test stayed green while the production path was completely dead. A fixture that agrees with the spec instead of with the data cannot detect spec-vs-reality drift.

**Impact.** The manual JSON import button had been silently broken for real files the whole time (nobody knew), and the new Purson worker path would have inherited the same silent zero.

**Fix.** Fixed at the root: added `canonicalPattern()` + `PATTERN_ALIASES` in the adapter and routed all 5 direct `f.pattern` comparisons across 2 files through it; the pre-existing manual import button benefited immediately. Added `tests/raw-extraction-pattern-aliases.test.js` (4 tests). After the fix: 7 model calls → 6 files → 24 elements / 10 specs / 14 grid lines. npm test 1153/1153.

**→ Rule.** Build fixtures from real production data, not from the spec document. If a test fixture uses a value that appears zero times in the real corpus, the test proves nothing.

<sub>`D:/00mk/steel project/training/Training/workmen's_diary/2026-08-30.md` · data-pipeline</sub>

#### 🔴 CRITICAL · 2026-09-01 · Footings with no rebar size produced '(DBnull)' and ฿0 steel with no warning flag — reading as if the footing genuinely has no reinforcement

**What happened.** Footings F3/F4/F6 had no `main_bar_dia_mm`, so `computeBOQ` emitted descriptions containing '(DBnull)' and rebar lines at ฿0 with no `needs_review` flag. On a real construction BOQ this reads as 'this footing has no reinforcement'.

**Root cause.** Missing data flowed through the cost path unflagged. `computeBOQ` had no guard for an absent rebar diameter, so absence was rendered as a legitimate zero rather than as an unknown.

**Impact.** Dangerous for a real construction BOQ — three footings appeared to require no reinforcement. Exactly the kind of wrong number that ships.

**Fix.** Added `needs_review` / `main_bar_missing` flags and replaced the text with '(ไม่ทราบขนาดเหล็ก — ตรวจสอบแบบ)'. Verified it matches exactly F4/F6/F3.

**→ Rule.** Missing input must never render as zero cost or zero quantity. Any cost path must distinguish 'measured as zero' from 'unknown' and flag the latter loudly — a silently-zero structural line is a safety issue, not a display issue.

<sub>`2026-09-01.md` · boq/correctness</sub>

#### 🟠 HIGH · 2026-07-05 · npm test ran a single file, so an entire test suite had never been executed and was silently broken

**What happened.** In the Constistant repo, `npm test` was configured to run one file rather than the whole tests/ folder. When it was widened to the full folder, the bbs-shape-allowance test turned out to have never actually run and needed a DOM stub fix plus a float assertion fix before it would pass.

**Root cause.** The test runner's scope was narrowed at some point (probably for speed or during a refactor) and never restored, so newly added test files entered the repo and rotted without anyone noticing they were not executing. Nothing reported the number of tests run against the number of test files present.

**Impact.** Unknown period of zero coverage on rebar shape allowance — a calculation that feeds cut lengths and steel weight. The broken test had to be fixed before it could pass, meaning it had been broken for as long as it had been ignored.

**Fix.** Changed npm test to run the whole tests/ folder; fixed the DOM stub and the float assertion in the bbs-shape-allowance test; also merged the stray test/ folder into tests/. Result: 48/48 passing.

**→ Rule.** The test command must always run the whole suite directory, never a hand-listed file. A test that is not run is worse than no test — it advertises coverage that does not exist. Assert that the file count and the executed count match.

<sub>`D:/00mk/steel project/training/Training/workmen's_diary/2026-07-05.md` · test-coverage-gap</sub>

#### 🟠 HIGH · 2026-07-28 · House 07 S-03: three structural members missing entirely from the staircase zone, and S1 slabs overcounted 4 vs 3

**What happened.** Clearing the staircase zone revealed three members that had never been extracted at all — B2 in the middle of bay 3-4, the 5th SP panel, and B6 at the ST2 edge — plus an S1 count of 4 where the real number is 3.

**Root cause.** Congested drawing regions (a staircase, where many symbol types overlap) were passed over at normal zoom rather than being cleared exhaustively piece by piece; missing items produce no error signal, unlike wrong items.

**Impact.** Three real members and one over-counted slab in the quantity data — omissions understate the BOQ, and nothing downstream can detect an element that was never recorded.

**Fix.** Zone fully cleared by opening the real images and zooming on every point; corrections appended with the reversal logged.

**→ Rule.** Congested regions must be cleared exhaustively at full zoom, member by member. A missing element is invisible to every downstream check, so absence has to be hunted deliberately.

<sub>`D:/00mk/steel project/training/Training/workmen's_diary/2026-07-28.md` · data-extraction</sub>

#### 🟠 HIGH · 2026-07-28 · Bug 3: max_seq_length defaulted to 2048, cutting through the middle of the image tokens, with no guard on the vision path

**What happened.** max_seq_length was left at its default of 2048. A single image is ~5,100 tokens, so the cut lands in the middle of the image token block. The audio path in the same codebase has a guard against this; the vision path has none.

**Root cause.** A second, independent length limit existed alongside max_length, and only one of the two was being managed. The library protects one modality against this and not the other, so the asymmetry was invisible to anyone assuming parity.

**Impact.** Would have fed the model image token sequences severed mid-image — worse than truncating text, since a partial image block is meaningless.

**Fix.** Corrected as part of the five-bug fix pass before renting.

**→ Rule.** Enumerate every length/size limit in the stack, not just the one you know about. Where a library guards one code path and not another, assume the unguarded path is the one you are on.

<sub>`D:/00mk/steel project/training/Training/workmen's_diary/2026-07-28.md` · config/silent-failure</sub>

#### 🟠 HIGH · 2026-08-24 · On house 08 page 20 the model emitted memorized boilerplate whose source_image pointed at a different house

**What happened.** t03 on the plan_beam page wrote only metadata and closed the JSON with no elements[], and the metadata itself referenced house 22 — the model pasted boilerplate from a similar-looking training example instead of reading the sheet.

**Root cause.** SFT on near-identical JSON envelopes teaches the envelope; when the hard part (elements[]) fails, the model still has a high-probability header to emit, and nothing in the output shape forces the header to be consistent with the input image.

**Impact.** An output that is JSON-valid, passes grammar, and is 100% wrong including its own provenance field — the worst failure mode for a downstream consumer, since it looks like a real extraction of the wrong building.

**Fix.** not fixed — recorded as evidence that plan_beam 0% is memorization, not partial reading

**→ Rule.** Add a mechanical check that a result's own metadata (source_image/house) matches the file it was generated from. That single assert catches memorized-boilerplate output that JSON validity and grammar both wave through.

<sub>`D:/00mk/steel project/training/Training/workmen's_diary/2026-08-24.md` · silent-wrong-output</sub>

#### 🟠 HIGH · 2026-08-25 · raw-extraction-adapter.js ADAPTED_PATTERNS still does not accept roof_plan — the bug can silently recur

**What happened.** The roof-beam-missing bug was closed by fixing the data side (retagging files to `plan`), but the consumer code in Constistant only reads `pattern:"plan"` and `ADAPTED_PATTERNS` was never widened to accept `roof_plan`. Found during the sweep, deliberately not fixed.

**Root cause.** The fix was applied at the data layer only. The code-side gap that made the mistagging fatal in the first place (silently dropping unrecognized patterns instead of warning) was left in place, so the failure mode is dormant, not removed.

**Impact.** Any newly extracted house that gets tagged `roof_plan` will have its roof framing silently disappear from the BOQ again, with no warning — exactly the original bug, re-armed.

**Fix.** Not fixed — recorded as a known open risk in the diary.

**→ Rule.** When a bug is closed by cleaning data, ask whether the code would still fail silently on the same bad input. A silent-drop path is a bug even after the current data is clean; make it warn instead of vanish.

<sub>`D:/00mk/steel project/training/Training/workmen's_diary/2026-08-25.md` · silent-failure</sub>

#### 🟠 HIGH · 2026-08-25 · Concrete/rebar strength values (fc_ksc, fy_*) had never reached any consumer in any house

**What happened.** `fc_ksc`, `fy_main_ksc`, `fy_stirrup_ksc` existed in the source `sections[]` of the JSON files but were never parsed into `notes{}` where consumers read them. 62 values across 26 files reached a consumer for the first time only during this session's sweep.

**Root cause.** The extraction wrote the values into a free-form section array but no parsing step ever lifted them into the structured field the consumers actually read. The gap was documented in the spec (§4a) but nobody had acted on it.

**Impact.** Every downstream calculation depending on concrete/steel grade ran without the real drawing values for the entire project history up to this date.

**Fix.** Parsed 62 values from the files' own `sections[]` into `notes{}`, keeping the literal printed text in `notes.parsed_as`.

**→ Rule.** Extracting a value is not the same as delivering it. For every field the spec defines, verify at least one consumer actually reads it end-to-end — a documented "never reaches consumer" note is an open bug, not a footnote.

<sub>`D:/00mk/steel project/training/Training/workmen's_diary/2026-08-25.md` · dead-data-path</sub>

#### 🟠 HIGH · 2026-08-25 · Images in Markdown silently never appeared in generated PDFs

**What happened.** `tools/md_to_book_pdf.py` writes the intermediate HTML to a temp directory, so every relative `![](...)` image path resolved to nothing. Chromium skipped each missing image without raising an error, so PDFs shipped with 0 of 4 figures and no warning.

**Root cause.** A deliberate workaround (temp dir, to dodge Chromium mishandling Thai/space paths on Windows) broke the relative-path assumption of image tags, and the renderer's failure mode for a missing image is silence rather than an error.

**Impact.** Teaching PDFs produced by this shared tool were figure-less; the defect was invisible until someone opened a PDF and looked. Unknown how many earlier documents shipped without their images.

**Fix.** Added `absolutize_images()` — rewrites relative `src` to a full `file://` URI via `Path.as_uri()` (which also percent-encodes Thai folder names), leaves http/data/file/absolute alone, and prints a warning for a genuinely missing file. Verified 0 → 4 images embedded.

**→ Rule.** When you relocate files to a temp dir, every relative reference in them breaks. And never accept a renderer that swallows missing assets — add an explicit warning so a missing file fails loudly instead of shipping a hole.

**What happened.** While simplifying fields/config from schema v2 to v3, three fields (confidence_flags, material_amount, labor_amount) silently disappeared from the output; the user had to catch it.

**Root cause.** No before/after audit of the full field list was done when simplifying the schema — fields were dropped without being deliberately decided on.

**Impact.** Real ground-truth fields (confidence tracking, cost breakdown) were missing from the simplified schema until caught by the user.

**Fix.** Adopted a standing rule: audit the complete before/after field list whenever fields/config are simplified, so no field silently disappears.

<sub>`d:/00mk/steel project/training/Training/No_touch_box/docs/rule_of_tune.md` · schema-simplification</sub>

#### 🟡 MEDIUM · 2026-07-06 · New spec_source and spec_confidence_score fields have no edit boxes, so reviewers cannot correct them

**What happened.** Generation 3.3 added spec_source and spec_confidence_score as new fields, deliberately separate from the main confidence_score so position confidence and spec confidence would not be conflated. The Label Studio XML has no edit boxes for them — they appear only inside the read-only other_fields_json block.

**Root cause.** The schema was extended without the review config being extended in the same change, so new fields defaulted into the read-only catch-all bucket that exists to prevent silent data loss.

**Impact.** A reviewer who spots a wrong spec_confidence_score cannot fix it. The field will carry whatever the extractor guessed for the life of the dataset, which defeats the purpose of separating it from position confidence.

**Fix.** Not fixed — noted that 'if direct editing is wanted, the fields need to be added to the XML later'.

**→ Rule.** Adding a field to the schema is not done until it is editable in the review UI. A read-only catch-all bucket is a safety net against data loss, not a home for fields that need human correction.

<sub>`2026-07-15.md` · data-extraction</sub>

#### 🟡 MEDIUM · 2026-07-20 · Dummy grid B' recorded as 10.2 when the real value is 10.1, cascading a wrong beam span

**What happened.** B' had been recorded as 10.2 (derived as 11.4+3.15-2.5). The user corrected it to 10.1 (formula 3+2.2+4+0.9), which cascaded to page32's B4X span changing from 1.0 to 0.9.

**Root cause.** The value was derived from one arithmetic chain without cross-checking against an independent chain; the two chains disagree by 0.1m and only one was tried.

**Impact.** A wrong grid value plus a wrong dependent beam span until corrected.

**Fix.** Corrected B' to 10.1 and cascaded the B4X span fix.

**→ Rule.** Derive every dummy grid position from at least two independent dimension chains and require them to agree before recording — a single chain has no error detection.

<sub>`2026-07-20.md` · data-extraction</sub>

#### 🟡 MEDIUM · 2026-07-28 · A typo printed on the drawing ('HITASHI') was silently auto-corrected to 'HITACHI' during extraction

**What happened.** The pump label on SN-04 prints HITASHI — a typo made by the drawing's author. Extraction had normalized it to the correct brand spelling HITACHI, changing what the source document actually says.

**Root cause.** Extraction applied helpful real-world knowledge to 'fix' the source instead of transcribing it verbatim. The distinction between transcribing a document and describing reality was not enforced.

**Impact.** The extracted record no longer matches the drawing it claims to represent; any later audit against the physical sheet would find a discrepancy with no trace of who changed it or why.

**Fix.** Reverted to the literal printed text with a note that it is a typo in the drawing and must be transcribed as-is.

**→ Rule.** Transcribe source documents verbatim, including obvious errors. Record the correction as a separate annotated field — never silently improve what the source says.

<sub>`D:/00mk/steel project/training/Training/workmen's_diary/2026-07-28.md` · data-extraction</sub>

#### 🟡 MEDIUM · 2026-08-29 · pass 2.5 self-harvest cannot recover any element type the central template library missed entirely

**What happened.** pass 2.5 rescans a page using templates harvested from that same page, recovering elements the central library missed across series. But by construction it can only recover a type where the central library already found at least one instance — a page where CV found zero is beyond help.

**Root cause.** The self-harvest mechanism bootstraps from its own first detection, so a cold-start miss is unrecoverable. This is a structural limit of the approach, not a tuning issue.

**Impact.** Element types with zero central-library coverage remain permanently missing from the confirmed inventory that feeds pass 3, and therefore from the BOQ.

**Fix.** Not fixed — documented as a known limitation of the approach ('ข้อจำกัดโดยหลักการ').

**→ Rule.** Document the structural blind spots of every recovery mechanism, and add explicit monitoring for the blind-spot case (pages where CV detects zero) so those pages are routed to human review rather than silently passing through.

<sub>`D:/00mk/steel project/training/Training/workmen's_diary/สอน_t04_Purson_2026-08-29.md` · data-pipeline</sub>

#### 🟡 MEDIUM · 2026-09-01 · The completely rebuilt loading screen was never opened in a real browser

**What happened.** The waiting/loading screen was rewritten from scratch (progress card, gradient bar, connected timeline with pulsing status dots, summary row, injected CSS, reduced-motion support) but never viewed in a real browser because no job was running when it was written. It stayed on the pending list across multiple entries.

**Root cause.** UI verification was blocked on an external dependency (a live job) and was deferred rather than worked around with a mocked state, so it silently rolled forward as debt.

**Impact.** A significant UI rewrite shipped with only HTML/CSS structural review, no visual confirmation, carried unverified across several sessions.

**Fix.** Not fixed — repeatedly recorded as pending.

**→ Rule.** Never block UI verification on a real job. Add a dev flag or seeded fake progress state so any loading/waiting UI can be eyeballed on demand — otherwise it ships unseen.

#### ⚪ LOW · 2026-08-25 · 1400px figures would have overflowed the A4 text column with no img CSS rule

**What happened.** The PDF generator had no CSS rule for `img`, so a 1400px-wide figure would have run past the A4 text column and could break across pages.

**Root cause.** The image path had never been exercised end-to-end (see the silently-dropped-images bug), so the styling gap that would only appear once images actually rendered had never been noticed.

**Impact.** Would have produced unreadable overflowing figures in every teaching PDF the moment images started working.

**Fix.** Added an `img` CSS rule (max-width 100%, centered, no page-break inside); regression-checked on a temp .md with no images.

**→ Rule.** Fixing a silently-dead code path exposes every unexercised bug behind it. After enabling a path for the first time, review the whole path, not just the line you changed.

## T03 — Measurement & Evaluation Methodology

*Metrics that measured the wrong thing, unfair comparisons, or evaluation setups that could not answer the question asked.*

**94 entries** · 23 critical · 33 high

#### 🔴 CRITICAL · 2026-07-28 · The silent-512px-resize bug was fixed only in t02's script, so t01 trained on ~14× blurrier images

**What happened.** During Phase 0.4 a bug was found where, without an explicit resize="max", the collator silently downscales images to 512px. It was fixed in t02's training script only. Nobody went back to check t01's script (written a month earlier), which had the same defect. Measurement confirmed t01 trained at ~266 visual tokens/image versus t02's ~3,796-5,100.

**Root cause.** A bug fix was applied at the site where the bug was noticed, not at every site sharing the same code path. The defect is invisible because it comes from an unset default, so there is no line of code to compare.

**Impact.** The entire t01-vs-t02 A/B comparison — the whole purpose of the t02 rental — became unfair. The conclusion 'Qwen3.6 beats Qwen3-VL' had to be downgraded to 'Qwen3.6 with much blurrier input still beat Qwen3-VL', which does not answer the original question.

**Fix.** Verified by actually loading the model and running the exact t01 collator on a real image, capturing the library's own log line 'Model does not have a default image size - using 512'. Makham chose option A: accept the results with explicit caveats everywhere rather than pay to retrain t01.

**→ Rule.** When you find a bug, grep every sibling call site before closing it — the lazy fix is the one in the shared function, not the one in the file you were reading. And prove the diagnosis by measurement, not by reading code.

<sub>`D:/00mk/steel project/training/Training/workmen's_diary/สอนมะขาม_รวม.md` · experiment-validity</sub>

#### 🔴 CRITICAL · 2026-07-28 · The entire A/B experiment was invalid: t01 trained on ~14x blurrier images because its collator was called with pure defaults and the parity table had no row for it

**What happened.** After the whole day's results were in, a 43-agent audit found that train_qwen36.py:164 (t01) calls the collator with no resize= argument at all — the exact bug found and fixed on the t02 side only. Measured live on the rented machine: t01 trained at ~266 visual tokens per image vs t02's ~3,796 — roughly 14x. The 16-line parity table, built specifically to control variables, had no collator row.

**Root cause.** The parity table compared only values deliberately set. A value never typed at all has no line to compare, so a differing default is structurally invisible to that kind of check — and bug 2 had been fixed forward on the new script without anyone going back to check whether the older script shared it.

**Impact.** The day's headline conclusion ('Qwen3.6 beats Qwen3-VL') had to be retracted and reduced to 'Qwen3.6, seeing far blurrier images, still does better'. The A/B question the round existed to answer remains unanswered; a paid training run plus a full day of analysis produced an uninterpretable comparison.

**Fix.** Verified by real measurement, not code reading (loading Qwen3.6 and building a t01-identical collator printed 'Model does not have a default image size - using 512'). Large warning boxes added to t02_workflow.md at Phase 7 and §0.0, 'clear win' retracted, and Lesson 12 added to rule_of_tune.md. Makham chose option A (accept with warnings) over option B (retrain t01 at resize='max' for ~$0.60-1.80).

**→ Rule.** A variable-control table must enumerate every argument passed into a shared function or class, read from the real source — not just the values you chose to change. An unset default is a variable too, and it is the easiest of all to miss because there is no line to compare. And when a bug is found in one script, immediately check every sibling script for the same shape.

<sub>`D:/00mk/steel project/training/Training/workmen's_diary/2026-07-28.md` · experiment-methodology</sub>

#### 🔴 CRITICAL · 2026-07-29 · The 90% / 28.2% headline numbers were measured on an artifact nobody actually runs

**What happened.** The team's headline figures (90% JSON valid, 28.2% element recall) came from eval_fields.py, which loads bf16 + adapter at runtime with load_in_4bit=False — i.e. no merge step and no quantization. Real use runs merged + Q4_K_M GGUF, whose accuracy has never been measured at all.

**Root cause.** Evaluation was performed on the convenient path (full precision, unmerged adapter) rather than the deployment path. The two paths differ by exactly the two steps most likely to degrade quality: merge and quantize.

**Impact.** The team's most-quoted quality number describes a configuration that never ships. Planning, confidence, and go/no-go decisions were made on a figure that does not apply to the running system.

**Fix.** partially — the discrepancy is now documented and the figures explicitly re-scoped to 'valid for the adapter only'; the GGUF still has no measured accuracy

**→ Rule.** Always attach 'measured on what?' to an accuracy number, and make the eval harness load the exact artifact that ships. If eval and production load different files, the eval number is a different model's number.

<sub>`D:/00mk/steel project/training/Training/workmen's_diary/2026-07-29.md` · eval-methodology</sub>

#### 🔴 CRITICAL · 2026-07-29 · After a full training round, GGUF export and real usage, rebar extraction — the actual goal — had never been tested once

**What happened.** No structural (S-*) sheet had ever been fully extracted. Pages 07-11 were only classified. The prompt's single biggest rule ('always split top/bottom rebar') had no evidence for or against it.

**Root cause.** Evaluation and real-use pages were selected by page order (01, 02, 03...) rather than by importance to the objective, so the highest-value pages were always last in the queue and never reached.

**Impact.** Every claim about the model's usefulness for the project's core purpose rests on zero measurements; weeks of work had not yet answered the primary question.

**Fix.** Not fixed. Recorded as the standing open question.

**→ Rule.** Test the highest-value case first, not the first case in the sequence — if the core capability is still untested after a full cycle, the cycle measured the wrong thing.

<sub>`D:/00mk/steel project/training/Training/workmen's_diary/สอนมะขาม_รวม.md` · measurement-methodology</sub>

#### 🔴 CRITICAL · 2026-08-21 · t02 saw only ~13 beam-plan pages in training and scored 11% element recall on them

**What happened.** Counting t02's actual training data showed it saw ~13 beam-plan pages versus ~158 material_list pages and ~24 door/window schedule pages. Measured performance tracked example count directly: door/window schedules 86%, beam plans 11%. Beam plans are also the hardest pattern (~25 beams per page, each needing correct start and end grid refs).

**Root cause.** Training-set composition mirrored raw page counts in the source drawings rather than being balanced toward the hardest, highest-value pattern. Hardest pattern + fewest examples = worst possible pairing, and nobody counted per-pattern examples before training.

**Impact.** Beam plans — the single pattern the BOQ most depends on — perform at 11% recall. Every downstream demo of the extraction loop is bottlenecked on this. Grammar-constrained decoding fixed format (57.9%→96.8% valid JSON) but left accuracy untouched.

**Fix.** Not fixed by code. dataset_sizing.md written with real counts; target set at 25-30 houses (~99 beam plans); op04 created to annotate only Pass 2 patterns so effort goes to beam plans rather than material lists.

**→ Rule.** Count training examples per page pattern before training and rebalance toward the hardest, highest-value pattern — the relationship between example count and accuracy is direct and measurable (13→11%, 24→86%), so a per-pattern census is a prerequisite for any fine-tune, not a post-mortem tool.

<sub>`D:/00mk/steel project/training/Training/workmen's_diary/2026-08-21.md` · eval-methodology</sub>

#### 🔴 CRITICAL · 2026-08-24 · Benchmark house 08 was sitting in t03's training set — cross-round comparison would have been meaningless

**What happened.** House 08 was picked as the cross-round benchmark because t02 and base-Qwen results already existed for it. But house 08 was in t03's *training* set while t02 had never trained on it, so t03's numbers would have been inflated by memorization and not comparable at all.

**Root cause.** The benchmark house was selected for the convenience of having prior results, without checking which side of the split it sat on in the current round. Split membership was never cross-referenced against the comparison plan.

**Impact.** Caught before the results were published — but if missed, the entire t02-vs-t03 comparison would have been invalid, with an inflated t03 number presented as a real improvement.

**Fix.** Moved house 08 into val and retrained: train 887→854 (42 houses), val 229→262 (6 houses), ratio 3.26:1. House 08 is now genuinely unseen by all three rounds.

**→ Rule.** Any house used as a cross-round benchmark must be verified held-out in *every* round being compared, not just the current one. Check split membership before, not after, choosing a benchmark.

<sub>`D:/00mk/steel project/training/Training/workmen's_diary/2026-08-24.md` · eval-methodology</sub>

#### 🔴 CRITICAL · 2026-08-25 · section 0% was mostly a broken metric, not a broken model — perfect AI could score at most 4%

**What happened.** The section evaluation compares element_id strings exactly. But section ground-truth IDs are human-invented labels (gate_front, door_lock_detail, SP_at_bathroom, purlin_rafter_connection, ห้องนอน) that appear nowhere on the drawing. Measured ceilings: section 37% overall, and only 1 of 23 = 4% on house 08, the house actually used for evaluation. notes was even worse at 2%.

**Root cause.** Ground-truth IDs were created for human bookkeeping convenience and then reused verbatim as the evaluation key, without checking whether the information needed to produce them exists on the source image at all.

**Impact.** A headline 0% metric was read as 'the model cannot read sections' and was on track to drive further model/prompt work — potentially another full paid training round aimed at something no model could ever achieve.

**Fix.** Wrote measure_id_ceiling.py to split IDs into readable-from-drawing vs. human-invented and compute a per-subtask achievable ceiling. Result reclassified section 0% as a measurement failure and plan_beam 0% (ceiling 88%) as a genuine model failure.

**→ Rule.** Before optimising against any metric, compute its achievable ceiling on the exact evaluation set. A metric whose ceiling is 4% is not measuring model quality — it is measuring the annotation convention.

<sub>`D:/00mk/steel project/training/Training/workmen's_diary/2026-08-25(teach mk).md` · measurement-methodology</sub>

#### 🔴 CRITICAL · 2026-08-25 · Workflow doc claimed images were never downscaled; measurement showed 100% of them were

**What happened.** `t03_workflow.md` row 7 recorded "ภาพจริง 2339×1654 ต่ำกว่า cap 5,120 อยู่แล้ว = ไม่ย่อเลย". A direct measurement found 973/973 image instances (100%) exceed the cap — the smallest image in train.jsonl is 3307×2339 (7,554 tokens) and the largest 4631×3473 (15,707 tokens, losing 67% of its detail). No image of the recorded size exists in the current train set.

**Root cause.** The earlier record was produced by looking at a single sample (`train_ds[0]`) and generalising it to the whole dataset — the same failure mode already recorded as rule_of_tune #12, repeating.

**Impact.** The team believed image resolution was not a bottleneck and made downstream decisions on that belief. Every training image was in fact being downscaled, up to 67% detail loss on the largest pages.

**Fix.** Built `measure_capacity.py` (read-only, no GPU) that computes visual tokens for every image in the set from file dimensions, and recorded the contradiction in the workflow doc rather than quietly overwriting the old row.

**→ Rule.** Never characterise a dataset from one sample. Any claim of the form "the images are size X" must come from a script that measures every item and reports the min/max/count over the cap.

<sub>`D:/00mk/steel project/training/Training/workmen's_diary/2026-08-25.md` · measurement-methodology</sub>

#### 🔴 CRITICAL · 2026-08-25 · Eval scored ids with raw exact string match, so trailing whitespace or case scored a correct answer as 0

**What happened.** `infer_house_t03.py:218` scored with `set(gt_ids) & set(pred_ids)` — exact string match with no normalization. A model answering `"B1 "` against GT `"B1"` scored zero. Self-check confirmed a fully correct model with stray whitespace/case scored 0% under the old scorer.

**Root cause.** The scorer was written as a one-line set intersection with no normalization layer, treating model output as if it were canonical data rather than free-form text.

**Impact.** Every reported recall number across t02/t03 history understates the model's real capability by an unknown margin. Tuning decisions were made against a metric that punishes formatting noise as if it were a reading failure.

**Fix.** Researched the standard first (KIE evaluation practice, KIEval arXiv:2503.05488, which reports exact and relaxed matching as separate columns), then added `norm_id()` (strip / collapse whitespace / casefold) before intersection. Old metric kept as a column for cross-round comparability.

**→ Rule.** Any string-comparison metric over model output needs an explicit normalization step, and the normalized and raw scores should be reported side by side. Check published evaluation practice for the task type before inventing a scorer.

<sub>`D:/00mk/steel project/training/Training/workmen's_diary/2026-08-25.md` · metric-bug</sub>

#### 🔴 CRITICAL · 2026-08-25 · Ground truth element_id mixed real printed marks with names the annotator invented, teaching the model to guess the unguessable

**What happened.** GT `element_id` contained both marks genuinely printed on the drawing (`B1`, `B3X`, `C1`, `F1A`, `RB1'`) and descriptive names the annotator invented to distinguish sub-details (`gate_front`, `SP_at_bathroom`, `purlin_rafter_connection`, `door_lock_detail`, `ห้องนอน`, `ระดับพื้นอาคาร`). No model can produce those strings — there is nothing on the paper that says them. Measurement showed 300/455 section training examples (66%) teach the model to guess invented names, half of them 100% invented.

**Root cause.** The schema's §0.2 actively instructed annotators to invent a descriptive name and forbade leaving the field blank, so the convention that made the field unlearnable was written into the spec itself.

**Impact.** Section id-recall pinned at 0% with a real ceiling of only 37% dataset-wide and 4% on the test house — so the number carried almost no information. Worse, 66% of section training examples were actively training the model to hallucinate names.

**Fix.** After explicit approval, batch-changed 343 section files: 1,534 elements moved to `element_id: null` with the original name preserved in a new `element_name_assigned` field (902 genuinely-printed marks kept, exactly matching the prior measurement). `strip_assigned()` added to build_dataset_t03.py so the invented name never enters the training target; `pass2_used/section.md` and schema §0.2 rewritten to say "mark present → copy it, no mark → null, never invent".

**→ Rule.** A ground-truth field must only contain what is physically present in the input. If an annotator has to invent a value to fill a field, the field is teaching hallucination — use null and put the human-readable label in a separate, non-target field.

<sub>`D:/00mk/steel project/training/Training/workmen's_diary/2026-08-25.md` · ground-truth-design</sub>

#### 🔴 CRITICAL · 2026-08-25 · Harvest round 2 reported a perfect 44/44 that was a fake number from a loose threshold and one-sided check

**What happened.** The second harvest round reported "44/44 ✅". It was fake: the threshold was loosened to 0.55 and the pass criterion checked only one direction (detected ≥ 70% of GT), so massive over-detection counted as success — house 27 has GT 20 and the tool detected 293, and still passed.

**Root cause.** A pass criterion with only a lower bound. Combined with a loose threshold this rewards over-detection, since detecting everything guarantees you detect at least 70% of the truth.

**Impact.** A perfect-looking coverage number that was meaningless. The diary explicitly notes this is the same bug class as the section metric found earlier the same evening — the team produced two broken metrics in one day.

**Fix.** Set HARVEST_THRESH = FOOTING_THRESH (0.72) and measured both directions (✅ 70–160% / 🔶 under / 🔺 over). Honest result: 23 correct / 19 under / 2 over.

**→ Rule.** A pass criterion must be bounded on both sides. A one-sided "at least X%" check rewards over-detection and will report perfect coverage for a detector that fires on everything.

<sub>`D:/00mk/steel project/training/Training/workmen's_diary/2026-08-25.md` · metric-bug</sub>

#### 🔴 CRITICAL · 2026-08-25 · The schema itself instructed annotators to invent descriptive names and forbade leaving the field blank

**What happened.** `primary_rawjson_schema.md` §0.2 said the opposite of what was needed: "ตั้งชื่อบรรยาย ห้ามเว้น" — invent a descriptive name, never leave blank. This is the written instruction that created the 66%-invented-names training problem in the section subtask.

**Root cause.** A schema rule was written to guarantee a non-empty field (nice for data completeness) without considering that the field is a model training target, so completeness was bought at the cost of teaching hallucination.

**Impact.** Root cause of the entire section-0% bottleneck: 300/455 training examples, 1,534 elements across 343 files. Required a full GT batch migration to undo.

**Fix.** Rewrote §0.2 to the repo's existing convention ("not on the paper = null, not an invented name"), logged the change in `primary_rawjson_schema_edit_log.md` per rule 7, and updated `pass2_used/section.md` to teach the model the same rule.

**→ Rule.** A schema rule that forbids null on a field the model must predict is an instruction to hallucinate. Check every required-field rule against the question "can this always be read off the input?" before writing it.

<sub>`D:/00mk/steel project/training/Training/workmen's_diary/2026-08-25.md` · ground-truth-design</sub>

#### 🔴 CRITICAL · 2026-08-29 · build_dataset was modified to put val houses (01-05) into train too — val stopped being held out

**What happened.** A code comment records "2026-08-29 มะขามสั่ง: val houses (01-05) go in train too". train.jsonl is now 956 rows (727+229), val 229, test 33. Val is no longer a clean held-out set — the model sees the exam during training, so val numbers will be inflated by memorization and only measure fit.

**Root cause.** A split change was made directly in code with only a comment, and it was discovered incidentally by a later session rather than announced. The consequence for metric interpretation was not recorded alongside the change.

**Impact.** Every val metric from this point on overstates real performance and cannot be compared to prior rounds' val numbers. Only test (house 08, held out from both) remains a valid cross-round benchmark — and that was itself later dissolved (see the TEST_HOUSES entry).

**Fix.** Flagged in the diary with an explicit statement that val now measures fit only, and that test remains valid.

**→ Rule.** A train/val split change is a measurement change and must be announced with its consequence for every metric, not left as a code comment. Never let contaminated val numbers be compared against clean historical ones.

<sub>`D:/00mk/steel project/training/Training/workmen's_diary/2026-08-29.md` · eval-methodology</sub>

#### 🔴 CRITICAL · 2026-08-29 · House 08 pulled into training — the cross-round benchmark deliberately protected on 2026-08-24 is now gone

**What happened.** `TEST_HOUSES = set()` was set permanently and house 08 moved into train (987→1020 examples), reversing the 2026-08-24 decision that had specifically retrained a model to keep house 08 held out as a t02-vs-t03 benchmark.

**Root cause.** Data volume was prioritized over measurement integrity. The earlier decision had cost a retrain (~$0.35 plus restart) specifically to protect this benchmark, and that cost was not weighed against the 33 examples gained.

**Impact.** No held-out house remains that all rounds share, so no future model can be compared to t02 or t03 on clean ground. Combined with val contamination (above), there is now *no* uncontaminated evaluation set at all.

**Fix.** Not fixed — recorded as a deliberate reversal with the benchmark loss accepted.

**→ Rule.** Before dissolving a held-out benchmark, check what it cost to establish and what comparison becomes impossible without it. 33 extra training examples is not worth the ability to measure progress.

<sub>`D:/00mk/steel project/training/Training/workmen's_diary/2026-08-29.md` · eval-methodology</sub>

#### 🔴 CRITICAL · 2026-08-30 · Validation split was 100% contaminated — all 5 val houses were also in train, so every recall number measured memorisation, not generalization

**What happened.** A script that extracted house names from image paths in train.jsonl vs val.jsonl found that all 5 val houses (บ้าน_เล็ก_1ชั้น_01/_02, บ้าน_เล็ก_2ชั้น_01/_02/_03) were present in train as well. This was a deliberate design decision inherited from the t03 era (val = 'houses already reviewed', highest-quality GT, used to test whether the model could reproduce known answers) but it was still being read as a generalization metric.

**Root cause.** A split built for one purpose (reproduce-known-GT sanity check) was silently reused for a different purpose (measure generalization) across model generations, and nobody re-verified the house-level overlap when the purpose changed.

**Impact.** Every recall number reported from val up to this point was inflated and measured nothing about unseen drawings. It also weakened the earlier recommendation Claude had made ('stay on one split to save budget for eval'), forcing a mid-flight replan into k-fold.

**Fix.** Switched to real k-folds from the existing k=5 manifest and verified before spending money: fold0 = 815/205, fold1 = 816/204 matching fold_manifest exactly, 0 houses overlapping in either fold, 0 missing images, `<image>` token count = len(images) on every row, train:val exactly 4.00:1.

**→ Rule.** Verify house-level (entity-level, not row-level) overlap between train and val with a script every time a split is reused, and never quote a recall number without first proving the eval set is disjoint from training.

<sub>`D:/00mk/steel project/training/Training/workmen's_diary/2026-08-30.md` · evaluation-methodology</sub>

#### 🔴 CRITICAL · 2026-08-31 · The go/no-go test prompt contained the ground-truth answers, so a blind model passed 3/3

**What happened.** The v1 vision gate prompt included examples 'เช่น F1, B2, C1, ผ2'. F1 and ผ2 happened to be in the GT. The model copied the examples back verbatim, gave the identical string for both a footing plan and a section drawing, and the scoring script counted it as correct. Another page 'passed' by counting B1..B34 which coincidentally started with the right marks.

**Root cause.** Test design leaked the answer into the input, and the scorer used string containment with no check that different inputs produce different outputs.

**Impact.** A totally blind model scored 3/3 green. Believing it would have burned the entire night on a model that sees nothing — an exact repeat of t04.

**Fix.** Rewrote as v2 (examples removed, different pages must give different answers, sequential enumeration rejected) then v3 with three questions per page and no 'unreadable' escape hatch. Recorded as rule_of_tune Lesson 16 items 1 and 2.

**→ Rule.** Never put any token that appears in the ground truth into a test prompt, and always assert that different inputs produce different outputs — identical answers across inputs is the signature of a model that never looked at the image.

<sub>`D:/00mk/steel project/training/Training/workmen's_diary/2026-08-31.md` · eval-methodology</sub>

#### 🔴 CRITICAL · 2026-08-31 · Reusing t04's fold split left validation sets with zero pass0 rows, making the round's main hypothesis unmeasurable

**What happened.** After adopting t04's folds as the single split authority, the validation sets contained almost no pass0/pass2.4/pass3 rows — fold1 had 0/0/0. t04 split 40 houses without knowing only 10 houses have pass0/2.4/3 data (pass0 only 5), so the special houses all landed in train.

**Root cause.** A split designed for a uniform dataset was reused for a dataset with a highly skewed, rare subset, with no stratification on data-type availability.

**Impact.** Four GPUs would have trained and the result would have been unreadable — no way to measure whether the model learned pass0/pass3, which was the entire hypothesis of the round. Caught by Makham, not by the team.

**Fix.** Wrote build_house_folds() with deterministic house-level stratification (5 pass0 houses one per fold, 5 rich non-pass0 houses one per fold, 30 ordinary houses six per fold), giving every fold a val set containing all four passes.

**→ Rule.** Stratify folds on the presence of the rare data type you are actually trying to measure, and always print a per-fold count of each data type in val before launching — an empty cell there means the run cannot answer its own question.

<sub>`D:/00mk/steel project/training/Training/workmen's_diary/2026-08-31.md` · experiment-design</sub>

#### 🔴 CRITICAL · 2026-08-31 · Worst-case VRAM probe underpredicted real training peak because it did not accumulate fragmentation

**What happened.** A SORT_LONGEST worst-case probe measured peak 91.4 GB and was treated as proof that OOM risk was eliminated. In real training, gpu1 (fold0) and gpu4 (fold3) both OOM'd, and the two survivors were sitting at 93.7 and 94.66 of a 94.97 GB ceiling.
