**Impact.** The t05 dataset cannot be built as planned until all three are addressed; the matcher in particular is flagged as a design task where a wrong pairing would teach the whole dataset incorrectly.

**Fix.** Gaps enumerated with concrete next steps: run `cv_scan.py --pass25` in batch over all 40 houses (CPU-local, ~25 minutes, no GPU rental needed) and design the cv_mark↔GT matcher deliberately.

**→ Rule.** Before planning a training round around new input signals, verify the required ground truth and sidecar files actually exist across the whole corpus — count them, don't assume from a plan document.

<sub>`D:/00mk/steel project/training/Training/workmen's_diary/2026-08-30.md` · data-pipeline</sub>

#### 🟡 MEDIUM · 2026-08-31 · Nearly set up a wrong conclusion: InternVL reads 3.3x fewer pixels than Qwen by architecture

**What happened.** Analysis found that InternVL at full 12+1 tiling reads only ~2.4 MP versus Qwen's 7.86 MP — 3.3x less by architecture — and research shows higher resolution keeps helping small text well past 6 MP.

**Root cause.** An architectural resolution ceiling that is invisible unless computed, and would have been silently attributed to model quality in an A/B comparison.

**Impact.** Had Voldemort lost the comparison, the conclusion 'this model is worse' would have been wrong; it was pre-emptively flagged as a resolution ceiling.

**Fix.** Recorded explicitly in the dossier as an interpretation warning before results existed.

**→ Rule.** Compute each candidate's architectural input ceiling before an A/B comparison and record it as an interpretation caveat in advance, so a ceiling effect is never mistaken for model quality.

<sub>`D:/00mk/steel project/training/Training/workmen's_diary/2026-08-31.md` · experiment-design</sub>

#### 🟡 MEDIUM · 2026-08-31 · CV detector found only a fraction of the boxes on ~20 pages, blocking pass3 auto-matching

**What happened.** After geometry-based matching lifted pass3 from 13 to 23 pages with no eyeballing, ~20 pages were still stuck. On those the CV detector returned absurdly few boxes — 3 of 6, 10 of 36 — so neither the geometric fit nor manual pairing had enough to work with.

**Root cause.** The detector itself misses elements on certain page layouts; the matcher was never the bottleneck on those pages.

**Impact.** ~20 pages left out of the pass3 training set for this round; a manual eyeball queue still open, and the true detector recall is unmeasured.

**Fix.** not fixed — diagnosed as a detector problem and deferred, no detector work done

**→ Rule.** When a downstream step keeps failing on a subset, check the detector's own recall on that subset before writing more matching logic — a matcher can never recover boxes that were never detected.

<sub>`D:/00mk/steel project/training/Training/workmen's_diary/2026-08-31.md` · data-pipeline</sub>

#### 🟡 MEDIUM · 2026-08-31 · Two different final-loss figures were recorded on the same day, and the overfit verdict rests on the lower pair

**What happened.** The merge entry records final loss for fold0/2/3 as 0.273/0.259/0.250. Hours later, when diagnosing the greedy failure, the diary states "loss < 0.2 = overfit — ของเราจบที่ 0.10-0.13". The two numbers cannot both describe the same metric, yet the overfit conclusion (and the plan to cut epochs next round) is built on 0.10-0.13.

**Root cause.** The metric behind each figure is not named (train vs eval, last step vs smoothed) and neither was traced back to the logs before being used as evidence.

**Impact.** If 0.250-0.273 is the real final loss, it sits above Unsloth's 0.2 overfit threshold and the overfit diagnosis — plus the resulting plan to cut epochs — is unsupported; the memorised house_001 filenames are then unexplained.

**Fix.** not fixed — both numbers stand in the diary unreconciled

**→ Rule.** Before using a loss number as evidence for a decision, state which metric it is and re-read it from the log; two numbers for one metric means neither is usable yet.

<sub>`D:/00mk/steel project/training/Training/workmen's_diary/2026-08-31.md` · evaluation</sub>

#### 🟡 MEDIUM · 2026-09-01 · The merged soup model ships permanently unmeasured because all 40 houses were consumed as training data

**What happened.** Once the 4 fold models are averaged, the combined model has collectively seen all 40 houses, so no clean holdout remains to evaluate it. The team decided to measure per-fold only and label the soup 'unbenchmarked'.

**Root cause.** The k-fold-then-merge design consumes the entire dataset across folds, structurally eliminating any clean test set for the merged artifact. This was a consequence of the plan not accounted for when the plan was chosen.

**Impact.** The artifact actually intended for production carries no trustworthy accuracy number. Saved $6–9 in eval cost, but at the price of shipping something unmeasured.

**Fix.** Explicitly tagged `unbenchmarked` rather than quoting a per-fold number as if it applied to the soup.

**→ Rule.** If you plan to merge k-fold models, reserve a separate global holdout set from the start that no fold ever trains on. Failing that, label the merged artifact honestly as unmeasured — never borrow a fold's score to describe it.

<sub>`D:/00mk/steel project/training/Training/workmen's_diary/สอนมะขาม_ทำไม_Purson_กับ_Voldemort_พัง_2026-09-01.md` · eval-methodology</sub>

#### 🟡 MEDIUM · 2026-09-01 · Destrier's ~43% recall was measured with forgiving name matching, making the number not comparable to strict scores

**What happened.** The only recall figure for Destrier was obtained under a scoring mode that forgives differences in element-name formatting. That figure is being carried forward as the model's headline number.

**Root cause.** The scoring leniency mode was applied without pairing the number with a strict-mode counterpart, so the reported metric silently encodes a scoring choice rather than model capability.

**Impact.** The project's single quality number for its live model is inflated by an unknown amount and cannot be compared against any strictly-scored baseline.

**Fix.** Not fixed — the leniency is disclosed in the diary but no strict-mode number exists alongside it.

**→ Rule.** Always report a strict-mode score next to any lenient/normalised score, and never quote a lenient number alone as 'the' accuracy. State the matching rule every time a recall figure is written down.

<sub>`D:/00mk/steel project/training/Training/workmen's_diary/สอนมะขาม_ทำไม_Purson_กับ_Voldemort_พัง_2026-09-01.md` · eval-methodology</sub>

#### 🟡 MEDIUM · 2026-09-01 · The first house simulation had Claude read the drawings itself, burning tokens for a less accurate result

**What happened.** `sim_house_run.py` had Claude read the drawings itself as a stand-in for Destrier. Mid-task Makham switched the approach to use the GT answers in `json_แก้ไขแล้ว` instead — which both saved tokens and turned out to be the more accurate simulation.

**Root cause.** The simulation initially replaced the model with an LLM reading the same drawings, which is both expensive and generates a different answer distribution than the fine-tuned model. Available ground truth on disk was overlooked as the obvious substitute.

**Impact.** Token cost on the first simulation round and a less faithful result; the work had to be redone as `sim_house01.py`.

**Fix.** Switched to using ground-truth answers, which directly exposed the count>1 pass3 bug the hand-authored version had hidden.

**→ Rule.** To simulate a model, substitute its known-correct outputs (ground truth) — not another model's improvised answers. It is cheaper and strictly more faithful.

<sub>`2026-09-01.md` · testing-methodology</sub>

#### 🟡 MEDIUM · 2026-09-01 · k-fold was designed as 5 groups but only 4 folds were run, so 8 houses sit in every training set and are never evaluated

**What happened.** The doc states the 40 houses were split into 5 groups of 8 ('5 กอง กองละ 8 หลัง'), but the fold table lists only fold 0–3, and the merge equation uses k = 4 with weight 0.25 each. Group 5 is therefore in the training set of all four models and is held out by none of them.

**Root cause.** A 5-way split was declared and a 4-way cross-validation was executed; nobody reconciled the two. The 'ทุกตัวเห็นข้อมูลเท่ากันเป๊ะ (32 จาก 40 หลัง)' justification for equal soup weights checks the count of training houses but not which houses, so the asymmetry is invisible to that argument.

**Impact.** 8 of 40 hand-annotated houses (20% of the most expensive asset in the project) produce zero evaluation signal, and every fold model has seen them, so no fold score is clean with respect to that group. The soup is 'unbenchmarked' partly for this structural reason, not only because the union covers 40.

**Fix.** Not fixed — the inconsistency is stated in the teaching doc without being flagged as a problem.

**→ Rule.** If you declare k groups, run k folds or say plainly which group was dropped and why. A held-out set that is never held out is training data wearing an eval label.

<sub>`D:/00mk/steel project/training/Training/workmen's_diary/สอนมะขาม_ทำไม_Purson_กับ_Voldemort_พัง_2026-09-01.md` · eval-methodology</sub>

#### 🟡 MEDIUM · 2026-09-01 · The warning printed when elements were dropped blamed the model ('generation หลุด') for data our own sanitizer had deleted

**What happened.** When `sanitize_elements()` discarded valid negative-level elements, the warning it emitted said the generation had been truncated — pointing every future debugger at the model, at 4-bit quantisation, at timeouts, at anything except the twelve-line regex that actually threw the data away. Confirmed on real ground truth: 07บ้าน_ใหญ่_2ชั้น_01 page 35 lost 3 of 11 elements under a 'model failed' banner while the model had answered correctly.

**Root cause.** The warning message asserted a cause the code had no way to verify — the sanitizer knows only that it deleted a field, not why the field looked odd, but it printed a model-side diagnosis anyway.

**Impact.** Misattributed blame on every occurrence; anyone acting on that message would have gone hunting in the model/serving stack instead of the 30-line sanitizer, and the bug survived until an unrelated 52-agent bug hunt found it by reading source.

**Fix.** Sanitizer changed to an allowlist of dimensions that genuinely cannot be negative; the misleading blame text went away with the false positive

**→ Rule.** An error message must name only what the emitting code can actually prove. A guessed cause in a log line is worse than no cause — it redirects the next debugger away from the real file.

<sub>`D:/00mk/steel project/training/Training/workmen's_diary/2026-09-01.md` · observability</sub>

#### ⚪ LOW · 2026-07-21 · Element result written with two different denominators in one cell, and precision never reported

**What happened.** The results row reads "16/170 (9.4%, out of 61 elements)" — 170 is the ground-truth count and 61 appears to be how many elements the model actually emitted. Only recall (16/170) is given a percentage; precision (16/61 ≈ 26%, i.e. most emitted elements were wrong) is never computed or stated.

**Root cause.** The eval script reports a single "element found" ratio, so over-generation (hallucinated elements) is invisible in the reported score.

**Impact.** The next tuning round is being aimed at "low recall" alone, when the data hints that roughly three quarters of the elements the model does emit are not matching — a different problem needing a different fix.

**Fix.** Not fixed.

**→ Rule.** For any extraction task, report precision and recall together (or F1) — a recall-only number hides hallucinated output and misdirects the next iteration.

<sub>`D:/00mk/steel project/training/Training/workmen's_diary/2026-07-21.md` · eval-methodology</sub>

#### ⚪ LOW · 2026-08-25 · Previously recorded that ERNIE-4.5-VL required ERNIEKit — actually an Unsloth notebook exists

**What happened.** An earlier assessment stated ERNIE-4.5-VL-28B-A3B could only be trained with Baidu's ERNIEKit. A recheck found a working Unsloth notebook. (The model was still rejected, at 28B versus the requested 122B±50.)

**Root cause.** A tooling-support claim was recorded from an incomplete search and not re-verified when it was written into the record, becoming a fact that could have wrongly eliminated a candidate.

**Impact.** Low here because the model failed on size anyway, but the same error pattern could eliminate a viable candidate on false grounds.

**Fix.** Corrected explicitly in the record, with the previous claim named as wrong rather than quietly replaced.

**→ Rule.** Tag every tooling-support claim with the date and source it was checked against, and re-verify before using it to eliminate a candidate — the ecosystem changes weekly.

<sub>`D:/00mk/steel project/training/Training/workmen's_diary/2026-08-25(teach mk).md` · vendor/evaluation</sub>

#### ⚪ LOW · 2026-08-25 · A 19-column detection count on บ้าน17 หน้า15 was reported without ever being verified against the drawing

**What happened.** Among the visual verification results, บ้าน17 หน้า15 was recorded as showing 19 columns with the caveat that it was "not individually verified — some may be doubles", sitting in the same list as the fully-checked 14/14 and 12/12 results.

**Root cause.** Verification was done by eyeballing overlays page by page, and one page was reported from the count alone without the per-box check the other pages received.

**Impact.** An unverified number sits in the same results table as verified ones; given a known doubling bug at (B,2) on another house, 19 is plausibly inflated and could be quoted later as a real count.

**Fix.** not fixed — the caveat was recorded honestly, but the page was never re-checked.

**→ Rule.** Either verify a number or leave it out of the results table — an unverified figure listed beside verified ones gets quoted as if it were verified.

<sub>`D:/00mk/steel project/training/Training/workmen's_diary/2026-08-25.md` · measurement</sub>

#### ⚪ LOW · 2026-08-29 · easyocr experiment failed — sheet_code 0/4 correct even after two rounds of tuning

**What happened.** easyocr (th+en) was tried as a replacement for the VLM in pass 0. Tested on 3 real pages, expanded to 5 houses, with a second round adding title-block cropping and preprocessing (autocontrast/sharpen/5x upscale). Result: sheet_code correct on 0 of 4 pages (A-01/A-02 were unreadable as codes), sheet_name only partially readable with inconsistent spelling.

**Root cause.** OCR engines trained on document text handle Thai construction drawing title blocks (mixed alphanumeric codes, thin CAD line weights, dense small text) poorly. The second tuning round was spent before accepting the first round's verdict.

**Impact.** A whole evening's experiment produced a negative result — though a genuinely useful one, and cheap (CPU only).

**Fix.** Decision recorded: pass 0 stays VLM. The original reason (views[]/layout need a VLM) now has an experimental reason added on top.

**→ Rule.** Set a stop condition before starting a tool bake-off ("if round 1 is under X, stop"). A negative result is valuable and worth documenting — but budget one tuning round, not two, before accepting it.

<sub>`D:/00mk/steel project/training/Training/workmen's_diary/2026-08-29.md` · failed-experiment</sub>

#### ⚪ LOW · 2026-08-30 · 'No truncation warnings' conclusion was based on a 40/1020 row sample, not full coverage

**What happened.** The dry-run reported no truncation warnings, but it only touched a random 40 of 1020 rows — coverage was explicitly not 100% and the residual risk was accepted.

**Root cause.** A 5-step dry-run cannot exercise the whole dataset; the absence of a warning on a small sample was used as evidence about the whole corpus.

**Impact.** Combined with the 17773 > 8192 finding later, this partial check gave false confidence that the sequence-length problem did not exist.

**Fix.** The gap was acknowledged in writing at the time; no full-corpus check was run.

**→ Rule.** A dry-run sample cannot prove a dataset-wide property. For length/truncation questions, run a cheap CPU-only pass over 100% of rows instead of inferring from a 4% sample.

<sub>`D:/00mk/steel project/training/Training/workmen's_diary/2026-08-30.md` · evaluation-methodology</sub>

#### ⚪ LOW · 2026-08-30 · Naive 'take first N rows' eval sampling would have landed entirely inside one house because the jsonl is house-ordered

**What happened.** When building the reduced eval set, taking the first N rows was rejected because the jsonl is sorted by house — the sample could have come from a single house and told nothing about the fold.

**Root cause.** Data files ordered by entity make sequential sampling non-representative; the default sampling approach would silently produce a biased eval.

**Impact.** Avoided before it happened. Had it shipped, per-fold recall numbers would have been meaningless and possibly misleading in either direction.

**Fix.** `make_eval_samples.py` uses stratified sampling across all houses, yielding 24 samples per fold covering all 8/8 houses in every fold (seed=42).

**→ Rule.** Never sample an ordered dataset sequentially — stratify by the grouping key (house/entity) and assert the sample covers every group before trusting the resulting metric.

<sub>`D:/00mk/steel project/training/Training/workmen's_diary/2026-08-30.md` · evaluation-methodology</sub>

#### ⚪ LOW · 2026-09-01 · A 2-anchor least-squares fit always yields residual 0, so a residual-based quality gate would have passed every bad fit

**What happened.** While building pass3's guard rails it was found that with only two anchors the fit is exactly determined — residual is 0 by construction, no matter how wrong the anchors are — so the residual quality check, the main defence against a bogus scale factor, could never fire. The minimum-anchor rule was set to 3 specifically because of this.

**Root cause.** A quality metric was about to be applied in a regime where it is mathematically incapable of failing — the same class as a validation gate whose prompt contains the answer.

**Impact.** Caught at design time; had it shipped, two-anchor pages would have emitted confidently-wrong px/m scales into real measured spans with a green quality reading.

**Fix.** Hard gate: fewer than 3 anchors returns None with a Thai reason instead of a number

**→ Rule.** Before trusting a validation metric, ask in which regimes it can return a pass without any information — a metric that cannot fail is not a gate, it is decoration.

<sub>`D:/00mk/steel project/training/Training/workmen's_diary/2026-09-01.md` · eval-methodology</sub>

---

## T04 — Data Quality, Integrity & Loss

*Wrong, missing, duplicated, contaminated, or destroyed data — including irreversible loss.*

**143 entries** · 26 critical · 45 high

#### 🔴 CRITICAL · 2026-07-02 · Model systematically misread main_bar_type DB↔RB while reading the same symbol correctly for stirrups on the same page

**What happened.** The first Claude-vs-Qwen pilot comparison (4 pages of house 01) found main_bar_type being misread DB↔RB systematically on one page, while the identical symbol was read correctly for stirrups on that same page. This became lesson #6 in No_touch_box/CLAUDE.md and is still cited today.

**Root cause.** The model was inferring bar type from diameter size or from surrounding context rather than from the Ø (circle) symbol itself, so the same glyph resolved differently depending on which field it was feeding. There was no rule in the spec at the time stating that Ø always means RB, so the inference was unconstrained.

**Impact.** Wrong bar type on main reinforcement propagates into rebar weight, BBS cut lists and BOQ steel cost for every affected element. Because it was systematic (not random), it would not average out. It later required an explicit correction pass on 2026-07-06 rewriting every element's main_bar.type from DB to RB in page 21 view1.

**Fix.** Recorded as lesson #6 in No_touch_box/CLAUDE.md; on 2026-07-06 codified as an explicit spec rule ('the Ø (circle) symbol always = RB — never infer DB from the diameter size alone') and the affected file was corrected.

**→ Rule.** Never let the model infer a categorical value (bar type, grade) from a continuous one (diameter). Write the symbol→value mapping into the spec as an absolute rule. And when the same glyph is read correctly in one field and wrongly in another on the same page, that is a prompt/spec defect, not a vision limit — fix the rule, not the sample.

<sub>`D:/00mk/steel project/training/Training/workmen's_diary/2026-07-02.md` · extraction-bug / wrong-data</sub>

#### 🔴 CRITICAL · 2026-07-05 · Concrete strength conflict 210 vs 240 ksc between fresh read and old Gen 1 data, never resolved

**What happened.** A fresh read of page 18 (S-01 notes) gave concrete_strength_ksc = 210 (Fc'=210 kg/cm², clearly labeled in the image), but the older Gen 1 file qwen-output/บ้าน_เล็ก_1ชั้น_01_หน้า18.json recorded 240. Neither was verified. The conflict was still open at the end of 2026-07-06 and rolled forward as a pending item across both days.

**Root cause.** Two independent extraction generations wrote the same physical fact to different files with no reconciliation step and no single source of truth for house-level constants. Nothing in the pipeline compares a new read against the prior generation's value or blocks on a mismatch, so a contradiction can sit silently in the dataset indefinitely.

**Impact.** A core structural constant for the whole house is ambiguous. Any downstream BOQ/BBS concrete pricing or strength-dependent calculation built on this house would be wrong 50% of the time. Because of this, concrete_grade was deliberately left null across every joined beam element in Gen 3.3, so the joined spec data is incomplete too.

**Fix.** Not fixed. Left as pending item #3 on the end-of-2026-07-06 list ('The concrete_grade 210 vs 240 ksc conflict'); concrete_grade was written as null everywhere rather than guessing.

**→ Rule.** House-level constants (concrete grade, steel grade, cover) must live in one master file per house and be reconciled against every prior generation before extraction continues. A detected conflict blocks the field — write null with a flag, never a guess — and gets a named owner and a deadline the same day, not a rolling pending line.

<sub>`D:/00mk/steel project/training/Training/workmen's_diary/2026-07-05.md` · data-conflict / wrong-number</sub>

#### 🔴 CRITICAL · 2026-07-09 · An order to rename raw/ to 'old data no longer in use' would have broken the live pipeline in 5 scripts

**What happened.** raw/ was believed to be obsolete and ordered renamed. A grep before acting found it is 533 MB and hardcoded as an active path in run_pipeline.py, analyze_folder.py, build_document_map.py, pdf-processor.py and upload-to-supabase-storage.js (7 spots). The rename was then done deliberately with the code paths fixed — and then cancelled, requiring a full undo.

**Root cause.** A folder's status was inferred from its name and from memory rather than from what the code actually references; a generic name like raw/ carries no signal about whether it is live.

**Impact.** Would have broken the main extraction pipeline instantly on a 533 MB data directory; instead cost a full rename-and-undo cycle across 5 scripts, .gitignore, and a locked-folder incident.

**Fix.** Grepped every hardcoded path before acting, asked before proceeding, then reverted the folder name, all 5 scripts and .gitignore to the original state; final git status was clean.

**→ Rule.** Never rename or move a data folder on the strength of its name — grep the whole repo for the path first, and treat 'the user says it's old' as a hypothesis to verify, not an instruction to execute.

<sub>`D:/00mk/steel project/training/Training/workmen's_diary/2026-07-09.md` · data-integrity/file-ops</sub>

#### 🔴 CRITICAL · 2026-07-10 · Running the task generator for house 2 would have silently overwritten house 1's output files

**What happened.** label-studio-tasks-makham.js wrote to fixed filenames (label-studio-tasks-makham-elements.json etc.) with no house name in them. Running it for house #2 would have overwritten house #1's already-generated (and already-uploaded) task files with no warning.

**Root cause.** The script was written for a single-house world and its output contract was never revisited when the workflow moved to a numbered multi-house folder structure.

**Impact.** Caught during a readiness check just before house #2 was started, so no data was lost — but it was a genuine blocker that stopped house #2 for a session.

**Fix.** Changed output filenames to include the house name, re-ran house 1 to confirm identical counts (34/39/26/99), and deleted the leftover fixed-name files.

**→ Rule.** Any script whose output is keyed by an input entity must put that entity in the filename from day one — a fixed output path plus a new input dimension equals silent overwrite.

<sub>`D:/00mk/steel project/training/Training/workmen's_diary/2026-07-10.md` · tooling/data-loss</sub>

#### 🔴 CRITICAL · 2026-07-19 · The 10-house price table was misread in many rows across all five houses' copies, not just the one row that triggered the sweep

**What happened.** The 8x reference-glyph sweep that reverted the house-10 'fix' also uncovered a series of further errors in the same table: #1 corrected to 1,020,000, #2 to 1,460,000 (this project's own house 2 price), #4 spread to 1,824,000, a house design size to 3/8=156, and in house 1's fifth copy #8 spread 1,662,000→1,622,000 and #10 spread 2,235,000→2,035,000.

**Root cause.** Thai numerals were being judged glyph-by-glyph in isolation at high zoom, where ๑ and ๙ are easily confused, instead of against a reference glyph elsewhere on the same sheet. The error was systematic, so it recurred in every independent reading of the same table.

**Impact.** Six-plus wrong price figures across five houses' files, including the project's own house price. Only found because one row's 'correction' happened to be checked a second time.

**Fix.** All five copies corrected on 2026-07-19 by comparing each digit against a reference glyph on the same sheet; the table now agrees across all five houses.

**→ Rule.** Numeral reading needs an in-sheet reference glyph as calibration, exactly like pixel measurement needs a calibrated scale. Never judge a Thai digit in isolation at zoom.

<sub>`D:/00mk/steel project/training/Training/workmen's_diary/2026-07-19.md` · data-quality</sub>

#### 🔴 CRITICAL · 2026-07-21 · Instance destroyed before any result file was downloaded — adapter, merged model and GGUF all lost

**What happened.** Makham destroyed the Vast.ai instance while the 7.5GB LoRA adapter, the 66GB merged model and the 21.2GB Q4_K_M GGUF still existed only on that machine. Vast.ai destroy is permanent (unlike stop), so all three were lost with no recovery.

**Root cause.** No backup gate existed in the workflow: results were treated as 'saved' because they were on disk, and the intended HuggingFace upload was deferred (blocked on a missing token) rather than treated as the completion condition of the run.

**Impact.** A whole night's training + merge + quantize work destroyed — GPU rental money, an all-nighter and a missed class, all for output that no longer exists; the full training run must be redone from scratch.

**Fix.** Not fixed — the files are unrecoverable. Only the bug-fixed scripts, the dataset and the written lessons survive.

**→ Rule.** An artifact on rented storage is not a backup. Before any instance is stopped or destroyed, verify by listing the file at its off-instance destination (HuggingFace/local) that every result has actually landed there.

<sub>`D:/00mk/steel project/training/Training/workmen's_diary/2026-07-21.md` · data-loss</sub>

#### 🔴 CRITICAL · 2026-07-21 · Rented instance destroyed before the LoRA adapter, merged model and GGUF were copied off

**What happened.** The Vast.ai instance was shut down before any of the day's outputs (LoRA adapter, merged model, GGUF) had been downloaded or uploaded anywhere. Rented-instance storage is ephemeral, so all of it was gone irrecoverably.

**Root cause.** No hard gate existed between 'work finished' and 'instance destroyed'. The reminder to back up was given softly rather than as a blocking step, and no backup destination (HuggingFace) had been set up in advance.

**Impact.** A full day of GPU rental, training and GGUF conversion had to be redone to obtain a usable model. Only the bug-fixed scripts and written lessons survived.

**Fix.** Adopted uploading results to HuggingFace as an explicit pipeline phase; a HF write token was tested in advance on the next round (Phase 0.1).

**→ Rule.** Backup-off-instance is a blocking phase, not a reminder: an ephemeral machine may only be destroyed after a verified copy exists somewhere durable, and the destination must be tested before the run starts.

<sub>`D:/00mk/steel project/training/Training/workmen's_diary/สอนมะขาม_รวม.md` · process/data-loss</sub>

#### 🔴 CRITICAL · 2026-07-24 · House 5's two beam-plan sheets were missing 31 beams, all supplied by the human rather than found by extraction or review

**What happened.** Reformatting house 5's pages 32/33 (floor 1 and floor 2 beam plans) required adding 31 beams (16 + 15) supplied directly by Makham, plus deleting three recorded lines that do not exist, plus adding a new dummy grid B'=12.2 so one of the added beams could land.

**Root cause.** The original extraction of these sheets captured only a fraction of the beams present, and the earlier review passes on this house did not perform a completeness check against the sheet.

**Impact.** Roughly half the beams on two sheets of a training-set house were absent until a human enumerated them by hand — extraction and automated review both scored zero on this sheet pair.

**Fix.** 31 beams added and 3 non-existent lines deleted on 2026-07-24, then cross-checked against page00 with no dangling grid_ref.

**→ Rule.** If a human has to enumerate 31 missing elements by hand, the extraction of that sheet type is not working — record the sheet type as a known weak spot and measure recall on it, rather than patching house by house.

<sub>`D:/00mk/steel project/training/Training/workmen's_diary/2026-07-24.md` · data-quality</sub>

#### 🔴 CRITICAL · 2026-07-28 · Proposed skipping Phase 8 because t02 lost the comparison — not noticing the adapter backup is bundled inside that same phase

**What happened.** After t02 lost on every metric, the assistant proposed skipping the export phase as pointless. The adapter backup is bundled into Phase 8; following the proposal literally would have left the entire round with no backup of anything at all — a direct repeat of the DAY OF SHAME failure.

**Root cause.** A phase was reasoned about by its headline purpose ('export GGUF') without enumerating what else it does. Bundling a safety-critical step (backup) inside an optional-looking deliverable step made the safety step skippable by accident.

**Impact.** Caught before execution. Had it been followed, the entire 85-minute paid training run would have produced nothing recoverable.

**Fix.** The LoRA adapter (5.14GB) was immediately backed up by hand to Sicilian44/qwen3vl-30b-thai-rc, outside the normal Phase 8 process, and the size verified through the HF API.

**→ Rule.** Never bundle a safety-critical backup inside a phase that can be skipped for business reasons. Backup must be its own unconditional step, and before skipping any phase, enumerate everything it does — not just its name.

<sub>`D:/00mk/steel project/training/Training/workmen's_diary/2026-07-28.md` · process/data-loss</sub>

#### 🔴 CRITICAL · 2026-08-02 · Houses 10/11 section files had no elements[] at all — each invented its own array name

**What happened.** `pattern=section` files in houses 10 and 11 contained no `elements[]`; instead each file invented a per-file array name (`beams`, `columns`, `slabs`, `footing_types`, `details`, `sections`) with a different element shape inside, so renaming the array would not have been enough.

**Root cause.** The schema described how to write each *field* but never locked the *shape of the file* — there was no rule saying 'the container is always elements[]', so an extraction could organise the file however seemed natural without violating anything written.

**Impact.** 30 files were structurally incompatible with every consumer; a full restructure (not a rename) was needed, and it required stopping to get explicit approval because it changed real schema structure.

**Fix.** Folded all the invented arrays into `elements[]` with `element_id`/`element_type`, converted units and rebar shapes, and kept every original value in a `*_printed_as` field. Later locked by the new §0 FORMAT LOCK.

**→ Rule.** Specify the container shape, not just the field rules. If the spec never says 'the file looks like THIS', extractions will each invent a reasonable-looking structure and none will be wrong by the written rules.

<sub>`2026-08-02.md` · data-quality</sub>

#### 🔴 CRITICAL · 2026-08-02 · Every reviewed beam plan in houses 01–05 was missing real beams (20→27, 22→36, 30→38, 5→21) — houses 06–11 never checked

**What happened.** When houses 01–05's beam plans were reviewed against the drawings, every single one was found to be missing real beams — in one case 5 extracted where 21 exist. Houses 06 through 11 have still never been checked, and the same defect must be assumed present.

**Root cause.** Beam extraction under-detects systematically — beams that continue across a page, are drawn faintly, or are labelled off to the side get skipped, and nothing counts extracted beams against a visual check.

**Impact.** The single most damaging data defect in the corpus: training on labels with beams missing teaches the model to under-predict, which is already the weakest measured metric. Six houses carry an unmeasured amount of it.

**Fix.** Houses 01–05 were corrected by review against the drawings. Houses 06–11 remain unchecked — repeatedly flagged as the highest-value pending item across four separate sessions.

**→ Rule.** A systematic under-detection defect found in every sampled house must be assumed present in every unsampled house. Never build a training dataset on unaudited beam plans — audit first, then train.

<sub>`2026-08-02.md` · data-quality</sub>

#### 🔴 CRITICAL · 2026-08-02 · The 'strip underscores from element_id' order would have collapsed 17 genuinely different elements into one

**What happened.** Following the instruction literally, `บันได_ST1` and `steps_ST1` both reduce to `ST1`; `B1_ชานพัก` (a landing beam) would have collapsed onto the ordinary `B1`; three eave materials and three separate rafters would each have merged. 17 collisions were found and 37 ids across 5 houses reverted.

**Root cause.** A blanket textual transformation was ordered without checking whether the suffixes carried real semantic distinctions — some did, encoding genuinely different structural members.

**Impact.** Silent data loss almost shipped: distinct structural members merged into one id, unrecoverable without going back to the drawings. Caught by a post-transform collision check.

**Fix.** Kept the suffix on the 17 colliding cases with a flag explaining why; final check confirmed 0 collisions.

**→ Rule.** Always run a collision check before and after any id-normalising transform. If two different things map to the same id, the transform is wrong for those cases — an order to normalise is not an order to lose data.

<sub>`2026-08-02.md` · data-quality</sub>

#### 🔴 CRITICAL · 2026-08-02 · element_type had grown to 359 distinct values across 4,507 elements

**What happened.** An audit found `element_type` — supposed to be a small closed vocabulary — had accumulated 359 distinct values across 4,507 elements.

**Root cause.** Free-text enum with no enforcement over 11 houses of extraction; every extraction that met an unfamiliar member invented a plausible type name.

**Impact.** Grouping, costing, or filtering by element_type was meaningless across the corpus; a model trained on it would learn 359 near-synonymous labels.

**Fix.** Added §0.4's canonical element_type list, enforced by the checker.

**→ Rule.** Any enum with no machine enforcement will grow to hundreds of values. Cap it in the checker from day one, and make an unknown value a hard failure — not a silent accept.

<sub>`2026-08-02.md` · data-quality</sub>

#### 🔴 CRITICAL · 2026-08-02 · ~500 elements had no element_id at all — and they were in houses 01–07, not the newer ones

**What happened.** An independent audit (comparing the JSON type of every key across all 2,366 files, deliberately not relying on the existing checker) found ~500 elements with no `element_id` in houses 01–07. Houses 08–11 were already complete — the opposite of the 'follow 01–05' assumption.

**Root cause.** Two causes: `element_id` presence was never checked, and the audit that found it only worked because it did NOT rely on the existing checker — which only tests rules it already knows about.

**Impact.** ~500 elements were unjoinable to any spec or schedule. And the reference-house assumption was disproven a second time in the same day.

**Fix.** Backfilled ids from printed marks/item_no/descriptive style with per-entry flags recording how each was derived.

**→ Rule.** Periodically audit with a method that does NOT use your own checker — a checker can only find defects someone already thought of. Type-profiling every key across the corpus finds the ones nobody predicted.

<sub>`2026-08-02.md` · data-quality</sub>

#### 🔴 CRITICAL · 2026-08-02 · CONTENT REGRESSION: house 05's price table still had the old wrong digits that the log said were 'fixed on all 5 copies'

**What happened.** Item 37 recorded that wrong price digits (1,060,000/1,560,000) had been fixed on all 5 copies, verified at 8x zoom. House 05's copy had escaped — it still carried the old wrong numbers. Houses 03/04 were checked and correct; only 05's copy was wrong.

**Root cause.** The fix was verified per *issue* ('the price problem is fixed') rather than per *copy* ('each of the 5 files now shows the right digits'). The log recorded completion of the decision, not completion of the application.

**Impact.** Wrong money figures — off by hundreds of thousands of baht — sat in the corpus for an extended period while the log claimed they were fixed. This is the second time the 'log says fixed' failure mode bit in the same project.

**Fix.** Restored the item-37 consensus digits (executing the already-verified decision, not making a new one); old digits kept in `*_printed_as` with RE-CORRECTED flags.

**→ Rule.** 'The log says fixed' must be verified per copy, not per issue. When a fix touches N copies, the completion check must count N verified copies — anything less is a claim, not a fix.

<sub>`2026-08-02.md` · data-quality</sub>

#### 🔴 CRITICAL · 2026-08-21 · roof_frame_plan split across two patterns — 8 of 11 houses' roof beams never reach the BOQ

**What happened.** All 12 roof-framing files across 11 houses carry discipline: "structural", but 4 are pattern: "plan" and 8 are pattern: "roof_plan". Constistant's buildElements() only reads pattern === 'plan', so the roof beams in 8 of 11 houses silently never reach the BOQ. Found while splitting the plan subtask by structural element.

**Root cause.** The 'roof_plan' pattern name reads as the obvious home for a roof framing sheet, but the taxonomy intends roof_plan for architectural roof sheets and structural roof framing as a plan. Annotators applied the intuitive label; nothing validated pattern against discipline, and the consumer silently filters rather than warning on an unrecognized pattern.

**Impact.** Live data-loss bug: an entire structural element class is missing from the BOQ for 8 of 11 annotated houses. Any t03 accuracy measured against this ground truth would be measured against incomplete data.

**Fix.** Not fixed in the data as of end of session — recorded as a required fix. Mitigated by rewriting §1 pattern #12 roof_plan plus a new '⚠️ roof_plan vs plan' warning block pinning structural roof framing as plan, and by writing the trap into the op04 skill.

**→ Rule.** Any consumer that filters on a taxonomy value must warn on values it does not recognize instead of silently dropping them, and every discipline+pattern combination should be validated by check_format.py — an intuitive-but-wrong label repeated by annotators is invisible without a cross-field rule.

<sub>`D:/00mk/steel project/training/Training/workmen's_diary/2026-08-21.md` · data-quality</sub>

#### 🔴 CRITICAL · 2026-08-24 · `roof_plan` mislabel on 8 houses' structural roof framing caused live BOQ data loss in Constistant

**What happened.** Eight houses had their structural roof-framing sheets labelled `roof_plan` instead of `plan`. Constistant's BOQ pipeline did not consume `roof_plan`, so those elements were silently dropped from quantity takeoff — a live production data-loss bug.

**Root cause.** A page-type vocabulary value existed in the GT that no downstream consumer handled. Nothing validated that every emitted page-type value had a consumer, so a mislabel became a silent drop rather than an error.

**Impact.** BOQ totals in the live Constistant app were understated for 8 houses' roof framing, with no error surfaced to anyone.

**Fix.** Relabelled `roof_plan`→`plan` on all 8 houses as part of the schema-normalize pass.

**→ Rule.** Every enum value a producer can emit must have an explicit consumer or an explicit loud rejection. A value that is silently ignored downstream is a data-loss bug waiting to happen.

<sub>`D:/00mk/steel project/training/Training/workmen's_diary/2026-08-24.md` · data-quality</sub>

#### 🔴 CRITICAL · 2026-08-24 · Beam plans have never been checked for missing beams in ANY house — the training GT quality is unknown

**What happened.** Houses 06-11 content review against the original drawings was still owed, and the note records that beam plans have never been verified for missing beams in any house at all.

**Root cause.** GT review effort went to schema/format correctness (which is scriptable) rather than content completeness (which requires opening the drawing). The bottleneck subtask's GT was never audited.

**Impact.** The model is being trained toward beam-plan GT that may itself be undercounting beams — meaning 0% recall might partly be measuring against incomplete ground truth. Cannot distinguish model failure from GT failure.

**Fix.** Not fixed — carried forward as pending.

**→ Rule.** Audit the ground truth of the subtask you are optimizing *before* spending GPU money optimizing toward it. A recall metric is only as trustworthy as its GT.

<sub>`D:/00mk/steel project/training/Training/workmen's_diary/2026-08-24.md` · data-quality</sub>

#### 🔴 CRITICAL · 2026-08-25 · Schema revised 43 times in 5 weeks with zero retrofit of already-extracted houses

**What happened.** Makham asked why the gridmaster files of house 20 and house 28 looked different from each other. Tracing it back revealed the primary schema had been edited 43 times over 5 weeks and older houses were never migrated forward, so the dataset contained many mutually incompatible generations of the same file type.

**Root cause.** No migration step was attached to the schema-change process. Each spec edit was treated as a forward-looking rule for new extractions only, with no obligation to sweep existing files, so drift accumulated silently one revision at a time.

**Impact.** 49 houses of training data internally inconsistent; the previous sweep on 08-24 had only covered 11 houses, so 38 houses remained stale until this session. Model was being trained on a mixture of schema generations.

**Fix.** Normalized both trees (`json_แก้ไขแล้ว/` and `rawjson_ยังไม่ได้แก้ไขโดนคน/`) against the current spec in one pass — 485 fixes / 423 files / all 49 houses.

**→ Rule.** Every schema revision must ship with either a retrofit script run over all existing data or an explicit written decision that old files stay on the old generation. Never leave "retrofit later" implicit — 43 unrecorded deferrals is what a silently forked dataset looks like.

<sub>`D:/00mk/steel project/training/Training/workmen's_diary/2026-08-25.md` · data-drift</sub>

#### 🔴 CRITICAL · 2026-08-25 · A 1,220-line old-value→new-value log was sitting inside the training-data folder as a cross-house contamination channel

**What happened.** `สิ่งที่ต้องแก้.md`, a 1,220-line log recording per-house old values and their corrections, was stored inside the training-data folder. A model extracting house 30 could read numbers belonging to house 01 out of that file and pick the wrong house's values.

**Root cause.** A human working document was filed in the same directory as machine-consumed training data, with no rule separating "notes about the data" from "the data itself".

**Impact.** Live cross-house data-contamination risk across the whole training set — the model could be fed another house's dimensions as if they were the current one.

**Fix.** Moved to `wait_for_ทิ้ง/stale_value_logs/` with a README explaining why.

**→ Rule.** Never put per-item human correction notes inside a folder a model reads. Working notes go in a separate tree; if a file lists concrete values from multiple subjects, it is a contamination vector by construction.

<sub>`D:/00mk/steel project/training/Training/workmen's_diary/2026-08-25.md` · data-contamination</sub>

#### 🔴 CRITICAL · 2026-08-31 · Inherited validation set was a 100% subset of training data

**What happened.** When merging the 4-pass dataset, the t04 validation file's 229 rows were found to overlap the training set completely (id overlap 229/229), and both of t05's chosen validation houses were inside t04's training set.

**Root cause.** Splits were inherited across rounds without re-verifying id overlap; earlier rounds split by row rather than by house, so the same house appeared on both sides.

**Impact.** Every validation number produced from that split was meaningless — the model was being evaluated on data it had memorized.

**Fix.** Discarded the old val set and re-split by house with one rule applied uniformly across all passes; added a val-contamination check to smoke_4pass.py.

**→ Rule.** Re-verify split integrity by id and by house every time a dataset is inherited or merged — never assume a previous round's val file is clean.

<sub>`D:/00mk/steel project/training/Training/workmen's_diary/2026-08-31.md` · data-integrity</sub>

#### 🔴 CRITICAL · 2026-08-31 · Batch-labelled 89 pass0 pages with sheet_code null even though the ground truth was clearly readable

**What happened.** While batch-labelling material_list pages, sheet_code and sheet_name were set to null on all 89 pages despite the GT plainly showing values like 'ปร.4 (แผ่นที่ 1/23)'. The pass0 prompt itself states this is the only chance to capture them because the title block is cropped away for later passes.

**Root cause.** The batch script was written for the layout question (which half is which sheet) and never revisited the other required fields; the prompt's own 'only chance' warning was not re-read before generating 89 labels.

**Impact.** Would have taught the model to skip text it can actually read, and permanently lost the sheet code for those pages since no later pass ever sees the title block. Caught only because Makham asked whether pass0 includes OCR.

**Fix.** Rewrote so the top-level field carries the lower-numbered sheet and the second sheet is preserved in warnings[] as readable text; made the script idempotent by locating target pages from GT directly. pass0 pages with a real sheet_code went from 63.2% to 80.1%.

**→ Rule.** When batch-generating labels, re-read the prompt contract for every required field, not just the field the batch is about — and any field the prompt calls 'the only chance to capture' must never be nulled while it is readable.

<sub>`D:/00mk/steel project/training/Training/workmen's_diary/2026-08-31.md` · data-quality</sub>

#### 🔴 CRITICAL · 2026-08-31 · A fixed VAL_HOUSES list collided with t04's fold split, leaking one house across passes

**What happened.** บ้าน_ใหญ่_1ชั้น_01 was in the fixed val-house list's train side but was val in t04's fold0. With a fixed VAL_HOUSES, that house would be in pass0's train and pass1's val inside the same model.

**Root cause.** Two independent split authorities (a hardcoded house list and t04's fold files) applied to the same model.

**Impact.** Cross-pass data leakage that would have inflated validation numbers invisibly.

**Fix.** Abandoned the fixed VAL_HOUSES list and made t04's house-to-split assignment the single source of truth per fold across all passes.

**→ Rule.** There must be exactly one authority for house-to-split assignment per model, applied identically to every data pass — a second hardcoded list is a leak waiting to happen.

<sub>`D:/00mk/steel project/training/Training/workmen's_diary/2026-08-31.md` · data-integrity</sub>

#### 🔴 CRITICAL · 2026-09-01 · All slabs price at ฿0 because floor_area_sqm has no producer in the raw-extraction path

**What happened.** Across every simulated house run, slab (พื้น) lines came out at ฿0. The cause was already documented in CLAUDE.md: `floor_area_sqm` has no producer anywhere in the raw-extraction path.

**Root cause.** The extraction pipeline never produces the one field the slab BOQ formula needs. Compounded by `plan_slab` having zero training examples in the entire system, so the model was never taught to answer slab plans at all.

**Impact.** Slab concrete, rebar and formwork all silently priced at ฿0 in every BOQ produced through the real extraction path — a systematically under-stated total on real construction quantities.

**Fix.** Not fixed — recorded plainly as still broken.

**→ Rule.** When a BOQ category consistently reads ฿0, treat it as a missing-producer bug, not an empty category. Trace every required field back to the stage that produces it, and if no stage does, the feature is not implemented regardless of how green the pipeline looks.

<sub>`2026-09-01.md` · data-completeness</sub>

#### 🔴 CRITICAL · 2026-09-01 · Multi-view pages queued for manual pass0 labelling were counted and printed but never entered the real training file

**What happened.** `build_pass0()` in `build_t05_night.py` reads only `pass0_labels.jsonl`. The manual queue — which holds all multi-view pages, mostly footing+beam pairs — was read only to print a count. It never entered the actual training data, and nobody has resolved it (about 40 pages per house on average).

**Root cause.** The manual queue was created as a holding area with no consumer wired to it. Reading it for a count gave the false impression it was integrated into the pipeline.

**Impact.** The single hardest and most valuable page category (multi-view pages — exactly the ones that keep failing at generation) has zero training signal. ~40 pages per house unlabelled.

**Fix.** Not fixed — recorded as still pending.

**→ Rule.** A holding queue that is only counted, never consumed, is a data-loss channel disguised as progress. Any queue must have a named consumer and an assertion that its items eventually leave it.

<sub>`2026-09-01.md` · training-data</sub>

#### 🔴 CRITICAL · 2026-09-01 · plan_slab has zero training examples anywhere in the system

**What happened.** Checking the real `pass0_train+val.jsonl` (171 rows) showed: plan_beam 14, plan_footing 7, also_gridline 32, and **plan_slab = 0 across the entire system**.

**Root cause.** Training-data coverage was never audited per subtask before training. A subtask existed in the taxonomy with no examples behind it, and nothing flagged the empty class.

**Impact.** The model can never answer slab plans — which is a second, independent cause of the ฿0 slab BOQ problem. Any slab result from the model is untrustworthy by construction.

**Fix.** Not fixed — recorded as needing added training data.

**→ Rule.** Before any training run, print a per-class example count and fail the build on any class with zero (or near-zero) examples. A subtask with no training data is a lie in the taxonomy.

<sub>`2026-09-01.md` · training-data</sub>

#### 🟠 HIGH · 2026-07-05 · deleteProject() did not delete Site/Foundation/manpower localStorage keys, orphaning project data

**What happened.** A bug was found and fixed in project-store.js: `deleteProject()` was not removing the Site Investigate, Foundation Design and manpower-config localStorage keys, leaving orphaned data behind after a project was deleted.

**Root cause.** The list of project-scoped storage keys was hand-maintained inside deleteProject(), while feature modules independently declared their own key strings. Every new project-scoped key had to be remembered in a second place, and it was not.

**Impact.** Deleted projects left residue in localStorage. Beyond the wasted space, orphaned Site/Foundation data can be picked up by a later project reusing an id, and it silently contradicts the user's belief that deletion removed everything.

**Fix.** Fixed the deletion, and structurally: created js/shared/storage-keys.js as the single registry of every localStorage key, with PROJECT_SCOPED_KEYS derived automatically from the registry instead of hand-maintained, and fixed 14 feature modules that had been declaring key strings themselves.

**→ Rule.** Any list that must stay in sync with a set of things (keys to delete, keys to sync, keys to migrate) must be derived from the registry, never hand-typed. A hand-maintained parallel list is guaranteed to drift the first time someone adds an entry in a hurry.

<sub>`D:/00mk/steel project/training/Training/workmen's_diary/2026-07-05.md` · code-bug / data-hygiene</sub>

#### 🟠 HIGH · 2026-07-06 · Round 1 wrongly classified real structural gridlines on MEP pages as free-text labels

**What happened.** On MEP pages 29, 35, 36, 37, grid circles marked 1/2/3/A/B/C/D appeared. Round t1 interpreted them as generic labels and tagged them `grid_ref_is_free_text_not_grid_notation: true`. The independent round-2 agent read the actual printed dimension numbers and found they matched the house's main grid exactly, including dummy grids A'/A'' — meaning they are a real structural grid shared across disciplines, and t1 was wrong.

**Root cause.** t1 judged the symbols by appearance and by discipline assumption ('MEP sheets don't carry structural grid') instead of verifying against the measurable evidence printed on the page — the dimension numbers. There was no central grid master file at the time of t1 to check against, so verification was not even possible.

**Impact.** Four pages of the dataset carried a wrong structural interpretation, and cross-discipline grid alignment was lost. At end of 2026-07-06 the conflict was still not decisively resolved ('need to decide which schema to treat as the standard'), so the dataset held two contradictory readings of the same pages.

**Fix.** Not fully fixed. t2 used `grid_source` referencing the central grid master file instead; the t1-vs-t2 conflict was left as pending item #4 with the note that t2 is likely more correct but the image should be re-checked before finalizing.

**→ Rule.** Classify a symbol by the measurable evidence next to it (printed dimensions matched against the house grid master), never by which discipline's sheet it appears on. A grid master file must exist before the first extraction round, not be invented after one round has already guessed.

<sub>`D:/00mk/steel project/training/Training/workmen's_diary/2026-07-06.md` · misdiagnosis / wrong-data</sub>

#### 🟠 HIGH · 2026-07-06 · Floor marker symbols SO/SI/SX/ST were classified as unknown_symbol when they are slabs

**What happened.** The floor marker symbols SO/SI/SX/ST had been extracted as 'unknown_symbol'. Comparison against claude_output_03 confirmed that the `slab` element_type covers them, and t2 changed their element_type to 'slab'.

**Root cause.** The extraction fell back to a catch-all 'unknown' bucket rather than looking up what the symbol legend on the drawing actually defines. A permissive unknown bucket removes the pressure to resolve the symbol.

**Impact.** Slab elements were invisible to any downstream consumer filtering by element_type — no slab area, no slab concrete, no slab rebar for these marks. Note the change was made under a 'refine as appropriate' mandate and was never formally confirmed by Makham, so the correction itself is unratified.

**Fix.** Generation 3.1 point 3: confirmed `slab` covers SO/SI/SX/ST; element_type changed in round t2. Formal confirmation still outstanding.

**→ Rule.** An 'unknown' classification is a defect report, not an answer — every unknown must be triaged against the drawing's own symbol legend before the round closes. And a schema change made under a broad 'refine as appropriate' mandate still needs explicit ratification, or the dataset carries an unsigned decision.

<sub>`D:/00mk/steel project/training/Training/workmen's_diary/2026-07-06.md` · misclassification / wrong-data</sub>

#### 🟠 HIGH · 2026-07-06 · Schema had no way to express an unnamed gridline, so beam B1 came out wrong in both the fresh extraction and Gen 2

**What happened.** Makham personally spotted on page 06 a wall/beam line running the full height of the building at 2.55 m from grid '1', with no grid-marker circle at all in the original drawing. This matched beam B1, which had been problematic in both the fresh self-extraction of page 19 and in claude_output_03 (Gen 2) — the same defect independently in two generations.

**Root cause.** The schema assumed every structural line sits on a named grid. Real drawings contain unnamed gridlines, so extraction had nowhere to put B1's position and produced low-confidence or wrong output every time — a schema gap presenting as an extraction quality problem.

**Impact.** Beam B1's position was unreliable across two independent extraction generations. It also took a human eyeballing the drawing to notice, not any automated check. Once found, it required a new convention, a new master file, and re-extraction of the affected pages.

**Fix.** Designed the Dummy Grid convention (prime notation appended to the nearest main grid: 1', A', 3', always stored with type: 'dummy', kept separate from type: 'named'), and created the central grid master file บ้าน_เล็ก_1ชั้น_01_หน้า00_gridline.json. Recorded as Generation 3.2.

**→ Rule.** When the same element reads badly across two independent extraction attempts, stop blaming the reader and check whether the schema can even represent the truth. A recurring low-confidence element is a schema gap until proven otherwise.

<sub>`D:/00mk/steel project/training/Training/workmen's_diary/2026-07-06.md` · schema-gap / wrong-data</sub>

#### 🟠 HIGH · 2026-07-06 · element_id read as 'S1' when the drawing says 'SI', with the sheet_name wrong on the same file

**What happened.** In mk_test page 23, element_id had been extracted as 'S1' when the correct value is 'SI'; the sheet_name on the same file was also wrong. Both were corrected with confidence_flags recording the source of the correction.

**Root cause.** Visual confusion between the digit 1 and the capital letter I at the drawing's resolution, with no zoom tool available and no cross-check against the set of valid slab marks for the house (SO/SI/ST/SX), which would have rejected 'S1' immediately.

**Impact.** A wrong element id breaks the spec-join by element_id, so that slab's specification would silently attach to nothing or to the wrong element. Since the same file also had a wrong sheet_name, the error was not isolated.

**Fix.** Corrected element_id S1 → SI and fixed sheet_name in mk_test page 23, adding confidence_flags explaining the source of the correction.

**→ Rule.** For character classes that look alike at drawing resolution (1/I, 0/O, 5/S, 8/B), validate every extracted id against the house's known mark vocabulary and reject anything outside it. Never accept a free-form id where a closed set exists.

<sub>`D:/00mk/steel project/training/Training/workmen's_diary/2026-07-06.md` · extraction-bug / wrong-data</sub>

#### 🟠 HIGH · 2026-07-10 · The same 101-file dataset exists in two folders with no decision on which is authoritative

**What happened.** mk_test/t4/ was copied (not moved) into rawjson_.../01House_Small_1Story_01/, leaving the identical dataset in two places. No official decision was made on which one is the real one to edit going forward; the hypothetical edit walkthrough had to assume an answer.

**Root cause.** A promotion from test folder to production folder was implemented as a copy without retiring the source, and the ownership decision was deferred.

**Impact.** Any future edit risks producing two conflicting versions of the same ground-truth data; the risk was still open at the end of the day and carried forward for several more.

**Fix.** Not fixed — rule_of_tune.md was extended to protect the new folder, and the ambiguity was recorded as a pending decision.

**→ Rule.** Promotion from test to production must retire or freeze the source in the same action — two live copies of ground truth is a data-integrity bug waiting for the first edit.

<sub>`D:/00mk/steel project/training/Training/workmen's_diary/2026-07-10.md` · data-integrity</sub>

#### 🟠 HIGH · 2026-07-12 · An abnormal 45% foundation price gap was written off as real source data instead of triggering a re-read

**What happened.** While reading house 4's 10-house price table, an anomaly was noted: house 10's price gap between spread footing and pile foundation was ~45% while every other house differed by only 5-10%. It was logged as an observation about the source document and left alone. A week later the 8x glyph-comparison sweep found house 10's numbers had actually been misread (2,945,000/2,034,000 vs the true 2,145,000/2,035,000) — which is exactly what produced the fake 45% gap.

**Root cause.** The team had already decided (from the house-6 spread-vs-pile anomaly) that odd numbers in this table are 'real data from the original', so a second, different anomaly inherited that conclusion instead of being investigated on its own merits. An outlier was treated as a documentation note rather than as a signal that the reading was wrong.

**Impact.** A digit error sat in the dataset across multiple houses' copies for roughly a week, and a free early-warning signal was discarded. It took a full multi-house glyph-comparison sweep on 07-19 to recover it.

**Fix.** Fixed indirectly on 2026-07-19 by the 8x reference-glyph sweep across all 5 copies, which corrected #10 to 2,145,000/2,035,000 (gap back to ~5%).

**→ Rule.** An internal-consistency outlier (a value far outside the pattern of its own neighbours) is a re-read trigger, not a note. Do not let a previously-confirmed 'the source really is odd here' conclusion license a second, unrelated outlier.

<sub>`D:/00mk/steel project/training/Training/workmen's_diary/2026-07-12.md` · data-quality</sub>

#### 🟠 HIGH · 2026-07-14 · Dummy grid values supplied verbally were stamped confidence_score 1 without the dimension line being verified

**What happened.** Dummy grid 1''=3.45 was added on direct instruction and given confidence_score: 1 by convention, while the entry itself records that the exact dimension line was not pinpointed 100%. The same convention was then applied to batches of grids across houses 2, 3, 4 and 5 ('per values Makham gave directly, all confidence 1').

**Root cause.** The convention conflates 'a human said so' with 'independently verified against the image'. confidence_score is the field downstream consumers use to decide what to trust, and it now carries provenance, not verification.

**Impact.** Unverifiable values are indistinguishable from measured ones in the dataset. B'=12.5 and B'=10.2, both entered at confidence 1, were both later found wrong (12.2 and 10.1) — proving the score does not mean what it says.

**Fix.** not fixed — the convention stands; the wrong values were caught individually and later corrected against source sheets.

**→ Rule.** confidence_score must describe evidence strength, not who supplied the number. A human-supplied value needs its own provenance flag so a later audit can find every one of them.

<sub>`D:/00mk/steel project/training/Training/workmen's_diary/2026-07-14.md` · data-quality</sub>

#### 🟠 HIGH · 2026-07-19 · The B2X misreading recurred in house 5 — a beam section was recorded as a 'notch F-E' instead of an extension F→F'

**What happened.** While establishing house 5's dummy grid F'(14.40), a misreading was found in pages 32/33: what had been recorded as a 'notch F-E' is actually a B2X section extending from F out to F' — exactly the same misinterpretation already found and fixed in house 2.

**Root cause.** A short beam stub extending past a main grid looks identical to an inward notch unless the dummy grid it reaches is already in the master. The dummy grid and the beam interpretation are mutually dependent, so the wrong reading is stable until one side is fixed.

**Impact.** The same class of error was carried into a second house; without the F' work it would have stayed undetected.

**Fix.** Corrected on 2026-07-19 when F'=14.40 was added, along with 4'(9.6) for the BX1 stub extending 0.60 past grid4.

**→ Rule.** After fixing an interpretation bug in one house, sweep the same sheet type in every other house immediately — B2X-class errors have now appeared in houses 2 and 5 and were found months apart by accident.

<sub>`D:/00mk/steel project/training/Training/workmen's_diary/2026-07-19.md` · data-quality</sub>

#### 🟠 HIGH · 2026-07-19 · Beam B3X carried a phantom additional_bars entry — rebar recorded that does not exist in the drawing

**What happened.** Zooming into house 5's S-08 (page36) and counting points in the real section showed that B3X's recorded additional_bars had no counterpart in the drawing at all; the entry was deleted rather than corrected.

**Root cause.** additional_bars were being transcribed from printed labels without verifying against the actual rebar points in the section — the same root cause as the wrong-face bug, but producing fabricated data rather than misplaced data.

**Impact.** Fabricated reinforcement in the dataset — worse than a missing bar, because it inflates steel quantities and teaches the model to invent bars.

**Fix.** Deleted after a zoom-and-count check on page36.

**→ Rule.** The wrong-face additional_bars bug has a twin: bars that do not exist at all. Every additional_bars entry needs point-counting confirmation, not just a face check.

<sub>`D:/00mk/steel project/training/Training/workmen's_diary/2026-07-19.md` · data-quality</sub>

#### 🟠 HIGH · 2026-07-20 · Duplicate footing entries at the same grid point double-counted on two sheets

**What happened.** House 3's page29 (S-02 spread footing) had a duplicate F0.90x0.90 at B3 in addition to the main entry, and page30 (S-03 pile footing) had the identical bug with a duplicate F5 at B3.

**Root cause.** No uniqueness check on (mark, grid_ref) within a footing plan, so the same physical footing recorded twice survived extraction.

**Impact.** Double-counted footings — a direct quantity and cost overstatement on two sheets, and the fact that it appeared identically on both variants means it was systematic, not a one-off.

**Fix.** Removed both duplicates and set confidence_score=1 for page29.

**→ Rule.** Enforce uniqueness on (element mark, grid point) within any plan sheet as a validation rule — a duplicate at the same grid point is always a bug, never data.

<sub>`2026-07-20.md` · data-extraction</sub>

#### 🟠 HIGH · 2026-07-20 · House 3's page31 (S-04) had seven wrong beam marks and endpoints, including beams placed on a grid line that has no beam

**What happened.** A calibrated full-sheet re-check of page31 fixed seven separate defects: D1-C1 was actually D1'-C1' (there is no vertical beam at grid1 in the D-C strip on either floor), two beams marked B3X were actually B3 with a separate B3X missing beside each, C2-C3 was B3 rather than B2, a vertical beam B1 B2-A2 was missing entirely, and two 'possibly void' flags were wrong and had to be released.

**Root cause.** The original extraction assigned marks by proximity and assumed a beam exists wherever a grid line crosses, without measuring against a calibrated scale or checking whether the column sits on the grid line or offset from it.

**Impact.** Seven wrong or missing structural elements on one sheet of a training-set house — wrong marks mean wrong specs downstream, since specs are keyed by mark.

**Fix.** All seven fixed on 2026-07-20 using the calibrated 78.1 px/m scale established for that sheet.

**→ Rule.** Beam-plan marks cannot be assigned by proximity. A calibrated scale plus an explicit 'is there actually a beam on this line?' check is required per strip, per floor.

<sub>`D:/00mk/steel project/training/Training/workmen's_diary/2026-07-20.md` · data-quality</sub>

#### 🟠 HIGH · 2026-07-20 · House 3's tie-beam sheet was missing six elements and carried a mislabeled offset that a 10x zoom disproved

**What happened.** Page33 (S-06 tie beams) went from 17 to 23 elements on a full-image check: vertical beams D2-C2 and B2-A2 were entirely absent, beams B'2-B'3 and B3-B'3 were missing, and D1'-C1' was a mislabel — a 10x zoom confirmed the column sits exactly on grid1 with no offset, so the tie beam is a continuous loop rather than broken at the staircase bay.

**Root cause.** The offset pattern seen on S-04/S-05 was assumed to carry over to S-06 without verifying it on that sheet; and 26% of the sheet's elements were never extracted at all.

**Impact.** A quarter of the tie beams on the sheet were missing from the dataset, and the loop topology was recorded incorrectly.

**Fix.** Fully re-checked against the original image on 2026-07-20; all six elements added and the mislabel corrected.

**→ Rule.** An offset convention observed on one sheet must be re-verified on each sheet it is applied to — sheets of the same house genuinely differ.

<sub>`D:/00mk/steel project/training/Training/workmen's_diary/2026-07-20.md` · data-quality</sub>

#### 🟠 HIGH · 2026-07-28 · Seven house-05 source files were corrected AFTER the dataset was built — including the gridmaster — so both t01 and t02 trained on known-wrong data

**What happened.** The t02 dataset was copied byte-identical rather than rebuilt, because 7 files in house 05 (including หน้า00_gridline.json) had been edited after the dataset was originally built. Rebuilding would produce a different set and destroy comparability, so the corrections were deliberately excluded — meaning the training data still carries the pre-correction versions, including for the gridmaster example type the scripts flag as the most-missed topic.

**Root cause.** No link between the corrected raw JSON and the built dataset — corrections to source files silently do not propagate, and there is no marker showing which built examples are stale.

**Impact.** Both t01 (28.2% recall) and t02 (20.6% recall) were trained on data known to contain corrected-away errors, and the dataset is now frozen: it can never be rebuilt without invalidating every A/B number measured against it.

**Fix.** Not fixed — deliberately frozen. Documented in tune_ai/t02/data_before_tune/DATASET_PROVENANCE.md with checksum evidence and the reason rebuilding is forbidden.

**→ Rule.** Record which source files a dataset build consumed and their hashes at build time. When a source file is later corrected, the build is stale — either rebuild before the comparison starts, or the whole experiment inherits the old errors permanently.

<sub>`D:/00mk/steel project/training/Training/workmen's_diary/2026-07-28.md` · data integrity / provenance drift</sub>

#### 🟠 HIGH · 2026-07-29 · Classification pass is itself wrong — elevations read as sections, 5 views claimed where 2 exist

**What happened.** Pages 07/08/09 were classified as section/section/title/gridline/notes; the gold is side_profile, side_profile. The model also claimed 5 views on a sheet that has 2.

**Root cause.** The same underlying model deficiency (likely untuned GGUF plus resolution mismatch) affects the classify pass, and no accuracy gate was placed on classification before making it the gatekeeper of the extraction pipeline.

**Impact.** Directly undermines the new 2-phase plan: wrong classification means needed pages get skipped and useless pages get extracted at 13-21 min each. Errors here are silent and expensive downstream.

**Fix.** not fixed — recorded as a caveat

**→ Rule.** When a cheap stage becomes the gate for an expensive stage, measure the cheap stage's accuracy first. A router that is wrong 30% of the time turns a saving into a loss.

<sub>`D:/00mk/steel project/training/Training/workmen's_diary/2026-07-29.md` · data-quality</sub>

#### 🟠 HIGH · 2026-07-29 · Cross-reference sheet numbers (A-05, A-07, A-09) hallucinated into element marks

**What happened.** On page 06 the model emitted 59 elements against a gold of 17 — inventing 12 columns, 8 doors and 4 windows that do not exist on the sheet, and naming them A-05/A-07/A-09. Those are sheet numbers: the drawing carries text like 'ดูรายละเอียดที่แผ่น A-05' (see detail on sheet A-05), which the model read as an element's name.

**Root cause.** The model reads text correctly but has no model of what each piece of text is for; cross-reference callouts and element marks look alike lexically and nothing in the pipeline distinguishes them.

**Impact.** 3.5× element over-count on one page. If such output reached a BOQ it would price a dozen non-existent columns.

**Fix.** not fixed

**→ Rule.** Add a validation rule that rejects element marks matching the sheet-code pattern (letter-dash-digits) as marks, and cross-check element counts against the sheet's own schedule. Never let a lexical match become a semantic claim without a structural check.

<sub>`D:/00mk/steel project/training/Training/workmen's_diary/2026-07-29(teach mk).md` · data-quality</sub>

#### 🟠 HIGH · 2026-07-29 · Grid letters reversed and a fictitious per-intersection grid_table invented — every downstream span wrong

**What happened.** Gold horizontal grid is D=0, C=4.0, B=6.0, A=9.5; the model answered A=0, B=1.5, C=5.0, D=9.5 — letters reversed and every interior distance wrong, only the 9.5 total correct. On page 06 it built a grid_table assigning a value to each grid *intersection*, which is not a real-world quantity, by shuffling the real drawing numbers (7.0, 9.5, 4.0, 3.5) into cells.

**Root cause.** The model reproduced the right numeric set without the right structure, and the prompt instructs that spans must come from the grid table — so a plausible-looking but fabricated table silently becomes the basis for every span.

**Impact.** Every span computed downstream of the grid is wrong, with plausible-looking values that no eyeball check would flag.

**Fix.** not fixed

**→ Rule.** Validate structure, not just value presence: assert grid labels are monotonic in the drawing's own direction and that a table's cells correspond to quantities that physically exist. Fabricated-but-plausible numbers are the most dangerous kind, because they pass every 'is it filled in?' check.

<sub>`D:/00mk/steel project/training/Training/workmen's_diary/2026-07-29.md` · data-quality</sub>

#### 🟠 HIGH · 2026-07-29 · Wall in clay brick reported as ceiling in AAC block — a BOQ wrong at two levels

**What happened.** On page 04 the gold records ผนัง (wall) built with มอญ (clay) brick; the model answered ฝ้าเพดาน (ceiling) built with มวลเบา (lightweight AAC) block — wrong on both the work category and the material.

**Root cause.** No cross-field consistency constraint exists between work category and material, so an independently-wrong pair produces an internally coherent but entirely false line item.

**Impact.** If used for pricing this is wrong at two levels simultaneously: wrong trade and wrong unit rate. Exactly the class of error that ships a wrong BOQ total quietly.

**Fix.** not fixed

**→ Rule.** Enforce a materials-by-work-category whitelist at extraction time (AAC block is not a ceiling material) so implausible pairings fail rather than price. Any field pair that jointly determines money needs a joint validity check, not two independent ones.

<sub>`D:/00mk/steel project/training/Training/workmen's_diary/2026-07-29.md` · data-quality</sub>

#### 🟠 HIGH · 2026-07-29 · confidence_score / confidence_flags absent from all 6 output files

**What happened.** The gold schema attaches confidence_score and confidence_flags to every element (e.g. 'ตัวหนังสือเล็กเกิน ต้อง zoom ตรวจ' — text too small, needs zooming to verify). The model produced zero of them across all six files.

**Root cause.** Same underlying schema-conformance failure — the model was not emitting the trained schema at all, and the confidence layer exists only in the trained targets.

**Impact.** No way at all to tell which parts of the output are trustworthy. The pipeline's entire mechanism for routing uncertain reads to human review is silently disabled.

**Fix.** not fixed

**→ Rule.** Treat the presence of the self-assessment layer as a hard output contract: reject any extraction with zero confidence fields rather than accepting it as complete. Output without uncertainty markers is not high-confidence output, it is unlabelled output.

<sub>`D:/00mk/steel project/training/Training/workmen's_diary/2026-07-29.md` · data-quality</sub>

#### 🟠 HIGH · 2026-07-29 · Page 06 returned 59 elements where the gold has 17 — and the same items were counted again in the roof view

**What happened.** On the floor-plan page the model emitted 59 elements against a gold of 17. The excess was 12 columns + 8 doors + 4 windows that do not appear on that sheet at all, and the diary notes the fabricated set was then 'duplicated again in the roof view' — i.e. the same non-existent items were counted twice across two views of one page.

**Root cause.** The model has no notion of 'this view already covered these items'; it re-enumerates per view and invents members to fill a schema slot rather than leaving it empty. Nothing downstream de-duplicates elements across views of the same sheet, and no count-vs-gold check ran before the file was written.

**Impact.** 3.5x element over-count on a single page. Any BOQ built on this would order roughly triple the columns/doors/windows for that floor; the double-counting across views means even a corrected per-view read would still double the quantity.

**Fix.** not fixed — only measured against gold; the extraction was halted pending the LoRA-in-GGUF test

**→ Rule.** Element counts are the cheapest possible validation signal: compare count-per-page against gold (or against a sanity bound) before writing output. And treat cross-view duplication as its own failure mode — a per-view extractor needs an explicit de-duplication step, or every multi-view sheet inflates quantities.

<sub>`D:/00mk/steel project/training/Training/workmen's_diary/2026-07-29.md` · extraction-quality</sub>

#### 🟠 HIGH · 2026-07-29 · Four pages of bad extraction were written into the real results folder before the pipeline was known to be broken

**What happened.** Pages 03-06 were extracted with the suspect GGUF and saved into the real ผล/ output folder before anyone knew the artifact might contain no fine-tuning. Continuing would have filled the folder with wrong data.
