**Fix.** Filename routing explicitly ruled out; routing moved to Pass 0 classification. floor_level and building pinned as fields.

**→ Rule.** Never let semantics live only in filenames — if a value matters, it goes in a field; once naming has drifted across a dataset, filename-based tooling is dead for good and must be replaced with content-based classification.

<sub>`D:/00mk/steel project/training/Training/workmen's_diary/2026-08-21.md` · data-quality</sub>

#### 🟡 MEDIUM · 2026-08-24 · 8 plan pages produced zero training examples — no element in them matched their own subtask

**What happened.** While building the expanded dataset, 8 plan pages were skipped because they contained no element matching the subtask they were classified as.

**Root cause.** Either the page classification is wrong, or the GT for those pages is missing the elements it should carry — the diary does not distinguish, it only records the skip.

**Impact.** 8 pages of extraction work contribute nothing to training, and the underlying cause (misclassification vs. missing GT) is still unknown, so it will recur on the next build.

**Fix.** builder skips them and reports the names, no guessed repair

**→ Rule.** A 'skipped and reported' line is a to-do, not a resolution. Route skipped-page names into the GT review queue, otherwise every rebuild silently drops the same pages forever.

<sub>`D:/00mk/steel project/training/Training/workmen's_diary/2026-08-24.md` · data-quality</sub>

#### 🟡 MEDIUM · 2026-08-24 · All 12 gridmasters still lack dimension_chains — the image sweep was never done, and back-computing was rejected as fake provenance

**What happened.** The gridmaster §4 upgrade added z_levels but deliberately left `dimension_chains[]`/`unassigned_dimensions[]` empty, because filling them requires a page-by-page image sweep nobody has done. Back-computing them from pos_m was rejected outright.

**Root cause.** The only honest source is manual transcription off the drawings; the tempting shortcut (derive from pos_m) produces values that look sourced but are actually circular.

**Impact.** Every gridmaster ships with a documented hole; the later span-scaling rule (2026-08-29) leans on grid geometry that is only partially transcribed. The manual sweep is still owed as of the last file read.

**Fix.** not fixed — warning written into every gridmaster stating both facts

**→ Rule.** Refusing to fabricate provenance was right. But a hole documented in 12 files is still a hole — schedule the manual sweep as real work, or later passes will quietly assume the field is complete.

<sub>`D:/00mk/steel project/training/Training/workmen's_diary/2026-08-24.md` · known-unfixed-data-gap</sub>

#### 🟡 MEDIUM · 2026-08-24 · ~132 MEP/arch/index/symbol files left with container drift after the schema normalization sweep

**What happened.** The 267-change normalization pass fixed structural files but deliberately left roughly 132 pass-3 files (MEP, architectural, index, symbol) with the old container drift, plus a long tail of reviewer-invented element_type values.

**Root cause.** Scoped the sweep to the files t03 trains on; the untouched ones were out of the current training scope so they were logged rather than fixed.

**Fix.** not fixed — logged as deliberately untouched

**→ Rule.** When a normalization pass is partial, say what fraction of the repo it covered next to the pass/fail line. 'All checks pass' next to '132 files untouched' is two facts that will get read as one.

<sub>`D:/00mk/steel project/training/Training/workmen's_diary/2026-08-24.md` · known-unfixed-data-gap</sub>

#### 🟡 MEDIUM · 2026-08-25 · มยผ. 1103-64 was recorded on 08-24 as an unreadable scanned image; the real PDF has a text layer

**What happened.** On 08-24 the standard's PDF was recorded as a scanned image with no OCR available, and ACI values were substituted with a note saying so. This session found an accessible copy at ei-auditor.com with a real text layer and read all 20 pages.

**Root cause.** A single source's failure was recorded as a property of the document itself, and no further search was made for another hosted copy.

**Impact.** A day of citing ACI values with an "unverified against มยผ." caveat that could have been resolved sooner; downstream, an entire standards registry was later migrated once the real text was read.

**Fix.** Found and read the text-layer PDF, corrected the 08-24 record, and re-verified the ปลายยื่นปลอก clause (5.3.4.2) in bbs-shapes.js against the real document.

**→ Rule.** "The PDF is a scan" is a property of one hosted copy, not of the standard. Search for another host before recording a source as unreadable and substituting a foreign standard.

<sub>`D:/00mk/steel project/training/Training/workmen's_diary/2026-08-25.md` · wrong-record</sub>

#### 🟡 MEDIUM · 2026-08-25 · 25 gridmaster files still lack dimension_chains[] and unassigned_dimensions[]

**What happened.** 25 gridmaster files are missing the required `dimension_chains[]` / `unassigned_dimensions[]` arrays. They were deliberately left incomplete rather than filled, because writing an empty array would assert "we read the drawing and found nothing" — a lie under §4.

**Root cause.** The arrays were added to the spec after these files were produced, and reconstructing them requires re-reading each drawing page image, which cannot be done by a batch script.

**Impact.** 25 files remain out of spec and will fail a strict validator; the work is queued behind manual image re-reading.

**Fix.** Deliberately not filled — recorded as pending work, explicitly paired with `tools/pattern_recognition.py` which can locate real grid tick pixel positions to assist the sweep.

**→ Rule.** Never fill a required field with an empty value to satisfy a validator — an empty array asserts a negative finding. Record the gap explicitly and queue the real work.

<sub>`D:/00mk/steel project/training/Training/workmen's_diary/2026-08-25.md` · incomplete-data</sub>

#### 🟡 MEDIUM · 2026-08-25 · ~76 notes files have no sections[] at all, so fc_ksc/fy_* can never be parsed for them

**What happened.** The normalization pass parsed fc_ksc/fy_main_ksc/fy_stirrup_ksc into notes{} for 62 values across 26 files by reading each file's own sections[]. Roughly 76 more notes files have no sections[] to parse from, so those houses' concrete/rebar strength values still never reach any consumer.

**Root cause.** The extraction that produced those notes files predates the sections[] container convention, and no retrofit pass re-extracted them; the parse fix could only work on files that already carried the newer shape.

**Impact.** Strength values stay missing for ~76 files — the same class of silently-absent data that §4a had already flagged as "never reached a consumer in any house", now only partly closed.

**Fix.** not fixed — recorded as deliberate ("จงใจไม่ทำ ไม่ใช่ลืม"); filling them requires re-reading the drawing pages, and writing empty arrays would be lying that the data was read and absent.

**→ Rule.** A parse-from-own-file fix only heals files already in the new shape; count and record the remainder explicitly, or the fix reads as complete when it covered half the set.

<sub>`D:/00mk/steel project/training/Training/workmen's_diary/2026-08-25.md` · data-quality</sub>

#### 🟡 MEDIUM · 2026-08-25 · 22 files had the wrong notes container shape and 20 more carried ad-hoc one-off keys outside notes{}

**What happened.** During the normalization sweep, 22 files had their notes content in the wrong container and had to be moved into sections[], and 20 files carried improvised one-off keys that had to be pulled into notes{}. Both are schema drift that the format checker had never flagged.

**Root cause.** The schema was revised 43 times in 5 weeks while extraction ran; annotators/extractions invented ad-hoc keys when the current schema had no slot, and no checker rule rejected an unknown key.

**Impact.** 42 files' notes content was in shapes no consumer reads, on top of the 345 discipline misspellings — data present on disk but invisible downstream.

**Fix.** Fixed in the 485-point / 423-file normalization pass; check_format.py gained a "notes one-off key" gate among its 5 new checks.

**→ Rule.** A schema with no closed key vocabulary invites improvised keys; the checker must reject unknown keys, not just validate known ones.

<sub>`D:/00mk/steel project/training/Training/workmen's_diary/2026-08-25.md` · data-quality</sub>

#### 🟡 MEDIUM · 2026-08-25 · The one available non-BMA-series house has no plan_footing/plan_beam GT, so cross-series validation is blocked by missing data

**What happened.** The template-matching tool was validated only on two houses of the same BMA "แบบบ้านยิ้ม" series. The obvious cross-series candidate, 07บ้าน_ใหญ่_2ชั้น_01, cannot be used as a numeric check because it has no plan_footing/plan_beam GT jsons to compare against.

**Root cause.** GT coverage grew per-house without tracking series diversity, so the houses with GT happen to cluster in one drawing office's series — the exact axis the tool most needs to be tested on.

**Impact.** The generalization claim for the whole detector stays untestable numerically; only an eyeball check is possible, and the cross-series over-detection later suspected on บ้าน 08/18 has no GT-backed way to be confirmed.

**Fix.** not fixed — recorded as pending ("Test on a non-BMA-series house once one has comparable pages"), with a visual-only check accepted as the interim.

<sub>`D:/00mk/steel project/training/Training/workmen's_diary/2026-08-25.md` · data-coverage</sub>

#### 🟡 MEDIUM · 2026-08-28 · Four hard validation FAILs: BOM in 22 files, dummy grid, prose in grid_ref

**What happened.** The repo-wide checker surfaced four hard failures: a UTF-8 BOM in 22 files of house 44, a dummy grid line A' in house 30, and prose text sitting in `grid_ref` fields in house 47 (two occurrences).

**Root cause.** Files were written by different tools/editors with different encoding defaults (BOM), and `grid_ref` had no format validation so free-text descriptions could be written into a field meant to hold a grid identifier.

**Impact.** BOM breaks naive JSON parsers; prose in grid_ref breaks any code that parses a grid reference. These would fail silently or crash downstream depending on the reader.

**Fix.** All four fixed; checker now reports ALL CHECKS PASS across the repo, Constistant 1288/1288.

**→ Rule.** Validate field *format*, not just presence — a grid_ref field should reject anything that isn't a grid identifier. And add a BOM check to the format checker; encoding bugs are invisible in every editor that hides them.

<sub>`D:/00mk/steel project/training/Training/workmen's_diary/2026-08-28.md` · data-quality</sub>

#### 🟡 MEDIUM · 2026-08-28 · Two source drawings contradict themselves — recorded, not resolved

**What happened.** House 32's ridge level reads +5.20 on one sheet but the dimension chain sums to 4.90. House 27's y-axis total reads 14.55 but the chain sums to 14.15. Both were recorded without deciding which value is correct, pending a zoom on the original.

**Root cause.** The source drawings themselves are internally inconsistent — this is a defect in the input data, not in extraction. But it means GT cannot be produced without a human judgment call on the original.

**Impact.** Two houses have known-ambiguous dimensions in GT. Any model trained on them learns from a value that may be wrong, and any BOQ computed from them inherits the ambiguity.

**Fix.** Recorded both readings without deciding, explicitly deferring to a zoom of the original drawing.

**→ Rule.** When source data contradicts itself, record both readings and flag it — never silently pick one. A guessed reconciliation is indistinguishable from real data once it's in GT.

<sub>`D:/00mk/steel project/training/Training/workmen's_diary/2026-08-28.md` · data-quality</sub>

#### 🟡 MEDIUM · 2026-08-28 · Four recurring drawing-classification traps documented after repeatedly getting them wrong

**What happened.** Four traps were added to §1 of the spec: 'แป' is a subset of 'แปลน' (substring collision), sheet_name on multi-view pages misleads classification, 'คานอะเส' is a beam_plan, and steel roof framing is entirely `steel_member`.

**Root cause.** Thai construction terminology has substring collisions and domain-specific meanings that a naive classifier (human or model) gets wrong repeatedly. These were being re-discovered each time rather than written down.

**Impact.** Repeated misclassification across houses until the traps were documented; the etc_plan bloat above is partly a symptom of the same confusions.

**Fix.** Documented all four as explicit traps in §1 of the spec.

**→ Rule.** Every time a classification mistake is made twice, write it into the spec as a named trap. A trap list is cheaper than re-deriving the same confusion on every house.

<sub>`D:/00mk/steel project/training/Training/workmen's_diary/2026-08-28.md` · data-quality</sub>

#### 🟡 MEDIUM · 2026-08-28 · House 08 flagged as CV garbage — but GT is the more likely one that's wrong

**What happened.** After the column template bank expansion, 16 of 30 houses matched GT exactly with 1 house (08) counted as garbage — and the note records the GT for house 08 probably undercounts columns itself.

**Root cause.** The detector was being scored against GT that has never been audited for completeness. When detector and GT disagree, the default assumption was that the detector is wrong.

**Impact.** A correct detection may be recorded as a false positive, and house 08's GT may be feeding an undercount into training.

**Fix.** Flagged in the diary; GT not corrected.

**→ Rule.** When a detector disagrees with GT, check the drawing before assuming the detector is wrong. Log the direction of every disagreement so GT errors surface instead of being absorbed into the detector's error rate.

<sub>`D:/00mk/steel project/training/Training/workmen's_diary/2026-08-28.md` · data-quality</sub>

#### 🟡 MEDIUM · 2026-08-29 · Houses 51/52 entered GT (as 39/40) carrying three unresolved drawing ambiguities

**What happened.** The two new op04 houses were flagged with three unresolved readings — mesh reinforcement direction on F8/F10 unconfirmed, the meaning of the 0.30|0.30 dimension straddling the pier unclear, and individual rafters never printed — then copied into json_แก้ไขแล้ว as houses 39/40 and added to train (+31 examples).

**Root cause.** op04 houses go into train un-reviewed by policy; flagging an ambiguity records it but does not gate the file from entering the training set.

**Impact.** Three known-uncertain readings are now training signal. If any is wrong, the model learns the wrong reading and the flag lives in a separate log rather than beside the data.

**Fix.** not fixed — flags recorded in No_touch_box/docs/raw_json_data_log.md, files added to train anyway

**→ Rule.** A flagged ambiguity that still enters train is a silent bet. Either carry the flag as a field on the element so downstream can weight it, or hold flagged pages out of train until someone zooms the original.

<sub>`D:/00mk/steel project/training/Training/workmen's_diary/2026-08-29.md` · data-quality</sub>

#### 🟡 MEDIUM · 2026-08-31 · Assistant message content mixed two shapes (list vs string) across the merged dataset

**What happened.** Rows merged from different passes carried assistant content sometimes as a list and sometimes as a bare string.

**Root cause.** Each pass builder emitted its own shape with no shared normalization step at the merge boundary.

**Impact.** Inconsistent training targets that could break the collator or silently train on differently-shaped labels.

**Fix.** Normalized all assistant content to list form during the merge.

**→ Rule.** Normalize every field shape at the merge boundary and add a schema assertion to the smoke test, rather than trusting that upstream builders agreed.

<sub>`D:/00mk/steel project/training/Training/workmen's_diary/2026-08-31.md` · data-integrity</sub>

#### 🟡 MEDIUM · 2026-08-31 · 89 pages were auto-labelled from a rule verified by eye on only 2 pages

**What happened.** The ปร.4 side-by-side/rotated-90-degree rule and the "lower number = right half" convention were confirmed on exactly two real pages (from two different houses), then applied as automatic labels to 89 pages across every house, tagged confidence 0.85 rather than 1.0.

**Root cause.** Deliberate speed/coverage tradeoff, honestly flagged — but the sample size behind a corpus-wide rule was two.

**Impact.** Any page in that batch where the convention differs is now mislabelled training data; the sheet_code null bug found in this same batch shows the batch path did carry real errors.

**Fix.** partially — confidence set to 0.85 and the script rewritten to be idempotent; the two-sample basis was not widened

**→ Rule.** When one rule labels a whole corpus, verify it on a sample sized to the corpus, not to the time available — and re-check the batch when any bug is found in it.

<sub>`D:/00mk/steel project/training/Training/workmen's_diary/2026-08-31.md` · data-quality</sub>

#### 🟡 MEDIUM · 2026-09-02 · RB1/RB2 appear twice with different sizes; BOQ silently uses only the first occurrence

**What happened.** A check found RB1/RB2 duplicated under the same name with different sizes. The real BOQ uses only the first record's values and does not double-count — judged safe for this house.

**Root cause.** Element marks are not unique keys in the extracted data, but the BOQ path treats the first match as authoritative with no duplicate detection. Safe here by coincidence of which record came first, not by design.

**Impact.** None on this house, but a silent wrong-size hazard on any house where the second occurrence is the correct one.

**Fix.** Verified safe for this run; no duplicate detection added.

**→ Rule.** If a mark is not guaranteed unique, first-match-wins is a coin flip. Detect duplicate marks with differing specs and flag them for review rather than silently picking one.

<sub>`2026-09-02.md` · data-quality</sub>

#### 🟡 MEDIUM ·  · Leftover dry-run/test data in annotated/ and manifest.json was not cleaned up automatically

**What happened.** After testing an import or generation mechanism, dry-run/test records were left behind in annotated/ and manifest.json instead of being cleaned up immediately.

**Root cause.** No standing habit of reverting manifest.json and clearing test artifacts right after a dry run, without being asked.

**Impact.** Test/dry-run data risked contaminating what should have been clean, real ground-truth state.

**Fix.** Adopted a standing rule: always clean up test/dry-run data from annotated/ and manifest.json immediately after testing, unprompted.

**→ Rule.** Never leave test/dry-run data in annotated/ or manifest.json — clean up and revert manifest.json immediately after testing, without being asked.

<sub>`d:/00mk/steel project/training/Training/No_touch_box/docs/rule_of_tune.md` · data-hygiene</sub>

#### ⚪ LOW · 2026-07-06 · Page 14 eave detail references letter 'E' which does not exist on the grid, left unresolved

**What happened.** On page 14 (eave R1/R2), R1 uses letter reference 'B' which matches the real grid, but R2 uses 'E', which is not on the grid. The architectural agent judged it was probably a general detail-callout letter rather than a structural coordinate, deliberately did not invent a dummy grid for it, and recorded it for someone to verify.

**Root cause.** The schema uses a single field for a letter reference without distinguishing a structural grid coordinate from a detail-callout label, so an ambiguous letter has no correct place to go and must be judged case by case.

**Impact.** One unresolved reference remaining in the dataset. Had the agent guessed and created a dummy grid 'E', it would have corrupted the grid master that every other page cites — so the honest non-decision was the right call, but the ambiguity is still open.

**Fix.** Not fixed — deliberately left unresolved and flagged for human verification rather than guessed.

**→ Rule.** Separate structural grid coordinates from detail-callout labels in the schema so an ambiguous letter cannot silently become a gridline. And keep rewarding agents that stop and flag instead of guessing — this restraint protected the grid master.

<sub>`D:/00mk/steel project/training/Training/workmen's_diary/2026-07-06.md` · ambiguous-data</sub>

#### ⚪ LOW · 2026-07-11 · House 6's price table shows spread footing costing more than pile foundation, in every independent read

**What happened.** The 10-house price comparison table shows an anomalous price for house design #6, where the spread-footing option costs more than the pile-foundation option — an inversion of the expected relationship. It appeared identically in house #2's and house #3's independent reads.

**Root cause.** Two independent reads producing the same anomaly rules out a misread, leaving either a genuine error in the published price table or a real but counter-intuitive figure; nothing in the process resolves which.

**Impact.** A price figure in the dataset that looks wrong and cannot be confirmed either way; still on the review list.

**Fix.** Not fixed — recorded as confirmed-across-two-reads and flagged for human review.

**→ Rule.** When two independent reads agree on an implausible value, stop re-reading and escalate to a domain expert — repeated agreement means the question has moved from extraction to the source document.

<sub>`D:/00mk/steel project/training/Training/workmen's_diary/2026-07-11.md` · source-data-quality</sub>

#### ⚪ LOW · 2026-07-12 · A 200W water pump was filed under the wrong BOQ category in the source table

**What happened.** While reading house 4's sanitary section, details of a 200W water pump were found recorded under the wrong category in the BOQ table.

**Root cause.** Source-document categorisation error; the extraction faithfully mirrors whatever category the sheet prints, so a mis-categorised line propagates into the dataset unchanged.

**Impact.** A BOQ line lands in the wrong cost category; if used for pricing/roll-up it shifts totals between categories.

**Fix.** not fixed — recorded as a finding during extraction.

**→ Rule.** Category assignments read off a BOQ sheet need a plausibility check (does this item belong in this category?), not just faithful transcription.

<sub>`D:/00mk/steel project/training/Training/workmen's_diary/2026-07-12.md` · data-quality</sub>

#### ⚪ LOW · 2026-07-30 · The same CN contradiction reappeared in house 09 — it was a real source defect, not a misreading

**What happened.** A CN contradiction found in house 08 turned up again identically on house 09's S-08 sheet. Only after seeing it twice was it confirmed to be a genuine inconsistency in the published drawings rather than an extraction error.

**Root cause.** A single-house anomaly is ambiguous between 'we read it wrong' and 'the drawing is wrong'; there was no cross-house anomaly index to check against, so the first occurrence could not be resolved.

**Impact.** Time spent re-verifying the same contradiction from scratch on the second house instead of recognising it immediately.

**Fix.** Recorded as a confirmed source-level inconsistency once seen in two independent houses of the same series.

**→ Rule.** Keep a cross-house anomaly index. When an oddity repeats across independent houses of the same series, classify it as a source defect and stop re-investigating it per house.

<sub>`2026-07-30.md` · data-quality</sub>

#### ⚪ LOW · 2026-07-30 · Two of house 10's BOQ sheets have an unclear work-category position, left flagged for zoom review

**What happened.** House 10 was signed off 100% done at 75/75 pages and 92 valid JSON files, but 2 files covering sheets 3-4 of 19 have a work-category position that could not be read confidently and were flagged needs_zoom_review.

**Root cause.** The BOQ tables in this series are low-resolution and rotated; a category position that determines where an item's cost rolls up was not legible.

**Impact.** A house declared complete carries two rows whose category assignment — which determines which subtotal the money lands in — is unresolved. Same pattern as houses 08 and 09, which were also signed off 100% done and then needed correction passes a week later.

**Fix.** not fixed — flagged needs_zoom_review

**→ Rule.** '100% done' should mean zero needs_zoom_review flags, or the phrase should be replaced with a count. A house signed off with open flags reads as finished to everyone downstream.

<sub>`D:/00mk/steel project/training/Training/workmen's_diary/2026-07-30.md` · data-quality</sub>

#### ⚪ LOW · 2026-07-31 · House 11's S-01 sheet index lists names that don't match the sheets themselves

**What happened.** The S-01 index page names sheets differently from what each sheet's own title block says — e.g. S-07 is really the column/spread-footing schedule, not the 'เชิงชายกันน้ำ' the index claims. The index file was left unfixed.

**Root cause.** The published index page is itself wrong (a source defect); extraction had been reading the index as an authority on what each sheet contains.

**Impact.** Anything routing by the index would send a sheet to the wrong pattern. Left unfixed, so the index file in the corpus still disagrees with the sheet files.

**Fix.** Not fixed — deliberately left, because each sheet's own file already carries the real sheet_code from its own title block, so the extracted data itself is unaffected.

**→ Rule.** A sheet's own title block outranks any index page. Never route a sheet by index metadata; read the sheet's title block and record any index disagreement as a source defect.

<sub>`2026-07-31.md` · data-quality</sub>

#### ⚪ LOW · 2026-08-02 · House 01's series price table is still unstructured raw text, flagged PENDING rather than converted

**What happened.** When the identical series price table was unified to series_price_table[] across five houses, house 01's copy on หน้า60 could not be converted and was left as raw text under a PENDING_STRUCTURING_2026-08-02 flag. It was still listed as outstanding at session close and again in the 2026-08-04 pending list.

**Root cause.** The other four copies had enough structure to map onto the majority form; house 01's did not, and guessing the structure was correctly refused.

**Impact.** One of five copies of the same table remains in a shape nothing can read, so the unification is incomplete and any per-house comparison of that table silently skips house 01.

**Fix.** not fixed — flagged PENDING_STRUCTURING_2026-08-02 rather than guessed

**→ Rule.** Flagging instead of guessing is right, but a PENDING flag needs a place it gets picked up from; three sessions later it was still only a line in a diary.

<sub>`D:/00mk/steel project/training/Training/workmen's_diary/2026-08-02.md` · data-quality</sub>

#### ⚪ LOW · 2026-08-02 · The same credits page was classified under four different patterns across houses

**What happened.** The round-5 audit found the credits page — byte-identical content shared across houses in the same series — stored under four different pattern values. It was unified to misc by majority plus a standing rule.

**Root cause.** No rule said which pattern a credits page takes, so each extraction run picked a plausible one; the same gap that produced five encodings of the price table.

**Impact.** Pages known to be byte-identical were labelled four different ways, which breaks any per-pattern selection and would teach a per-pattern model four contradictory labels for one image.

**Fix.** Unified to misc by majority and a standing rule added

**→ Rule.** Byte-identical pages across houses are a free consistency check — a page that is the same file should never carry more than one label, and that is worth asserting in the checker.

<sub>`D:/00mk/steel project/training/Training/workmen's_diary/2026-08-02.md` · data-quality</sub>

#### ⚪ LOW · 2026-08-02 · The same physical quantity is named three ways — height_mm, height_m and depth_m

**What happened.** A unit-corruption scare prompted a check of every _mm field under 5 and every _m field: no corrupt values were found (the small _mm values are genuinely thin steel, 3.2mm channel and 4mm mesh). But the check confirmed a naming split where the same quantity appears as height_mm, height_m and depth_m depending on the file.

**Root cause.** Units were made part of field names without a single canonical choice per quantity, so each extraction picked whichever matched what was printed.

**Impact.** Values are correct but a consumer must know three field names for one quantity; this is exactly the kind of ambiguity that leads to a real unit mix-up later. Left unfixed and carried as pending.

**Fix.** not fixed — verified as a naming problem, not corrupt data, and left

**→ Rule.** One quantity, one field name, one unit — enforced by the checker. Names that encode units invite a second name for the same thing.

<sub>`D:/00mk/steel project/training/Training/workmen's_diary/2026-08-02.md` · data-quality</sub>

#### ⚪ LOW · 2026-08-21 · 18 precast plank layout sheets carry pattern:section despite plank_layout filenames — probably right, easy to 'fix' wrongly

**What happened.** 18 files whose filenames contain *_plank_layout* carry pattern: "section". This is probably correct but reads as an error, so it was explicitly flagged so nobody 'fixes' it blindly.

**Root cause.** Filenames and pattern labels encode different things (what the sheet is called vs how it should be extracted), and nothing in the data records why a counterintuitive pairing is deliberate — so it is indistinguishable from the roof_frame_plan mislabeling found in the same session.

**Impact.** No current impact, but a real risk that a future cleanup pass conflates this correct case with the genuine roof_frame_plan bug and corrupts 18 files.

**Fix.** Flagged in the diary only; no marker written into the data.

**→ Rule.** When a correct labeling looks like a bug, write the justification into the files (warnings[] or a note field), not just the diary — a diary line will not stop the person doing a bulk cleanup six weeks later.

<sub>`D:/00mk/steel project/training/Training/workmen's_diary/2026-08-21.md` · data-quality</sub>

#### ⚪ LOW · 2026-08-25 · Three files had the literal strings 'grid'/'dummy' sitting in grid_ref instead of a real grid reference

**What happened.** The normalization sweep found 3 files whose grid_ref field carried the placeholder words 'grid' or 'dummy' rather than an actual grid reference like 'A-1'.

**Root cause.** Placeholder text written during extraction was never replaced, and no checker validated grid_ref's format.

**Impact.** Small in count, but a grid_ref that reads as a placeholder will resolve to nothing downstream and silently drop the element's position — the same silent-loss class as the discipline misspelling.

**Fix.** Fixed as part of the 485-point normalization pass.

**→ Rule.** Placeholder values are worse than empty ones — they pass presence checks and fail meaning checks; validate the format of every reference field.

<sub>`D:/00mk/steel project/training/Training/workmen's_diary/2026-08-25.md` · data-quality</sub>

#### ⚪ LOW · 2026-08-31 · 151 images were downscaled for exceeding the pixel cap by only 0.13%

**What happened.** Image size analysis found 151 pages at 3355x2347 which exceed the 7.86 MP cap by 0.13% and are therefore downscaled for essentially no reason. An earlier suspicion of an inconsistent rasterizer/DPI problem was disproven — DPI is uniform.

**Root cause.** A hard pixel cap with no tolerance band, combined with an initially wrong hypothesis about the source of size variation.

**Impact.** Marginal unnecessary resolution loss on 151 pages of training data.

**Fix.** Recorded but not changed.

**→ Rule.** Give hard resolution caps a small tolerance band, and disprove a suspected root cause with measurements before acting on it — the DPI-inconsistency theory here was wrong.

<sub>`D:/00mk/steel project/training/Training/workmen's_diary/2026-08-31.md` · data-quality</sub>

---

## T05 — Schema, Contract & Convention Drift

*Two places that had to agree about a shape, name, or unit — and quietly stopped agreeing.*

**40 entries** · 4 critical · 10 high

#### 🔴 CRITICAL · 2026-07-08 · The task generator was never updated for the Gen 4 schema, so every beam showed empty grid_ref and no rebar in the labeling UI

**What happened.** label-studio-tasks-makham.js still read el.grid_ref and mainBar.count, but Gen 4 had split those into grid_ref_start/grid_ref_end/span_length_m and nested main_bar into {top,bottom}. The real values fell into the read-only other_fields_json, so every beam's grid_ref and every beam/column's main rebar appeared blank in Label Studio. The bug had silently affected t3 from the start.

**Root cause.** A schema change was made in the spec and the extraction without auditing downstream consumers, and the generator failed soft — missing fields rendered as empty boxes instead of raising an error.

**Impact.** Every t3 task JSON already generated (and possibly already imported to Label Studio Cloud) presented annotators with blank rebar and grid data — the two most important fields in the dataset — and needed regeneration and re-import.

**Fix.** Generator taught to read both the new and old field shapes; elements XML given grid_ref_start/end/span_length_m boxes and split top/bottom rebar (6 boxes instead of 3); task JSON regenerated and spot-checked against a regular beam (B1) and an asymmetric one (B5, top=2/bottom=3).

**→ Rule.** A schema change is not done until every consumer is updated in the same change; and a generator must fail loudly on a field it cannot resolve, never emit an empty box.

<sub>`D:/00mk/steel project/training/Training/workmen's_diary/2026-07-08.md` · schema-drift/tooling</sub>

#### 🔴 CRITICAL · 2026-08-25 · standards-config.js carried wrong lap and cover values; real BBS cut lengths changed once corrected against มยผ.

**What happened.** Reading มยผ. 1101-64 (31 pages) and 1103-64 showed the registry's values were wrong: deformed-bar lap was a single 48d instead of grade-split 30/36/45d, round-bar lap 36d instead of 40d, and covers 40/40/25 instead of beam 30 / column 35 / slab 20; the 180° hook had no 60mm minimum. A sample beam's main bar cut length moved 4998→4749 mm and its stirrup 952→1032 mm.

**Root cause.** The registry had been populated from a different standard (วสท.) and never reconciled against the มยผ. documents it claimed to follow, with no per-value clause citation to make the mismatch visible.

**Impact.** Every BBS cut length and rebar quantity computed before this correction was wrong. Seven regression-pin test files had to be updated, each recomputed by hand.

**Fix.** Migrated the whole registry to มยผ. values with per-value clause citations; values the standard does not define (top-bar 1.3×, SDM Ld) kept with the gap stated in the clause field. npm test 1249/1249 with all pins recomputed by hand.

**→ Rule.** Every engineering constant must carry the standard and clause it came from, so a mismatch is visible on inspection rather than discovered years later. When constants change, recompute every regression pin by hand — never bulk-update pins to whatever the new code outputs.

<sub>`D:/00mk/steel project/training/Training/workmen's_diary/2026-08-25.md` · wrong-constant</sub>

#### 🔴 CRITICAL · 2026-09-01 · worker.py wrote result files without the `pattern` field, so the adapter could not read the grid master and every beam lost its quantity

**What happened.** The worker's output files omitted the `pattern` field entirely. Without it the adapter cannot recognise the grid-master page, so every beam ends up with `span_source: 'unresolved'` — meaning zero beam quantities in the BOQ for the entire house. The training team's GT files already carried `pattern: "grid_master"`; only the worker side had forgotten it.

**Root cause.** The worker relied on the model to supply metadata that the worker itself already knows — it dispatched a specific subtask and therefore knew the pattern before the call was even made. Trusting the model's output for a field you already have is a needless dependency.

**Impact.** Would have caused a complete loss of beam quantities (the single largest BOQ category — ฿106,821 of ฿144,704 on house01) on the very first real run. Caught only because a full house was simulated end-to-end without a GPU.

**Fix.** Added a `SUBTASK_PATTERN` table and stamped the pattern from the worker side, not from the model response.

**→ Rule.** Never ask the model for metadata you already possess. Any field determined by which subtask you dispatched must be stamped by the dispatcher, deterministically.

<sub>`2026-09-01.md` · pipeline-contract</sub>

#### 🔴 CRITICAL · 2026-09-01 · normalizeMainBar() only understood top/middle/bottom, so all column rebar came out null ('DBnull')

**What happened.** `normalizeMainBar()` in `js/shared/schema.js` only read the nested top/middle/bottom rebar shape. Columns naturally answer flat — drawings write only '4-DB12' with no top/bottom split — so the flat `{count, dia_mm}` form yielded null and all column steel vanished from the house, surfacing downstream as 'DBnull'.

**Root cause.** The normalizer was written against the beam data shape and assumed it was universal. Columns genuinely have a different, simpler natural shape on Thai drawings, and no fallback existed for it.

**Impact.** All column reinforcement missing from BOQ/BBS for every house; the wrong value surfaced as a visible 'DBnull' string rather than an error.

**Fix.** Extended `normalizeMainBar()` to accept the flat `{count, dia_mm}` form.

**→ Rule.** A normalizer must handle every shape the source domain naturally produces, not just the first one you built it for. When a field renders as literal 'null' text downstream, that is a normalizer gap, not a display bug.

<sub>`2026-09-01.md` · schema/adapter</sub>

#### 🟠 HIGH · 2026-07-06 · span_source field had been dropped from the spec and had to be added back after it caused a low-confidence extraction

**What happened.** The `span_source` field ('grid_table' / 'local_dimension' / 'unresolved') for beam elements in the `plan` pattern was not in the Gen 3 spec. Extracting page 19 fresh hit a low-confidence problem precisely because the field was missing, and it was added back in Generation 3.1 as 'proven genuinely necessary'.

**Root cause.** The Gen 3 schema was designed by simplifying Gen 2 without checking, field by field, why each dropped field had existed. A field that recorded provenance of a measurement was treated as noise until its absence made a measurement unverifiable.

**Impact.** Page 19 view2 (beam plan) came out at ~0.4 confidence and had to be completely re-extracted in round t2 with atomic segments plus span_source. A whole page of structural beam data was redone.

**Fix.** Added `span_source` back into the spec for beam elements in the plan pattern (Generation 3.1 point 1) and re-extracted page 19 view2 in mk_test/t2/.

**→ Rule.** When simplifying a schema, never drop a provenance field without writing down why it existed and what breaks without it. Provenance fields (where did this number come from) are the cheapest possible insurance against unverifiable data — keep them by default.

<sub>`D:/00mk/steel project/training/Training/workmen's_diary/2026-07-06.md` · schema-regression / rework</sub>

#### 🟠 HIGH · 2026-07-06 · Beam grid_ref was modelled as a rough aggregate count instead of atomic spans, losing per-span data

**What happened.** The original Gen 3 rule stored a beam's grid_ref as a rough aggregate with a `count`. Comparison against claude_output_03 showed this was wrong; the rule was changed so 1 entry = exactly 1 grid span, grouped by (element_id, span_length_m, span_source).

**Root cause.** The schema modelled a beam mark as a single object because that is how it appears in the schedule, not as the set of physical segments it actually is on the plan. Aggregating before recording destroyed the per-span lengths needed downstream.

**Impact.** Every beam plan extracted under the old rule had to be rewritten. Page 19 view2 and page 20 view1 were both completely redone with atomic segments; page 20 went from ~0.5 confidence to 0.87 and yielded a complete set of 17 atomic segments that the aggregate form could never have expressed.

**Fix.** Generation 3.1 point 2: grid_ref for beam changed to an atomic segment, one entry per grid span. Pages 19 and 20 re-extracted in mk_test/t2/.

**→ Rule.** Record data at the atomic level it physically exists at, and let aggregation happen downstream. Aggregating during extraction is irreversible information loss — a count can always be derived from segments, segments can never be recovered from a count.

<sub>`D:/00mk/steel project/training/Training/workmen's_diary/2026-07-06.md` · schema-design / rework</sub>

#### 🟠 HIGH · 2026-07-06 · Two agents spelled the same schema key differently (element vs elements), and the fix was to tolerate the drift rather than eliminate it

**What happened.** mk_test/t2/บ้าน_เล็ก_1ชั้น_01_หน้า29_floor_plan.json, produced by the MEP agent, used the key `elements` (plural) while the spec and every other file used `element` (singular). The Label Studio task script was written to check both names as a fallback instead of the data file being corrected.

**Root cause.** Multiple agents were dispatched in parallel against a prose spec with no machine-checkable schema and no validation step on agent output. Nothing rejected a file whose top-level key did not match the spec, so drift landed silently in the dataset.

**Impact.** The dataset now contains two spellings of the same key, and every future consumer must know to handle both. The diary itself flags this as a signal that parallel agents will keep introducing this class of variation.

**Fix.** Partially fixed — the task-generation script accepts both key names. The underlying data file was deliberately not corrected, and the choice between forcing exact field names vs staying tolerant was left open.

**→ Rule.** Validate every agent's output against a machine-readable schema before it is accepted into the dataset. Making the reader tolerant of drift is a one-way ratchet: the second spelling never gets removed and every downstream tool inherits the branch forever.

<sub>`D:/00mk/steel project/training/Training/workmen's_diary/2026-07-06.md` · schema-drift / process-failure</sub>

#### 🟠 HIGH · 2026-07-06 · Gen 2 and the self-done extraction had swapped the meaning of the grid axis labels

**What happened.** Comparing Gen 2 (claude_output_03) against the fresh extraction revealed that the two had swapped the meaning of the grid axes — the underlying data matched, only the labels were reversed. A clear convention was proposed: x_lines = horizontal/numeric, y_lines = vertical/alphabetic.

**Root cause.** The axis naming convention was never written down, so each generation picked an interpretation independently. Because the data itself was identical, nothing downstream failed loudly enough to expose the disagreement.

**Impact.** Two datasets that look consistent but describe axes oppositely. Any consumer joining them by axis name would produce a transposed building. It was caught only by a deliberate manual comparison, not by any check.

**Fix.** Proposed the explicit convention (x_lines=horizontal/numeric, y_lines=vertical/alphabetic) as Generation 3.1 point 9.

**→ Rule.** Write down the meaning of every axis, direction and orientation convention in the spec, with an example, before the first extraction. Label-level disagreements where the data matches are the hardest class to detect — nothing crashes, the numbers just mean the opposite thing.

<sub>`D:/00mk/steel project/training/Training/workmen's_diary/2026-07-06.md` · convention-drift</sub>

#### 🟠 HIGH · 2026-07-07 · Garden-fence marks C1/F/GB collide with the house's real structural marks

**What happened.** Pages 16-17 (garden fence) reuse the marks C1, F and GB, which on the structural sheets mean the main column and the footing. Nothing in the data distinguishes a fence C1 from a structural C1.

**Root cause.** Element identity in the schema is the mark string alone, with no scope/discipline qualifier — the drawing set reuses marks across unrelated sub-structures and the schema has no way to express that.

**Impact.** Merging the dataset would silently fuse a garden-fence post with a main structural column; still unresolved at the time of the entry.

**Fix.** Not fixed — flagged as needing a decision on how to separate them before combining the dataset.

**→ Rule.** Element ids must be scoped by their drawing/discipline context, not by mark alone; assume any mark string will be reused somewhere in a 60+ page set.

<sub>`D:/00mk/steel project/training/Training/workmen's_diary/2026-07-07.md` · schema-design</sub>

#### 🟠 HIGH · 2026-07-07 · The pre-Gen4 flat main_bar shape could not represent asymmetric top/bottom reinforcement — B5's 2-top/3-bottom collapsed to a single count

**What happened.** Re-reading page 21 (S-04) produced direct image evidence that beams B5/B5X carry separate top reinforcement of 2-Ø16mm and bottom of 3-Ø16mm. The schema up to Gen 3 stored main_bar as a flat `{count, dia_mm, type}` with no top/bottom split, so this beam could only be recorded as one combined number.

**Root cause.** The original schema modelled main reinforcement as a single quantity because the first sample beams happened to be symmetric. The field shape encoded an assumption about the data rather than the structure of the real drawing.

**Impact.** Any beam extracted under the flat shape lost the engineering distinction between top and bottom steel — the two are structurally different (hogging vs sagging) and cannot be recovered from a combined count. Fixing it forced the schema change that then broke the Label Studio generator (see the empty-main_bar bug) and created the fence double-count risk on pages 16/17.

**Fix.** Gen 4 mandates the nested `main_bar: {top:{...}, bottom:{...}}` split for every element, with page 21 as the cited justification.

**→ Rule.** Design the field shape from the hardest real drawing you can find, not the first easy one. A flattened field that loses a distinction can never be un-flattened from stored data — you have to re-read every image.

<sub>`D:/00mk/steel project/training/Training/workmen's_diary/2026-07-07.md` · schema-design</sub>

#### 🟠 HIGH · 2026-07-08 · The mandatory top/bottom rebar split creates a double-count when the drawing prints a single line

**What happened.** Pages 16/17 (fence) print one rebar spec line for C1 and the lintel, not a top/bottom split, but the schema mandates filling both. Anyone later summing top.count + bottom.count would count the same bars twice.

**Root cause.** A schema rule written for the common case (asymmetric beams genuinely have separate top and bottom bars) was made mandatory with no way to express 'this element has one undivided set'.

**Impact.** A latent 2x rebar overcount for every single-spec element, unresolved at the schema level and still flagged as a risk a day later.

**Fix.** An agent added a total_main_bar_count field as a guard; the underlying schema gap was not closed.

**→ Rule.** A mandatory field must have a legal way to say 'not applicable' — forcing a split the source does not make manufactures data that looks real and sums wrong.

<sub>`D:/00mk/steel project/training/Training/workmen's_diary/2026-07-08.md` · schema-design</sub>

#### 🟠 HIGH · 2026-07-10 · The annotation import-back scripts were never adapted to the Gen4 schema and stayed untouched for days

**What happened.** label-studio-import-annotations.js and -import-repeater-annotations.js still speak the pre-Gen4 schema. They were listed as a gap on July 7, again on July 8, and were still explicitly untouched on July 10 and July 11 — meaning annotated work in Label Studio has no working path back into the dataset.

**Root cause.** The schema migration covered the outbound half of the round trip (extraction and task generation) but not the inbound half, and the missing half was never scheduled.

**Impact.** Three houses of data have been pushed into Label Studio for annotation with no working way to bring corrections back — the entire annotation effort has no return path.

**Fix.** Not fixed — carried as a pending item across at least four days.

**→ Rule.** Migrate both directions of a round trip in the same change; an export path with no working import path means the annotation work has nowhere to land.

<sub>`D:/00mk/steel project/training/Training/workmen's_diary/2026-07-10.md` · schema-drift/tooling</sub>

#### 🟠 HIGH · 2026-09-01 · Footing rebar was missing only because SPEC_FIELDS lacked `dowel_bar` — the join already worked and the data was already there

**What happened.** The real root cause of the footing rebar loss was not a broken join. `buildSpecs()` in `raw-extraction-adapter.js` is already a generic element_id join, and the pile-cap detail pages (S-11/S-12) carry `element_id` matching the plan pages exactly (F4/F6/F3) with width_mm/height_mm/dowel_bar all present. The only problem was that the field is called `dowel_bar`, not `main_bar`, and `SPEC_FIELDS` did not list it.

**Root cause.** The schema has no official field-set for footings (noted in the files' own `schema_note`), so the training data used a domain-correct but unlisted field name. The adapter's field allowlist silently ignored it. First diagnosis blamed a missing join mechanism; the real cause was one absent field name.

**Impact.** All footing reinforcement lost across the corpus while concrete and formwork were correct all along — which made the failure look like a deep join problem rather than a one-line allowlist gap, and led to an initial misdiagnosis.

**Fix.** `buildSpecs()` now falls back to `dowel_bar` when `main_bar` is absent (engineering-correct: dowel steel from the pedestal into the footing is the footing's main reinforcement, same shape, already parsed by `normalizeMainBar()`). F4/F6/F3 now yield 39.34/199.33/19.67 kg with status=ok, plus 2 tests.

**→ Rule.** When data 'doesn't arrive', check the field allowlist before redesigning the join. And when the schema has no official field-set for a category, its field names will drift — grep the actual data files for the names in use rather than assuming the schema covers them.

<sub>`2026-09-01.md` · schema/adapter</sub>

#### 🟠 HIGH · 2026-09-01 · Spread footings use element_id: null and share no key at all with the plan page

**What happened.** Spread footings (ฐานรากแผ่, drawn by convention on S-09) use `element_id: null` and are matched by size instead — but the plan page carries no width_mm/height_mm either, so there is literally no shared key between the two pages.

**Root cause.** The drawing convention for spread footings omits the identifier the join relies on, and the schema provides no alternative correlation key. This is a genuine data-model gap, not a code defect.

**Impact.** Spread footings can never be joined to their detail pages; their reinforcement is unrecoverable with the current schema.

**Fix.** Not fixed — declared out of scope and requiring a redesign, not another field addition.

**→ Rule.** When two records must be joined, verify a shared key exists in the *real* data before building the join. If none exists, that is a schema design task — do not paper over it by adding fields one at a time.

<sub>`2026-09-01.md` · schema-design</sub>

#### 🟡 MEDIUM · 2026-07-05 · Nine new element_types were invented mid-extraction and written into the dataset without spec approval

**What happened.** During extraction, element_types not in the original spec were added and used: purlin, rafter (page 20 steel roof frame), slab_edge, parapet (page 23), precast_plank_detail (pages 24-25), and room/door/window/wall (pages 4-17 architectural). Whether this vocabulary is adopted permanently was left as open question #8 and was still unanswered a day later.

**Root cause.** The original spec scoped element_type to structural members only, but the work scope was expanded to 'do every pattern actually encountered'. The vocabulary was not expanded with the scope, so extraction had to invent terms on the fly to have anywhere to put the data.

**Impact.** The dataset contains an unratified type vocabulary. If it is later rejected or renamed, every file using those types must be rewritten; if it is accepted, it was accepted by default rather than by decision.

**Fix.** Not fixed — recorded as open question #8, still pending at end of 2026-07-06.

**→ Rule.** Expand the controlled vocabulary in the same decision that expands the scope. When extraction has to invent a term to proceed, that is a spec decision being made by the fastest available person — stop and get it ratified before it is written across dozens of files.

<sub>`D:/00mk/steel project/training/Training/workmen's_diary/2026-07-05.md` · unratified-schema-change</sub>

#### 🟡 MEDIUM · 2026-07-06 · After creating the central grid master, existing pages were never retrofitted to reference it

**What happened.** The rule was set that every plan/section page should reference the grid from หน้า00_gridline.json instead of re-writing the grid. Existing files (pages 19/20/21 and the per-page gridline files) were not retroactively edited to do so — only a pointer note was added to the old gridline files.

**Root cause.** A new convention was introduced without a migration pass over existing data. The cost of retrofitting was deferred and never scheduled, leaving two conventions live at once.

**Impact.** The dataset contains both per-page grid copies and a central master, so a grid correction made in the master does not reach pages holding their own copy — the exact duplication problem the master was created to eliminate.

**Fix.** Partially fixed — notes were added to _หน้า19_gridline.json and _หน้า06_gridline.json pointing at the new master; the originals were deliberately kept for traceability, and the pages themselves were not migrated.

**→ Rule.** Introducing a single source of truth is only half the job — the other half is migrating existing data off the old copies in the same session. Two live conventions is worse than one bad one, because corrections now reach only part of the data.

<sub>`D:/00mk/steel project/training/Training/workmen's_diary/2026-07-06.md` · incomplete-migration</sub>

#### 🟡 MEDIUM · 2026-07-06 · Spec join was done for beams only, leaving slab markers with a pointer flag instead of joined data

**What happened.** Generation 3.3 joined the beam cross-section spec directly into the plan pattern for pages 19 and 20. Slab markers SO/SI/ST/SX were not joined — their spec lives in a separate file (page 23) — and only a flag pointer was added instead.

**Root cause.** The join was instructed for beams specifically, and the scope was followed literally rather than being applied to every element type that has a separate spec file. The result is a schema where the same concept is represented two different ways.

**Impact.** The dataset now has two representations of element specification — joined-in for beams, pointer-only for slabs — so every downstream consumer needs both code paths. Anything that only implements the joined path silently gets no slab specs.

**Fix.** Not fixed — added as pending item #6, 'Join the slab marker (SO/SI/ST/SX) spec from page 23 into plan (if wanted)'.

**→ Rule.** When changing how a relationship is represented, apply it to every element type in the same change or explicitly document the exception in the spec. A half-applied representation change is a permanent branch in every consumer.

<sub>`D:/00mk/steel project/training/Training/workmen's_diary/2026-07-06.md` · incomplete-migration</sub>

#### 🟡 MEDIUM · 2026-07-06 · The Generation 4 merged schema doc was superseded within 48 hours of being written

**What happened.** merged_pattern_gen4_20260706.md merged two independently evolved schema lines — Claude's Gen 2 and Makham's Gen 3.1-3.3 — under an explicit rule never to drop a feature from either side without recording what was chosen and why. It was superseded on 2026-07-08 by '20260708draft of prime rawjson.md', two days later.

**Root cause.** Two schema lines were allowed to evolve independently in parallel and only reconciled after both had accumulated substantial divergence, so the merge document was large, immediately contested, and rewritten almost at once.

**Impact.** The merge document's real value ended up being only as an audit trail of how the two lines were reconciled — the reconciliation work itself was redone two days later. Four schema generations churned in roughly one week.

**Fix.** Archived on 2026-08-04 to wait_for_ทิ้ง/ rather than deleted, specifically because it is the only record of how the two schema lines were reconciled.

**→ Rule.** Do not let two schema lines evolve in parallel — reconcile continuously (daily) or designate one as authoritative. A big-bang merge of divergent schemas produces a document that is obsolete before anyone can adopt it.

<sub>`D:/00mk/steel project/training/Training/workmen's_diary/2026-07-06.md` · schema-churn</sub>

#### 🟡 MEDIUM · 2026-07-08 · The pattern type 'site_profile' meant a facade elevation, not site data

**What happened.** During the Gen 4 revision the type site_profile was renamed to side_profile and redefined as a side-elevation/facade view, not site-location data — and the 'section' type was narrowed to structures with actual rebar, forcing reclassification of pages 07/08/09/12/14 that t3 had typed as sections.

**Root cause.** Type names in the original taxonomy were chosen before the categories were exercised on real pages, so a name implied a meaning the data never had.

**Impact.** Every earlier round carried mis-typed pages; each new house's classification had to be redone against the corrected taxonomy.

**Fix.** Renamed and redefined the type, expanded the taxonomy from 10 to 13 types with a description for each, and reclassified the affected pages during the t4 read.

**→ Rule.** Give every enum value a written definition at the moment it is created — a type whose meaning lives only in its name will be used wrongly and then have to be migrated.

<sub>`D:/00mk/steel project/training/Training/workmen's_diary/2026-07-08.md` · schema-design</sub>

#### 🟡 MEDIUM · 2026-07-08 · Three new pattern types were added to the schema with no validated field-set

**What happened.** title, symbol and roof_plan were added to the taxonomy and immediately used to classify real pages in the t4 extraction, while their field-sets were explicitly acknowledged as not validated against real-world testing.

**Root cause.** Classification was needed before field design was finished, so the types entered production data ahead of their contract.

**Impact.** Data written under three types whose shape may still change; still listed as an open item ('the field-set for the 3 new pattern types is still draft') at the end of the day.

**Fix.** Not fixed — the gap was flagged in the spec and carried on the pending list.

**→ Rule.** If a schema type must ship before its fields are settled, mark every record written under it so a later migration can find them — do not rely on the pending list to remember.

<sub>`D:/00mk/steel project/training/Training/workmen's_diary/2026-07-08.md` · schema-design</sub>

#### 🟡 MEDIUM · 2026-07-14 · Range grid_ref written horizontal-axis-first, contradicting the project's own existing convention

**What happened.** When condensing page06's `grid_ref` the first time, the horizontal axis was written first (`"1-1' x D-C"`). The existing `"A-1"` convention is row-before-column, so it had to be reversed to `"D-C x 1-1'"`.

**Root cause.** The axis-order convention existed implicitly in point-refs but had never been written down for range-refs, so a new format was invented rather than derived from the existing one.

**Impact.** Every affected file had to be rewritten; the convention then had to be retro-applied across houses 2, 3, 4, 5.

**Fix.** Reversed to vertical-axis-first and wrote the rule into `primary_rawjson_schema.md` section 4.

**→ Rule.** When inventing a new field format, derive it from the nearest existing convention and write it into the schema in the same change — an unwritten convention gets violated the first time a new shape appears.

<sub>`2026-07-14.md` · schema-convention</sub>

#### 🟡 MEDIUM · 2026-07-14 · Point-type grid_ref dashes stripped in data while the schema still documents the opposite

**What happened.** Point refs were changed from `"C-2"` to `"C2"` across house 1's files, but `primary_rawjson_schema.md` section 4 still states point-type uses `"A-1"` with a dash. The question of whether the convention is project-wide or house-1-only went unanswered across several days.

**Root cause.** Data was changed before the spec decision was made, leaving the spec and the data actively contradicting each other with no owner for the discrepancy.

**Impact.** Long-running spec/data drift; other houses were later fixed by hand to a convention the spec still denied, and the scope question stayed open on the pending list for days.

**Fix.** Data fixed in houses 1, 2, 3, 5; the schema section was still not updated as of the entries.

**→ Rule.** Never let the data lead the spec. If a convention change is worth applying to files, block on the spec decision first — a spec that contradicts the data is worse than no spec.

<sub>`2026-07-14.md` · schema-convention</sub>

#### 🟡 MEDIUM · 2026-07-14 · A footing plan carried both grid_source and a full inline grid copy, violating the spec's own no-duplication rule

**What happened.** `หน้า19_view1_footing_plan.json` had a correct `grid_source` pointer to the grid master and also a duplicated inline `"grid": {...}` object, directly contradicting the spec rule 'never re-embed the full grid inline inside every view'.

**Root cause.** No automated validation enforces the spec's structural rules, so a violation written during extraction survived until a human eyeballed it.

**Impact.** A second, silently-divergent copy of the grid inside a data file — the same class of problem as the circular-reference bug, since a stale inline copy would win over the master for any reader that trusts it.

**Fix.** Inline grid removed; the rest of the house was swept and no other occurrence was found.

**→ Rule.** Structural spec rules need a validator script, not just prose. Any rule phrased as 'never do X' should be a check that runs over every file before a house is declared done.

<sub>`2026-07-14.md` · schema-convention</sub>

#### 🟡 MEDIUM · 2026-07-14 · Identical beam specs repeated character-for-character on every occurrence of the same mark

**What happened.** Every occurrence of a beam mark in `หน้า19_view2_beam_plan.json` printed the full spec (width, height, main_bar, stirrup, additional_bars, concrete_grade, steel_grade, spec_source, spec_confidence_score) identically — B2 twice, B4 three times, B5 three times, B3 three times, B4X twice.

**Root cause.** The original schema had no place to put per-mark data, so per-mark data was written per-instance; nothing forced it to stay consistent.

**Impact.** Bloated files and, more dangerously, N copies of a spec that can silently diverge when one occurrence is edited — which is exactly the failure mode the additional_bars bugs later exhibited.

**Fix.** Split into a `specs{}` object keyed by `element_id`, after first verifying every occurrence genuinely had an identical spec. `elements[]` now holds only position and point-specific confidence.

**→ Rule.** Data that is per-mark belongs in a per-mark object, never repeated per instance. Duplicated identical values are a divergence bug waiting for its first edit.

<sub>`2026-07-14.md` · schema-convention</sub>

#### 🟡 MEDIUM · 2026-07-15 · Element-ordering rule was written in the wrong direction and had to be redone the next day

**Root cause.** The rule was written into the schema and applied to files before the direction was confirmed against a worked example with the user.

**Impact.** A 20-element file reordered twice, plus a schema edit that had to be reverted and rewritten, plus the risk that other files reordered under the wrong rule would need finding.

**Fix.** Re-ordered the file, validated all 20 elements intact, and fixed the schema direction after confirming with the user first.

**→ Rule.** Confirm an ordering or sequencing rule against a concrete worked example before applying it to files — a directional rule applied backwards costs the full rewrite twice.

<sub>`2026-07-15.md` · schema-convention</sub>

#### 🟡 MEDIUM · 2026-07-15 · Series-wide promo pages were classified as title/unknown in every house until a 14th pattern was invented

**What happened.** The 10-house price-comparison table and the series collage cover were being recorded as pattern 'title' or 'unknown' because the taxonomy had no category for content belonging to the whole product series rather than to this house. A 14th pattern 'misc' was added, then retrofitted across houses 1 (pages 60/61), 2 (71/72), 3 and 4 (3 pages each).

**Root cause.** The pattern taxonomy was fixed at 13 types before the full range of page content had been seen; pages that fit nothing got dumped into the nearest-looking bucket instead of being flagged as unclassifiable.

**Impact.** Mislabeled pattern values in five houses' worth of files, retrofitted page-by-page after the fact — and 'unknown' was in use as a real value, meaning genuinely unclassified pages and wrongly-classified ones looked the same.

**Fix.** Pattern 'misc' added to primary_rawjson_schema.md (taxonomy 13→14) and applied retroactively to houses 1-5.

**→ Rule.** A closed taxonomy needs an explicit escape hatch that is distinguishable from a default. Forcing a page into the nearest bucket hides the fact that the taxonomy is incomplete.

<sub>`D:/00mk/steel project/training/Training/workmen's_diary/2026-07-15.md` · schema</sub>

#### 🟡 MEDIUM · 2026-07-19 · House 5's grid y-axis origin differed from every other house and had to be re-originated

**What happened.** House 5's grid master had its y-axis origin at A, unlike the other houses. It was flagged awaiting a decision on 2026-07-19, then on 2026-07-24 re-originated from A=0 to F=0 — which made the previously-misplaced-looking e'/f' dummy grids come out correct.

**Root cause.** No project-wide convention for grid origin was written down, so each house's grid master was built with whatever origin seemed natural for that house's sheets.

**Impact.** Dummy grids appearing misplaced and unresolvable until the origin was flipped; a full re-origination of the house's grid master plus renaming (Aprime→A', e'/f'→E'/F').

**Fix.** Re-originated the y-axis from A=0 to F=0, which resolved the apparently-misplaced dummy grids, and normalised the label casing.

**→ Rule.** Fix the grid-origin convention project-wide before extracting the first house. An inconsistent origin makes every derived position look wrong in a way that is easy to misdiagnose as a measurement error.

<sub>`2026-07-19.md` · schema-convention</sub>

**What happened.** A sweep of all 20 pattern=plan files in house 3 found pages 06/07 still carrying text referencing '1''(2.25)' from before the face/centreline distinction was settled, and page21's description ambiguous between centreline (2.25) and master (2.35).

**Root cause.** When the master value changed, only the structured fields were cascaded; free-text descriptions, notes and warnings referencing the old value were not swept.

**Impact.** Files internally contradicting the master; a reader taking the prose at face value gets the old value.

**Fix.** Adjusted the text to the master's current 2.35 face value and clarified page21's ambiguity.

**→ Rule.** Cascading a value change must include free-text descriptions, notes and warnings — grep for the old numeric literal across the house, not just for the field name.

<sub>`2026-07-20.md` · data-extraction</sub>

#### 🟡 MEDIUM · 2026-07-20 · A beam sits at a different position on floor 1 and floor 2 beyond measurement tolerance, unresolved

**What happened.** The beam east of the staircase bay measures at centreline 2.25 / face 2.35 on floor 1 (matching `1''` exactly) but at 1.96 on floor 2 — a 0.29m (~23px) difference, beyond measurement tolerance.

**Root cause.** The grid master carries one value per dummy grid, but the building genuinely differs between floors at this location; the model has no way to express a per-floor dummy grid.

**Impact.** A real geometric difference recorded provisionally under one label; blocked pending a decision on whether floor 2 needs its own dummy grid.

**Fix.** Recorded provisionally under `1''` with a prominent flag, awaiting a decision.

**→ Rule.** When measurement finds a per-floor difference beyond tolerance, that is a data-model gap, not a measurement error — the schema needs per-floor grid values rather than a flag that defers the problem.

<sub>`2026-07-20.md` · schema-convention</sub>

#### 🟡 MEDIUM · 2026-08-20 · King-try's resolve_grid.py KeyErrors on every current grid file after a schema move

**What happened.** resolve_grid.py reads data["grid"]["x_lines"], but grid files at the time of review put x_lines/y_lines at top level — so the tool raises KeyError on any current file.

**Root cause.** The tool was written against the schema shape as it existed on King-try's 2026-07-25 branch point and was never re-run against current data after the schema normalization. Nothing in the tool validates the shape it expects, so it fails with a raw KeyError rather than a useful message.

**Impact.** The Gemini overlay prototype is unusable on any current grid file without editing it first; part of why the branch stayed un-cherry-picked.

**Fix.** Not fixed — recorded as one of 3 open King-try tooling gaps, still open at end of 2026-08-20.

**→ Rule.** Any tool that reads the rawjson schema must be re-run against a current file whenever the schema moves a field, and should assert the shape it expects with a named error rather than KeyError-ing on a nested lookup.

<sub>`D:/00mk/steel project/training/Training/workmen's_diary/2026-08-20.md` · schema-drift</sub>

#### 🟡 MEDIUM · 2026-08-21 · First fix for the repetition loop only made failure less likely, and its n-gram guard was trivially evaded

**What happened.** The 2026-08-21 fix added `repetition_penalty=1.15` + `no_repeat_ngram_size=8` to treat a structural output problem with a scoring nudge. Result: 'พังทุกครั้ง' became 'พังบางครั้ง' — it never removed the failure. Worse, the n-gram guard was directly evaded on house 08 หน้า07 because the model alternated its separators (`_ide`, `_ida`, `_ife`), so no exact 8-token window ever repeated.

**Root cause.** A probabilistic penalty ('asking') was applied to a problem that required a hard constraint ('forbidding'). The n-gram rule matches exact token windows, which a varying-separator loop slips past by construction.

**Impact.** A whole extra day and an extra GPU rental cycle before the real fix (grammar-constrained decoding) was tried; the parameter fix was written into two scripts and shipped as if it might be sufficient.

**Fix.** Grammar-constrained decoding (xgrammar) added; valid-page rate went 57.9% → 96.8%. The penalty parameters were kept but are no longer the load-bearing fix.

**→ Rule.** A structural guarantee (bracket balance, schema shape) needs a constraint that makes the bad output impossible, not a penalty that makes it less probable — and never assume an exact-match n-gram guard covers a loop that can vary its filler.

<sub>`D:/00mk/steel project/training/Training/workmen's_diary/2026-08-21(teach mk).md` · wrong-fix-approach</sub>

#### 🟡 MEDIUM · 2026-08-25 · Candidate filenames read as "this is a footing" when they only meant "harvested from a footing page"

**What happened.** Makham asked why a picture of a grid bubble containing the letter A was named as a footing. The prefix `cand_footing__` reads as "this is a footing", but its real meaning is "collected from a footing-plan page". The harvester has no concept of a footing — it only finds similarly-sized icons repeating 3 or more times, and grid bubbles A/B/C/D repeat 8 times, matching perfectly.

**Root cause.** A filename encoded the source of a sample as if it were the sample's class label, conflating provenance with classification.

**Impact.** Human reviewers (including Makham) were misled about what they were being asked to approve — a direct risk of promoting garbage into the template bank.

**Fix.** Renamed the prefix to `cand_fromFootingPage__`, renamed the 75 existing files, and wrote the warning into the docstring.

**→ Rule.** Never let a filename or field name imply a classification the code did not actually make. Name artifacts by their provenance when provenance is all you know.

<sub>`D:/00mk/steel project/training/Training/workmen's_diary/2026-08-25.md` · misleading-naming</sub>

#### 🟡 MEDIUM · 2026-08-25 · Files printing both SD-40 and SD-50 on one page were left blank rather than resolved by guessing

**What happened.** Some drawing pages print both SD-40 and SD-50 steel grades. Rather than picking one, the field was left empty during the normalization sweep.

**Root cause.** The extraction schema has one grade field per page while real drawings can specify two on the same sheet for different element classes — a schema/reality mismatch.

**Impact.** Those files carry no steel grade at all, so downstream consumers see a gap. Correct behavior, but a real data hole and a sign the schema needs a per-element grade.

**Fix.** Left blank deliberately, recorded in the "deliberately not done" section.

**→ Rule.** When the source is genuinely ambiguous, leave the field empty and record why — never let a script pick for you. Repeated ambiguity of the same kind is a signal the schema shape is wrong, not the data.

<sub>`D:/00mk/steel project/training/Training/workmen's_diary/2026-08-25.md` · schema-mismatch</sub>

**What happened.** After fixing the null-sheet_code bug, it was recognised that a page containing two physical sheets should carry a sheet_code per view, but the pass0 prompt contract does not support that.

**Root cause.** The original pass0 schema assumed one sheet per page; the two-sheet-side-by-side layout was discovered later.

**Impact.** Second-sheet codes are stored only as free text in warnings[], so downstream consumers cannot reliably attribute a code to a view.

<sub>`D:/00mk/steel project/training/Training/workmen's_diary/2026-08-31.md` · schema-gap</sub>

#### 🟡 MEDIUM · 2026-08-31 · No decision yet on whether the model or the adapter should split combined marks like 'F4,C1'

**What happened.** The model writes ids exactly as printed on the drawing ("F4,C1"), while the GT convention splits them into separate elements. This costs strict recall points for correct readings and is unresolved.

**Root cause.** The training-data convention and the drawing's own notation diverge, with no decided ownership for reconciling them.

**Impact.** Recall metrics understated, and downstream ingestion may or may not handle combined marks — unverified whether raw-extraction-adapter.js on the Constistant side copes.
