<sub>`D:/00mk/steel project/training/Training/workmen's_diary/2026-08-31.md` · schema-gap</sub>

#### 🟡 MEDIUM ·  · Numeric/array fields risked silently becoming strings when written for real use

**What happened.** A pattern was identified where numeric or array fields (needed as numbers/arrays for real use) could accidentally become strings (e.g. a number becoming a quoted string, an array becoming a joined string) when passing through a display layer (Label Studio) and back.

**Root cause.** No standing rule enforcing type round-tripping — display-format conversions were not guaranteed to convert back before being written as real ground truth.

**Impact.** Risk of ground-truth files carrying wrong-typed fields, which downstream consumers assume are correctly typed.

**Fix.** Adopted a standing rule: numeric/array fields must match raw-data source types exactly before being written to a file used for real.

**→ Rule.** Numeric/array fields must match raw-data types exactly before being written to a file used for real — never let a number become a string or an array become a string by accident.

<sub>`d:/00mk/steel project/training/Training/No_touch_box/docs/rule_of_tune.md` · type-contract</sub>

#### ⚪ LOW · 2026-07-05 · A block of SQL was living as a comment inside schema.js instead of in the database folder

**What happened.** Phase A cleanup found an SQL comment block sitting in js/shared/schema.js and moved it out to database/resource_hub_tables.sql where the rest of the schema SQL lives.

**Root cause.** SQL was written where it was first needed (next to the JS entity shapes it mirrored) rather than in the directory that owns database definitions, so it was invisible to anyone looking for table definitions and dead weight to anyone reading the JS.

**Impact.** Small — a database definition that could not be found by looking in database/, and dead comment bulk inside the single most-read file in the codebase.

**Fix.** Moved the SQL comment block from schema.js into database/resource_hub_tables.sql.

**→ Rule.** Artifacts belong in the directory that owns their type, not next to the code that inspired them — a comment is not a storage location for another language's source.

<sub>`D:/00mk/steel project/training/Training/workmen's_diary/2026-07-05.md` · code-hygiene</sub>

#### ⚪ LOW · 2026-07-08 · The pattern taxonomy shipped with 9 types and no catch-all; `unknown` had to be bolted on during real extraction

**What happened.** Answering 'how many types does Makham's Pattern have' produced: 10 types = the 9 originally designed plus `unknown`, which was added during real-world testing when pages turned up that fit none of the 9.

**Root cause.** The taxonomy was designed from a survey of expected sheet kinds rather than from a full page-by-page walk of a real drawing set, so it had no escape hatch for the pages nobody anticipated (committee rosters, price comparison tables, back-cover ads).

**Impact.** Small — the gap was closed by adding a type. But without `unknown`, an extractor facing an unclassifiable page has only two options, both bad: force it into the nearest wrong type, or drop it. Later rounds confirmed the risk was real (pages 70-72 of house 2 were correctly parked as unknown/title rather than stuffed into notes).

**Fix.** `unknown` added to the taxonomy and honored by Gen 4; later expanded to 13 types.

**→ Rule.** Any closed classification applied to real-world documents needs an explicit 'does not fit' value from day one — otherwise the first unmatched item silently becomes a wrong classification.

<sub>`D:/00mk/steel project/training/Training/workmen's_diary/2026-07-08.md` · schema-design</sub>

#### ⚪ LOW · 2026-07-15 · House 2 pages 07/10 had grid row order written reversed in the original extraction

**What happened.** Pages 07 and 10_section2 recorded row ranges as `D-E`/`E-F` when the correct top-to-bottom order (F>E>D>C>B>A) requires `E-D`/`F-E`.

**Root cause.** Row order was written in whatever direction it was read off the sheet rather than in the project's canonical top-to-bottom order, and the convention had not yet been written down at the time of extraction.

**Impact.** Reversed ranges across multiple files, fixed only when the convention sweep reached them.

**Fix.** Fixed during the house-2 format pass alongside the other grid_ref convention fixes.

**→ Rule.** Ordering conventions must be in the schema before the first house is extracted; every convention settled late costs a retro-sweep across every house already done.

<sub>`2026-07-15.md` · schema-convention</sub>

#### ⚪ LOW · 2026-09-01 · CV/pass3 sidecar files would have been fed into the raw-extraction adapter as unknown patterns

**What happened.** `cv15_*`, `cv25_*` and `pass3_measure.json` are not raw-extraction pattern files, but they were about to flow into the file-selection screen and then into the adapter, which would emit pointless 'unknown pattern' warnings for each.

**Root cause.** New pipeline stages wrote their outputs into the same result-file collection the adapter consumes, without any tagging distinguishing 'extraction output' from 'diagnostic sidecar'. The adapter's contract (only known patterns) was never enforced at the producer side.

**Impact.** Caught before shipping. Would have produced a wall of meaningless warnings that masks real ones.

**Fix.** Filtered sidecars out of the selection UI and summarized them instead in a single `renderPass3Summary` card (pages measured, px/m scale, max error, CV-seen-but-AI-silent points, mismatched refs).

**→ Rule.** When a new stage writes files into a shared results directory, decide at the producer side whether each file is consumable output or a diagnostic sidecar — and give consumers an explicit allowlist rather than letting them warn about everything they don't recognize.

## T06 — Config, Environment & Dependency Traps

*A setting, default, version, or environment difference that silently changed behaviour.*

**87 entries** · 18 critical · 26 high

#### 🔴 CRITICAL · 2026-07-21 · Parallel `pip install` for llama.cpp downgraded transformers and torch under a running training job

**What happened.** While the 3-epoch training was running, a second tmux window ran `pip install -r requirements.txt` for llama.cpp in the same global Python environment; it downgraded transformers 5.5.0→4.57.6 and torch 2.10.0+cu128→2.11.0+cpu. The training script's final sample-generation step then crashed with FileNotFoundError on `modeling_qwen3_5_moe.py`.

**Root cause.** No virtual environment isolation — two jobs shared one interpreter, and a third-party requirements.txt was allowed to resolve unpinned versions of the packages the live job depended on.

**Impact.** The running job broke mid-flight (the adapter had luckily just finished saving); the CUDA torch build was replaced by a CPU-only build; a three-step repair plus a re-run of verify_env.py was needed before quality could be measured.

**Fix.** pip install transformers==5.5.0 (exact version from the successful run's log), then pip install torch==2.10.0 --index-url .../cu128 to restore the CUDA build; verify_env.py re-passed.

**→ Rule.** Never pip install anything on a machine while an important job runs there — always use a separate venv/container for side work, and record the exact working package versions from the run log so recovery is a pin, not a guess.

<sub>`D:/00mk/steel project/training/Training/workmen's_diary/2026-07-21.md` · environment</sub>

#### 🔴 CRITICAL · 2026-07-21 · CUDA OOM on a 95GB card because LORA_R=64 is multiplied by 256 MoE experts

**What happened.** Training crashed with CUDA out of memory: 94.87GB of 95GB VRAM was consumed, leaving ~100MB. LORA_R had been set to 64.

**Root cause.** LoRA memory cost was estimated as if the model were dense. Qwen3.6-35B-A3B is MoE with 256 experts, so every LoRA adapter is instantiated 256 times — rank choice is multiplied by expert count, not additive.

**Impact.** Training aborted on a paid instance; required a config change and restart of the run.

**Fix.** Reduced LORA_R from 64 to 32 (research also indicates smaller rank suits a 226-example dataset better).

**→ Rule.** On an MoE model, size LoRA rank against expert count, not parameter count — budget VRAM as rank × experts before the first run, not after the first OOM.

<sub>`D:/00mk/steel project/training/Training/workmen's_diary/สอนมะขาม_รวม.md` · training-config</sub>

#### 🔴 CRITICAL · 2026-07-21 · pip install in a second terminal overwrote transformers and crashed the still-running training script

**What happened.** While the 3-epoch training ran, a second SSH window ran pip install to prepare llama.cpp ahead of time. That install upgraded/replaced `transformers`, removing the Unsloth-provided Qwen3.5-MoE support file. The training script — which had already saved the LoRA adapter but had not exited — then crashed with a file-not-found error on its final sample-generation step.

**Root cause.** Both terminals shared one system-wide Python environment. Nothing isolated the side task from the live critical job; the risk was not considered because the install was in a 'different window'.

**Impact.** Environment had to be repaired before eval could run at all; the LoRA adapter survived only by timing luck — a few minutes earlier and the entire training run would have had to be repeated (time + money).

**Fix.** Repaired the environment afterwards, then ran eval_fields.py. Rule adopted: never touch shared packages while a critical job runs; use a virtual environment for side work.

**→ Rule.** Treat a running training job as holding a lock on the whole Python environment. Any preparatory install goes into an isolated venv, or waits until the job has fully exited.

<sub>`D:/00mk/steel project/training/Training/workmen's_diary/สอนมะขาม_รวม.md` · environment/infra</sub>

#### 🔴 CRITICAL · 2026-07-24 · MAX_LENGTH=9216 silently truncated the answers of the 5 grid-master training examples

**What happened.** MAX_LENGTH had been set from single-image examples. The dataset contains 5 special 'grid master' examples using 2-4 images each, needing ~22,000 tokens — 2.4× the limit. Everything past the limit is cut from the tail, and the tail is the correct answer being taught.

**Root cause.** The sequence-length budget was computed from the typical example rather than the worst case, and truncation is silent by design — no error, no warning. The bug had existed since before house 05 was added and was only found by reading the script against real dataset token counts.

**Impact.** Would have trained the model on mutilated answers for the only examples that teach whole-building grid lines — the topic the script itself flags as the most error-prone. Caught before the paid run.

**Fix.** Raised MAX_LENGTH from 9,216 to 24,576 (Makham's choice, to preserve full image detail), accepting higher OOM risk on those 5 examples.

**→ Rule.** Set sequence length from the measured worst-case example in the actual dataset, and assert/log any example that would be truncated — silent truncation destroys labels without failing.

<sub>`D:/00mk/steel project/training/Training/workmen's_diary/สอนมะขาม_รวม.md` · data/training-config</sub>

#### 🔴 CRITICAL · 2026-07-24 · MAX_LENGTH of 9,216 was derived from a 1-image example, silently truncating the 5 multi-image gridmaster examples that carry the answers

**What happened.** train_qwen36.py's MAX_LENGTH was set to 9,216 tokens, a figure computed from an example containing one image. The dataset contains 5 'grid master' examples using 2-4 images at once, needing up to ~22,000 tokens — 2.4x the limit. Anything over the limit is truncated from the tail, and the tail is the JSON answer being taught.

**Root cause.** A configuration constant was sized against a typical example rather than against the measured maximum of the real dataset, and nothing in the training run reported truncation as an error — it silently trimmed.

**Impact.** If unfixed, the only 5 examples that teach whole-building grid lines (the topic the script itself flags as most often missed) would have been trained on with their answers cut off. The bug predated house 05 and had never been caught.

**Fix.** MAX_LENGTH raised to 24,576 (Makham's choice, preserving full image detail); later re-proved by measurement — longest real row is 22,515 tokens, 0 rows over the limit, 2,061 tokens of headroom.

**→ Rule.** Size every length/size limit against the measured maximum of the real dataset, not a representative sample — and make truncation raise a loud error, never a silent trim.

<sub>`D:/00mk/steel project/training/Training/workmen's_diary/2026-07-24(teach mk).md` · data/config</sub>

#### 🔴 CRITICAL · 2026-07-28 · Bug 1: t02's max_length of 10240/13312 would have truncated gridmaster examples down to 42%/39%, cutting the JSON label off the tail

**What happened.** The t02 presets still carried max_length values of 10,240 and 13,312 — the stale pre-fix values from before the 2026-07-24 decision. Gridmaster examples need ~22,500 tokens, so they would have been cut to 42% and 39%, and the truncated tail is the JSON answer.

**Root cause.** A decision made on one script (train_qwen36.py, 2026-07-24) was never propagated to its sibling. Two files carried the same configuration with no mechanism keeping them in sync.

**Impact.** Would have repeated the exact bug fixed four days earlier, on the more expensive round, silently.

**Fix.** Changed to 24576 in every preset; noted explicitly that these were the foreign values and that if OOM hits the order is max_pixels → lora_r → bigger card, never lowering max_length back.

**→ Rule.** When a configuration decision is made, grep for every other file carrying that same setting and fix them in the same commit. A fix applied to one of two twins is a bug waiting for the twin's turn.

<sub>`D:/00mk/steel project/training/Training/workmen's_diary/2026-07-28.md` · config/process</sub>

#### 🔴 CRITICAL · 2026-07-28 · Three more bugs found only by comparing t02's hyperparameters against t01 one by one — a check the diary says should have been done from the start

**What happened.** A late line-by-line comparison of t02's settings against t01's surfaced three additional bugs: lora_dropout=0.05 (MoE ParamWrapper does not support dropout≠0 — confirmed from a real t01 error), optim='adamw_8bit' (the exact value t01 hit OOM with, needing paged_adamw_8bit), and no bf16=True at all (this MoE family requires a bf16 setup per t01). All three were values t01 had already failed on and moved away from.

**Root cause.** The new round started from the stale original script rather than from the round that had already been debugged, and no systematic diff against the known-good configuration was performed until late. Hard-won failure knowledge lived only in t01's files.

**Impact.** Three known-failing values were still in place at the point of nearly renting; all three had already cost real failures in the t01 round.

**Fix.** All three corrected, and a 16-line parity table built in §0.4 confirming the only remaining differing variable is the model family.

**→ Rule.** Start a new round by diffing its configuration against the last known-good round, argument by argument, before anything else. Any value the previous round moved away from is a value that already caused a failure.

<sub>`D:/00mk/steel project/training/Training/workmen's_diary/2026-07-28.md` · process/config</sub>

#### 🔴 CRITICAL · 2026-07-28 · transformers 5.5.0 removed ip.max_pixels/min_pixels entirely, crashing Phase 4 on the paid machine

**What happened.** The first real run on the rented machine errored immediately with AttributeError: property of 'Qwen2VLImageProcessor' object has no setter. The transformers version pip pulled (5.5.0) had removed the max_pixels/min_pixels attributes altogether — not made them read-only, removed. Both train_qwen3vl.py and eval_fields.py used the removed path.

**Root cause.** Library version drift against code that had never been run since it was written. Dependencies were not pinned, so pip resolved to a version newer than anything the code had been tested against, and the API it depended on was gone.

**Impact.** A hard crash on Phase 4, on paid GPU time, after every Phase 0 check had passed — proving Phase 0 could not catch this class of failure because it ran on a different machine's library versions.

**Fix.** Read the library's real source rather than guessing; found ip.size['longest_edge'] / ['shortest_edge'] still works; deleted the two broken lines from both files.

**→ Rule.** Pin dependency versions for any run that costs money, and when an API breaks, read the library's actual source instead of guessing at the replacement. Code that has sat unrun is riskier than it looks — the world moved even though the code didn't.

<sub>`D:/00mk/steel project/training/Training/workmen's_diary/2026-07-28.md` · dependency-drift</sub>

#### 🔴 CRITICAL · 2026-07-29 · t01's GGUF may contain no tuning at all — silent LoRA merge failure on MoE ParamWrapper

**What happened.** t01 (tuned 21-24 Jul, converted to GGUF, used locally ever since) produced unusable extractions. Tracing showed the format/schema was entirely wrong (0/6 pages) while content reading was good — the signature of an untuned base model following a prompt. Suspicion: merge_and_unload() never actually merged the LoRA into the weights before GGUF conversion.

**Root cause.** peft/Unsloth's merge_and_unload() merges a ParamWrapper-style LoRA on an MoE model incorrectly — proven on the 28th by measuring a 201M-value tensor where only 0.67% of values changed. The structure passes and no error is raised, so the failure is completely silent. t01 used the same function on the same model family.

**Impact.** Every conclusion drawn from the t01 GGUF since 24 Jul may be about the base model, not the tuned one. Six pages of house 01 extraction output are contaminated. All local inference work since the 24th is of unknown value. Blocks both t01 and t02 rounds.

**Fix.** not fixed — test designed but not yet run: run page 03 through the untuned base Qwen3.6 GGUF with the same prompt and compare against t01's output (~20 min, free)

**→ Rule.** A merge/convert step that raises no error has NOT proven it worked. After any weight-merging operation, numerically diff the merged tensors against the base (percentage of values changed) before converting or shipping — structural success is not behavioural success.

<sub>`D:/00mk/steel project/training/Training/workmen's_diary/2026-07-29.md` · gguf-conversion</sub>

#### 🔴 CRITICAL · 2026-07-29 · t02 still has no GGUF at all — the MoE merge bug now blocks both tuning rounds

**What happened.** t02's GGUF conversion was caught failing on the 28th by its stricter guard and remains unconverted. As of the 29th the same peft/Unsloth MoE merge bug is understood to block t01 as well, so neither round has a trustworthy deployable artifact.

**Root cause.** A single unresolved upstream defect in merge_and_unload() for ParamWrapper LoRAs on MoE models, with no workaround yet found.

**Impact.** Two full tuning rounds with no shippable local artifact. Notably t02 was trained at 3,796 tokens/image — exactly what llama.cpp feeds — so it may be the better local model, and the merge bug is what prevents finding out.

**Fix.** not fixed — alternatives identified: find a different merge path, or abandon GGUF and serve bf16+adapter on a rented machine (that path is known to give 90%)

**→ Rule.** When a single upstream defect blocks the deploy path for every artifact you produce, stop producing artifacts and fix the deploy path. Also: keep a known-good fallback serving mode (bf16 + runtime adapter) so a broken conversion never blocks all delivery.

<sub>`D:/00mk/steel project/training/Training/workmen's_diary/2026-07-29.md` · gguf-conversion</sub>

#### 🔴 CRITICAL · 2026-08-25 · 973 of 973 training images were being downscaled — 100% of the dataset, unnoticed for multiple rounds

**What happened.** Measurement with a purpose-built tool (measure_capacity.py) showed every single image in the training set exceeded the MAX_PIXELS cap of 5,120 visual tokens. The most common size (3309×2339, 615 images) needed 7,558 tokens and lost 32%; the largest (4631×3473) lost 67%. Even the smallest image in the set exceeded the cap.

**Root cause.** MAX_PIXELS was set at 5,120 without ever computing what the actual dataset images required. The token cost of an image was never derived from real file dimensions until this day.

**Impact.** Every training round to date trained on degraded images. Beam lines and small symbols were being destroyed before the model ever saw them — a plausible direct cause of plan_beam 0%. Multiple paid rounds ran on damaged input.

**Fix.** Wrote measure_capacity.py to compute tokens from actual image dimensions (patch 16 × merge 2 → 1 token = 32×32 px). Raised MAX_PIXELS to 7,680 and MAX_LENGTH to 47,104, dropping downscaled images from 100% to 30% with no extra hardware cost (peak VRAM 87.5 → 90.9 GB on the same 96GB card).

**→ Rule.** Compute the real resource cost of your actual dataset before setting any cap. A cap chosen without measuring the data is a silent data-destruction setting.

<sub>`D:/00mk/steel project/training/Training/workmen's_diary/2026-08-25(teach mk).md` · config/data-pipeline</sub>

#### 🔴 CRITICAL · 2026-08-30 · Missing `crop_to_patches: true` collapsed every training image to one 256-token tile, so the 78B model never learned to read drawings

**What happened.** After 4 folds of InternVL3-78B QLoRA training finished, eval showed plan_beam 6/6 = 0% and plan_footing 1/1 = 0%. Opening the raw outputs (not just the recall number) showed the model answered with a completely different house and different sheet — fed a footing plan, it returned another house's roof plan. Investigation with three independent evidences: (1) counting image tokens in the training log dump = 768 tokens / 3 images = exactly 256/image, (2) reading `llamafactory/data/mm_plugin.py` source showed tiling requires `crop_to_patches: true` which the yaml never set, (3) downscaling a real beam plan to 448×448 (what the model actually saw) made every beam mark, dimension and rebar note unreadable by eye.

**Root cause.** The LLaMA-Factory training config was written by copying an official example without tracing the framework source for how many tokens per image it actually produces. InternVL3's dynamic tiling is opt-in via one flag; without it every image, no matter its original megapixels, is squashed into a single 256-token tile. Nobody probed the real token-per-image count before spending money on a full run.

**Impact.** ~$63 and roughly 15-16 hours × 4 GPUs of training burned producing adapters that only learned the JSON schema (96-100% valid) and memorised answers for houses seen in training — 0% element recall on real reading. The whole 4-fold k-fold round, the new test house, and the planned soup were made worthless. Third occurrence of the same bug class (t01 Unsloth 512px fallback → t02 data_collator resize not compared → t04 crop_to_patches unknown).

**Fix.** Root cause documented as rule 15 in `rule_of_tune.md`: before any real training on a new framework/model pair, trace the source for actual tokens-per-image and measure it with a CPU-only probe (`probe_img_tokens.py`) before paying for a full run. The fix itself (adding `crop_to_patches: true` and retraining) was not applied — direction deferred to Makham.

**→ Rule.** Before paying for a full fine-tune on a new framework+model pair, run a CPU-only probe that prints the real tokens-per-image and the real pixel size the model sees, and eyeball a downscaled sample image yourself. If you cannot read it, the model cannot either.

<sub>`D:/00mk/steel project/training/Training/workmen's_diary/2026-08-30.md` · model-training-config</sub>

#### 🔴 CRITICAL · 2026-08-31 · t04 trained on 1-tile images because LLaMA-Factory and transformers default crop_to_patches oppositely

**What happened.** The whole t04 (InternVL3-78B) run produced valid JSON but 0% recall. Root cause traced this day: the model's preprocessor_config ships crop_to_patches:false, which LLaMA-Factory obeys at training time, while transformers' InternVLProcessorKwargs._defaults hardcodes True at inference. Every training image collapsed to one 256-token tile regardless of source megapixels.

**Root cause.** Two libraries in the same stack chose opposite defaults for the same field, and nobody verified the effective tiling value on a real training batch — the config was written from documentation, not from an observed token count.

**Impact.** An entire 4-GPU training round wasted (money + a full day), the resulting model had to be discarded, and the failure looked like a data/pipeline problem for days.

**Fix.** Set crop_to_patches: true in the LF yaml (LF >=0.9.3, PR #7817) and control tile count indirectly via image_max_pixels, since max_patches=12 is hardcoded in the plugin. Later verified live on the training machine at mm_plugin.py:843 that the flag really flips tiling to 13 tiles / 3,482 tokens.

**→ Rule.** Never trust a preprocessing default that two libraries can disagree on: before any paid training run, print the real per-image tile count and visual token count from an actual batch and assert it matches the intended resolution.

<sub>`D:/00mk/steel project/training/Training/workmen's_diary/2026-08-31.md` · config-bug</sub>

#### 🔴 CRITICAL · 2026-08-31 · LLaMA-Factory 4-bit quantization also quantized the vision tower, blinding InternViT-6B

**What happened.** A second, hidden defect under the tiling bug was found: InternVL's own docs warn that BNB 4-bit on InternViT-6B produces nonsensical outputs and fails to understand images, and LF's quantization_bit:4 quantizes the whole model with no modules_to_not_convert exclusion for the ViT.

**Root cause.** The quantization config was applied model-wide without checking whether the vision encoder tolerates 4-bit; the vendor's own warning existed but was not read before committing the arm.

**Impact.** The entire Voldemort (InternVL3-78B) arm was unusable and had to be amputated after the model proved totally blind, even after the crop_to_patches fix was correct.

**Fix.** Verified from quantization.py source that no ViT exclusion exists; killed the arm after a ~$2 go/no-go gate and reallocated the 2 GPUs to Courser k-fold instead of burning a full training run.

**→ Rule.** Before quantizing a vision-language model, check the vendor's documented quantization limits for the vision tower specifically, and prove the base model can still read a real page at that precision before spending on a training run.

<sub>`D:/00mk/steel project/training/Training/workmen's_diary/2026-08-31.md` · model-config</sub>

#### 🔴 CRITICAL · 2026-08-31 · Greedy decoding produced 0% recall and a 16,363-character multilingual hallucination

**What happened.** The first real recall measurement of destrier scored 0/34. Page 26 returned elements: [] with confidence 1.0 and a flag claiming no footings were drawn, when six were clearly present. Page 27 spewed 16,363 characters over 18 minutes: leaked chain-of-thought despite thinking being disabled, an English synonym chain, a switch into Chinese at the phrase 'losing getting lost' -> 迷路, then Chinese idiom chains, a motivational passage, a self-written disclaimer, and a final attempt to resume JSON before running out of tokens.

**Root cause.** do_sample=False had been used throughout, but Qwen explicitly documents 'DO NOT use greedy decoding' as it causes endless repetitions. This was compounded by repetition_penalty=1.15 and no_repeat_ngram_size=8, which punish the naturally repetitive content of construction drawings, forcing the model to escape into unrelated vocabulary.

**Impact.** A full evaluation round scored 0% and appeared to prove the model could not read at all; 18 minutes of paid GPU per page wasted.

**Fix.** One-line change to serve_purson.py: do_sample=True, temperature=0.7, top_p=0.8, top_k=20, removing repetition_penalty and no_repeat_ngram_size. Recall went 0% -> 11.8% strict / 43.5% position+mark_base, and the Chinese output disappeared entirely.

**→ Rule.** Read and apply the model vendor's published generation settings before running any evaluation, and never apply repetition penalties to domain content that is legitimately repetitive.

<sub>`D:/00mk/steel project/training/Training/workmen's_diary/2026-08-31.md` · model-config</sub>

#### 🔴 CRITICAL · 2026-09-01 · t04 (Purson) trained with images silently downscaled to 448×448 because crop_to_patches was never set

**What happened.** The t04 fine-tune finished and scored 0% read accuracy on plan_beam and plan_footing. The config file was missing the line `crop_to_patches: true`, so instead of tiling each drawing into patches the loader shrank the whole A1 sheet into a single 448×448 image. Measured from the training log: 768 tokens for 3 images = exactly 256 tokens per image, where a real construction drawing needs thousands.

**Root cause.** The image-tiling behaviour was opt-in via a config flag the team did not know existed, and the library emitted no warning or error when it was off. Nothing in the pipeline asserted a minimum tokens-per-image, so an invisible default silently destroyed every training sample.

**Impact.** A full training run wasted — several thousand baht of GPU spend — plus the eval cycle on top of it. plan_beam and plan_footing recall both 0%. The model was dead on arrival and this was only discovered after paying.

**Fix.** Root cause traced three independent ways (token count from the log, reading mm_plugin.py source, and manually downscaling a real beam plan to 448×448 and confirming it is unreadable). New standing rule added as rule_of_tune.md #15: before every real training run, measure tokens-per-image first — this runs on CPU, costs nothing, and needs no GPU.

**→ Rule.** Before spending money on any fine-tune, measure and assert the actual tokens-per-image the loader produces on a real sample. Never trust a vision pipeline's default image handling; a silently downscaled image produces no error and no clue, only garbage results after you have already paid.

<sub>`D:/00mk/steel project/training/Training/workmen's_diary/สอนมะขาม_ทำไม_Purson_กับ_Voldemort_พัง_2026-09-01.md` · training-config</sub>

#### 🔴 CRITICAL · 2026-09-01 · t44 (Voldemort) 4-bit quantization was applied to the vision encoder too, against an explicit vendor warning

**What happened.** To fit InternVL3-78B on the GPU, 4-bit quantization was applied across the whole model — including the InternViT-6B vision tower. InternVL's official documentation warns verbatim that quantizing the vision encoder will 'produce nonsensical outputs and fail to understand images'. The model then described a Thai footing plan as a round document with a pink background and Facebook/Apple/Barbie logos saying 'Happy Birthday', and a beam plan as a Star Wars BB-8 logo.

**Root cause.** Quantization was applied model-wide as a memory-fitting operation without reading the model's own documentation about which submodules must stay in full precision. The vision tower was treated as just more weights rather than as the component whose fidelity the entire task depends on.

**Impact.** The model was completely blind. Caught at the $2 gate before full training, so the direct loss was small — but the branch itself (model selection, setup, rental) was wasted effort.

**Fix.** Stopped immediately after the gate failed 0/3. Model branch abandoned.

**→ Rule.** Read the model vendor's own quantization guidance before quantizing anything, and never quantize a vision encoder in a vision task. When memory-fitting, quantize selectively and record which submodules stayed in full precision.

<sub>`D:/00mk/steel project/training/Training/workmen's_diary/สอนมะขาม_ทำไม_Purson_กับ_Voldemort_พัง_2026-09-01.md` · model-config</sub>

#### 🔴 CRITICAL · 2026-09-02 · Server had its own 25-minute generation timeout that was never updated when the client's was raised, truncating JSON mid-answer

**What happened.** Job f63bc71e finished 9/9 but 3 pages produced broken JSON (page_03_notes, page_12_plan_footing, page_13_notes). The real cause was that `serve_purson.py` holds its own `PAGE_TIMEOUT_S = 25*60`, entirely separate from `worker.py`'s client timeout which had been raised to 2700s the previous day. The server-side one is enforced as a `StoppingCriteria` that cuts generation mid-stream with no regard for whether the JSON is complete.

**Root cause.** Two independent timeout definitions for the same operation, in two files, with only one of them updated. Worse, the server's mechanism truncates output silently rather than raising an error — so a cut answer looks like a model formatting failure rather than a timeout.

**Impact.** 3 pages of a paid GPU run destroyed; then a full re-run of the whole house (job 43323920). Wasted a complete GPU cycle plus debugging time chasing a suspected model problem.

**Fix.** Raised the server timeout to `40*60` (2400s, deliberately below the client's 2700s so the client is never the one to give up first), restarted the server, resubmitted the house reusing the stored image paths rather than re-uploading.

**→ Rule.** A timeout must be defined once. If client and server both need one, derive them from a single source and assert server < client. And any timeout that truncates output rather than erroring must stamp a 'was truncated' marker so the failure is not misattributed to the model.

<sub>`2026-09-02.md` · config-drift</sub>

#### 🟠 HIGH · 2026-07-02 · GPU rental template documented an instance, a model and an approval process that none matched what actually happened

**What happened.** No_touch_box/vast-template/ (README.md + onstart.sh) specified an RTX 3090 24GB instance defaulting to Qwen3-VL-8B-Instruct, deferring the real model choice to 'King's sign-off'. The actual fine-tuning (t01/t02) was run by Makham and Claude directly on a rented RTX PRO 6000 96GB, landing on Qwen3.6-35B-A3B.

**Root cause.** Infrastructure and process were written up in advance of doing the work, then the work was done differently and the template was never updated or retired. It described an intended future rather than an observed reality, and nothing tied it to an actual run.

**Impact.** A runnable-looking template pointing at the wrong GPU class and the wrong model sat in the repo for a month. Anyone provisioning from it would have rented a 24GB card for a model that needed far more, burning rental money on an instance that cannot run the job. The 'King's sign-off' step also described an approval chain that was not being followed.

**Fix.** Archived on 2026-08-04 to wait_for_ทิ้ง/No_touch_box/vast-template/ and flagged in ARCHIVE.md as safe to delete for real, since nothing in the repo still follows that process.

**→ Rule.** Never leave a provisioning template in the repo that has not been used for a real run. Update it from the run that actually happened, or delete it — a stale infra template is an invitation to rent the wrong hardware and pay for it.

<sub>`D:/00mk/steel project/training/Training/workmen's_diary/2026-07-02.md` · infra-drift / money-risk</sub>

#### 🟠 HIGH · 2026-07-05 · Schema definitions scattered across 5 places, with dead factories and 3 mismatched pricing enum vocabularies

**What happened.** The Data Schema / Data Flow review found: schema definitions spread across 5 different places, v2 factories in schema.js that are dead code, site/foundation/BBS-manual declaring their own object shapes outside schema.js, and 3 mismatched pricing enum sets.

**Root cause.** schema.js was nominally the single source of truth, but nothing enforced it — feature modules could construct entity objects ad hoc, and there was no rule that a shape must come from a create* factory. Over time each module grew its own definition of the same concept.

**Impact.** Three different vocabularies for the same price-source concept means any consumer comparing them gets wrong answers; dead v2 factories mislead anyone reading schema.js about which shape is current; and shapes declared outside schema.js can never be validated centrally.

**Fix.** Documented in docs/DATA_SCHEMA_REVIEW.md with a 4-phase plan. Only Phase A was completed on this day; the factories and the canonical enum were left to Phases B-D.

**→ Rule.** A 'single source of truth' that is only a convention is not one. Enforce it: never construct an entity object ad hoc, always through a create* factory, and add a test that fails when a shape is declared outside the schema module.

<sub>`D:/00mk/steel project/training/Training/workmen's_diary/2026-07-05.md` · architecture-drift</sub>

#### 🟠 HIGH · 2026-07-05 · Site, Foundation and Planner communicated by reading each other's localStorage keys directly, outside any contract

**What happened.** The schema review found an informal Site → Foundation → Planner data flow in which modules read each other's localStorage keys directly, bypassing schema.js and the PIPELINE_EVENT mechanism that the rest of the app uses.

**Root cause.** No explicit cross-module contract existed for this chain, so the fastest path to the data — reading the neighbour's storage key — became the actual integration mechanism. The formal path (factories plus events) only covered the pipeline chain.

**Impact.** Any rename of a storage key or change of shape in Site silently breaks Foundation and Planner with no compile-time or test-time signal, and no event fires so consumers cannot know when the data changed.

**Fix.** Documented; the explicit Site → Foundation → Planner contract (createSiteInvestigation() / createFoundationDesign() factories plus getters and events) was scheduled as the first item of Phase B, not done on this day.

**→ Rule.** Cross-module data must move through named getters/setters and an event, never by one module reading another's storage key. If a shortcut integration exists, write the contract for it before it acquires a third consumer.

<sub>`D:/00mk/steel project/training/Training/workmen's_diary/2026-07-05.md` · architecture-drift</sub>

#### 🟠 HIGH · 2026-07-06 · The whole existing Label Studio review flow was hard-wired to the Gen 1 schema and could not read Gen 3 data at all

**What happened.** Both existing Label Studio variants (the whole-JSON-per-house 'Constistant01' and King's per-page Repeater 'Structural Review'/'BOQ Review') were tied to the Gen 1 schema — flat plan[]/section[]/schedule[] or categories[].items[] — and read from qwen-output/. Neither supported Gen 3's nested main_bar{}/stirrup{}, the new pattern types, or files already split one-per-pattern/view.

**Root cause.** The review tooling was built against a specific schema shape with the shape assumptions embedded in both the task generator and the XML configs, and it was not revisited across three schema generations. The schema evolved on one track and the tooling on none.

**Impact.** A complete rewrite of the review tooling was required in the middle of an extraction push: a new task generator plus three new XML configs, then five more rounds of fixes the same day. All Gen 3 data was unreviewable until this was done.

**Fix.** Wrote label-studio-tasks-makham.js plus label-studio-makham-elements.xml, -material_list.xml and -single.xml, grouping files by their actual structure rather than by pattern name.

**→ Rule.** Review/QA tooling is part of the schema, not downstream of it. When a schema generation is designed, budget the tooling update in the same plan — otherwise data accumulates faster than it can be verified and the review step becomes the bottleneck at the worst moment.

<sub>`D:/00mk/steel project/training/Training/workmen's_diary/2026-07-06.md` · tooling-drift</sub>

#### 🟠 HIGH · 2026-07-21 · LORA_R=64 chosen without accounting for 256 MoE experts (and for a 226-example dataset)

**What happened.** LoRA rank 64 / alpha 128 was configured up front; on this MoE model the per-expert LoRA buffers multiply by 256 and blew past 95GB VRAM. Reducing to 32/64 fixed the OOM — and prior research already said a low rank suits a 226-example dataset better.

**Root cause.** Rank was picked as a generic default without multiplying the memory cost by the model's expert count, and without applying the dataset-size guidance the team had already recorded on 2026-07-20.

**Impact.** Four TEST_STEPS rehearsal rounds and multiple OOM crashes on a $1.056/hr machine before the real fix; the original setting was arguably also worse for quality (overfitting/catastrophic-forgetting risk).

**Fix.** LORA_R 64→32, LORA_ALPHA 128→64 (same ratio), decided by Makham after being shown three options per rule_of_tune.md rule 2.

**→ Rule.** For MoE models, size LoRA rank against experts×rank memory, and cross-check the rank against dataset size before the first paid run — research you already wrote down counts as a constraint, not a footnote.

<sub>`D:/00mk/steel project/training/Training/workmen's_diary/2026-07-21.md` · config-bug</sub>

#### 🟠 HIGH · 2026-07-24 · Vast.ai's default 150GB disk would have reproduced the previous round's disk-full failures if left alone

**What happened.** A screenshot of the Vast.ai rental page revealed the Container Size / Disk slider defaults to 150GB. The known requirement, learned from the 2026-07-21 round's repeated disk-full failures, is at least 300GB. Clicking Rent with the default would have hit the identical failure immediately.

**Root cause.** A vendor default silently disagreed with a hard requirement the team had already learned the hard way, and that requirement lived only in a prior diary entry — not in any pre-rental check or the rental procedure itself.

**Impact.** Caught before renting, so zero cost this round — but the same default had already caused multiple disk-full failures during the 2026-07-21 round.

**Fix.** Added to Phase 0.2 as an explicit item, and later hardened in verify_env.py as a check that fails when the whole volume is under 280GB ('forgot to drag the slider').

**→ Rule.** Every vendor default that has ever bitten you must become an automated assertion, not a note to remember. Write the check into the environment verifier, not into a document.

<sub>`D:/00mk/steel project/training/Training/workmen's_diary/2026-07-24(teach mk).md` · infra/config</sub>

#### 🟠 HIGH · 2026-07-28 · Training crashed immediately on library drift: ip.max_pixels is no longer settable in transformers 5.5.0

**What happened.** On the first real t02 run, the script died at once with AttributeError: property of 'Qwen2VLImageProcessor' object has no setter. The code set image resolution via ip.max_pixels, which the library's newer version made read-only.

**Root cause.** train_qwen3vl.py had been written months earlier and never executed. pip installed a newer transformers on the fresh rented box; the library's API moved while the code sat idle. No version pin existed.

**Impact.** Failure occurred after the meter had started, on the very first paid step of the run.

**Fix.** Read the library's actual source (not guessed) and switched to ip.size["longest_edge"], deleting the old path entirely.

**→ Rule.** Code that has never been executed is untested code, regardless of age. Either pin library versions in the environment spec, or smoke-run every script end-to-end locally before renting hardware.

<sub>`D:/00mk/steel project/training/Training/workmen's_diary/สอนมะขาม_รวม.md` · dependency-drift</sub>

#### 🟠 HIGH · 2026-07-28 · onstart.sh pip-installs every library unpinned — the actual root cause of the version drift was never fixed

**What happened.** The Vast.ai on-start script installs triton, unsloth, trl, peft, accelerate, bitsandbytes and pillow via plain pip with no version pins. That is precisely the mechanism that installed transformers 5.5.0 on 2026-07-28 and crashed training at startup. The fix applied was to the calling code (use ip.size['longest_edge']), not to the install step.

**Root cause.** Every rental provisions a fresh, unpinned environment, so each new instance can silently differ from the one the scripts were last tested against; nobody added a lockfile or version pins after the drift bug.

**Impact.** Guarantees the same class of failure will recur on the next rental, and it recurs at the worst moment — right after the money starts being spent. It also means no two rentals are strictly comparable, which is the same doubt that forced the unplanned Phase 7.5 re-measurement.

**Fix.** Not fixed — onstart.sh is still documented in Appendix A as installing unpinned packages.

**→ Rule.** Pin every library version (or ship a lockfile) in the provisioning script; an unpinned environment on a rented machine turns a free, local, reproducible setup into a paid lottery.

<sub>`D:/00mk/steel project/training/Training/workmen's_diary/สอนมะขาม_รวม.md` · infra-config</sub>

#### 🟠 HIGH · 2026-08-24 · Two training variables silently drifted out of control between t01/t02 and t03

**What happened.** A parity table run before renting (rule_of_tune #12) found `PYTORCH_ALLOC_CONF=expandable_segments` had disappeared from t03 (t01 had it, added after an OOM that was 100MB short) and `FINETUNE_VISION` had been hardcoded in t03 where t01/t02 had it as an env var.

**Root cause.** train_t03.py was written fresh rather than copied, so hard-won environment fixes from prior rounds were not carried forward. There is no machine-checked contract between rounds — only the manual parity table.

**Impact.** Would have reproduced a known OOM (the exact one expandable_segments was added to fix) and made an A/B variable un-togglable at runtime. Caught before rental, so cost was zero.

**Fix.** Restored both, with defaults byte-identical to the previous rounds.

**→ Rule.** The parity table before renting is not optional. Every value in a fresh training script must be diffed call-site-by-call-site against the last working round, especially environment variables added to fix a past failure.

<sub>`D:/00mk/steel project/training/Training/workmen's_diary/2026-08-24.md` · config-drift</sub>

#### 🟠 HIGH · 2026-08-25 · Historical: t01 set MAX_PIXELS to 512px, blurring every image and invalidating the whole round's results

**What happened.** In training round t01, MAX_PIXELS was misconfigured so images were shrunk to 512px — extremely blurry. The entire round's evaluation numbers were therefore measured on garbage input.

**Root cause.** A resolution parameter was set without validating what the model actually received; no visual sanity check of a rendered training sample was performed before the run.

**Impact.** A full training round's results were invalid and had to be discarded; recorded as lesson #12 in rule_of_tune.md — and the same class of error recurred on 2026-08-25.

**Fix.** Documented as rule_of_tune.md lesson 12. The 2026-08-25 measurement pass is the systematic fix that should prevent a third occurrence.

**→ Rule.** Before any training run, dump one preprocessed image exactly as the model will receive it and look at it with your eyes. A blurry sample invalidates every number the run produces.

<sub>`D:/00mk/steel project/training/Training/workmen's_diary/2026-08-25(teach mk).md` · config</sub>

#### 🟠 HIGH · 2026-08-25 · t03 OOM'd twice from raising numbers without sizing first, forcing a LoRA rank cut

**What happened.** In the previous round, MAX_LENGTH was raised to 32,768 without a VRAM sizing pass. It OOM'd, forcing LoRA rank down 32→16, and even then the eval step OOM'd again from fp32 logit upcasting at that same length. Last round OOM'd with only 470 MiB free.

**Root cause.** Configuration values were raised on intuition instead of being decomposed against measured VRAM. Also, the eval path's fp32 logit upcast was not accounted for in the sizing at all — only the training step was considered.

**Impact.** Two failed GPU runs (rental time burned), a forced reduction in LoRA capacity (r 32→16) that degraded the round's ceiling, and a lost eval.

**Fix.** This session decomposed peak VRAM from the one real measurement available (87.5 GB @ seq 32,768, r=16): weights bf16 74.0 + LoRA/grad/optim 5.7 + activation 7.8, with only the activation term scaling with sequence length. Raised MAX_PIXELS 5120→7680 / MAX_LENGTH 32768→47104 against that model instead of blind.

**→ Rule.** Never raise a memory-bound constant without a decomposition of where the memory actually goes and which terms scale. Size on paper first, then confirm with a short TEST_STEPS run before committing to a full rental.

<sub>`D:/00mk/steel project/training/Training/workmen's_diary/2026-08-25.md` · config-blind-change</sub>

#### 🟠 HIGH · 2026-08-25 · Training MAX_PIXELS raised to 7680 while the inference script still sits at 5120 — a train/eval mismatch waiting to happen

**What happened.** train_t03.py was raised to MAX_PIXELS=7680, but `infer_house_t03.py` was deliberately left at 5120 to match the existing t03 adapter. It must be moved to 7680 before evaluating t03b, or the next round will be evaluated at a different resolution than it was trained at.

**Root cause.** A resolution constant is duplicated across the training script and the inference script with no shared source, so raising one silently desynchronizes them.

**Impact.** If missed, t03b would be evaluated at the wrong input resolution, producing numbers that measure the mismatch rather than the model — and the mismatch would look like a model regression.

**Fix.** Not fixed — a loud in-file comment was left on the infer script's MAX_PIXELS, plus an entry in the end-of-day mandatory-gate list for the next round.

**→ Rule.** Constants that must match between training and inference belong in one shared config, not duplicated in two scripts. A comment is a reminder, not a guarantee — the durable fix is a single source both scripts import.

<sub>`D:/00mk/steel project/training/Training/workmen's_diary/2026-08-25.md` · config-duplication</sub>

#### 🟠 HIGH · 2026-08-25 · Gridline training labels were being silently truncated mid-JSON at MAX_LENGTH=24,576 through the t01/t02 rounds

**What happened.** MAX_LENGTH was 24,576 in t01/t02. Gridline examples use 4 images and measure ~26,791 tokens, so their JSON answers were cut off mid-object during training. It was only found and raised to 32,768 in the t03 round; the earlier rounds trained on truncated labels. The same failure class is named again later in the day as the reason you must never lower MAX_LENGTH alone without lowering MAX_PIXELS ("t01 §0.4 bug class").

**Root cause.** Sequence length was set as a round number rather than measured against the longest real example in the dataset; nothing asserted that a label fit inside the budget, so truncation produced a plausible-looking run instead of an error.

**Impact.** Two whole tuning rounds (t01, t02) trained the gridline subtask on labels whose JSON was cut off — unknown but non-zero degradation of gridline accuracy, and any gridline metric from those rounds is untrustworthy.

**Fix.** MAX_LENGTH raised 24,576 → 32,768 in t03, then → 47,104 later this day; the fallback order written into train_t03.py explicitly forbids lowering MAX_LENGTH alone.

**→ Rule.** Measure the longest real example's token count before setting a sequence-length cap, and assert on it — a truncated label never raises an error, it just teaches the model garbage.

<sub>`D:/00mk/steel project/training/Training/workmen's_diary/2026-08-25.md` · training-config</sub>

#### 🟠 HIGH · 2026-08-29 · MAX_PIXELS differed between training (7680) and inference (5120)

**What happened.** Inference was running at MAX_PIXELS 5120 while training used 7680 — the two were fixed to match only on 2026-08-29, and then the model change made the fix moot for t04.

**Root cause.** Train and infer scripts each carry their own copy of image-preprocessing constants with no shared source, so they drift whenever one is tuned.

**Impact.** Inference was feeding the model images at a different effective resolution than it was trained on — a silent quality degradation invisible in any metric that doesn't isolate it.

**Fix.** Set infer MAX_PIXELS to 7680 to match train, alongside OUT_DIR/out-root renames outputs_t03→t04.

**→ Rule.** Image preprocessing constants must live in one shared module imported by both train and infer. Any value that must match across scripts should not exist in two places.

<sub>`D:/00mk/steel project/training/Training/workmen's_diary/2026-08-29.md` · config-drift</sub>

#### 🟠 HIGH · 2026-08-30 · Decoder settings inherited from t03/Qwen forbade the repeated answers the ground truth actually requires

**What happened.** The eval decoder carried `no_repeat_ngram_size=8` and `repetition_penalty=1.15` inherited from the t03/Qwen era. Real GT for construction drawings legitimately repeats marks many times (B2×10, RB1×24), so these settings actively suppressed correct output. Proven in isolation with a fixtest: removing them raised extracted elements from 0 to 10 (though recall stayed 0% because of the separate crop_to_patches root cause).

**Root cause.** Generation hyperparameters were copied forward between model generations without re-asking whether the output distribution had changed. Anti-repetition penalties are a text-generation heuristic that is simply wrong for structured extraction where duplicates are semantically required.

**Impact.** Compounded the recall failure and would have masked or distorted any future measurement; on its own it zeroed out element extraction.

**Fix.** Carried directly into t05: removed `no_repeat_ngram_size=8` and lowered `repetition_penalty` from 1.15 to 1.0.

**→ Rule.** Never inherit decoder/generation hyperparameters across a model or task change without justifying each one against the target output format — anti-repetition penalties must be off for structured extraction whose ground truth repeats.

<sub>`D:/00mk/steel project/training/Training/workmen's_diary/2026-08-30.md` · model-training-config</sub>

#### 🟠 HIGH · 2026-08-30 · AutoProcessor gave the model 13 image tiles at inference vs 1 tile at training — a 13× preprocessing mismatch

**What happened.** During the recall investigation it emerged that at inference time AutoProcessor tiled each image into 13 tiles, while training (missing `crop_to_patches`) produced exactly 1 tile per image.

**Root cause.** Training used LLaMA-Factory's mm_plugin path with tiling disabled, while inference used the plain HF AutoProcessor default with tiling enabled — two different preprocessing stacks were never compared against each other.

**Impact.** Even after any other fix, the model was being shown inputs in a form it had never been trained on, guaranteeing degraded output.

**Fix.** Documented as a compounding factor in the root-cause report; the structural fix (make preprocessing identical on both sides) rolls into the t05 probe rule.

**→ Rule.** Assert that the exact tensor shape / token count the model receives at inference equals what it received at training — print and compare both, don't assume two libraries agree.

<sub>`D:/00mk/steel project/training/Training/workmen's_diary/2026-08-30.md` · model-training-config</sub>

#### 🟠 HIGH · 2026-08-31 · Three hyperparameters silently differed between arms because the yaml omitted them and took library defaults

**What happened.** A parity check found weight_decay (0.01 vs HF default 0.0), optim (adamw_8bit vs default adamw_torch) and lora_dropout differed between the two arms because the yaml simply did not write them and inherited silent defaults. The same optim gap existed in t04 and nobody had noticed.

**Root cause.** Parity was assumed from the values that were written, without enumerating the values that were omitted and resolving each library's default.

**Impact.** The two arms were not actually comparable; the same gap had already corrupted t04's comparability unnoticed.

**Fix.** Wrote all three explicitly into both fold yamls and confirmed they parse.

**→ Rule.** When comparing two training stacks, enumerate every hyperparameter each framework can default silently and write it explicitly on both sides — omission is a difference, not a match.

<sub>`D:/00mk/steel project/training/Training/workmen's_diary/2026-08-31.md` · config-bug</sub>

**What happened.** Model loading failed because transformers 4.57.6 does not recognise qwen3_5_moe.

<sub>`D:/00mk/steel project/training/Training/workmen's_diary/2026-08-31.md` · dependency</sub>

#### 🟠 HIGH · 2026-08-31 · unsloth pulled a cu130 torch build onto a CUDA 12.8 image, breaking JIT kernel compilation mid-training

**What happened.** Training crashed during JIT kernel compilation because nvrtc could not find libnvrtc-builtins.so.13.0 — the file existed but was not on the library path, since unsloth had installed a torch cu130 wheel on a CUDA 12.8 image.

**Root cause.** Package manager resolved a CUDA build mismatched to the base image, and the failure only surfaces during in-training JIT compilation, not at import.

**Impact.** A crash that only appears once training is under way, i.e. after money has already been spent starting the run.

**Fix.** Pointed LD_LIBRARY_PATH at nvidia/cu13/lib instead of downgrading torch.

**→ Rule.** After installing an ML stack on a rented box, assert the torch CUDA build matches the image's CUDA version, and force at least one JIT-compiling step in the dry-run so this class of failure surfaces before the real run.

<sub>`D:/00mk/steel project/training/Training/workmen's_diary/2026-08-31.md` · dependency</sub>

#### 🟠 HIGH · 2026-08-31 · Two instances rented two hours apart installed different peft versions, factorizing MoE layers transposed

**What happened.** During the merge, fold0's MoE-layer LoRA factors were oriented the opposite way from fold2/3 because gpu1 had peft 0.18.1 while the later machines got 0.20.0 — the rentals were two hours apart and unpinned.

**Root cause.** No version pin on a library that decides an on-disk weight format; unpinned installs drift between machines rented minutes apart.

**Impact.** Adapters were silently incompatible for averaging; required writing a permutation converter and proving max|ΔW_old − ΔW_newᵀ| = 0.00e+00.

**Fix.** Wrote the permute converter, merged successfully, and recorded rule_of_tune Lesson 18: pin every library that writes a format.

**→ Rule.** Pin the exact version of any library that determines an artifact's on-disk layout, and pin it identically across every machine in a parallel run.

<sub>`D:/00mk/steel project/training/Training/workmen's_diary/2026-08-31.md` · dependency</sub>

#### 🟠 HIGH · 2026-08-31 · Loading the merged adapter with the older peft would produce silent garbage

**What happened.** The merged destrier adapter follows peft 0.20 conventions; the machine's existing peft 0.18.1 would load it into silent garbage rather than erroring.

**Root cause.** Format convention differences between peft versions fail silently rather than raising.

**Impact.** Any evaluation run on the wrong peft version would produce meaningless numbers that look valid.

**Fix.** Created a dedicated venv with peft 0.20 for the smoke test.

**→ Rule.** Pin and verify the exact library version an artifact was produced with before evaluating it — a version mismatch that loads silently is worse than one that crashes.

<sub>`D:/00mk/steel project/training/Training/workmen's_diary/2026-08-31.md` · dependency</sub>

#### 🟠 HIGH · 2026-08-31 · GPU-A produced zero output for ~$2.4 because its worker used a vanilla PeftModel with no generation guards

**What happened.** GPU-A's worker_page_raw_pratyad.py used vanilla AutoModelForImageTextToText + PeftModel — very slow on a 256-expert MoE LoRA — and set no repetition_penalty or no_repeat_ngram_size, unlike serve_purson.py. Pages 09 and 10 timed out at 25 minutes on both the normal and xgrammar attempts, producing no output at all.

**Root cause.** Two divergent inference code paths in the same project, one of which never received the accumulated configuration knowledge from the other.

**Impact.** ~$2.4 and ~2 hours of a rented GPU for zero results.

**Fix.** Instead of renting more, wrote pure_power_endpoint.py to fire raw-power prompts at GPU-B's already-running endpoint, getting comparable results in 133-364s per page instead of 25+ minutes.

<sub>`D:/00mk/steel project/training/Training/workmen's_diary/2026-08-31.md` · config-bug</sub>

#### 🟠 HIGH · 2026-08-31 · The launcher menu started the wrong model because it inherited another file's default adapter

**What happened.** Pressing menu option 1 started the server with --adapter Sicilian44/t03, an old model, because go.py called `up` without arguments and picked up presentation.py's default. Makham caught it.

**Root cause.** Relying on another module's default value instead of passing the parameter explicitly.

**Impact.** A rented card was launched with the wrong model (instance 49410094), caught and swapped in time.

**Fix.** Renamed the preset to destrier after the real adapter, made the menu always ask which model, always pass --model explicitly rather than relying on any other file's default, and display the currently loaded model at all times.

**→ Rule.** Never let a launcher inherit a default from another file for a value that determines what is being run — pass it explicitly and display it in the UI.

<sub>`D:/00mk/steel project/training/Training/workmen's_diary/2026-08-31.md` · config-bug</sub>

#### 🟠 HIGH · 2026-08-31 · repetition_penalty and no_repeat_ngram_size — added as a safeguard — were themselves wrong for construction drawings

**What happened.** serve_purson.py ran with repetition_penalty=1.15 and no_repeat_ngram_size=8. Construction drawings are naturally repetitive (F7,C1 / F7,C1, repeated grid refs), so the model was penalised for producing the correct repeated content and was pushed to invent new words instead — feeding the runaway output.

**Root cause.** Generic anti-repetition settings were copied in without asking whether the domain's correct output is repetitive; a known Qwen3-VL issue (#1611) documents exactly this.

**Impact.** Combined with greedy decoding, produced 0% recall and the 16,363-character multilingual runaway; both were removed to reach 11.8% strict / 43.5% position recall.

**Fix.** removed both, switched to Qwen's recommended sampling (temperature 0.7 / top_p 0.8 / top_k 20)

**→ Rule.** An anti-degeneracy knob is domain-specific: if the correct answer repeats by nature, penalising repetition is a bug, not a safeguard.

<sub>`D:/00mk/steel project/training/Training/workmen's_diary/2026-08-31.md` · model-config</sub>

#### 🟠 HIGH · 2026-09-01 · pass3 anchored on `cv_mark`, a field the model answers only 9% of the time

**What happened.** pass3 required elements carrying `cv_mark` to form anchors. Destrier only saw `cv_mark` in 92 of 1034 training examples (9%), so in practice the model almost never emits it — producing 0 anchors on every page and no measurement at all.

**Root cause.** The design picked an anchor key without checking its frequency in the actual training data. A dependency on a model output was chosen from the schema, not from measured model behaviour.

**Impact.** pass3 would produce zero measurements on real runs despite the fit logic being correct.

**Fix.** Added a fallback `anchors_by_shape()`: match 'points the model gave a grid_ref' to 'points CV saw' by spatial distribution shape (normalise both sets into [0,1], mutual nearest neighbour). Safe because a wrong pairing spikes the residual and `build_transform` rejects it itself.

**→ Rule.** Before depending on any model-emitted field, measure how often it actually appears in the training data. Model-optional fields need a fallback path, and the fallback should be self-checking (a bad match must fail loudly, not produce a plausible wrong number).

<sub>`2026-09-01.md` · model-dependency</sub>

#### 🟠 HIGH · 2026-09-01 · BOQ export used document.createElement for HTML escaping — unrunnable outside a browser and missing quote escaping

**What happened.** `boq-export-variants.js` implemented `escapeHtml` via `document.createElement`, so none of the 4 export variants could run outside a browser (no tests possible, no server-side document generation). It also never escaped `"` or `'`, because `textContent` doesn't — an injection hole if the output is placed in an HTML attribute.

**Root cause.** Borrowing the DOM as an escaping utility couples pure string logic to a browser runtime, and inherits `textContent`'s escaping semantics (which cover text context only, not attribute context). The same attribute-escaping class of bug had already been fixed elsewhere in the codebase (`escAttr` in planner) but was not applied here.

**Impact.** Blocked all automated testing of exports and any server-side generation; latent XSS/attribute-breakout vector in exported documents.

**Fix.** Replaced with pure string-replacement escaping and added `"` and `'` to the escaped set.

**→ Rule.** Escaping must be a pure string function, never DOM-based — and it must cover attribute context (`"` and `'`), not just text context. When one instance of a bug class is fixed, grep for every other implementation of the same helper.

<sub>`2026-09-01.md` · security/portability</sub>

#### 🟡 MEDIUM · 2026-07-01 · Documentation for a dead pipeline generation stayed in the repo for a month after being superseded

**What happened.** No_touch_box/QUICKSTART.md and No_touch_box/raw/README.md both documented the pdf-processor.py → qwen-processor.js → review.html → annotated/ pipeline. That generation was superseded by run_pipeline.py + build_document_map.py, and the review/annotate step they describe is the pre-Label-Studio flow — with Label Studio itself cancelled on 2026-08-02. The docs were only archived on 2026-08-04.

**Root cause.** Replacing a pipeline was treated as done when the new code worked, without a step to retire the documentation for the old one. Nothing links a doc to the code path it describes, so no signal fires when that path dies.

**Impact.** A quickstart guide describing a non-existent workflow sat in the repo for a month. It is the first document a new contributor would open, and it would have walked them through a pipeline that no longer exists — including a review step for a tool that had since been cancelled.

**Fix.** Archived on 2026-08-04 to wait_for_ทิ้ง/ rather than deleted, and flagged in No_touch_box/docs/ARCHIVE.md as safe to delete for real with confirmation.

**→ Rule.** When a pipeline is replaced, retire its documentation in the same change — especially the quickstart, which is exactly what a newcomer reads first. Docs are recoverable from git history, so delete or archive without hesitation rather than leaving a misleading guide in place.

<sub>`D:/00mk/steel project/training/Training/workmen's_diary/2026-07-01.md` · documentation-drift</sub>

#### 🟡 MEDIUM · 2026-07-06 · Generated Label Studio task image URLs point at raw.githubusercontent, so images cannot load until the repo is pushed

**What happened.** The generated task JSON emits image URLs of the form raw.githubusercontent.com/.../image/<house>/<house>_หน้าNN.png against the Training repo main branch. The repo has to be pushed to GitHub before those images will load in Label Studio; that push had not happened.

**Root cause.** The review pipeline has a hard external dependency on a pushed public repo state, inherited from the pre-existing flow, and nothing in the task-generation step verifies that the referenced URLs actually resolve.

**Impact.** A reviewer opening the project would see broken images and no drawing to review against — the tasks would be present but useless. This blocker sat behind the already-blocked import step.

**Fix.** Not fixed — recorded as a precaution that the repo must be pushed first, same as the existing flow.

**→ Rule.** When a generator emits external URLs, have it verify at least one of them resolves before declaring success. A silent dependency on 'someone pushed the repo' will be discovered by the reviewer, not by the author.

<sub>`D:/00mk/steel project/training/Training/workmen's_diary/2026-07-06.md` · missing-dependency</sub>

#### 🟡 MEDIUM · 2026-07-06 · The work diary itself carried 4 stale file paths and an already-done item still listed as pending

**What happened.** When asked to update the work log, a review of the diary's own earlier entries found several stale paths — files recorded at mk_test/ when Makham had since moved everything into mk_test/t1/ — plus one pending item (redoing page 19 view2 beam plan) that had actually already been completed but was never struck through.

**Root cause.** Makham's reorganization of mk_test into t1/t2 was done outside the logging flow, and nothing swept the log for references to the old layout. Pending lists were appended to but never reconciled against what had actually been finished during the same session.

**Impact.** The log — the artifact specifically meant to be the reliable handoff record — pointed at paths that no longer existed and overstated the amount of outstanding work. Anyone resuming from it would have followed dead paths and redone finished work.

**Fix.** Annotated all 4 stale paths in place with ⚠️ notes (originals deliberately kept for historical accuracy) and struck through the completed pending item.

**→ Rule.** Any directory reorganization must be followed immediately by a grep of the logs and docs for the old paths. And close out the pending list at the end of every session — an unreconciled pending list is actively misleading, worse than none.

<sub>`D:/00mk/steel project/training/Training/workmen's_diary/2026-07-06.md` · documentation-drift</sub>

#### 🟡 MEDIUM · 2026-07-06 · Only half the Label Studio round-trip was built — nothing existed to convert reviewed export back into annotated/*.json

**What happened.** A full day was spent building the outbound side (label-studio-tasks-makham.js plus five XML configs) so Gen 3 data could be reviewed. The inbound side — a label-studio-import-*.js converting a project export back into annotated/*.json — was never written and is recorded as 'doesn't exist yet, currently only the task-creation side exists', still open at end of day as pending item 8.

**Root cause.** Work was sequenced by what was immediately visible (getting tasks to display) rather than by the end-to-end goal (corrected data landing back in the dataset); the round-trip was never treated as one deliverable, so the half that produces actual value was deferred indefinitely.

**Impact.** Even if the review UI had worked that evening, any human corrections made in Label Studio would have had nowhere to go — the entire day's review infrastructure could not have produced a single corrected ground-truth file.

**Fix.** not fixed — listed as pending item 8 at end of day

**→ Rule.** Build the thinnest possible end-to-end path first (one task in, one correction out) before polishing the display side; a review tool whose output can't be ingested produces zero corrected data no matter how good it looks.

<sub>`D:/00mk/steel project/training/Training/workmen's_diary/2026-07-06.md` · incomplete-implementation</sub>

#### 🟡 MEDIUM · 2026-07-07 · The Constistant copy of label-studio-tasks.js was a known-broken version reading one shared qwen-output path instead of a per-house path

**What happened.** While deleting the 4 Label Studio files from the stale Constistant/No_touch_box/ duplicate, a diff showed label-studio-tasks.js was NOT identical to the Training copy: the Constistant side read `qwen-output/<house>-qwen.json` at a single path covering all houses, while the Training side had already been fixed to read `raw/image/<house>/qwen-output/<house>-qwen.json` split per house. No_touch_box/CLAUDE.md had already recorded this as a 'pointing at the wrong path' bug.

**Root cause.** A path bug was fixed in one repo only; the duplicate copy in the other repo kept the pre-fix version, and nobody diffed the two until a cleanup pass forced it. A single-path layout that can't distinguish houses was the original design defect.

**Impact.** For however long the duplicate existed, anyone opening the Constistant copy would have run a generator that mixes every house's qwen output into one file. Caught only incidentally during a folder cleanup, not by any test.

**Fix.** Deleted the stale Constistant copy after confirming the Training side already carried the fix — no merge needed.

**→ Rule.** Before deleting a 'duplicate', diff every file. A file that differs is not a duplicate — it is either a lost fix or a resurrected bug, and you need to know which before pressing delete.

<sub>`D:/00mk/steel project/training/Training/workmen's_diary/2026-07-07.md` · duplicate-code-drift</sub>

#### 🟡 MEDIUM · 2026-07-07 · All 5 Label Studio configs shipped with the header fields as read-only text, so annotators could not correct house/page/sheet/pattern

**What happened.** The 5 existing config files (elements, elements-freezeR, single, single-freezeR, material_list) rendered the header block (house/page/sheet_code/sheet_name/pattern/view_title) as fully read-only `<Text>`. An annotator who spotted a wrong sheet code or a wrong pattern label had no way to fix it. Changed to `<TextArea editable="true" rows="1">`.

**Root cause.** The header was treated as display metadata rather than as data that the labeling pass is supposed to correct — the whole point of the human-in-the-loop step. A second trap sat under the fix: putting the label text and the value in one box would have leaked the prefix text into the saved value, so the label had to be split out from the editable field.

**Impact.** Every labeling session before this fix could only correct element bodies, never the page-level metadata. The prefix-leak trap would have silently corrupted every saved header value had the obvious one-box fix been used.

**Fix.** Changed all 5 XML configs to editable single-row TextAreas with the label rendered separately from the value; re-validated all files well-formed with no duplicate field names.

**→ Rule.** Any field the human reviewer might need to correct must be editable, not display-only. And when making a field editable, keep its label outside the input — a label baked into the box becomes part of the saved data.

#### 🟡 MEDIUM · 2026-07-21 · MAX_LENGTH set to 10,240 by estimate when stats.json said the real maximum was 8,890

**What happened.** MAX_LENGTH was set from a rough estimate ('instruction ~1,020 + image 5,120 + longest answer ~2,750 + margin'), leaving ~1,350 tokens of headroom no example could ever use; stats.json already contained the measured maximum (1,022 + 5,120 + 2,748 = 8,890).

**Root cause.** A configuration value that determined VRAM reservation was guessed even though a measured value from the dataset-prep step was already sitting in stats.json unread.

**Impact.** Unnecessary activation-memory reservation contributing to the OOM investigation; an extra fix/upload/test cycle on the paid GPU.

**Fix.** Reduced MAX_LENGTH 10,240 → 9,216 using the measured 8,890 plus a ~330-token special-token buffer.

**→ Rule.** Any capacity constant (sequence length, batch size, buffer size) must come from the measured dataset statistics you already produced — never from a mental estimate plus 'safety margin'.

**What happened.** The MAX_LENGTH fix was applied on a configuration where the previous run had left only ~100MB free out of 95GB VRAM at the old, smaller limit. The 5 multi-image examples now demand far more activation memory.

**Root cause.** Two constraints (label completeness vs VRAM) were traded off without re-measuring peak memory at the new limit before renting.

**Impact.** Open risk of OOM specifically on the grid-master batches; the correct remedy had to be pre-planned rather than improvised on paid time.

**Fix.** Documented in advance that if OOM hits there, the response is to lower LoRA rank or lower image resolution for those 5 examples — never to lower MAX_LENGTH back (which would re-truncate answers).

#### 🟡 MEDIUM · 2026-07-24 · The MAX_LENGTH fix knowingly pushes the run toward OOM, with only ~100MB of 95GB spare in the previous round

**What happened.** Raising MAX_LENGTH from 9,216 to 24,576 was accepted knowing it makes out-of-memory failures more likely on exactly those 5 gridmaster examples — the previous round had only ~100MB of 95GB VRAM left at the lower value.

**Root cause.** Correctness and memory headroom are in direct tension here, and the correct value was chosen without a proven mitigation path in place first.

**Impact.** An OOM crash mid-training on a paid instance would waste the run; the exposure was accepted rather than eliminated.

**Fix.** Documented an ordered escalation to use if OOM hits: shrink LoRA rank, or lower image resolution for just those 5 examples — explicitly never lower MAX_LENGTH back, since that restores answer truncation.

**→ Rule.** When accepting a known risk, write down the ordered remediation ladder in advance and name the one action that is forbidden, so the wrong fix isn't reached for under pressure.

#### 🟡 MEDIUM · 2026-07-28 · llama-server hung with 'non-consecutive token position' on the first inference run and had to be killed

**What happened.** The first attempt to run the tuned t01 model through llama-server hung without completing, producing a 'non-consecutive token position' error. The run had to be killed. The fix is to pass --parallel 1 --ubatch-size 2048.

**Root cause.** llama-server's default batching/parallelism settings are incompatible with this multimodal model's token layout, and the failure mode is a silent hang rather than an immediate error — so it consumed a full attempt before being recognised as a config problem.

**Impact.** A wasted inference run on a machine already saturated by a 21GB model; the failure looked like slowness rather than an error.

**Fix.** Always launch with --parallel 1 --ubatch-size 2048.

**→ Rule.** Record the exact required launch flags for every serving binary alongside the model, and treat a hang with no output as a configuration failure to investigate immediately, not as slow progress to wait out.

<sub>`D:/00mk/steel project/training/Training/workmen's_diary/2026-07-28.md` · tooling/config</sub>

#### 🟡 MEDIUM · 2026-07-28 · --ctx-size 8192 cut inference output off mid-sentence because prompt plus image plus answer needs 8,960 tokens

**What happened.** Inference output was being truncated mid-sentence. The arithmetic is explicit: 1,022 (prompt) + 5,120 (image) + 2,818 (answer) = 8,960, which exceeds the 8,192 context that had been set. Raised to 16,384.

**Root cause.** The context size was set without adding up the three real components. The image alone consumes 5,120 tokens — more than half the budget — and that had not been accounted for.

**Impact.** Truncated JSON output from inference; had this gone unnoticed the results would have been scored as model failures rather than a config limit.

**Fix.** --ctx-size raised to 16384.

**→ Rule.** Compute the context budget as prompt + image tokens + expected answer length before setting it, and treat mid-sentence truncation as a context-size symptom first, never as a model quality problem.
