**Root cause.** The enable_thinking flag suppresses the dedicated thinking channel but does not prevent the model from emitting reasoning text as ordinary output; the serving path assumed the flag was a hard guarantee and did no output validation.

**Impact.** Broke JSON parsing on that page and was one of the visible steps on the way to the 16k-character runaway.

**Fix.** not fixed directly — mitigated by switching to sampling and by sanitize_elements()/xgrammar plans

**→ Rule.** A config flag that turns off a channel is not a guarantee about content; validate the output shape rather than trusting the flag.

<sub>`D:/00mk/steel project/training/Training/workmen's_diary/2026-08-31.md` · model-output</sub>

#### 🟡 MEDIUM · 2026-08-31 · Beam-plan reading errors beyond the missing slabs: row B all labelled B2, B3 drawn on the wrong axis, B0 classified as a slab

**What happened.** On page 27 in the sampling round, the model put B2 on all three row-B segments (the key has B3+B2+B3), placed B3 vertically when it is horizontal on rows B and B', classified B0 (a stair-landing beam) as a slab, and named the dummy gridlines 1.5B/3.5B instead of the conventional 1'/4'.

**Root cause.** Mark identity and orientation are being inferred from local context rather than read per segment; naming conventions for dummy lines were never taught.

**Impact.** Wrong marks and wrong orientations reach the takeoff as confident data; the dummy-line naming alone costs strict-recall credit on beams whose physical position was correct.

**Fix.** not fixed — recorded per-item in appendix E as the accuracy baseline for the next training round

**→ Rule.** Record per-item error modes, not just an aggregate recall number — "row B all B2" and "B3 on the wrong axis" point at different training fixes than a low score does.

<sub>`D:/00mk/steel project/training/Training/workmen's_diary/2026-08-31.md` · model-accuracy</sub>

#### 🟡 MEDIUM · 2026-09-02 · pass3 finds zero CV anchors on steel C-channel drawings — an entire drawing style it can never measure

**What happened.** Running pass3 retroactively over the two salvaged house2 pages returned ok:false 'หมุดไม่พอ'. Investigation showed the CV scanner found not a single symbol anywhere on the page, because it is a special-style steel C-channel drawing with no coordinate anchor points of the kind CV was built to recognise — a different failure from the already-known beam-centroid limitation.

**Root cause.** cv_scan's symbol vocabulary was built from RC footing/column drawings; a steel-member drawing presents none of those shapes, so the anchor set is empty rather than merely sparse.

**Impact.** pass3 contributes nothing on any steel-structure house — silent on those pages forever, not just on this one. Correctly refused rather than guessing (BOQ unchanged at ฿170,396.09), but the coverage hole was unknown until measured.

**Fix.** not fixed — recorded as correct-refusal, result stored in pass3_measure.json; no steel-drawing anchor support added

**→ Rule.** Before claiming a measurement stage 'works', name the drawing classes it was built from — a CV vocabulary trained on one construction style returns an honest zero on another, and zero coverage is easy to mistake for a bug or for a pass.

<sub>`D:/00mk/steel project/training/Training/workmen's_diary/2026-09-02.md` · cv-coverage</sub>

#### ⚪ LOW · 2026-08-25 · Near-miss: translating the whole prompt set to English would have cost ~8% accuracy

**What happened.** Investigating the advisor's Thai↔English dictionary suggestion, research showed that translating an entire prompt into English can reduce accuracy by about 8%, because the source language carries context the translation loses. The correct technique is DIP (Dictionary Insertion Prompting) — inserting short glossary entries beside the prompt, not translating it.

**Root cause.** The intuitive reading of 'the prompt is English but the drawings are Thai, so align the languages' points toward wholesale translation, which is the wrong intervention.

**Impact.** None yet — the research was done before implementation. Acting on the intuition would have degraded results by ~8% while appearing to be an improvement.

**Fix.** Not implemented. Deliberately parked pending clarification from the advisor about which problem the dictionary is meant to solve.

**→ Rule.** For cross-lingual prompting, insert a term glossary rather than translating the prompt wholesale — and confirm which concrete problem a proposed change is meant to fix before building it.

<sub>`D:/00mk/steel project/training/Training/workmen's_diary/2026-08-25(teach mk).md` · prompt-engineering</sub>

#### ⚪ LOW · 2026-08-29 · The Thai→field dictionary was placed too late in the prompt and had to be moved to the top

**What happened.** The shared Thai-to-field-name dictionary in _common.md was positioned somewhere other than the start of the prompt. On 2026-08-29 it was moved to the beginning, following the DIP principle Makham had researched.

**Root cause.** Prompt section ordering was decided by document readability rather than by how the model attends to context; definitions the model needs while parsing were placed after the content they apply to.

**Impact.** Sub-optimal field mapping across every pass 2 subtask until corrected — degraded quality with no visible failure.

**Fix.** Moved the dictionary to the head of the prepended _common.md block.

**→ Rule.** Put definitions, vocabularies and constraints at the top of a prompt, before the task and the data. Prompt ordering is a functional parameter, not a formatting choice.

<sub>`D:/00mk/steel project/training/Training/workmen's_diary/สอน_t04_Purson_2026-08-29.md` · prompt-engineering</sub>

---

## T10 — Code Bugs & Logic Errors

*Ordinary defects: wrong formula, wrong branch, off-by-one, bad regex, broken UI.*

**53 entries** · 6 critical · 14 high

#### 🔴 CRITICAL · 2026-07-28 · Bug 4: enable_thinking=False was missing again — the identical bug that had already made t01 measure 0/3

**What happened.** train_qwen3vl.py lacked enable_thinking=False. The diary states plainly that this is the same bug that caused t01 to measure 0 out of 3, i.e. a known past failure being reintroduced verbatim in a new file.

**Root cause.** A previously-diagnosed failure was fixed in one script only and never captured as a required setting in a shared config, template, or check — so a new file started from scratch reproduced it exactly.

**Impact.** Would have produced another 0-score measurement round, wasting the paid run and the analysis time behind it. Caught pre-rental.

**Fix.** Added enable_thinking=False.

**→ Rule.** Every bug that has ever produced a zero score must become an assertion in the environment verifier, not a fix in one file. If a past failure can be reintroduced by writing a new script, it was never really fixed.

<sub>`D:/00mk/steel project/training/Training/workmen's_diary/2026-07-28.md` · regression</sub>

#### 🔴 CRITICAL · 2026-08-21 · Greedy decoding with no repetition guard made the model loop until the token cap, destroying whole pages of valid output

**What happened.** House 08's beam-plan page (หน้า20, S-03) failed to parse. Root cause: run_house_batch.py and infer_t02.py used pure greedy decoding (do_sample=False) with no repetition guard, so the model looped repeating fake B2 beam entries across nearly every grid cell until hitting max_new_tokens, never closing the JSON. The page had 31 real beams; all 31 were lost because the brackets never closed.

**Root cause.** Autoregressive decoding is self-reinforcing on repetitive content: each repeated pattern raises the evidence for repeating again, so the stop token never wins. Greedy decoding with no penalty and no structural constraint makes this a guaranteed failure mode on element-dense pages, and JSON is all-or-nothing so partial correct output is worth zero.

**Impact.** Element-dense pages — exactly the highest-value structural sheets — produced zero usable output. The 57.9% JSON-valid rate and the 11% element recall are both largely this bug; หน้า20 alone had 31 uncounted ground-truth elements.

**Fix.** Added repetition_penalty=1.15 and no_repeat_ngram_size=8 to both scripts (partial fix, 'asking' not 'forbidding'), then grammar-constrained decoding via xgrammar the following night, which took JSON validity from 57.9% to 96.8%.

**→ Rule.** Never run structured-output generation with pure greedy decoding and no structural constraint — use grammar-constrained decoding (xgrammar) as the default for JSON output; a soft penalty makes looping harder but only a grammar makes an unclosed bracket impossible.

<sub>`D:/00mk/steel project/training/Training/workmen's_diary/2026-08-21.md` · bug</sub>

#### 🔴 CRITICAL · 2026-08-21 · parseGridMaster could not read a single current grid file since 2026-08-02 — every import silently produced an empty grid

**What happened.** Constistant's parseGridMaster reads f.x_lines / f.y_lines at top level, but the schema moved them into a nested grid{} object. Counted across both dataset folders: 37 of 37 grid files are nested, 0 are top-level. Every raw-extraction import since that normalization therefore produced an empty grid and silently marked every span unresolved.

**Root cause.** A schema field move on the data side was never propagated to the platform consumer, and the consumer's failure mode for a missing key is an empty result rather than an error — so a total failure was indistinguishable from 'this house has no grid'.

**Impact.** Silent since 2026-08-02: every raw-extraction import in the platform produced zero grid data and therefore zero resolved beam spans. Beam lengths never reached the BOQ at all.

**Fix.** Fixed to read nested grid{} first with a fallback to top level for old files; proven against real data (adaptRawExtraction over ground-truth house 09 went from span 0/87 to 18/87 with real values). 4 new regression tests in tests/raw-extraction-grid.test.js. npm test 1122/1122.

**→ Rule.** A parser that returns empty for an unrecognized shape must warn instead — and every schema field move needs a grep across all consumers plus a regression test using a real current file, not a hand-written fixture that was updated alongside the parser.

<sub>`D:/00mk/steel project/training/Training/workmen's_diary/2026-08-21.md` · bug</sub>

#### 🔴 CRITICAL · 2026-08-21 · parseGridRef accepted only the dashed grid-ref form, but the spec mandates no-dash — every beam span was null

**What happened.** parseGridRef does trimmed.split('-') and rejects anything not yielding exactly 2 parts. But spec §0.8 mandates the no-dash form ("C1", not "C-1") and all real data uses it. Every beam span in every import was therefore null.

**Root cause.** The parser was written to a format assumption ('grid refs are letter-dash-number') that contradicts the spec's own §0.8 rule, and no test used a real spec-conforming value. The failure returns null rather than throwing, so it never surfaced.

**Impact.** Every beam span in every raw-extraction import resolved to null — the second of two silent bugs that together meant beam geometry never reached the BOQ at all.

**Fix.** Accept ^([A-Za-zก-ฮ]{1,3}'*)(\d+'*)$ alongside the existing dashed form; ~-prefixed approximate refs still correctly rejected. Verified against real data (span 0/87 → 18/87) plus 2 new regression tests.

**→ Rule.** Write parser tests from the spec's canonical examples, not from the format you assumed — and make a parse failure on a required field loud (warn/count) rather than returning null, which is indistinguishable from legitimately absent data.

<sub>`D:/00mk/steel project/training/Training/workmen's_diary/2026-08-21.md` · bug</sub>

#### 🔴 CRITICAL · 2026-08-28 · Dedup by NCC similarity broke real detection coverage in 4 houses — similarity ≠ interchangeability

**What happened.** Running dedup on the already-promoted footing bank removed tpl_footing13/15/17 (each scoring 0.80–1.00 against templates 7/6/16). Real coverage then broke: houses 04, 05, 17 and 26 dropped out of green. Templates that look near-identical at 64x64 NCC behave differently under multi-scale sliding-window matching on a full page.

**Root cause.** NCC on a resized 64x64 crop measures appearance similarity, which is not the same property as "produces the same matches on a full-page multi-scale sweep". The dedup metric was a proxy for the property that actually mattered.

**Impact.** Four houses lost detection coverage. Had this been applied without a coverage check, the loss would have shown up much later as unexplained detection regressions.

**Fix.** Added a second gate to `--bank --apply`: measure real coverage before and after using house_pages() + match_bank via the same path as harvest_templates.py. If any house drops out of green, the whole kind is cancelled and files auto-restored (tested — caught footing, restored 14 to 14 automatically). Column dedup was verified safe with real match_points before applying: 7 templates → 3, coverage unchanged at 16/30 houses.

**→ Rule.** When deduplicating anything that feeds a detector, validate against the detector's real output, not an appearance-similarity score. Build the before/after coverage check with auto-rollback into the tool itself.

<sub>`D:/00mk/steel project/training/Training/workmen's_diary/2026-08-28.md` · bug</sub>

#### 🔴 CRITICAL · 2026-08-29 · Dataset builder still filtered old pattern names after a rename — plan_footing/plan_beam/gridline were 0 examples for a full day

**What happened.** build_dataset_t03.py still filtered on the old pattern names "plan" and "gridline". After the 28 Aug rename, plan_footing, plan_beam and gridline vanished entirely from train/val.jsonl — 0 examples each — and nobody noticed until a prompt-hygiene sweep stumbled into it. After the fix: gridline 40 / plan_footing 100 / plan_beam 125.

**Root cause.** A rename in one place (page-type vocabulary) was not propagated to the consumer's filter, and the builder reports total example count rather than per-subtask counts, so "0 plan_beam" looked like a normal successful build.

**Impact.** The three most important subtasks — including plan_beam, the entire point of the round — were completely absent from the training data. Any training run in that window would have been worthless for those subtasks and the reason would have been invisible.

**Fix.** Fixed the filter. Verified 257 real rows in train+val.jsonl.

**→ Rule.** A dataset builder must assert a minimum example count per subtask and fail loudly on zero. A silent empty filter after a rename is the most expensive class of bug there is — it makes an entire training run meaningless with no error.

<sub>`D:/00mk/steel project/training/Training/workmen's_diary/2026-08-29.md` · bug</sub>

#### 🟠 HIGH · 2026-07-09 · The Label Studio pinned column silently cut off content instead of scrolling

**What happened.** An annotator reported the left tab would not scroll. Diagnosis found .stickycol had no max-height or overflow-y, so any content taller than the viewport was not merely unreachable — it was invisible, with no indication anything was missing.

**Root cause.** A sticky column was styled for a fixed-size assumption and never tested with content taller than the screen; CSS overflow defaults to clipping silently.

**Impact.** Annotators could not see part of the plan they were meant to label, on the very first real project created in Label Studio Cloud, across all 5 config files.

**Fix.** Added max-height:96vh; overflow-y:auto; padding-right:6px to .stickycol in all five XML config files.

**→ Rule.** Any pinned/sticky pane needs an explicit max-height plus overflow-y:auto from the start — the default failure mode is invisible data loss, not a visible layout break.

<sub>`D:/00mk/steel project/training/Training/workmen's_diary/2026-07-09.md` · ui-bug</sub>

#### 🟠 HIGH · 2026-07-19 · RB2 recorded at a guessed position with confidence 0.4 that turned out to be entirely wrong

**What happened.** RB2 in house 2's tie-beam plan had been recorded at B3-A3 with confidence 0.4 — a guess. It is actually C4-B4 (1.8) + B4-A4 (3.15) on the column-4 side. The 2.50 number that had been mis-attached to RB2 actually belongs to dummy grid B'.

**Root cause.** A low-confidence guess was written as data rather than left null with a flag, and a nearby unexplained dimension (2.50) was attached to the nearest plausible element instead of being left unassigned.

**Impact.** A tie beam recorded on the wrong side of the building; a dimension attributed to the wrong element, which also delayed discovering dummy grid B'.

**Fix.** Corrected RB2 to C4-B4 + B4-A4, and used the freed 2.50 to derive B' = A-2.50, then added RB1A at B'3-B'4.

**→ Rule.** A confidence-0.4 position is a guess, and a guess written into a position field is indistinguishable from data downstream. Leave it null with an explicit flag, and never attach an unexplained dimension to the nearest plausible element.

<sub>`2026-07-19.md` · data-extraction</sub>

#### 🟠 HIGH · 2026-07-21 · `isinstance(ip.size, dict)` guard silently false — image resolution setting was skipped with no error

**What happened.** A defensive `if isinstance(ip.size, dict)` added while fixing the max_pixels bug always evaluated False, so the intended 5,120-visual-token resolution was never applied; the model silently ran at the 16,384 default.

**Root cause.** `ip.size` is a `SizeDict`, which supports `["key"]=value` but does not inherit from `dict` — the guard tested inheritance instead of behaviour, and the failure path was a silent skip rather than an error.

**Impact.** Training/eval ran at the wrong image resolution with no visible symptom; contaminated at least the baseline measurement and cost an extra debug cycle on the paid machine.

**Fix.** Removed the isinstance condition and wrote the value directly; verified by a tiny on-machine test script that read the resulting value back (no full model load needed).

**→ Rule.** Never guard a config write with a type check that can silently skip it — write the value, then read it back and assert it matches the intent. A silent no-op is more dangerous than a crash.

<sub>`D:/00mk/steel project/training/Training/workmen's_diary/2026-07-21.md` · code-bug</sub>

#### 🟠 HIGH · 2026-08-20 · Unsloth's from_pretrained silently ignores the subfolder kwarg, so the LoRA adapter could not be loaded

**What happened.** The t02 adapter files live at lora-adapter/ inside the HF repo, not at root. Unsloth's from_pretrained does not forward the subfolder kwarg to its internal AutoConfig/PeftConfig probes, so loading failed. Traced by reading unsloth/models/loader.py source rather than guessing.

**Root cause.** Unsloth's loader accepts **kwargs at the top level but does not thread them through to the config-probe calls it makes internally — a silent kwarg drop, not an error. The caller had no way to know the argument was ignored.

**Impact.** Blocked the entire inference run until diagnosed; would have been easy to misattribute to a broken adapter upload or a bad HF repo layout.

**Fix.** Pre-download with snapshot_download(allow_patterns=[...]) and point from_pretrained at the resulting local path. Applied to both run_house_batch.py and infer_t02.py.

**→ Rule.** When a wrapper library ignores an argument, read its source rather than theorising — and prefer resolving remote artifacts to a local path yourself (snapshot_download) instead of trusting a wrapper to forward path kwargs it never documented.

<sub>`D:/00mk/steel project/training/Training/workmen's_diary/2026-08-20.md` · bug</sub>

#### 🟠 HIGH · 2026-08-24 · The MAX_LENGTH assert checked "most images" instead of the actual longest sequence and was blind to a real overflow

**What happened.** After op04 expanded the dataset from 452 to 1,116 examples, one example was found to exceed MAX_LENGTH. The existing assert only checked the example with the most images, which is not the longest sequence. Fixing the assert to check the top 3 by image+prompt+GT combined revealed real sequences of 30,368 / 28,008 / 28,035 — only 7% margin under 32,768, and the original assert could not see any of them.

**Root cause.** The guard used a proxy metric (image count) for the thing it was actually protecting (total token length). Prompt text and GT length were excluded from the calculation entirely.

**Impact.** Silent truncation of training examples, or an OOM mid-run, would have been the first symptom. This is the same bug class already documented as t01 §0.4.

**Fix.** Rewrote the assert to compute image + prompt + GT tokens and check the top 3 longest; also asserts visual-token count on the first batch to catch silent 512px resizing.

**→ Rule.** A guard must measure the exact quantity it protects, never a proxy. When adding data to a dataset, recompute the length distribution — do not trust a guard tuned on the old distribution.

<sub>`D:/00mk/steel project/training/Training/workmen's_diary/2026-08-24.md` · bug</sub>

#### 🟠 HIGH · 2026-08-24 · First house-08 inference run died on both of its first two jobs, from two unrelated JSON bugs

**What happened.** The t03 inference run on house 08 failed 2/2 on its first jobs: (1) gridline output had genuinely broken structure — missing the opening `{` of an array element and a corrupted `pox_M` field name; (2) notes output had `"confidence_score": 0.,` (decimal point with no digit) plus a second bug in the same file, `{item_no":` missing the opening quote on a key name.

**Root cause.** Grammar (xgrammar) was only attached to plan_beam per the standing rule, leaving every other subtask generating free-form JSON. gridline additionally has the fewest training examples (45) and is the hardest task.

**Impact.** A paid inference run wasted on 2 jobs before anyone noticed; a regex-patching approach would have been an endless whack-a-mole.

**Fix.** Decided ✅ to switch to `--grammar-all` (force xgrammar on every subtask, not just plan_beam), killed the running process at 2/33 and re-ran the whole set (~$0.4).

**→ Rule.** If a structural constraint is correct for one subtask it is almost certainly correct for all of them — apply it globally by default. Never fix malformed model output with per-pattern regex patches.

<sub>`D:/00mk/steel project/training/Training/workmen's_diary/2026-08-24.md` · bug</sub>

#### 🟠 HIGH · 2026-08-28 · BEAM_GAP hardcoded to a single 21px value was blind to half the drawing library

**What happened.** Beam detection used one hardcoded gap of 21px. Measuring 33 houses revealed two distinct series: the กรมโยธา series at ~16px and the house-17 series at ~21px. The single value could only ever see one of them.

**Root cause.** The constant was derived from whichever house was open when the detector was written, and never validated against the corpus. Drawings from different issuing bodies use different line spacings.

**Impact.** Beam detection was structurally impossible on roughly half the library, for as long as the constant existed.

**Fix.** Replaced with BEAM_GAPS = (16, 21), measured across 33 houses.

**→ Rule.** Any geometric constant derived from a drawing must be measured across the whole corpus, and stored as a set of series values rather than a single number. Different issuing bodies produce different conventions.

<sub>`D:/00mk/steel project/training/Training/workmen's_diary/2026-08-28.md` · bug</sub>

#### 🟠 HIGH · 2026-08-28 · Column match threshold of 0.65 produced garbage detections in 10 of 30 houses

**What happened.** At threshold 0.65 the column detector produced garbage in 10 of 30 houses. A sweep raised it to 0.75, cutting garbage houses to 1. Two small templates (t6/t7) still sprayed 49–96 garbage points per page onto other drawing series at 0.75; a new rule (small template + ink coverage < 0.15 → require 0.85) fixed them with zero garbage and full true-positive retention.

**Root cause.** A single global threshold cannot serve templates of different sizes and ink densities — a small, sparse template matches noise almost anywhere. Thresholds were set by intuition rather than by sweeping across the corpus.

**Impact.** Up to 96 false detections per page would have been fed to the model as "hints", actively poisoning the pass the hints exist to help.

**Fix.** Swept 30 houses to set 0.75, added the small-template/low-ink → 0.85 rule, and placed the rule in match_bank as the single decision point so analyze and harvest cannot drift apart. Result: columns matching GT went 4→16 houses, val 01–05 all green.

**→ Rule.** Sweep detection thresholds across the full corpus, and make the threshold a function of template properties (size, ink density) rather than a global constant. Put the rule in exactly one place so callers cannot drift.

<sub>`D:/00mk/steel project/training/Training/workmen's_diary/2026-08-28.md` · bug</sub>

#### 🟠 HIGH · 2026-08-28 · Union-find dedup created transitive chain drift, merging two crops of completely different words

**What happened.** dedup_templates.py first used union-find (transitive grouping) at NCC ≥ 0.8. Files A~B scored 1.0 and B~C scored 0.80, so A was grouped with C even though A~C is only 0.737 — and the pair it merged turned out to be two text crops of different words, not icons at all.

**Root cause.** Similarity is not transitive. Union-find over a similarity threshold builds chains where the endpoints are arbitrarily dissimilar, bridged by an intermediate file.

**Impact.** Would have silently discarded genuinely distinct templates, and the reported similarity score would have been a lie (the reported score was never the actual pair score).

**Fix.** Rewrote as greedy — each file is compared only against already-kept representatives, never through another file. Guarantees every reported score is a real pairwise score.

**→ Rule.** Never use transitive clustering on a similarity threshold. Compare against retained representatives only, so the score you report is the score you measured.

<sub>`D:/00mk/steel project/training/Training/workmen's_diary/2026-08-28.md` · bug</sub>

#### 🟠 HIGH · 2026-08-29 · Human reviewer prose leaks into the model's prompt via the grid master JSON block

**What happened.** All prose prompt files scanned clean of forbidden characters, but the *assembled* prompts for plan_footing/plan_beam/plan_slab append a real grid master JSON block from GT — and that block carries `source` and `confidence_flags` fields containing human reviewer explanations full of `.`, `_`, `—`. Those reach the model.

**Root cause.** The hygiene scan checked the prose `.md` source files, not the assembled prompt that the model actually receives. The grid-master block is injected at build time from GT, so it bypasses the source-file scan entirely, and no field whitelist limits what gets pasted in.

**Impact.** The exact characters being systematically removed from prompts to reduce hallucination are still reaching the model, plus irrelevant reviewer commentary the model must ignore. Not yet fixed.

**Fix.** Not fixed — flagged as a separate concern awaiting Makham's ruling on whether to strip source/confidence_flags and keep only id/pos_m/type.

**→ Rule.** Scan the assembled artifact the model actually sees, not the source templates. When injecting real data into a prompt, whitelist the fields the model needs — never paste the whole record.

<sub>`D:/00mk/steel project/training/Training/workmen's_diary/2026-08-29.md` · bug</sub>

#### 🟠 HIGH · 2026-08-30 · Known-since-t03 and still unfixed: JSON grammar constrains structure only, so generation can loop forever inside a string value — that is what hung the server for 7+ hours

**What happened.** xgrammar enforces that output is valid JSON but places no constraint on the content of a string value, so a request can enter an endless repetition inside a string and never terminate. This behaviour was already known from t03. It was still unfixed when `serve_purson.py` was put on a rented card, and one such runaway request is exactly what blocked the event loop and made the whole server unreachable for 7+ hours, including the trivial `/v1/models` health check.

**Root cause.** A known generation-level failure mode was carried forward without either a mitigation (max-token cap that actually fires, stop condition, repetition guard) or an architectural containment, so the first time it met a single-threaded blocking server it took the whole process down.

**Impact.** A rented GPU billed for 7+ hours while producing nothing; two planned test runs (including the `test_browser_path.py` end-to-end with a real user JWT) never completed and the instance had to be torn down with `presentation.py down`.

**Fix.** Not fixed. The recorded next step addresses only the amplifier (wrap `generate()` in `asyncio.to_thread()` or a separate queue thread); the runaway generation itself is still open, as is why `PAGE_TIMEOUT_S` never fired.

**→ Rule.** A known failure mode carried into production is a scheduled outage. Grammar-constrained decoding guarantees shape, never termination — pair it with a hard token cap and a timeout that is proven to actually fire.

<sub>`D:/00mk/steel project/training/Training/workmen's_diary/2026-08-30.md` · bug/known-unfixed</sub>

#### 🟠 HIGH · 2026-08-31 · The 1/sqrt(k) adapter-averaging formula was measured and found wrong — norms blew up 3x to 16x

**What happened.** The planned 1/sqrt(k) averaging was measured against real weights: because the folds point in nearly the same direction, cross terms add constructively and ‖ΔW‖ came out 3.0x (attention) and 16.3x (MoE) too large.

**Root cause.** A scaling formula was adopted from theory that assumes near-orthogonal contributions, without measuring the actual alignment between folds.

**Impact.** Would have produced a badly mis-scaled merged model; caught by measuring rather than assuming.

**Fix.** Switched to exact rank-axis concatenation (r 16->48, alpha 32->96), measured ratio 1.000 on both layer types — equivalent to PEFT's combination_type="cat" done manually.

**→ Rule.** Measure the norm ratio of any merge/averaging formula against real weights before shipping it — theoretical scaling assumes independence that fine-tuned folds do not have.

<sub>`D:/00mk/steel project/training/Training/workmen's_diary/2026-08-31.md` · math-error</sub>

#### 🟠 HIGH · 2026-09-01 · pass3 double-counted points into the BOQ across three separate layers

**What happened.** Points that had already been matched, points used as anchors, and points belonging to a different subtask were each re-added as new elements into the BOQ. Fixing it layer by layer took the duplicate count from 48 → 33 → 7 → 0.

**Root cause.** No single ledger of 'points already accounted for'. Each consumption path removed points from its own view but not from a shared consumed-set, so a point could legitimately pass three different 'is this new?' checks.

**Impact.** Up to 48 phantom elements inflating the BOQ. Required three successive rounds of fixing — work redone twice.

**Fix.** Tracked consumed points across all three layers until the duplicate count reached 0.

**→ Rule.** When several code paths can each claim the same item, keep one shared consumed-set rather than per-path filters. And when a de-dup fix reduces but doesn't eliminate duplicates, keep going — a partial fix here means another claiming path exists.

<sub>`2026-09-01.md` · logic-bug</sub>

#### 🟠 HIGH · 2026-09-01 · If the network died while reporting a job failure, the exception escaped the loop and killed the entire worker

**What happened.** In `main()`, a network error during the 'report job failed' call threw an exception that propagated out of the `while` loop, terminating the worker process entirely.

**Root cause.** The error-reporting path was itself unprotected — the code that handles failures could fail in a way nothing handled. Additionally the done and failed paths shared code, so a 'failed' stamp could overwrite an already-completed job.

**Impact.** A single network blip during error reporting would take down the worker completely, leaving the rented GPU idle and billing.

**Fix.** Separated the done and failed paths and forbade stamping `failed` over a job that already completed.

**→ Rule.** The failure-reporting path is the one that must never throw. Wrap it, and never let done/failed share a write path where the failure branch can clobber a success.

<sub>`2026-09-01.md` · resilience</sub>

#### 🟡 MEDIUM · 2026-07-06 · Long unbroken values overflowed their box in the Label Studio review UI, making review data unreadable

**What happened.** A real Label Studio screenshot from Makham showed text overflowing its box. The offenders were long values with no spaces — snake_case confidence_flags, other_fields_json, and file_warnings — which have no natural wrap points.

**Root cause.** The XML configs were written and shipped without ever being viewed with real data. The layout was reasoned about rather than looked at, and snake_case field values are precisely the case default word wrapping cannot handle.

**Impact.** Human reviewers could not read the flags and warnings that exist specifically to tell them what to check — the review UI failed at its one job until fixed. Required an edit pass across four XML files.

**Fix.** Added `overflow-wrap:break-word; word-break:break-word` for Text elements displaying long values, in label-studio-makham-elements.xml, -freezeR.xml, -single.xml and -single-freezeR.xml.

**→ Rule.** Never ship an annotation UI config without rendering it against real data at least once. And assume every machine-generated value (snake_case flags, JSON blobs, ids) is unbreakable text — set break-word on those fields by default.

<sub>`D:/00mk/steel project/training/Training/workmen's_diary/2026-07-06.md` · ui-bug</sub>

#### 🟡 MEDIUM · 2026-07-09 · Adding an empty xml-stylesheet to hide a browser notice produced garbled output and was fully reverted

**What happened.** To remove the browser's standard 'This XML file does not appear to have any style information' notice, an xml-stylesheet processing instruction with an empty data: CSS was added to all 5 configs. Opening the file then rendered garbled text — the CSS from <Style> and the text inside <Choice> leaked out and mixed together — because any stylesheet, even an empty one, switches the browser's render mode.

**Root cause.** A cosmetic fix was applied to a symptom in a context that was never supported: these files are not meant to be opened in a browser at all, only pasted into Label Studio's Code editor.

**Impact.** A worse-than-before rendering, real user frustration, and a full revert across five files.

**Fix.** Removed the xml-stylesheet line from all 5 files and documented that the configs are not browser-viewable by design.

**→ Rule.** Do not fix cosmetic complaints about an unsupported usage path — state that the path is unsupported instead; a workaround for a non-problem can create a real one.

<sub>`D:/00mk/steel project/training/Training/workmen's_diary/2026-07-09.md` · ui-bug/regression</sub>

#### 🟡 MEDIUM · 2026-07-10 · findProductionDir() silently falls back to mk_test/t2 — two generations of schema out of date — when a house folder is not found

**What happened.** The new auto-lookup in label-studio-tasks-makham.js searches rawjson_ยังไม่ได้แก้ไขโดนคน/ for a folder ending in the house name, and if it finds none, falls back to the old mk_test/t2 'for backward compatibility'. It was tested and confirmed that the fallback still pulls from mk_test/t2 normally.

**Root cause.** Backward compatibility was implemented as a silent default rather than an explicit opt-in. t2 predates both the Gen 4 field shapes (grid_ref_start/end, main_bar.top/bottom) and the source_image requirement, so the fallback path produces exactly the empty-grid_ref/empty-rebar output that was fixed two days earlier.

**Impact.** Not yet triggered in anger, but a typo in a house name, or running before the production folder exists, silently regenerates the labeling tasks from a two-generations-old dataset with no error and no warning — reproducing an already-fixed bug and looking like it worked (it prints task counts either way).

**Fix.** not fixed — the fallback is still in place as written.

**→ Rule.** A fallback to stale data must be loud or absent. If the requested input does not exist, fail with the path you looked for; never quietly substitute an older dataset that still parses.

<sub>`D:/00mk/steel project/training/Training/workmen's_diary/2026-07-10.md` · pipeline-script</sub>

#### 🟡 MEDIUM · 2026-07-21 · eval_fields.py crashed: `ip.max_pixels` became a read-only property in the installed transformers

**What happened.** The first run of `eval_fields.py --base` crashed with `AttributeError: property ... has no setter` on the line setting image resolution via `ip.max_pixels = ...`.

**Root cause.** The scripts were written against an older transformers API; the version installed on the rental image had changed max_pixels from a settable attribute to a computed read-only property, and no version pin or compatibility check existed.

**Impact.** First real run on the paid GPU aborted; required a source fix and re-upload mid-session.

**Fix.** Set the resolution through `ip.size["longest_edge"]/["shortest_edge"]` instead, per Qwen/HuggingFace GitHub, then re-uploaded the file.

**→ Rule.** Pin library versions used by training/eval scripts, and validate every model-config write against the exact library version installed on the rental image before the paid run.

<sub>`D:/00mk/steel project/training/Training/workmen's_diary/2026-07-21.md` · code-bug</sub>

#### 🟡 MEDIUM · 2026-08-25 · Raw template matching reported 235 detections for 14 real footings

**What happened.** Because a template still scores highly when shifted by a single pixel, each real footing generated a cluster of hundreds of high-scoring points. 14 actual footings produced 235 reported detections.

**Root cause.** Raw matchTemplate output is a dense score map, not a detection list. Treating every above-threshold pixel as a separate object is a fundamental misuse of the operator's output.

**Impact.** Detection counts were useless (~17× inflated) until deduplication was added; any downstream consumer of the raw count would have been badly wrong.

**Fix.** Implemented NMS (Non-Maximum Suppression): sort by score, keep the top point, delete every point closer than half a template dimension, repeat. 235 → 14, exact match to ground truth.

**→ Rule.** Any sliding-window or score-map detector needs NMS before its output can be counted. Never report a raw above-threshold pixel count as an object count.

<sub>`D:/00mk/steel project/training/Training/workmen's_diary/2026-08-25(teach mk).md` · algorithm</sub>

#### 🟡 MEDIUM · 2026-08-26 · Self-harvest threshold set on the wrong side — seed 0.85 could never fire

**What happened.** The pass-2.5 self-harvest criterion was first written as seed threshold 0.85, which could never trigger because cross-series matches only reach 0.72-0.80. The criterion was inverted: it should be a loose seed with a strict match.

**Root cause.** Threshold values were chosen by intuition about "high confidence" rather than measured against the actual score distribution of the data. Nobody looked at what scores real cross-series matches produce before picking a number.

**Impact.** The self-harvest feature was a silent no-op — it would have appeared to work while recovering nothing.

**Fix.** Flipped to loose seed / strict match at 0.90. Results: บ้าน_ใหญ่_2ชั้น_08 15→16 = GT, บ้าน_เล็ก_2ชั้น_19 17→18 = GT, both eyeball-verified as real footings. Real ceiling recorded: can only recover kinds the template bank already catches (house 10's other 16 are a different kind — correctly +0).

**→ Rule.** Never pick a similarity threshold without first plotting the score distribution of real positives and real negatives. A threshold above the positive distribution is a silent no-op, not a strict filter.

<sub>`D:/00mk/steel project/training/Training/workmen's_diary/2026-08-26.md` · bug</sub>

#### 🟡 MEDIUM · 2026-08-26 · Two Set-of-Mark label-overlap bugs that unit tests could not see

**What happened.** On the marked images produced by cv_scan.py, column labels were being drawn on top of footing labels, and one label covered a printed F1 mark on the drawing itself. Unit tests passed; the bugs were only found by looking at the images.

**Root cause.** The tests verified that labels were *generated* with correct data, not that they were *legible* in the rendered output. Visual occlusion is invisible to any assertion on the underlying data structure.

**Impact.** The model would have received marked images where a real drawing mark was hidden and two annotations were unreadable — corrupting exactly the hint the pass exists to provide.

**Fix.** Moved the label positions.

**→ Rule.** Anything whose output is an image must be eyeballed before it ships. Unit tests prove the data is right; only looking proves the render is readable.

<sub>`D:/00mk/steel project/training/Training/workmen's_diary/2026-08-26.md` · bug</sub>

#### 🟡 MEDIUM · 2026-08-28 · `--pass25` wrote only `*25` sidecar files while `apply_arm()` reads the plain ones

**What happened.** The `--pass25` flag writes sidecar files suffixed `25`, but `apply_arm()` reads the unsuffixed files. Running only `--pass25` therefore leaves apply_arm with nothing to read — two separate sets are required (plain = pass 1.5 feeding arm 2.4, `25` = pass 2.5 feeding pass 3).

**Root cause.** Two passes producing similar artifacts adopted different filename conventions independently, with no shared constant defining the sidecar naming. The producer and consumer were written at different times.

**Impact.** A silently empty hint — arms would run with no CV hint and appear to work while receiving nothing. Caught before the GPU run.

**Fix.** Documented in the RUNBOOK that both sets must be produced.

**→ Rule.** Producer and consumer of a file-naming convention must share one constant. When two passes emit similar artifacts, verify the consumer actually finds the producer's output — an empty read is not an error.

<sub>`D:/00mk/steel project/training/Training/workmen's_diary/2026-08-28.md` · bug</sub>

#### 🟡 MEDIUM · 2026-08-28 · pass3 prompt asked for `stirrup_tie_count`, a field name the schema does not have

**What happened.** The pass3_takeoff prompt specified `stirrup_tie_count` where the schema defines `stirrup:{count}`. Fixed as a leftover item under §6b.

**Root cause.** The prompt was written against an earlier/imagined schema shape and never cross-checked against the actual field definition; nothing mechanically validates prompt field names against the schema.

**Impact.** Had pass 3 been run before this was caught, every output would have carried an off-schema field — silently dropped or failing validation downstream. Pass 3 had no runner yet, which is the only reason it cost nothing.

**Fix.** prompt changed to `stirrup:{count}`

**→ Rule.** Field names inside a prompt are part of the schema contract. Add a check that every field name a prompt asks for exists in the schema — the same class of guard already used for forbidden characters.

<sub>`D:/00mk/steel project/training/Training/workmen's_diary/2026-08-28.md` · bug</sub>

#### 🟡 MEDIUM · 2026-08-28 · Column templates t6/t7 sprayed 49–96 garbage detections per page at the newly-raised 0.75 threshold

**What happened.** After raising the column match threshold 0.65→0.75, two of the new templates (t6/t7, small and low-ink) still produced 49–96 false detections per page against other drawing series. A second rule was needed: small template plus ink density below 0.15 must use 0.85.

**Root cause.** A single global threshold cannot serve templates of different size and ink density — a small, sparse template matches almost anything at a correlation score that is fine for a large dense one.

**Impact.** A second garbage-detection failure hiding behind the first threshold fix; without the sweep across 30 houses it would have poisoned the CV hints feeding the plan_footing/plan_beam arms.

**Fix.** added a size+ink-density rule (0.85 for small low-ink templates), implemented once in match_bank so analyze and harvest share the path

**→ Rule.** One threshold per detector is a per-template property, not a global constant. Sweep across the whole library before promoting a template, and check garbage counts per template, not just the aggregate pass/fail.

<sub>`D:/00mk/steel project/training/Training/workmen's_diary/2026-08-28.md` · bug</sub>

#### 🟡 MEDIUM · 2026-08-29 · OCR crop used PDF-native proportions on already-organized PNGs — cropped the wrong box entirely

**What happened.** The first title-block OCR run used crop proportions derived from the PDF's native page geometry, applied to PNGs that organize.py had already processed. The crop landed on the director's signature box instead of the sheet_code/sheet_name box.

**Root cause.** Coordinates were taken from one representation of the page (PDF) and applied to a different one (organized PNG) without verifying the two share the same aspect/margins. The intermediate processing step changed the geometry.

**Impact.** A full OCR run produced results from entirely the wrong region of every page.

**Fix.** Re-measured the crop coordinates from the actual PNG images (0.84–1.0 width, 0.73–0.98 height). Result: sheet_code correct 24/26 on บ้าน_ใหญ่_2ชั้น_02's 27 pages, sheet_name legible on nearly every page — a working tool where easyocr scored 0/4.

**→ Rule.** Derive crop coordinates from the exact image the code will actually read, never from an upstream representation. Verify one crop visually before running a batch.

<sub>`D:/00mk/steel project/training/Training/workmen's_diary/2026-08-29.md` · bug</sub>

#### 🟡 MEDIUM · 2026-08-29 · Glossary was almost embedded only in rendered files — the next re-render would have silently erased it

**What happened.** When embedding the Thai→field glossary per subtask, the plan-family glossary was initially going into the rendered plan_footing/plan_beam/plan_slab/plan_column prompt files. Those are generated from the pass2/plan.md template, so the next re-render would have wiped the glossary. Caught during review just before commit.

**Root cause.** A generated file was edited as if it were a source file. The generated/source distinction was not enforced by any marker or check in the rendered outputs.

**Impact.** Would have silently lost the glossary from every plan prompt at the next re-render, with no error — and the loss would only show up as a mysterious quality regression.

**Fix.** Embedded the glossary into pass2/plan.md (the template) instead, so re-renders preserve it.

**→ Rule.** Never edit a generated file. Put a 'generated — do not edit' header on every rendered output so the mistake is impossible to make silently.

<sub>`D:/00mk/steel project/training/Training/workmen's_diary/2026-08-29.md` · bug</sub>

#### 🟡 MEDIUM · 2026-08-29 · Glossary was being injected twice — once from _common.md and once from each subtask prompt

**What happened.** After moving the glossary into each subtask's own prompt, build_dataset_t03.py was still also injecting the shared GLOSSARY block from _common.md on top, so every subtask except gridline received two overlapping glossaries.

**Root cause.** A migration from centralized to per-subtask content was done without removing the centralized injection — the old and new mechanisms coexisted.

**Impact.** Duplicate content in every prompt, wasting context tokens against a MAX_LENGTH ceiling that was already being watched closely.

**Fix.** Removed the central injection so COMMON carries only output-shape and honesty rules; verified by grep that "Thai to field glossary" appears exactly once per subtask that should have it, and zero times in gridline.

**→ Rule.** When migrating shared content to per-item content, delete the shared injection in the same change and verify by counting occurrences in the final artifact — not by reading the code.

<sub>`D:/00mk/steel project/training/Training/workmen's_diary/2026-08-29.md` · bug</sub>

#### 🟡 MEDIUM · 2026-08-30 · `subprocess(shell=True)` on Windows made `>` in `gpu_ram>=90` a file redirect — `vastai search` returned empty with no clue

**What happened.** `presentation.py` used `subprocess(shell=True)`, which on Windows always goes through cmd.exe. The `>` inside the search filter `gpu_ram>=90` was interpreted as an output redirect, so `vastai search` returned an empty result with no error message.

**Root cause.** Shell string interpolation on Windows: any argument containing shell metacharacters is reinterpreted by cmd.exe, and the failure surfaces as empty output rather than an error.

**Impact.** GPU search silently returned nothing, blocking the rental flow with no diagnostic. Fixed across all 14 call sites.

**Fix.** Converted all 14 subprocess calls in `presentation.py` from shell strings to argv lists.

**→ Rule.** Never use `shell=True` with interpolated arguments — always pass an argv list. On Windows this is not a style preference, it silently corrupts any argument containing `>`, `<`, `&` or `|`.

<sub>`D:/00mk/steel project/training/Training/workmen's_diary/2026-08-30.md` · code-bug</sub>

#### 🟡 MEDIUM · 2026-08-30 · `serve_purson.py`: image-less request crashed with `images[0]` IndexError, and `return dict, 500` was treated by FastAPI as a list, not an HTTP status

**What happened.** The smoke test caught two defects: a request without an image raised `IndexError` on `images[0]`, and returning `(dict, 500)` from a handler made FastAPI serialise a list rather than set an HTTP status code.

**Root cause.** Missing input validation on an externally-reachable endpoint, plus using a Flask-style `(body, status)` return convention in FastAPI, which does not support it.

**Impact.** Errors would have been reported to callers as HTTP 200 with a two-element list body — an error path that reads as success to the worker.

**Fix.** Added the missing guard and switched error returns to `JSONResponse`.

**→ Rule.** Validate request payloads at every server boundary, and confirm the framework's own error-return convention (`JSONResponse` for FastAPI) — a wrong status code turns every failure into a silent success downstream.

<sub>`D:/00mk/steel project/training/Training/workmen's_diary/2026-08-30.md` · code-bug</sub>

#### 🟡 MEDIUM · 2026-08-31 · load_split() resolved images relative to the script directory instead of the repo root

**What happened.** The loader opened image files relative to wherever the script lived rather than the repository root.

**Root cause.** Implicit relative path resolution instead of an explicit REPO_ROOT anchor.

**Impact.** Images would fail to load whenever the script was invoked from a different working directory; found during the CPU-side merge.

**Fix.** Changed to resolve against an explicit REPO_ROOT constant.

**→ Rule.** Anchor every file lookup to an explicit repo-root constant; never rely on the process working directory or the script's own location.

<sub>`D:/00mk/steel project/training/Training/workmen's_diary/2026-08-31.md` · code-bug</sub>

#### 🟡 MEDIUM · 2026-08-31 · The batch-check guard raised NameError on an already-deleted variable and reported failure after passing

**What happened.** del _b, _b2, _gt referenced _b2 which had already been deleted inside the loop, raising NameError every time and printing 'first batch check failed' even though all three checks had actually passed with visible ticks.

**Root cause.** Cleanup code was not exercised on the success path, so a guard that worked reported failure.

**Impact.** A working guard reported false failures, which erodes trust in guards generally — the diary notes a broken guard is more dangerous than none because people stop believing it.

**Fix.** Removed the duplicate del.

**→ Rule.** Test the guard on the success path too, and treat a guard that cries wolf as a priority bug — a distrusted guard is worse than no guard.

<sub>`D:/00mk/steel project/training/Training/workmen's_diary/2026-08-31.md` · code-bug</sub>

#### 🟡 MEDIUM · 2026-08-31 · UI progress bar could never reach 100% when a job included a gridline page

**What happened.** pass2 total was computed as len(tasks)+1 while the counter only ran 1..len(tasks), so the progress bar could never complete. It was never observed because the e2e test job had no gridline page (job_full.json was exactly 4/4).

**Root cause.** An off-by-one between the total and the counter, hidden because the only test fixture happened to lack the case that triggers it.

**Impact.** Users would see a progress bar stuck below 100% on real jobs containing a grid page.

**Fix.** Fixed the count; npm test 1160/1160.

**→ Rule.** Ensure test fixtures cover the case that changes a computed total — a fixture where the special case is absent will pass an off-by-one forever.

<sub>`D:/00mk/steel project/training/Training/workmen's_diary/2026-08-31.md` · code-bug</sub>

#### 🟡 MEDIUM · 2026-09-01 · UI button relabelled 'Read with Gemini' while the backend actually calls Qwen

**What happened.** Per instruction, the button 'Read Drawing with AI' was renamed to 'Read with Gemini'. The button in fact calls Qwen, not Gemini, so the label is factually wrong to every user. This was flagged to Makham and carried unresolved across at least three subsequent entries.

**Root cause.** A label change was applied as a verbal instruction without checking what the code behind the button actually invokes. Compounded by leaving the known-false label live in the UI while waiting for a decision, instead of reverting to a neutral label.

**Impact.** Users (including judges/demo audiences) are told the wrong model is doing the work. Remained an open item across the whole diary window.

**Fix.** Not fixed — flagged to Makham, still listed as pending in three consecutive entries.

**→ Rule.** Never ship a user-visible label that you know is false while waiting on a decision — revert to a provider-neutral wording ('Read with AI') until the backend actually matches the name.

<sub>`2026-09-01.md` · ui/correctness</sub>

#### 🟡 MEDIUM · 2026-09-01 · Progress UI hid the bar while waiting and never said which pass was running

**What happened.** The progress bar was hidden entirely while waiting for a worker (rather than showing 0%), and the UI never told the user which pass was executing. Makham's direct complaint was that the UI didn't say which pass it was on.

**Root cause.** The UI treated 'no data yet' as 'render nothing' instead of 'render the honest empty state'. With a 75–80 minute job, an invisible progress bar is indistinguishable from a hung system — which is exactly what caused users to restart workers (see the requeue_stale double-run risk).

**Impact.** Users could not tell a running job from a dead one, encouraging duplicate worker launches; direct user complaint.

**Fix.** Progress bar always visible (0% while waiting, elapsed/ETA-based estimate when done/total unknown), plus a prominent 'ตอนนี้: <current step>' line.

**→ Rule.** For any long-running job, the UI must always show a state — 0% plus the current step name beats a hidden bar. An invisible progress indicator on a 75-minute job actively causes duplicate-run bugs.

<sub>`2026-09-01.md` · ui/ux</sub>

#### 🟡 MEDIUM · 2026-09-01 · Adding pass3 made the ETA jump back to hours right when the job was nearly finished

**What happened.** `estimateRemainingSec` checked steps with a chain of individual `if` statements. When `pass3` was added as a new step, `pass2` fell through into the `else` branch and its full duration was counted again — so the ETA spiked back up to hours at the exact moment the job was closest to done.

**Root cause.** Per-step `if` branches instead of ordinal reasoning over the step sequence. The function had no concept of 'steps already passed', so adding any new step at the end broke the classification of every earlier step.

**Impact.** Users were shown a wildly wrong ETA at the most critical moment (near completion), undermining trust in the whole progress display. Caught during development, not shipped.

**Fix.** Rewrote to decide from step ordinal (any step earlier in the sequence contributes 0) plus regression tests (`tests/purson-progress-eta.test.js`, +3 tests).

**→ Rule.** Anything that reasons about pipeline stages must derive from the ordered step list, never from hand-written per-step conditionals — otherwise every new stage silently corrupts the older ones.

<sub>`2026-09-01.md` · logic-bug</sub>

#### 🟡 MEDIUM · 2026-09-01 · 3D structure model rendered ceiling fans, drain pipes and power outlets as structural boxes

**What happened.** `buildStructureModel` drew every element as a box with no type filter, so 41 of 112 pieces in the 3D structural model were ceiling fans, waste pipes, electrical outlets and rooms.

**Root cause.** The 3D builder consumed the full element list without applying the structural-type filter that `structuralWorkPackages()` already used elsewhere — a filter existed in the codebase but was not reused.

**Impact.** A visibly wrong 3D structural model (37% non-structural objects) that would have been shown in demos.

**Fix.** Filtered by `STRUCTURAL_ELEMENT_TYPES` (the same list `structuralWorkPackages()` uses, so the two cannot drift) and returned `skipped_types` so the UI can tell the user what was excluded rather than silently dropping it.

**→ Rule.** Reuse the existing filter list rather than consuming raw collections — and when you drop items, report what you dropped instead of dropping silently.

<sub>`2026-09-01.md` · ui/data-filtering</sub>

#### 🟡 MEDIUM · 2026-09-01 · Beam-only plan pages can never be measured — a beam's box centroid sits on no grid ref

**What happened.** pass3 cannot find anchors on pages containing only beams, because a beam's bounding-box centroid does not correspond to any grid intersection. Measurement only works when footings or columns appear on the same page.

**Root cause.** The anchoring model assumed every element's centroid is a meaningful (pixel, metre) pair. That holds for point elements (footings, columns) but not for linear elements, whose refs describe endpoints, not centres.

**Impact.** Beam plan pages — a major page category — get no measurement at all; confirmed again on house02 where 3 beam pages produced 0 anchors.

**Fix.** Not fixed. Noted that the fix would require using beam endpoints as anchors instead of centroids.

**→ Rule.** Geometric anchoring must respect element topology — a point element and a linear element cannot share the same 'where is it' rule. Check the assumption against each element class before generalising.

<sub>`2026-09-01.md` · algorithm-design</sub>

#### ⚪ LOW · 2026-07-09 · The Single project's header stacked 5 fields as full-width rows, pushing the actual content off-screen

**What happened.** A screenshot of the Single project drew the complaint 'why does this look so awful' — the five header fields (house/page/Sheet/sheet name/Pattern) each occupied a full-width row with large gaps before any JSON content appeared.

**Root cause.** The header markup was written field-by-field with no layout intent, and was never viewed at a real annotator's screen size before being used.

**Impact.** Wasted screen height in the labeling UI, on the surface annotators stare at all day; required a redesign of .hdrbar/.hdrfield in two files.

**Fix.** Laid the five fields out as a single horizontal flex-wrap bar, applied only to single.xml/single-freezeR.xml as explicitly instructed.

**→ Rule.** Screenshot every annotation config at a real working resolution before handing it to annotators — header chrome that eats a third of the viewport is a throughput cost, not a cosmetic one.

<sub>`D:/00mk/steel project/training/Training/workmen's_diary/2026-07-09.md` · ui-design</sub>

#### ⚪ LOW · 2026-07-29 · GPU showed 100% utilisation at only 33.7W — the real bottleneck was CPU offload

**What happened.** Running the 21GB Q4_K_M model on an 8GB card meant only about a third fit in VRAM; the rest ran on CPU. nvidia-smi read 100% utilisation while power draw was just 33.7W, and the log said 'failed to fit params to free device memory ... abort'.

**Root cause.** GPU utilisation percentage counts time-with-work-queued, not work done. With most layers on CPU the GPU spends its time waiting, which registers as busy.

**Impact.** 13-21 minutes per page for full extraction (3.46 tokens/second); a misleading metric could easily have sent optimisation effort at the wrong component.

**Fix.** Cross-checked power draw against utilisation to identify CPU as the true bottleneck; adopted the 2-phase (fast classify then selective extract) design to reduce tokens generated.

**→ Rule.** Never read GPU utilisation alone — pair it with power draw and memory-fit logs. And when generation is the cost, reduce tokens emitted rather than chasing hardware.

<sub>`D:/00mk/steel project/training/Training/workmen's_diary/สอนมะขาม_รวม.md` · performance/diagnosis</sub>

#### ⚪ LOW · 2026-08-25 · House 12 footing plan reports 13 columns where 12 exist — one duplicate box survives NMS

**What happened.** Column detection on house 12's footing plan returns 13 for 12 real columns; one location produces two overlapping boxes that NMS did not merge.

**Root cause.** The NMS suppression radius (half the template dimension) is too small for this particular near-duplicate, so two peaks from the same object both survive.

**Impact.** Small over-count that would propagate into any automated count check built on the tool. Left unfixed as low-impact.

**Fix.** Not fixed — consciously deferred as having little effect on the overall result.

**→ Rule.** Record known off-by-one detection errors explicitly rather than rounding them away; any downstream consumer comparing counts needs to know the tool has a small over-count bias.

<sub>`D:/00mk/steel project/training/Training/workmen's_diary/2026-08-25(teach mk).md` · algorithm</sub>

#### ⚪ LOW · 2026-08-25 · Junk detections sitting 4px outside a beam band escaped the footing-in-beam filter

**What happened.** The filter that drops footing detections falling inside a detected beam band was defeated by junk sitting about 4px outside the band edge.

**Root cause.** The filter used the beam band's exact geometric bounds with no tolerance, while real detection centers land slightly off the ideal band due to matching jitter.

**Impact.** False footing detections survived the filter on beam pages.

**Fix.** Widened the beam band in the footing-in-beam filter by 10px, and made the page-type hint in cv_scan tolerate single-digit false positives (beam-plan-like when f<=2).

**→ Rule.** A geometric exclusion filter needs a tolerance margin sized to the detector's own positional jitter. An exact-bounds filter always leaks at the edge.

<sub>`D:/00mk/steel project/training/Training/workmen's_diary/2026-08-25.md` · off-by-margin</sub>

#### ⚪ LOW · 2026-08-28 · Variable `h` shadowed in the mining script — house name became a box height

**What happened.** In the template-mining script, the variable `h` was shadowed, so a house name ended up being used where a bounding-box height was expected.

**Root cause.** Single-letter variable name reused for two different meanings in overlapping scopes, with no type checking to catch a string flowing into a numeric slot.

**Impact.** Corrupted mining output until caught.

**Fix.** Renamed/fixed the shadowing.

**→ Rule.** Do not reuse single-letter names across scopes in scripts that mix strings and numbers. A one-character name is not worth the class of bug it enables.

<sub>`D:/00mk/steel project/training/Training/workmen's_diary/2026-08-28.md` · bug</sub>

#### ⚪ LOW · 2026-08-29 · cv_scan --demo self-check broke on our own format change ("4." → "4)")

**What happened.** The prompt-hygiene sweep changed numbered list markers from "4." to "4)" (removing the forbidden `.` character), which broke cv_scan.py's `--demo` self-check assertion that still expected "4.".

**Root cause.** A self-check assertion was written against a literal formatting detail of the output rather than its semantic content, so a deliberate cosmetic change broke the test.

**Impact.** The self-check — the tool's own safety net — was broken by us. Small, but if it had been noticed later it would have looked like a real regression.

**Fix.** Updated the assertion.

**→ Rule.** Write self-check assertions against semantic content, not literal formatting. When running a repo-wide character sweep, re-run every self-check afterwards — the sweep will break some of them.

<sub>`D:/00mk/steel project/training/Training/workmen's_diary/2026-08-29.md` · bug</sub>

#### ⚪ LOW · 2026-08-29 · Accidentally introduced a forbidden `**` while writing the very prompt cleanup that removes them

**What happened.** During the prompt-hygiene work that strips `.` `_` `*` `#` `:` `;` `\` `|` `—` from prompts, one `**` was accidentally typed into a new prompt block. The repeat character scan across 1218 text blocks caught it before render.

**Root cause.** Markdown emphasis is muscle memory when writing prose, and the forbidden set includes markdown's own syntax characters. Nothing prevented writing them — only a post-hoc scan detected them.

**Impact.** Caught before it reached the dataset. Would otherwise have shipped exactly the character the cleanup exists to remove.

**Fix.** Fixed before render; the scan is now run after every rebuild (1218 blocks, 0 violations).

**→ Rule.** When a rule bans characters that are also your editor's default syntax, the automated scan is not optional — run it after every single edit, including edits made by the rule's own author.

<sub>`D:/00mk/steel project/training/Training/workmen's_diary/2026-08-29.md` · bug</sub>

#### ⚪ LOW · 2026-08-30 · A hand-written selftest assertion was itself wrong, briefly implicating `strip_fence` as buggy

**What happened.** While running the new `--selftest` on `infer_house_t04.py`, one assertion failed. Investigation showed the assertion itself was written incorrectly, not `strip_fence`.

**Root cause.** The test expectation was authored from assumption rather than from the function's documented/observed behaviour.

**Impact.** Small — a short detour investigating a non-existent bug in production logic.

**Fix.** Fixed the assertion; all 5 pure-logic functions then passed without a GPU.

**→ Rule.** When a new test fails on ported, previously-working code, suspect the test before the code — verify the expected value against the original implementation's real output.

<sub>`D:/00mk/steel project/training/Training/workmen's_diary/2026-08-30.md` · code-bug</sub>

#### ⚪ LOW · 2026-08-31 · bash reported 'unbound variable' for arguments that were passed, due to local declarations on one line under set -u

**What happened.** With set -u, `local a=$1 b=$2 c=$a/${b}...` on a single line reported an unbound variable for the later name even though all arguments were supplied — variables declared with local on the same line are not yet visible to each other until that local statement completes.

**Root cause.** A bash scoping subtlety in combination with set -u.

**Impact.** The page-processing queue failed to launch until diagnosed.

**Fix.** Split each local onto its own line; confirmed with bash -x tracing rather than guessing.

**→ Rule.** Declare each `local` on its own line in bash, especially under set -u, and confirm shell bugs with bash -x rather than reasoning about them.

<sub>`D:/00mk/steel project/training/Training/workmen's_diary/2026-08-31.md` · code-bug</sub>

**What happened.** Three UI files assigned to window.x unconditionally, so importing them in a test environment failed.

**Root cause.** Missing the repo's existing guard convention for window attachments.

**Impact.** The affected code could not be tested at all until fixed.

**Fix.** Applied the repo's existing convention (as used at bbs-index.js:1495).

**→ Rule.** Follow the repo's existing guard convention for global attachments so every module remains importable in a test environment.
