## T11 — Git, Repo Hygiene & Lost Artifacts

*Commits, branches, merges, and work products that were never saved or came back from the dead.*

**19 entries** · 2 critical · 3 high

#### 🔴 CRITICAL · 2026-07-10 · Someone force-rewrote the whole Constistant repo history, forcing a local hard reset

**What happened.** A git divergent-history incident occurred earlier in the same day's session: the entire history of the Constistant repo had been force-rewritten upstream, and the local main had to be reset to match origin/main. It was judged unrelated to the raw_json work and deliberately not logged in detail.

**Root cause.** A force-push rewrote published history, which every other clone then diverges from; no notice or coordination is recorded.

**Impact.** A forced hard reset of local main, with any local-only commits on that branch at risk; the incident's details were never written down, so its cause remains unknown.

**Fix.** Reset local main to origin/main.

**→ Rule.** Never force-push a shared branch; and when it happens anyway, record what was rewritten and what local work was discarded — 'not related to today's task' is exactly how the cause gets lost.

<sub>`D:/00mk/steel project/training/Training/workmen's_diary/2026-07-10.md` · git/process</sub>

#### 🔴 CRITICAL · 2026-07-11 · Reading pages 50-51 in parallel then writing from memory swapped data between three BOQ sheets

**What happened.** Pages 50 and 51 of house #2 were read in parallel and written up afterwards. The steel-roof-structure data from page 50 (sheet 3/19) was written into the roof-covering file (sheet 5/19); sheet 5/19's real data was never written at all; and sheet 6/19 (ceiling work) was left blank on the belief it was unreadable, when the data existed and had simply been misfiled.

**Root cause.** Multiple visually similar BOQ tables were held in working memory across several page reads before any of them was committed to disk, so page identity was lost between reading and writing.

**Impact.** Three ground-truth files wrong at once — one containing another page's data, one empty that should have had data, one falsely marked unreadable — in the dataset intended for fine-tuning.

**Fix.** Re-read pages 50 and 51 separately from scratch, rewrote all three files correctly, and recorded a warning in each fixed file explaining the cause.

**→ Rule.** Read one page and write its file before reading the next — never batch reads and write from memory afterwards, especially for repetitive tables like BOQ sheets where pages look alike.

<sub>`D:/00mk/steel project/training/Training/workmen's_diary/2026-07-11.md` · extraction-accuracy</sub>

#### 🟠 HIGH · 2026-07-07 · An entire pipeline folder existed as a stale duplicate in a second repo for 5 days

**What happened.** Constistant/No_touch_box/ turned out to be a full copy of the Training repo's pipeline folder frozen at a July 2 snapshot — missing mk_test/, the Label Studio Makham configs, and carrying an older CLAUDE.md. One of its files (label-studio-tasks.js) was a pre-bugfix version still pointing at the old single-path qwen-output location.

**Root cause.** Work was propagated between the two repos by copying folders instead of designating one owner repo per artifact, so the copy silently stopped receiving updates the moment the original moved on.

**Impact.** Five days of divergence; a deprecated buggy script sitting on disk where someone could have run it; a multi-round cleanup (July 7 twice, plus still-unfinished remainder) spent just proving the duplicate had no unique content.

**Fix.** Diffed each file against its Training-repo twin (3 identical byte-for-byte, 1 clearly older), then deleted rule_of_tune.md and the 4 Label Studio files; the rest of the folder was left pending a decision.

**→ Rule.** Every artifact has exactly one owning repo. If a file must be visible from two repos, link or reference it — never cp it, because a copy is a fork that nobody remembers to merge.

<sub>`D:/00mk/steel project/training/Training/workmen's_diary/2026-07-07.md` · process/repo-hygiene</sub>

#### 🟠 HIGH · 2026-07-10 · Four days of work (t4 onward) went uncommitted, still pending as of July 11

**What happened.** From the t4 round onward, nothing was committed. The pending list on July 9 said 'nothing has been committed at all since the t4 round', July 10 repeated it as 'pending for several days now', and July 11 still listed it — spanning the schema rewrite, the generator fixes, five XML configs, three houses of raw JSON, and the raw/ rename incident.

**Root cause.** Commits were deferred to a single end-of-work sweep, while each day added more unrelated changes and at least one incident (the raw/ rename) that touched the same working tree.

**Impact.** Days of irreplaceable extraction work living only in an uncommitted working tree, in a repo whose history was force-rewritten in the same window; and a growing commit that will mix a rename incident, config fixes and three houses of data together.

**Fix.** Not fixed — still on the pending list at the end of July 11.

**→ Rule.** Commit at the end of every work session, scoped to that session — an uncommitted backlog is both an unrecoverable-loss risk and a guarantee that the eventual commit will be unreviewable.

<sub>`D:/00mk/steel project/training/Training/workmen's_diary/2026-07-10.md` · git/process</sub>

#### 🟠 HIGH · 2026-09-02 · Work committed to `main` was invisible to Makham, who was working on the diverged `Presentation-demo` branch

**What happened.** The house09 results were committed to `main`, but Makham works on `Presentation-demo`. He went looking for the house09 files through GO.bat and could not find them, because the two branches have separate histories with a different merge-base and were never merged.

**Root cause.** Two long-lived branches diverged with no merge plan and no agreement about which is the working branch. Output was committed to a branch the actual user was not on, with nothing surfacing the mismatch.

**Impact.** Makham could not find deliverables he had just asked for; required a manual copy of all 17 files to `D:\000download\09` outside git as a workaround, and left an unresolved merge decision hanging.

**Fix.** Files copied out to `D:\000download\09` as a backup outside the repo; the merge itself was recorded as an open decision.

**→ Rule.** Agree on one working branch before committing deliverables, and if branches must diverge, decide the merge point immediately — do not let 'we'll merge later' persist while output lands where the user cannot see it.

<sub>`2026-09-02.md` · process/git</sub>

#### 🟡 MEDIUM · 2026-07-08 · t3 recorded the roof slope as 9 degrees; the drawing says 6

**What happened.** A t4 agent re-reading pages 1-9 read page 07's roof slope as 6 degrees, conflicting with t3's 9. Cross-checking pages 06 and 08, where the digit prints more clearly, confirmed 6 — the agent correctly did not follow t3's lead.

**Root cause.** A single ambiguous glyph on one page was recorded without cross-checking the same value on the other pages that also carry it.

**Impact.** A wrong roof slope in the t3 dataset; caught only because t4 was a genuine fresh read rather than a migration.

**Fix.** Corrected to 6 degrees, verified against two other pages.

**→ Rule.** Any value printed on more than one sheet must be read from the clearest sheet and cross-checked; and a re-extraction round must never be allowed to see the previous round's answer.

<sub>`D:/00mk/steel project/training/Training/workmen's_diary/2026-07-08.md` · extraction-accuracy</sub>

#### 🟡 MEDIUM · 2026-07-10 · Pages predicted from the table of contents to be site-plan criteria were something else entirely

**What happened.** The page-to-sheet mapping predicted pages 70-72 would continue the site-plan criteria; they were actually a working-committee roster and a price comparison table across all 10 house designs, plus a drawing-set cover. The agent noticed and classified them as unknown/title rather than forcing them into notes.

**Root cause.** The page mapping was derived from the table of contents and treated as authoritative for content, but the real document contains back-matter the ToC does not describe.

**Impact.** Would have produced mis-typed data on 3 pages and polluted the notes pattern with a price table; caught because the agent read the pages rather than trusting the plan.

**Fix.** Reclassified those pages by what they actually contain; the same pattern was later confirmed on house #3.

**→ Rule.** A table-of-contents mapping predicts structure, not content — every page must be classified from the page itself, and an agent must be allowed to contradict the plan it was given.

<sub>`D:/00mk/steel project/training/Training/workmen's_diary/2026-07-10.md` · extraction-accuracy</sub>

#### 🟡 MEDIUM · 2026-07-16 · House 7's price misread as 1,572,000 instead of 1,528,000

**What happened.** During the house-4 cross-house price check, house 7's price had been recorded as 1,572,000; houses 2 and 3 both read 1,528,000, and the cross-check confirmed the latter.

**Root cause.** Digit-level misreading of a small table entry with no same-sheet reference-glyph comparison — the same failure mode that later produced the much larger ๑/๙ price-table incident.

**Impact.** A wrong price in the dataset until the cross-house check caught it; part of a pattern of three digit errors found across two rounds.

**Fix.** Corrected to 1,528,000 across every related file.

**→ Rule.** Small-print numeric tables need a cross-source check as a standard step, not an occasional one — the cross-house tie-break technique found three digit errors in two rounds and should run on every house.

<sub>`2026-07-16.md` · data-extraction</sub>

#### 🟡 MEDIUM · 2026-07-28 · House 07 S-05: BS1's position recorded as 1.1 m below grid C when it is ~2.1 m

**What happened.** The mid-bay beam BS1 had been extracted at 1.1 m below grid line C; the real offset is approximately 2.1 m — a one-metre error, plausibly a transposed leading digit.

**Root cause.** A single-digit misread with no cross-check against the bay's total dimension, which would have shown the position to be inconsistent.

**Impact.** A one-metre position error on a structural member, affecting layout and any span derived from it.

**Fix.** Corrected during the zoom-on-every-point pass, reversal recorded.

**→ Rule.** Sanity-check every offset against the enclosing bay dimension — an offset that does not fit inside its bay, or that leaves an implausible remainder, is a digit error.

<sub>`D:/00mk/steel project/training/Training/workmen's_diary/2026-07-28.md` · data-extraction</sub>

#### 🟡 MEDIUM · 2026-08-20 · King-try's 12 commits (overlay prototype, hooks, skills, agent) stayed stranded — nothing cherry-picked, decision deferred across sessions

**What happened.** On 08-18 the recommendation was to cherry-pick the overlay prototype plus the hooks/skills/agent onto `main` rather than merge (the 277-commit gap makes a real merge messy). On 08-20 the same work was reviewed again, three of its bugs catalogued, and still 'nothing was cherry-picked onto `main` this session'. The gap widens with every commit to main.

**Root cause.** The decision was logged as 'left pending' twice without an owner or deadline, while main continued moving away from the branch.

**Impact.** A working Gemini overlay prototype with a proven 24/24 result, two safety hooks, two skills and a review agent remain unavailable on main; the same three tooling bugs had to be re-described in a second session because the code was never brought over.

**Fix.** Not fixed — still pending as of the 08-20 entry.

**→ Rule.** A divergent branch holding wanted work is a decaying asset: cherry-pick the wanted commits in the same session they are reviewed, or the review has to be repeated and the gap only grows.

<sub>`D:/00mk/steel project/training/Training/workmen's_diary/2026-08-20.md` · branch-management</sub>

#### 🟡 MEDIUM · 2026-08-31 · Output correctness is enforced by post-hoc filtering rather than by grammar at generation time

**What happened.** Malformed keys and impossible values are currently caught by sanitize_elements() after the fact; full per-subtask xgrammar schema enforcement was not implemented.

**Root cause.** Grammar enforcement was deferred while the more urgent decoding bug was fixed.

**Impact.** Bad output is discarded rather than prevented, so data is lost rather than corrected and reading accuracy is unimproved.

**Fix.** Not fixed — queued as a next action.

**→ Rule.** Constrain generation with a schema grammar at source rather than filtering downstream; filtering removes garbage but never recovers the information that was lost.

<sub>`D:/00mk/steel project/training/Training/workmen's_diary/2026-08-31.md` · tech-debt</sub>

#### ⚪ LOW · 2026-07-05 · A killed agent left a scratch file in the ground-truth folder that was never cleaned up

**What happened.** _PROGRESS_NOTES_pages38-47.md was a scratch file from agent 4's incomplete BOQ work. The agent was meant to delete it once done, but was killed first, so it was left sitting in mk_test/ — a folder that otherwise contains only ground-truth JSON.

**Root cause.** Cleanup was assigned to the agent as its own last step, so any abnormal termination guarantees the scratch file survives. Temporary files were also written into the same directory as authoritative data.

**Impact.** A non-ground-truth markdown file sits inside the ground-truth folder, at risk of being picked up by any glob-based consumer or mistaken for real output. Deletion was still listed as an outstanding item.

**Fix.** Not fixed — kept deliberately because it documents the crop/page-number pattern method needed to resume pages 38-47, with deletion listed as pending item #6.

**→ Rule.** Write scratch and progress files to a separate scratch directory, never into the data directory. Cleanup that only happens on the agent's happy path is not cleanup — assume abnormal termination as the default case.

<sub>`D:/00mk/steel project/training/Training/workmen's_diary/2026-07-05.md` · cleanup-failure</sub>

#### ⚪ LOW · 2026-07-05 · Repo accumulated empty scaffolding folders, empty files, temp scripts and duplicate test directories

**What happened.** Phase A cleanup deleted a schema/ folder containing 9 empty directories, an empty hetad.md, tmp-bbs-*.js scratch scripts and price/test.csv*, moved a test fixture out of the repo root into tests/fixtures/, and merged a stray test/ folder into tests/ — plus moved an SQL comment block that was living inside schema.js into database/resource_hub_tables.sql.

**Root cause.** Scaffolding was created ahead of the code that would fill it, temp files were written to the repo root rather than a scratch directory, and two test directories with near-identical names were allowed to coexist — which is what let a whole test file go unrun.

**Impact.** Navigational noise, and one concrete consequence: the split test/ vs tests/ directories contributed directly to the npm-test-scope bug where an entire suite had never executed. Empty scaffolding also misleads readers about what is implemented.

**Fix.** All of it deleted or relocated as part of Phase A, with the test fixture moved to tests/fixtures/ and test/ merged into tests/.

**→ Rule.** Do not create scaffolding before the code that fills it, never write temp files to the repo root, and never allow two directories whose names differ only by a plural — that pair silently splits tooling scope.

<sub>`D:/00mk/steel project/training/Training/workmen's_diary/2026-07-05.md` · repo-hygiene</sub>

#### ⚪ LOW · 2026-07-08 · The cancelled migration script was left on disk with no owner and no decision

**What happened.** migrate_t3_to_t4.js survived the deletion of everything it produced and sat in the main folder as an unused file; whether to delete or keep it was still an open pending item a day later, and it was finally swept into trash/ on July 9.

**Root cause.** The cancellation order named the output folder, not the tooling that produced it, and nothing in the process cleans up code whose output was discarded.

**Impact.** A runnable script that would regenerate the exact data that was deliberately deleted, sitting where someone could run it; two days of pending-list noise.

**Fix.** Moved into trash/ during the July 9 file cleanup.

**→ Rule.** When output is discarded, delete or quarantine the tool that produced it in the same action — leaving it runnable is an invitation to recreate the mistake.

<sub>`D:/00mk/steel project/training/Training/workmen's_diary/2026-07-08.md` · process/repo-hygiene</sub>

#### ⚪ LOW · 2026-07-09 · An 11-file trash/ holding folder sits inside the repo, not gitignored

**What happened.** Eleven retired files (pre-Makham configs, old task JSON, first-round experiments, migrate_t3_to_t4.js) were moved into a folder named trash/ inside the repo, which is not in .gitignore and would be committed along with everything else.

**Root cause.** A quarantine folder was created without deciding its git status, in a repo that already had many days of uncommitted work waiting to be swept up in one commit.

**Impact.** Retired files would be committed into repo history, in a repo that also holds protected raw-JSON training data; the decision was still open at the end of the day.

**Fix.** Not fixed — recorded as a pending decision: .gitignore it or commit it deliberately.

**→ Rule.** Decide a quarantine folder's git status at the moment you create it — the default is that it gets committed, and a large uncommitted backlog makes that easy to miss.

<sub>`D:/00mk/steel project/training/Training/workmen's_diary/2026-07-09.md` · process/repo-hygiene</sub>

#### ⚪ LOW · 2026-07-28 · The only copy of the working 61-page inference driver lives in a scratchpad, not in the repo with the results it produced

**What happened.** The house-01 inference run produced results committed to tune_ai/t01/ผล/, but the script that produced them — resumable, skipping already-done pages, and carrying the hard-won llama-server flags (--parallel 1 --ubatch-size 2048 --ctx-size 16384) — was left in the scratchpad. The run is stopped at page 2 of 61 and explicitly marked resumable, so this script is needed again.

**Fix.** Not fixed — recorded only as 'the script is in the scratchpad'.

**→ Rule.** A script that produced committed results is a work product; commit it next to them, especially when the run is explicitly resumable.

**What happened.** manifest.json, review.html, pdf-processor.py and qwen-processor.js are all one older generation, superseded by run_pipeline.py + build_document_map.py, which CLAUDE.md's Architecture section already tells people to use instead. The question of whether the whole generation is dead was raised at round 8 and left unanswered at session close.

#### ⚪ LOW · 2026-08-29 · Dead TARGET/ELEMENT_TYPES substitution logic lived on in the dataset builder

**What happened.** build_dataset_t03.py still carried TARGET and ELEMENT_TYPES substitution code, though ELEMENT_TYPES had never actually been present in the real prompt. PLAN_SUBTASKS' `target` key was likewise read by nobody.

**Root cause.** When the prompt template was replaced by four real rendered files, the substitution machinery that served the template was left behind. Dead code in a dataset builder is invisible because it produces no error.

**Impact.** Misleading code suggesting a substitution mechanism that never worked, in the file most critical to dataset correctness — the same file that had just been found silently emitting 0 examples for three subtasks.

**Fix.** Deleted the substitution logic and the unused target key; PLAN_SUBTASKS reduced to types/type_regex for GT element filtering. Dataset rebuild confirmed 989 examples, no regression.

**→ Rule.** Delete the machinery when you delete its reason to exist. Dead substitution code in a data pipeline is worse than dead code elsewhere — it implies a transformation is happening when nothing is.

## T12 — Documentation, Naming & Communication

*Docs that lied, names that misled, and warnings that were never escalated.*

**34 entries** · 3 critical · 7 high

#### 🔴 CRITICAL · 2026-07-21 · Known permanent-data-loss risk was never raised as a hard-block warning

**What happened.** The risk that destroying the instance would permanently delete the results was known from the moment the GGUF conversion finished, but was only mentioned as a soft plan item ('HuggingFace hasn't been uploaded yet, will do it later') — never as an explicit 'do not shut down before backing up' block.

**Root cause.** Irreversible-risk communication was folded into a to-do list instead of being escalated to a blocking warning; deferred tasks and destructive-risk warnings were treated as the same category of message.

**Impact.** Directly enabled the total loss above; recorded as a 'Mark of Shame' rule in rule_of_tune.md.

**Fix.** Added a standing rule: any risk that can permanently destroy data must be stated as a separate, explicit hard-block warning.

**→ Rule.** Separate destructive-risk warnings from ordinary to-dos — state them standalone, in plain language, immediately before the moment the risk becomes live.

<sub>`D:/00mk/steel project/training/Training/workmen's_diary/2026-07-21.md` · communication</sub>

#### 🔴 CRITICAL · 2026-07-24 · Files were lost on the rented GPU because the 'not backed up yet' warning was phrased softly instead of as a blocking stop

**What happened.** On 2026-07-21 work was lost on a rented machine. The diary's post-mortem is explicit that this was not a code bug: the assistant mentioned that files were not yet backed up in a soft, passing way rather than raising it as a firm blocking warning, so nobody acted on it before the instance went away.

**Root cause.** Risk communication had no severity tier. A destructive-risk condition (unbacked-up work on ephemeral rented hardware) was delivered in the same register as ordinary progress commentary, so the human reader could not distinguish 'FYI' from 'stop now'.

**Impact.** Work on the rented instance was lost; the whole of 2026-07-24 was spent building and running a Phase 0 pre-flight regime specifically to prevent a repeat — a full day of unplanned process work.

**Fix.** Became Rule 4 in rule_of_tune.md and the origin of the 'Phase 0' pre-rental checklist in RETUNE_WORKFLOW.md; backups must be verified before anything ephemeral is torn down.

**→ Rule.** Anything that can destroy unrecoverable work must be stated as a hard blocking stop with the word STOP, never as a soft aside. If the consequence is irreversible, refuse to proceed rather than mention it in passing.

#### 🔴 CRITICAL · 2026-08-21 · The notes → Constistant path produces nothing: the adapter reads fields the schema never defined

**What happened.** raw-extraction-adapter.js reads notes.fc_ksc / fy_main_ksc / fy_stirrup_ksc / cover_mm to build extractedNotes, but primary_rawjson_schema.md never defines that shape. fc_ksc appears nowhere in the spec and in exactly 1 of 55 real notes files. So the project-wide concrete and steel specification never reaches the pipeline for essentially any house.

**Root cause.** The consumer was written against a hoped-for field shape rather than against the spec, and the spec was never updated to match. Nothing checks that fields an adapter reads actually exist in the schema, so a whole data path can read undefined fields and return empty forever without erroring.

**Impact.** Concrete grade, steel grade and cover — the project-wide material specification — reach the BOQ pipeline for at most 1 of 55 notes files, i.e. essentially never. Silent since the adapter was written.

**Fix.** Makham chose 'define the fields in the spec' over changing the consumer. New §4a added: a nested layer recording what the drawing prints (concrete{}, steel{round_bar{},deformed_bar{}}, cover{default_mm,by_condition[]}) plus four flat one-way aliases (fc_ksc/fy_main_ksc/fy_stirrup_ksc/cover_mm) so the adapter needs no change. Migrating the 55 existing files remains pending.

**→ Rule.** Every field an adapter reads must exist in the spec — add a test that cross-checks adapter field reads against the schema, because an adapter reading undefined fields fails silently by returning empty, which looks identical to 'this house has no notes'.

#### 🟠 HIGH · 2026-07-10 · Condensing the schema silently dropped 3 real operational rules

**What happened.** A section-by-section comparison of primary_rawjson_schema.md against the 219-line original found three genuine rules missing, not deliberately trimmed history: the automation scope (run_pipeline.py auto-extracts only 6 of 13 patterns), the atomic-segment rule (beams must be reported per grid span, never pre-aggregated), and the open question about element_id colliding across section files.

**Root cause.** The condensation was done by rewriting rather than by mapping the source section-by-section, so omissions were invisible until an explicit diff was performed.

**Impact.** The live schema — the file that drives every future house extraction — was missing the beam atomicity rule and the automation-scope boundary; had it not been diffed, every subsequent house would have been extracted against an incomplete contract.

**Fix.** Compared section by section against the full original and added all three rules back.

**→ Rule.** After condensing any spec, diff it back against the original section by section and prove nothing operational was lost — a rewrite cannot be trusted to have kept what it does not mention.

#### 🟠 HIGH · 2026-07-21 · Called the GGUF 'ready to use' when it could not read images at all

**What happened.** The quantized GGUF was described as ready to use even though the mmproj/vision component was missing, i.e. it could not perform the one function the entire project exists for (reading construction drawings).

**Root cause.** Status was reported on pipeline completion ('the conversion ran') instead of on capability ('the artifact does the job'), overstating readiness.

**Impact.** Created a false sense that a usable deliverable existed — which contributed to the decision to shut the instance down.

**Fix.** Corrected in the diary and added as a rule: never call a result ready when it cannot perform its primary function.

**→ Rule.** Report readiness against the artifact's primary function, verified by an actual end-to-end run, not against the fact that the build/convert step exited 0.

#### 🟠 HIGH · 2026-07-21 · Assistant warned too weakly about the missing backup and declared the model ready while it could not read images

**What happened.** The 07-21 loss was attributed not to a code bug but to two communication failures: the backup warning was phrased mildly instead of as a stop-the-line alert, and the artifact was described as ready to use although its vision path was known not to work.

**Root cause.** Severity of a warning was not matched to the irreversibility of the action it guarded; and 'ready' was reported against the steps completed rather than against the actual project goal (reading drawings).

**Impact.** Directly enabled the irreversible loss of a day's work, and set a wrong expectation about what the GGUF could do.

**Fix.** Established Phase 0 pre-rental checks and the rule that documented checklists must be actually executed, not merely written.

**→ Rule.** Scale warning strength to irreversibility — anything that destroys data gets a blocking confirmation. And never report a deliverable as ready against completed steps; report it against the capability the user actually needs.

#### 🟠 HIGH · 2026-07-28 · Workflow files for different tuning rounds shared the same name, so a previous round's ✅ could be mistaken for this round's completion

**What happened.** Both rounds' workflow documents were called RETUNE_WORKFLOW.md-style names. Reading a ticked checkbox from an earlier round recreates the belief that the current round's work is finished — the exact mechanism behind the DAY OF SHAME incident.

**Root cause.** Round identity was carried only by directory path, not by filename or document header, so a file opened out of context gave no signal about which round its checkmarks belonged to.

**Impact.** A live risk of a false 'finished' conclusion — the same failure class that already cost the team a lost round.

**Fix.** git mv to t01_workflow.md / t02_workflow.md preserving history; both headers now state the round, the status, and a warning that a ✅ belongs to whichever round it is in; the naming convention added as a rule.

**→ Rule.** Name per-round artefacts with the round in the filename and restate the round in the document header. A status marker must carry its own scope, since it will be read out of context.

#### 🟠 HIGH · 2026-08-21 · The vertical axis had no field anywhere in the schema despite levels being printed on every elevation and section

**What happened.** z-levels such as +3.75 ระดับหลังคาน, +0.60 ระดับพื้นชั้น 1 and ±0.00 ระดับอ้างอิง are printed on every elevation and section in the set, yet the schema had no field for them at all — x_lines/y_lines are plan axes only. Discovered when Makham instructed 'make the grid master record every value it finds on every page'.

**Root cause.** The schema's grid model was built entirely from plan-view thinking (two horizontal axes) and nobody checked it against a section or elevation sheet. Compounded by the earlier assumption that elevations were low-value.

**Impact.** Every house extracted to date recorded zero vertical levels. Floor heights and beam soffit levels — needed for any volume or 3D reconstruction — were never captured, across the whole dataset.

**Fix.** Added z_levels[] under grid{} in primary_rawjson_schema.md §4, extended dimension_chains[] to the z axis, added unassigned_dimensions[] as the catch-all, and added two §0 checklist items so check_format.py enforces it.

**→ Rule.** Audit the schema against one sheet of every drawing type before locking it — an entire missing axis is the kind of gap that survives 22 houses because nothing ever asks for it.

#### 🟠 HIGH · 2026-08-25 · Teaching PDF shipped a wrong claim that raising MAX_LENGTH requires renting a bigger card

**What happened.** The teaching document written at 15:00 said §2.3 "MAX_LENGTH เพิ่มได้ แต่ต้องเช่าการ์ดใหญ่ขึ้น = จ่ายแพงขึ้น". The VRAM decomposition done an hour later showed 79.7 of 87.5 GB does not scale with sequence length at all, so +32% resolution fits the existing card with 4.0 GB spare and no extra cost. The document had gone stale inside the same session.

**Root cause.** A conclusion was written into a durable document before the measurement that would decide it had been done, and the document had no mechanism linking it back to the numbers it depended on.

**Impact.** A factually wrong cost claim in a document Makham may show his professor — it would have argued for spending money that is not needed.

**Fix.** Corrected §2.3 immediately rather than deferring, and added §2.3.1/§2.3.2 with the real 100%-downscale measurement and the VRAM decomposition. PDF regenerated 12 → 19 pages, verified by extracting text back out and checking six markers.

**→ Rule.** Do not write a conclusion into a shareable document ahead of the measurement that decides it. If a doc is published before the data lands, put a dated "unmeasured" marker on the claim so it cannot be read as fact.

#### 🟠 HIGH · 2026-08-25 · Five BBS minimum-rebar values were slated to cite มยผ. 1103-64, which contains no design minimums at all

**What happened.** Ton ordered the BBS fallback's third gate (assumeRebarFromRules) to cite มยผ. 1103 for accuracy. Reading all 20 pages of the real document showed มยผ. 1103-64 is a materials and workmanship standard (มอก. / cutting / bending / hooks / lapping / testing) and contains none of the five design-minimum reinforcement values.

**Root cause.** The standard was assumed to cover design minimums based on its subject area (rebar) without anyone having read its scope. Rebar materials standards and rebar design standards are different documents.

**Impact.** Would have shipped five values falsely attributed to a Thai standard that does not contain them — a citation error in engineering output.

**Fix.** Kept the ACI values and flagged `dpt1103: 'not_found'` on every row, with a Thai label appended to each `label_th` making the non-attribution explicit in the UI.

**→ Rule.** Read a standard's scope before citing it. A standard covering the same material can cover a completely different aspect of it — and a false citation is worse than an honest foreign one.

#### 🟡 MEDIUM · 2026-07-06 · Label Studio showing '↳ reads as: undefined' was investigated as a code bug when the real cause was stale imported task data

**What happened.** A screenshot showed the grid_ref hint rendering as 'undefined'. Investigation confirmed it was not a code bug — the regenerated task JSON already had `grid_ref_display` present on every item (verified directly with node -e). The actual cause was that Label Studio was still serving the previously imported task JSON, from before the field existed.

**Root cause.** Label Studio holds an immutable snapshot of task data at import time; changing the generator and re-running it does not update tasks already in the project. Nothing in the workflow made that separation visible, so a data-staleness symptom presented as a template/code symptom.

**Impact.** Debugging time spent chasing a non-existent code defect, plus an unnecessary regeneration cycle. This is the second staleness-shaped Label Studio failure the same day (the other being config-vs-task import order).

**Fix.** Confirmed the generated JSON was correct, then instructed re-import of the latest task JSON (delete old tasks or create a new project) rather than editing code.

**→ Rule.** In any system where data is imported as a snapshot (Label Studio tasks, seeded fixtures, caches), check whether the consumer is holding stale data before reading a single line of the generator's code. Verify the artifact on disk first — that check is one command and eliminates the whole class.

#### 🟡 MEDIUM · 2026-08-21 · Printed dimensions with nothing sitting on them (edge-to-first-grid offsets) were silently dropped by the dummy-grid rule

**What happened.** The existing beam-endpoint-only dummy-grid rule silently dropped edge-to-first-grid offsets such as the 1.30 printed before grid 1, because nothing sits on them. A new dimension_chains[] array was added under the gridline pattern's grid{} container to capture every printed dimension segment verbatim.

**Root cause.** The dummy-grid rule was defined by what elements need (an endpoint to anchor to) rather than by what the drawing prints. Any printed value with no element on it therefore had no home in the schema and was discarded without a warning.

**Impact.** Every house extracted before this change lost its edge offsets — a real geometric loss that cannot be recovered without re-reading the sheets. No warning was emitted, so the loss was invisible.

**Fix.** Added the Dimension chain subsection under §4 of primary_rawjson_schema.md capturing every printed dimension segment verbatim, including edge offsets.

**→ Rule.** Schema fields must be defined by what the drawing prints, not by what the current consumer needs — and any value the extractor decides not to record must go into a catch-all array with a warning, never be dropped silently.

**Root cause.** Documentation held a hard-coded path to a file that was renamed, with no link check tying the two together.

**Impact.** A rule that cannot be followed because its reference is dead — degrading the credibility of the rules file itself.

**Fix.** Changed to point at 'that round's own document' instead of a fixed path, and the naming convention added as a rule.

**→ Rule.** Reference documents by role ('that round's own workflow'), not by a fixed path, so a rename can't silently break the rule. And re-check every cross-reference in the same commit as a rename.

<sub>`D:/00mk/steel project/training/Training/workmen's_diary/2026-07-28.md` · documentation</sub>

#### ⚪ LOW · 2026-07-28 · A correct token count of 5,100 would have been read as a failure because the documentation stated the expected value as 5,120

**What happened.** Measuring real images with Qwen3-VL's own smart_resize formula gave 5,100 tokens per image, not the documented 5,120 — the difference is rounding to a multiple of 32. Without updating the document, an operator seeing 5,100 during Phase 5 would have diagnosed a failure.

**Root cause.** An expected value was documented as an idealised round number rather than the value the real formula produces, creating a built-in false-positive for anyone checking against it.

**Impact.** Caught pre-rental. Would otherwise have caused a false failure diagnosis at Phase 5 on paid time.

**Fix.** Phase 5 updated to state 5,100 explicitly, with the reason.

**→ Rule.** Document expected values as the number the real computation actually produces, including rounding artefacts — and state why. An idealised expected value manufactures false alarms.

<sub>`D:/00mk/steel project/training/Training/workmen's_diary/2026-07-28.md` · documentation</sub>

#### ⚪ LOW · 2026-08-18 · Grid master hit a dummy-grid naming case the spec had no rule for, decided ad hoc

**What happened.** House 24's grid master had two dummy grid lines anchored to the same named grid 1 from opposite sides — one before it, one between it and grid 2 — and the second had no printed dimension at all (recorded pos_m: null). The existing naming scheme only covered one gap, so a scheme spanning both sides of a named grid had to be invented on the spot with no prior spec precedent.

**Root cause.** The dummy-grid naming rule in the spec was written from the cases seen in the first few houses and never generalized to 'a named grid can have dummies on either side'. Real drawings exceeded the rule's imagination.

**Impact.** One house carries a naming convention decided without spec backing; if a later house names the same situation differently, the dataset will be inconsistent and nothing will flag it.

**Fix.** Documented the judgment call in the grid file's own dummy_grid_rule_check field. The spec itself was not updated.

**→ Rule.** When a real drawing forces a naming decision the spec does not cover, record it in the file AND raise it as a spec amendment the same day — an undocumented precedent only in one file's metadata will be silently contradicted by the next house.

<sub>`D:/00mk/steel project/training/Training/workmen's_diary/2026-08-18.md` · spec-gap</sub>

The 2026-08-20 entry describes rendering an overlay on 'house 01 หน้า19 (S-02) beam plan' with '24/24 beam segments resolved'. Same house, same page number, same 24/24, two incompatible sheet-type labels.

**Root cause.** Two sessions wrote up the same artifact from memory/context without checking the page's actual pattern field; nothing cross-checked the two entries.

**Impact.** The only recorded 100%-accuracy proof in the whole overlay effort is ambiguous about what page type it proves. Anyone citing it later — e.g. to argue beam plans can be read reliably — may be citing a footing/column result instead.

**Fix.** Not fixed — both labels stand.

**→ Rule.** When logging a measured result, copy the page's recorded `pattern`/`sheet_code` verbatim into the diary rather than describing it; a proof whose subject is ambiguous cannot be reused.

**Root cause.** The table was built pattern-by-pattern by hand with no completeness check that every grid-master-consuming subtask declares the grid master as an input — an omission a table cannot self-detect.

**Impact.** Caught during review. Had it shipped, Pass 1 would not have copied/referenced the grid master into the roof_plan folder and every roof_plan extraction would have had no grid context.

**Fix.** Added 'json ของ Gridmaster' as roof_plan's input in pass_design.csv.

**What happened.** Earlier the same session, tracing `raw-extraction-adapter.js` established that Constistant consumes exactly six patterns: plan / section / schedule / notes / gridline / material_list. A few hours later Pass 2 was written up as 'the 7 patterns Constistant actually consumes' with `soil_boring_log` added. The two statements in the same diary entry contradict each other and nothing reconciles them.

**Impact.** t03's Pass 2 scope (and by inheritance the op04 skill's page selection) may carry a subtask whose output has no consumer on the traced path, spending annotation and inference effort on it under a false justification.

**Fix.** Not fixed — both statements stand in the entry unreconciled.

**→ Rule.** When a scope is justified by 'the code consumes this', name the consuming module per pattern; one traced module is not the whole platform, and one extra entry in a justified list is how scope quietly inflates.

<sub>`D:/00mk/steel project/training/Training/workmen's_diary/2026-08-21.md` · spec-inconsistency</sub>

#### ⚪ LOW · 2026-08-29 · The operator asked about 'apply_arm.py', a file that does not exist — the arm switcher is a function buried inside the inference runner

**What happened.** The whole teaching doc was written in response to 'ผมอยากเข้าใจ apply_arm.py and all file in t04_Purson'. There is no apply_arm.py; apply_arm() is a function inside tune_ai/t03/data_before_tune/infer_house_t03.py, in a different training round's folder than the one being asked about.

**Root cause.** The experiment-arm switch — the single most consequential runtime knob, deciding whether a GPU night is arm 2 or arm 2.4a — lives as an unnamed function inside a large runner file in t03, while the arm's contract and examples live in t04. The pointer-README structure that prevents drift also makes the real code hard to locate.

**Impact.** The person about to spend money on a two-arm GPU run did not know where the arm logic lived. A whole explanatory document had to be written to answer it.

**Fix.** Documented — the doc states plainly where the function lives and what the --arm flag does. The code was not moved or renamed.

**→ Rule.** If a knob decides how an expensive run behaves, its location must be guessable from its name. A README pointer chain is fine for stages; it is not fine for the one function an operator must trust at 2am.

#### ⚪ LOW · 2026-09-01 · Diary entries written in Thai despite the diary's own rule requiring English

**What happened.** The README states rule #1: every entry must be written in English the first time, with only specific identifiers kept verbatim in Thai. Most of the 2026-09-01 and all of the 2026-09-02 entries are written in Thai prose.

<sub>`2026-09-01.md` · process/documentation</sub>

#### ⚪ LOW · 2026-09-01 · A parallel English translation folder fell out of date and had to be deleted

**What happened.** The diary used to keep a parallel `en/` translation folder alongside the Thai entries. It fell out of date after 2026-07-21 and was deleted on 2026-08-02 when the whole diary was converted to English, on the reasoning that one English source of truth beats two folders that disagree.

**Root cause.** Maintaining a translated duplicate of a living document requires discipline on every write; the first missed translation makes the two copies disagree, and it degrades from there. Translate-later is always deferred.

**Impact.** Roughly six weeks of divergent documentation, then a full conversion pass plus a folder deletion to clean it up.

**Fix.** Full Thai→English conversion of the diary and deletion of the `en/` folder; the rule became 'write it in English the first time'.

**→ Rule.** Never maintain a translated duplicate of a living document. Pick one language and write it that way from the first keystroke — translate-later never happens.
