**Impact.** Deleting `manifest.json` would have broken both `pdf-processor.py` and `qwen-processor.js` the next time anyone ran them — a silent breakage that would only surface later. Caught before real deletion only because staging was used instead of `rm`.

**Fix.** Both files restored to `No_touch_box/`; the round-6 classification corrected in the record.

**→ Rule.** Before deleting a file, grep for every *reader*, not just the writer. A file that a script opens with `open(..., 'r')` and never creates is a dependency, not an artifact.

<sub>`2026-08-02.md` · process</sub>

#### 🟠 HIGH · 2026-08-02 · The reviewed working copy and the ground-truth raw folder had never once been synced in the project's entire history

**What happened.** Round 4 of 2026-08-02 performed what the entry itself calls 'the first sync-back in the project's history' — 362 files pushed into rawjson_ยังไม่ได้แก้ไขโดนคน/. Until that moment every correction made in json_แก้ไขแล้ว/ existed only there, while the folder designated as ground truth still held the uncorrected version. 'Sync back still not started for any house' appears as a pending item in three consecutive rounds before it was finally done.

**Root cause.** Two folders were maintained with no defined sync step and no check that they agreed; the workflow only ever wrote forward into the reviewed copy.

**Impact.** For the whole period before this, anything reading the raw folder — including dataset builders — was reading pre-correction data while the team believed the corrections were applied. The eventual sync required a full Rule 2 warning and explicit permission because it touched the protected folder in bulk.

**Fix.** Synced 362 files into the raw folder under explicit permission, logged in raw_json_data_log.md and No_touch_box/CLAUDE.md, backed by commit 0029264; a 0-file-difference check between the folders became part of the close-out

**→ Rule.** Two copies of the same data need a sync step in the workflow and an automated equality check, or one of them silently becomes stale. Add the 'folders differ in 0 files' assertion to the gate, not to the closing summary.

<sub>`D:/00mk/steel project/training/Training/workmen's_diary/2026-08-02.md` · process</sub>

#### 🟠 HIGH · 2026-08-05 · House 13's 10 missing pages were only caught after all 7 background agents had already finished

**What happened.** The coordinator's page-coverage check found 10 missing files (หน้า01/02/28-33 plus a grid_ref fix on หน้า34) for house 13 only after all 7 parallel background agents had already returned. A follow-up run was needed to complete the house.

**Root cause.** Page coverage was checked as a final gate rather than as an assignment-time invariant — nothing verified that the union of the agents' assigned page ranges covered all 92 pages before dispatch.

**Impact.** A house was reported as extracted while 10 pages were missing; a second dispatch round was needed, and had the check not run, the gap would have entered the corpus silently.

**Fix.** The 10 files were extracted in a follow-up commit completing the house; noted that the coverage check should run earlier.

**→ Rule.** Verify page coverage at dispatch time, not at completion time — assert that the union of assigned ranges equals the full page set before any agent starts.

<sub>`2026-08-05.md` · process</sub>

#### 🟠 HIGH · 2026-08-07 · Houses 08 and 09, both signed off '100% done' on 07-30, each needed correction passes a week later

**What happened.** House 08 — declared '100% done, 63/63 pages, all 97 JSON files valid' on 2026-07-30 — needed 4 files corrected on 08-07 (gridline, beam plan, ring beam plan, beam-column expand). House 09, also declared 100% done, needed 3 files corrected on 08-08.

**Root cause.** 'Done' was defined as 'all pages extracted and the format checker passes' — which measures completeness of coverage and legality of shape, not correctness of content. Nothing in the done-criteria checks the extracted values against the drawing.

**Impact.** Two houses were recorded as finished while carrying content errors, and by extension every other house's 'done' status is unreliable in the same way. The corrections landed only because someone happened to look again.

**Fix.** Correction passes applied to both houses' files.

**→ Rule.** Separate 'extraction complete' from 'content verified' as two distinct states with two distinct checks. A format checker passing is not a content review — never let ALL CHECKS PASS be read as 'this house is correct'.

<sub>`2026-08-07.md` · process</sub>

#### 🟠 HIGH · 2026-08-18 · King-try branch drifted 277 commits behind main, carrying a schema copy stale by dozens of rules

**What happened.** Reviewing kingparadorn's King-try branch found it diverged 2026-07-25 and sat 277 commits behind main — predating the entire op01/op03 22-house campaign and the §0 FORMAT LOCK schema overhaul. Its own copy of primary_rawjson_schema.md lived under the old raw_json_ตัวที่ใช้งานจริง/ 5-house folder and was stale by dozens of rules.

**Root cause.** A long-lived feature branch was never rebased or synced while the shared spec it depends on was being rewritten on main. Because the branch carried its own copy of the schema doc rather than referencing one canonical location, the drift was invisible from either side until someone diffed them.

**Impact.** A real merge became impractical; the 12 commits of genuinely useful work (Gemini overlay prototype, hooks, skills, agent) were left stranded and still not cherry-picked as of 2026-08-20. Any tooling written on that branch targets a schema shape that no longer exists.

**Fix.** Not fixed. Recommendation recorded: cherry-pick the overlay prototype + hooks/skills/agent onto main rather than attempt a merge. Still open on 2026-08-20 ('nothing was cherry-picked onto main this session').

**→ Rule.** Sync a feature branch with main at least weekly, and never let a branch keep its own copy of a shared spec — reference the canonical file, so spec changes force a visible conflict instead of silent drift.

<sub>`D:/00mk/steel project/training/Training/workmen's_diary/2026-08-18.md` · process</sub>

#### 🟠 HIGH · 2026-08-20 · Built a text checklist accept/reject gate when the ask was clicking the green overlay on the plan itself

**What happened.** A full accept/reject gate was built into Constistant's raw-JSON import path — a checklist of every element with mark/type/floor/grid position/confidence, plus a preview/save split of qt_importRawExtractionFiles(). Makham's verdict: not good enough. The original ask was clicking the green overlay drawn on the plan, not a text list. The visual version still needs building.

**Root cause.** The requirement 'click to accept elements' was interpreted as a data-review problem (list of rows) rather than a spatial-review problem (marks on the drawing). The ask was not restated back before building, so the mismatch surfaced only at demo.

**Impact.** A session's implementation work plus an uncommitted UI change that does not satisfy the requirement; the real feature (clickable SVG over the grid, drawn from the saved GridReference) still unbuilt. Underlying preview/save split was salvageable.

**Fix.** Not fixed this session — the visual overlay version is recorded as still pending. The qt_buildRawExtractionPreview / qt_saveRawExtractionPreview split was kept as reusable groundwork.

**→ Rule.** Before building any review UI, restate the interaction back in one sentence naming the surface the user will click ('you click the green box on the scan') and get confirmation — a spatial requirement answered with a table is a full rebuild, not a tweak.

<sub>`D:/00mk/steel project/training/Training/workmen's_diary/2026-08-20.md` · requirements</sub>

#### 🟠 HIGH · 2026-08-20 · Run scope collapsed from 4 houses to 19 pages because per-page inference time was never measured first

**What happened.** Real per-page timing came in at 1.5–15 minutes with huge variance, worse on unseen pages that hit the token cap. Scope was cut live several times: 4 houses → 2 houses → house 08 alone → capped at 25 of 63 pages → ended at 19/25 pages. Houses 09/10/11 never started.

**Root cause.** The plan was built on an unmeasured per-page time estimate. The variance driver (unseen pages looping until max_new_tokens) was itself the undiagnosed repetition-loop bug, so the slowest pages were slow for a reason nobody had found yet.

**Impact.** A 4-house generalization test degraded to 19 pages of one house — the resulting recall number (11%) rests on a much thinner sample than planned, and houses 09/10/11 were still unstarted a day later.

**Fix.** Scope cut repeatedly during the run; PAGE_FILTER gained a list-as-explicit-order mode to allow mid-run reordering. Houses 09/10/11 recorded as not started.

**→ Rule.** Time two representative pages (one easy, one hardest-pattern) on the rented box before committing to a scope, and treat wildly variable page times as a bug signal to investigate, not just a budgeting problem.

<sub>`D:/00mk/steel project/training/Training/workmen's_diary/2026-08-20.md` · planning</sub>

#### 🟠 HIGH · 2026-08-21 · Two schema edits made silently all day, violating rule_of_tune Lesson #7's announce-and-log requirement

**What happened.** After reading rule_of_tune.md on Makham's instruction, it emerged that Lesson #7 had been violated all day: primary_rawjson_schema.md is exempt from Rule 1 (it is a .md doc) but Lesson #7 requires stating the exemption out loud before editing and logging every edit in primary_rawjson_schema_edit_log.md immediately. Both of the day's earlier schema edits were made with neither.

**Root cause.** The governing rules file was not read at session start, so the edit protocol for the single most consequential document in the project was unknown while editing it. The exemption from Rule 1 was noticed; the additional obligations attached to that exemption were not.

**Impact.** Two schema changes to the project's canonical spec landed with no audit trail and no warning to the human — exactly the situation the edit log exists to prevent. Recovered retroactively, but the window existed.

**Fix.** Both edits logged retroactively and marked as rule violations in the log itself; the Rule 2 warning was given properly before the next two edits, which were warned first and logged immediately.

**→ Rule.** Read rule_of_tune.md at the start of every session that will touch a spec file — and treat an exemption from one rule as a signal to read what other obligations attach to it, never as blanket permission.

<sub>`D:/00mk/steel project/training/Training/workmen's_diary/2026-08-21.md` · process</sub>

#### 🟠 HIGH · 2026-08-21 · Two folders one letter apart held two contradictory designs, with nothing saying which was live

**What happened.** tune_ai/t03 contained both prompt/ (the 2-pass draft from 2026-08-04) and prompts/ (the 4-pass work from 2026-08-21). Nothing indicated which was current. Reorganized after midnight into one folder per pass, with prompt/ renamed to _old_2026-08-04_two_pass/ and given a ⛔ banner.

**Root cause.** A superseded design was left in place under a name one character from the new one, with no deprecation marker. Directory naming was not treated as load-bearing.

**Impact.** A real chance of running the obsolete 2-pass prompts against the 4-pass folder tree. Also produced duplicated spec-gap text across two READMEs that would have drifted.

**Fix.** One folder per pass (pass0_classify/, pass1_organize/, pass2_used/, pass3_unused/); prompt/ → _old_2026-08-04_two_pass/ with a ⛔ banner; _common.md hoisted to t03 root; prompts/README.md deleted with its unique sections folded into t03/README.md. No prompt text changed — moves and links only.

**→ Rule.** Mark a superseded design at the moment it is superseded — rename it with a date prefix and put a ⛔ banner in its README; never leave two candidate designs distinguishable only by a trailing 's'.

<sub>`D:/00mk/steel project/training/Training/workmen's_diary/2026-08-21.md` · process</sub>

#### 🟠 HIGH · 2026-08-21 · Two critical adapter fixes and their regression tests left uncommitted in the Constistant repo

**What happened.** The parseGridMaster nested-grid fix and the parseGridRef no-dash fix in js/drawing/raw-extraction-adapter.js, plus 4 new regression tests in tests/raw-extraction-grid.test.js, were left uncommitted at end of session. The 08-20 checklist UI change in raw-extraction-import.js was likewise left uncommitted.

**Root cause.** Session ended without a commit step, and the files touch a pure module with a purity guard which the author wanted reviewed first — but 'needs review' was recorded as a pending item rather than as a commit on a branch.

**Impact.** Two fixes for critical silent bugs (every import producing empty grids and null spans since 2026-08-02) exist only in one working tree. A lost working tree, a branch switch, or a stash would erase them along with their tests. This repo's own history already records a plan and an approved mockup lost exactly this way.

**Fix.** Not fixed — recorded as pending: 'The two adapter fixes are uncommitted in the Constistant repo — they touch a pure module with a purity guard; review and commit them.'

**→ Rule.** Never end a session with a fix for a critical bug uncommitted — commit to a branch and request review there; 'needs review' is a reason to commit, not a reason to leave work in a working tree.

<sub>`D:/00mk/steel project/training/Training/workmen's_diary/2026-08-21.md` · process</sub>

#### 🟠 HIGH · 2026-08-24 · Misdiagnosis: assumed xgrammar would prevent generation stalls — page 25 stalled anyway

**What happened.** After xgrammar fixed page 22, the assumption was that stalls were solved. Page 25 then stalled again with grammar attached, costing more rental time before the real distinction was understood.

**Root cause.** Conflated two different failure modes. Grammar constrains token *validity* ("JSON won't close"), it does not bound output *length* ("generates too long"). Nothing in the runner enforced a wall-clock ceiling.

**Impact.** A second multi-tens-of-minutes stall on paid GPU time, and Makham ultimately cut every page t01 couldn't finish — shrinking the comparison from 34 → 22 → 12 → 6 usable pages.

**Fix.** Added PAGE_TIMEOUT_S=25min as a StoppingCriteria, separate from grammar.

**→ Rule.** Grammar fixes malformed JSON, not runaway length. Every generation loop needs an independent wall-clock stopping criterion regardless of what decoding constraints are attached.

<sub>`D:/00mk/steel project/training/Training/workmen's_diary/2026-08-24.md` · misdiagnosis</sub>

#### 🟠 HIGH · 2026-08-25 · Whole t03 training round spent on plan_beam, which moved 0% → 0%

**What happened.** Training round 3 (t03) was run specifically to fix plan_beam element recall. It improved schedule (0→21.9%) and plan_slab (0→20%), but plan_beam stayed at exactly 0%. Cost ~$5 and 5 hours for zero movement on the one metric the round existed to fix.

**Root cause.** The round was launched without first diagnosing WHY plan_beam was 0%. The failure mode was 'the model does not see the beams at all' (empty elements array), not 'the model misreads numbers' — retraining on the same silently-downscaled images could never fix a visibility problem.

**Impact.** ~$5 GPU spend and 5 hours of wall-clock training time produced no progress on the round's primary objective; the team only learned the diagnosis afterwards.

**Fix.** Diagnosed after the fact: recall 0% = model never emits any element, plus images were 100% downscaled (separate finding). Both root causes identified same day; retrain not yet redone.

**→ Rule.** Never launch a paid training round to fix a metric until you have a written diagnosis of why that metric is bad. Diagnosis first, GPU spend second.

<sub>`D:/00mk/steel project/training/Training/workmen's_diary/2026-08-25(teach mk).md` · process/planning</sub>

#### 🟠 HIGH · 2026-08-25 · Started building a fix for section 0% before diagnosing why it was 0%

**What happened.** Asked whether pattern recognition could help the section subtask, work began immediately on applying the tool. Mid-work the author caught himself doing the steps in the wrong order, backed out, and diagnosed first — at which point the answer changed completely.

**Root cause.** A request phrased as 'can tool X help problem Y' was taken as an instruction to apply X, skipping the step of establishing what Y actually is.

**Impact.** Partial wasted effort, caught before it became a full implementation. Had it not been caught, effort would have gone into a tool that provably cannot help this metric.

**Fix.** Backed out and wrote measure_id_ceiling.py to diagnose the metric instead, which revealed the real problem was the evaluation, not the model.

**→ Rule.** When asked 'can we use tool X here', answer the diagnostic question first: what is actually broken. A request to try a tool is not a diagnosis.

<sub>`D:/00mk/steel project/training/Training/workmen's_diary/2026-08-25(teach mk).md` · process</sub>

#### 🟠 HIGH · 2026-08-25 · Started building a fix for section 0% before diagnosing it; the diagnosis changed the answer completely

**What happened.** Asked whether pattern recognition could rescue section's 0% id-recall, the work started by trying the tool, then stopped and went back to diagnose. The diagnosis found the real cause was the scoring metric, not the model — so the tool being built could not possibly have helped.

**Root cause.** Jumping to a proposed solution because it was the tool already at hand, instead of first establishing what the failing number actually measures.

**Impact.** Time spent on three failed pattern-recognition experiments on section (HoughCircles, contour box detection, rebar-dot counting) that were never going to address the real cause. Caught before committing a whole tuning round.

**Fix.** Went back and diagnosed first, building `measure_id_ceiling.py` to compute the achievable ceiling per subtask before proposing any fix.

**→ Rule.** Diagnose before building, every time — especially when a tool you just built looks like it fits. If you cannot state what the failing number measures and what its theoretical maximum is, you are not ready to fix it.

<sub>`D:/00mk/steel project/training/Training/workmen's_diary/2026-08-25.md` · process-order</sub>

#### 🟠 HIGH · 2026-08-25 · The professor's max_frames=768 suggestion pointed at a knob this project never invokes

**What happened.** `max_frames: 768` was found in `processor_config.json` and proposed as a tuning target. It is the hardcoded default in Qwen's video frame sampler. This project sends every drawing page as a still image content item, never as video, so the video processor path is never invoked and raising the value would have zero effect.

**Root cause.** A configuration value was identified by name-matching in a config file without tracing whether the code path that reads it is ever executed.

**Impact.** Would have burned a tuning round changing a value with no effect. Instead the trace surfaced the real knobs (MAX_PIXELS, MAX_LENGTH) and led to the 100%-downscale discovery.

**Fix.** Grepped the whole repo for `max_frames` (single hit, an auto-saved config), confirmed the training/inference code sends `{"type": "image"}`, and reported back that the real knobs are MAX_PIXELS and MAX_LENGTH.

**→ Rule.** Before tuning any config value, trace the code path that reads it and prove it executes in your setup. A value present in an auto-saved config file is not evidence that your code uses it.

<sub>`D:/00mk/steel project/training/Training/workmen's_diary/2026-08-25.md` · wrong-diagnosis</sub>

#### 🟠 HIGH · 2026-08-25 · A full day of tool, config, doc and metric changes left uncommitted at end of day

**What happened.** At day's close the uncommitted list included measure_id_ceiling.py, infer_house_t03.py (the new metric), measure_capacity.py, train_t03.py (7680/47104), the teaching .md + .pdf + image folder, md_to_book_pdf.py (the image fix), t03_workflow.md, and the day's diary. Only the first two commits of the day (pattern recognition) had been committed by Makham.

**Root cause.** Commits were deferred pending Makham's review, so a whole day of interdependent changes accumulated in the working tree as a single unreviewed blob.

**Impact.** A crash, a stray `git checkout`, or a branch switch loses the day. The related risk is already documented in the Constistant repo: an approved plan and mockup were lost precisely because they were never committed. It also makes the changes hard to review or bisect since they arrive as one lump.

**Fix.** Not fixed — the uncommitted list was written into the diary so nothing is silently lost track of.

**→ Rule.** Commit each self-contained change as it lands, on a branch if review is pending. "Waiting for review" is not a reason to leave work only in the working tree — an unreviewed commit is recoverable, an uncommitted file is not.

<sub>`D:/00mk/steel project/training/Training/workmen's_diary/2026-08-25.md` · process-failure</sub>

#### 🟠 HIGH · 2026-08-25 · pass0 page classification — the riskiest stage in the pipeline — had no cross-check of any kind

**What happened.** Makham proposed Pass 0.5 (a CV template scan of every page producing a page fingerprint) specifically because pass0's page labels are "ด่านเสี่ยงสุด เดิมไม่มีใครตรวจ" — the stage everything downstream depends on had zero verification. A mislabeled page silently routes to the wrong extraction prompt and its content disappears.

**Root cause.** Verification effort went to the extraction outputs (element counts, ids, recall) and none to the routing decision upstream of them, so a whole class of failure could only surface as unexplained missing data much later.

**Impact.** Every page mislabeled by pass0 to date went uncaught — this is the same shape as the roof_plan→plan bug where mis-tagged pages made roof-beam BOQ quantities vanish with no error anywhere.

**Fix.** tools/cv_scan.py built this evening as the Pass 0.5 cross-check; not yet wired into the real pipeline ("ต่อ cv_scan เข้าสายพาน: เริ่มจาก pass0 cross-check" is still pending).

**→ Rule.** Verify the routing stage, not just the output stage — an unchecked classifier turns every downstream error into an unexplained absence.

<sub>`D:/00mk/steel project/training/Training/workmen's_diary/2026-08-25.md` · process</sub>

#### 🟠 HIGH · 2026-08-26 · plan_beam 0% recall had been attributed to image downscaling — the real cause was answer length

**What happened.** The teaching PDF documents the plan_beam 0%-recall investigation and its real cause: answer length causing one-bad-token JSON collapse, not image downscaling. The downscaling theory was disproven visually with a real before/after crop comparison from an actual training image.

**Root cause.** Image resolution was the intuitive suspect (and had been a real bug in t01 at 512px), so it was assumed again without testing. The actual mechanism — long answers giving more chances for a single token to break the JSON — was only found by investigating rather than assuming.

**Impact.** Investigation time spent on the wrong hypothesis; if uncorrected, the fix would have been more VRAM for higher resolution rather than shorter answers.

**Fix.** Proven with a real crop comparison from a training image and documented in the PDF. Recommended fix direction: split plan_beam into per-grid-zone sub-answers.

**→ Rule.** A cause that was real in a previous round is the most seductive wrong hypothesis in the next one. Disprove it with a direct measurement before acting on it.

<sub>`D:/00mk/steel project/training/Training/workmen's_diary/2026-08-26.md` · misdiagnosis</sub>

#### 🟠 HIGH · 2026-08-28 · Renumbering 22 house folders broke every reference in prior logs and desynced from rawjson_

**What happened.** 22 folders under json_แก้ไขแล้ว were git-mv'd to renumber 01–38 (01–16 unchanged). The original gaps were 12 houses nobody had reviewed yet, not broken names. After the renumber, numbers no longer match the `rawjson_` tree from 17 upward.

**Root cause.** The number gaps were misread as a naming problem to fix rather than a meaningful signal (unreviewed houses). The renumber then broke the identity mapping between two parallel trees and invalidated every numeric reference in prior diary/log entries.

**Impact.** Every prior log entry referencing a house number is now ambiguous; the only way to read them is the old→new mapping table. Two trees now use different numbering for the same houses.

**Fix.** An old→new mapping table lives at the head of json_แก้ไขแล้ว/README.md, marked ห้ามลบ (must not be deleted) — it is the only way to read old logs. Standing rule: reference houses by name when unsure.

**→ Rule.** Never renumber identifiers that appear in historical records. Use stable names as the identity and treat numbers as display-only — and if you must renumber, the mapping table becomes permanent load-bearing documentation.

<sub>`D:/00mk/steel project/training/Training/workmen's_diary/2026-08-28.md` · process</sub>

#### 🟠 HIGH · 2026-08-29 · Copying unchanged stage files between t03 and t04 previously caused silent drift between duplicated copies

**What happened.** The project had previously experienced 'drift': the same file existing in two places, someone editing one copy, and the other going stale with nobody noticing. For t04 the team deliberately avoided copying unchanged pass 0/1/2 files and left small pointer READMEs instead.

**Root cause.** Duplicating a file creates two sources of truth with no mechanism to keep them in sync; divergence is silent because both copies remain syntactically valid.

**Impact.** Previously caused stale copies to be used unknowingly; the cost is invisible until wrong behaviour surfaces far downstream.

**Fix.** Adopted the rule that the real file lives in exactly one place and every other location holds only a pointer README.

**→ Rule.** Never duplicate a file across training rounds or folders. One source of truth, many pointers — if a copy is unavoidable, add an automated check that fails when the copies diverge.

<sub>`D:/00mk/steel project/training/Training/workmen's_diary/สอน_t04_Purson_2026-08-29.md` · process</sub>

#### 🟠 HIGH · 2026-08-29 · jsonl rebuilt at least five times in one day — real risk of training on a stale set already on the rented machine

**What happened.** train/val.jsonl was rebuilt repeatedly through the day (prompt hygiene, glossary move, split change, span rule, house 51/52, house 08). Each time the diary had to repeat the same warning: upload the latest set before firing the GPU, do not use the stale one already on the rental.

**Root cause.** There is no version/hash stamp on the dataset and no check on the training machine that the uploaded jsonl matches the local build. The only defence is a human remembering to re-upload — and the warning had to be written four separate times, which is the tell.

**Impact.** A single forgotten upload means paying for a full training run on the wrong data, discovered only after the fact if at all.

**Fix.** Not fixed — mitigated by repeating the warning in the diary and RUNBOOK.

**→ Rule.** Stamp the dataset with a content hash and have the training script assert it matches the expected hash before step 0. A warning repeated four times in one day is a missing automated check.

<sub>`D:/00mk/steel project/training/Training/workmen's_diary/2026-08-29.md` · process</sub>

#### 🟠 HIGH · 2026-08-29 · t04 had been running for days with no Phase 0 round doc, which rule_of_tune §4 requires

**What happened.** The t04_workflow.md Phase 0 document was created only at the point of the InternVL3 model switch, with the note that this round had never had one.

**Root cause.** The t04/Purson conveyor work started as a continuation of t03 rather than as a declared new round, so the round-opening checklist was never triggered.

**Impact.** Days of pass-v2 design, prompt rewrites, CV template work and dataset rebuilds happened without the round's model/framework/GPU decisions written down — which is exactly why the model switch invalidated a whole toolchain that was still being extended the day before.

**Fix.** wrote t04_Purson/t04_workflow.md with a Phase 0 gap list (framework, GPU strategy, dataset converter, new train/infer scripts, xgrammar probe)

**→ Rule.** A round that gets a new folder name is a new round — open its Phase 0 doc before writing any of its code. The decisions it forces (which model, which framework, which GPU) are the ones that invalidate work retroactively.

<sub>`D:/00mk/steel project/training/Training/workmen's_diary/2026-08-29.md` · process</sub>

#### 🟠 HIGH · 2026-08-29 · InternVL3-78B does not fit the single 96GB card the entire rental workflow was built around

**What happened.** Alongside the Unsloth incompatibility, the model switch also broke the hardware assumption: LoRA in bf16 on a dense 78B needs at least 2×H100-class cards, or an untried single-card QLoRA 4-bit path.

**Root cause.** The model was chosen on capability grounds (OmniDocBench score, license) with the VRAM consequence discovered afterward, not as part of the decision.

**Fix.** not fixed — recorded in t04_workflow.md Phase 0 as an open GPU-strategy decision

<sub>`D:/00mk/steel project/training/Training/workmen's_diary/2026-08-29.md` · planning</sub>

#### 🟠 HIGH · 2026-08-30 · The 25-minute `PAGE_TIMEOUT_S` safety net silently failed to cut off the hung request

**What happened.** `PAGE_TIMEOUT_S=25 นาที` existed specifically to kill a runaway page job, but during the 7-hour server hang it never fired — the request was never terminated and no timeout error was raised.

**Root cause.** Suspected (not yet confirmed) that the blocking `generate()` call prevented the event loop from ever getting control back to evaluate the deadline — a timeout implemented on the async side cannot preempt synchronous code holding the loop.

**Impact.** The one mechanism designed to bound the damage from a bad request did nothing, turning a 25-minute worst case into a 7-hour outage and wasted GPU rental.

**Fix.** Not fixed. Listed as item 2 of the pre-presentation must-do list: investigate why the timeout did not cut off the job.

**→ Rule.** A timeout that lives in the same execution context as the thing it is supposed to interrupt is not a timeout. Test every safety net by actually triggering the failure it guards against, don't assume it works because the code exists.

<sub>`D:/00mk/steel project/training/Training/workmen's_diary/2026-08-30.md` · serving-architecture</sub>

#### 🟠 HIGH · 2026-08-30 · Hand-written SKIP_SUBTASKS blocklist missed 3 subtasks with prompts but zero training examples — worker would have fired prompts the model never saw

**What happened.** Makham caught that 'ระบบ pass ผิด'. The SKIP_SUBTASKS list had been written from memory rather than checked against `pass_io_table_detailed.csv`, so it missed 3 subtasks that have prompts but 0 training examples: `plan_column` (dead), `material_list` (prompt never loaded into training) and `soil_boring_log` (no GT at all).

**Root cause.** A blocklist was authored by guessing what to exclude instead of deriving from the authoritative training manifest. A blocklist fails open — anything forgotten gets executed — which is exactly the wrong failure direction here.

**Impact.** Would have sent prompts the model has never been trained on into production, producing plausible-looking garbage with no error.

**Fix.** Replaced with an allowlist `TRAINED_SUBTASKS` containing only the 7 subtasks that were actually trained, derived from the real training table. Forgetting to add one now means skipping it, not firing blind.

**→ Rule.** When the cost of a false positive is silent garbage, use an allowlist derived from the authoritative source file, never a hand-written blocklist. Fail closed.

<sub>`D:/00mk/steel project/training/Training/workmen's_diary/2026-08-30.md` · process</sub>

#### 🟠 HIGH · 2026-08-30 · The 78B adapter the whole round paid for cannot be served at all — trained with LLaMA-Factory, but the only working server loads via Unsloth, so `--model t04` is rejected outright

**What happened.** vLLM was ruled out because Unsloth's MoE LoRA layout matches neither format it accepts, so `serve_purson.py` was written around Unsloth's load/generate path lifted from `infer_house_t03.py`. That server can only load Unsloth-trained adapters, so `--model t04` (the InternVL3-78B trained with LLaMA-Factory) is refused with a message saying the loader from `infer_house_t04.py` must be ported first. The round's actual output has no production path.

**Root cause.** Training framework and serving framework were chosen independently at different times — LLaMA-Factory was picked for training because it was the only route to QLoRA on InternVL3-78B, and Unsloth for serving because it was the only proven load path — and nobody checked at decision time that the two could meet.

**Impact.** The 78B round produces artefacts that cannot be served without an unbudgeted loader port; the presentation stack falls back to the older t03 adapter instead.

**Fix.** Not fixed. `--model t04` fails fast with an explicit message rather than breaking mid-demo — deliberately chosen over letting it fail live.

**→ Rule.** Pick the serving path at the same time as the training framework and prove one loads the other's output before paying for a training run — 'we trained it' and 'we can run it' are two separate claims.

<sub>`D:/00mk/steel project/training/Training/workmen's_diary/2026-08-30.md` · architecture/planning</sub>

#### 🟠 HIGH · 2026-08-31 · Fixing one confirmed root cause was mistaken for unblocking the whole round

**What happened.** After Lesson 15 identified crop_to_patches as t04's root cause and it was verified correct, the team assumed the arm was fixed. A second disease (4-bit killing the ViT) sat underneath and would have produced identical symptoms — beautiful JSON, ~0% recall.

**Root cause.** Treating 'root cause found and fixed' as terminal, rather than re-walking the remaining known risk list that the design dossier had already written down.

**Impact.** Would have burned another full multi-GPU night on a model that could not see, had the ~$2 gate not caught it.

**Fix.** Recorded as rule_of_tune Lesson 16 item 3: after fixing a root cause, walk the remaining risk list from the round's design doc and build a gate for each item.

**→ Rule.** A confirmed root cause fix is not a green light — re-read the round's own risk list and put a cheap detection gate on every remaining item before spending money.

<sub>`D:/00mk/steel project/training/Training/workmen's_diary/2026-08-31.md` · process</sub>

#### 🟠 HIGH · 2026-08-31 · Sequence-length headroom was only 2.8% and the guard against silent label truncation was only a comment

**What happened.** Measured longest sequence was 45,839 against MAX_LENGTH 47,104 — a 2.8% margin, below the 5% that should exist. An audit had already noted that the t01-class bug (labels silently truncated mid-JSON) had comments but no actual runtime check.

**Root cause.** Capacity was computed on paper and documented as an intention rather than enforced by a preflight assertion at data-load time.

**Impact.** Any slightly longer row would have silently truncated a training label mid-JSON, teaching the model malformed output with no error raised.

**Fix.** Added preflight_seq_lengths() to the training script: measures visual tokens from real image dimensions plus text tokens from the real tokenizer for every row at load time and halts immediately if any row exceeds the cap.

**→ Rule.** A documented limit with no runtime assertion is not a guard — enforce every capacity constraint with a hard fail at data-load time, before the first training step.

<sub>`D:/00mk/steel project/training/Training/workmen's_diary/2026-08-31.md` · process</sub>

#### 🟠 HIGH · 2026-08-31 · MAX_PIXELS and MAX_LENGTH had been paper-calculated since 2026-08-25 and never actually run

**What happened.** The workflow doc had recorded since 25 Aug that MAX_PIXELS=7680 / MAX_LENGTH=47104 with a 4.0 GB margin was a calculation on paper that had never been executed, and required TEST_STEPS=5 confirmation. This round was the first to actually run it — and it hit the ceiling.

**Root cause.** A capacity budget was documented as validated-looking numbers when it was in fact an untested projection.

**Impact.** OOM at step 2 during dry-run, then real OOMs on 2 of 4 folds in the full run.

**Fix.** Followed the pre-written fallback order: reduce gridline images 4->3 first, then MAX_PIXELS, never reduce MAX_LENGTH (which truncates labels).

**→ Rule.** Label every untested capacity figure as untested in the doc, and require a real measured run before any spend that depends on it.

<sub>`D:/00mk/steel project/training/Training/workmen's_diary/2026-08-31.md` · process</sub>

#### 🟠 HIGH · 2026-08-31 · Extracting the data tarball overwrote the already-fixed training script with an old copy inside it

**What happened.** folds4.tar.gz contained an old version of train_t05_courser.py. Extracting it after pushing the fixed script overwrote the fix, so gpu4 ran the probe with the old code and died with 401 (still pushing during dry-run).

**Root cause.** A data bundle also carried source files, and the operation order was push-script-then-extract-tarball.

**Impact.** One machine failed its probe and time was lost diagnosing an already-fixed bug.

**Fix.** Re-sent the new script and grep-verified a marker string on all four machines rather than trusting scp.

**→ Rule.** Never let a data bundle carry source files; if it must, extract first then push code, and always grep-verify a version marker on every machine instead of assuming the copy landed.

<sub>`D:/00mk/steel project/training/Training/workmen's_diary/2026-08-31.md` · process</sub>

#### 🟠 HIGH · 2026-08-31 · The demo launcher has still never completed end-to-end — all three evening rentals ended without a working server

**What happened.** Evening demo prep burned three instances in a row: 49408084 rented after Makham said stop, 49410094 started the wrong model (t03), 49411642 hit the pgrep self-match and never started the server. The fixed path is scheduled to be tried for the first time the next morning.
