**Impact.** A fix of unknown effectiveness sat in the repo as if it were the answer. When it was finally tested the next night, it turned out to be insufficient anyway — grammar-constrained decoding was needed.

**Fix.** Tested the following night (คืน → เช้า 2026-08-22); the real fix turned out to be xgrammar grammar-constrained decoding, taking validity from 57.9% to 96.8%.

**→ Rule.** A decoding-parameter change is untested until it has generated real tokens on the failing page — label it explicitly as unverified in both the code and the diary, and do not let it close the bug.

<sub>`D:/00mk/steel project/training/Training/workmen's_diary/2026-08-21.md` · process</sub>

#### 🟡 MEDIUM · 2026-08-21 · pass1_organize.py written and shipped without ever touching a real image

**What happened.** Pass 1 (tune_ai/t03/pass1_organize.py) — which cuts multi-view pages into one image per view with OpenCV, scatters into pass2/pass3 subtask folders and writes manifests — was written on Makham's explicit instruction not to test it. None of the cropping logic (title-block strip, divider detection, ~2% padding, the not-guessing fallback) has seen a real drawing.

**Root cause.** A deliberate instruction to skip testing, accepted without a compensating guard. The riskiest logic in the file is the image cropping, which cannot be reasoned about — a padding or divider-detection error would clip the edge-sitting grid markers, and losing those kills span calculation for the whole sheet.

**Impact.** An untested cropping stage sits in the pipeline; if run on 62 multi-view pages unverified, silent clipping of grid markers would corrupt spans across the highest-value structural sheets.

**Fix.** Not fixed. Recorded prominently as pending: 'Run pass1_organize.py on one house. The 62 multi-view pages are the test set and they're already on disk, so this costs nothing but time.'

**→ Rule.** When told to skip testing, ship the code with an explicit blocking note naming what has never been exercised, and identify the cheapest available test set in the same breath — untested image-cropping logic fails by silently producing plausible-looking wrong crops.

<sub>`D:/00mk/steel project/training/Training/workmen's_diary/2026-08-21.md` · process</sub>

#### 🟡 MEDIUM · 2026-08-21 · Pass 0 classifying to the 16 pattern values would have made Pass 1 routing impossible

**What happened.** Writing the Pass 0 → Pass 1 contract surfaced that Pass 0 must classify straight to the fine-grained subtask label, not to one of the 16 pattern values — otherwise Pass 1 cannot route a 'plan' page to one of seven destination folders (plan_footing / plan_column / plan_beam / plan_slab / plan_architectural / plan_electrical / plan_sanitary), and filename-based routing is ruled out by the documented naming drift.

**Root cause.** The pass design inherited the existing 16-pattern taxonomy as the classification target without checking whether that taxonomy is granular enough for the routing decision the next pass has to make. The plan pattern is one-to-seven.

**Impact.** Caught while writing the contract, before any prompt ran. Had Pass 0 shipped emitting patterns, Pass 1's entire folder tree would have been unbuildable and the whole multi-pass design would have needed rework after GPU time was spent.

**Fix.** Documented in pass0_output_example.json as the Pass 0 → Pass 1 contract: Pass 0 emits the subtask label.

**→ Rule.** Write the inter-stage contract file before writing either stage — the contract is where an insufficiently granular classification target becomes obvious, and it is far cheaper to find there than after a training run.

<sub>`D:/00mk/steel project/training/Training/workmen's_diary/2026-08-21.md` · design</sub>

#### 🟡 MEDIUM · 2026-08-21 · run_house_batch.py output shape is incompatible with the platform's importer

**What happened.** run_house_batch.py stores {ok, parsed, raw_text, grammar} with pattern and elements nested inside parsed.views[], while raw-extraction-adapter.js reads f.pattern and f.elements at file level. A converter had to be written to flatten views into one file per view and fill the §2-required wrapper fields.

**Root cause.** The inference runner's output format was designed for debugging (keeping raw text and validity flags) with no reference to the consumer contract, so the two ends of the loop were never able to meet without a translation layer.

**Impact.** The 'complete loop' from model output to platform import was blocked until a whole new converter tool was written. Multi-view pages also needed a _view1_ file-splitting convention invented on the spot.

**Fix.** New tools/export_qwen_to_platform.py — flattens views to one file per view, fills wrapper fields, copies element content verbatim (unusable entries reported, never repaired), records every generated value in warnings[], and stamps _provenance.human_reviewed: false.

**→ Rule.** Define the consumer's file contract before writing the producer's output format — and when a converter is unavoidable, make it copy content verbatim and record every field it generated, so a converted file can never be mistaken for a human-reviewed one.

<sub>`D:/00mk/steel project/training/Training/workmen's_diary/2026-08-21.md` · design</sub>

#### 🟡 MEDIUM · 2026-08-21 · op04 skill written and registered without ever being run on a house

**What happened.** The new op04 skill (op1 scoped to Pass 2 subtasks only, ~38 pages instead of ~107) plus its canonical op4 README section were written and registered, but never executed. Recorded as 'op04 has never been run. Written and registered only.'

**Root cause.** Written as the last task of a session before shutdown, with no GPU/session time left to exercise it. Same pattern as pass1_organize.py earlier the same day.

**Impact.** An unvalidated page-selection rule set is now the registered path for all future house annotation. If its subtask ordering or its skip rules are wrong, every house annotated with it inherits the error.

**Fix.** Not fixed — recorded as pending with explicit caution: 'Run it on one house and read the output before trusting the page-selection rules — same caution as pass1_organize.py.'

**→ Rule.** A registered skill is a promise that it works — never register an untested workflow without a blocking note at the top of the skill itself saying it has never been run, and run it on one item before the next campaign starts.

<sub>`D:/00mk/steel project/training/Training/workmen's_diary/2026-08-21.md` · process</sub>

#### 🟡 MEDIUM · 2026-08-24 · Local GGUF inference path built, then abandoned after measuring 23 min/page

**What happened.** A local GGUF inference workflow was built for the t01 tuned-vs-untuned comparison, then dropped in favour of renting an RTX PRO 6000 and running bf16 via transformers/PEFT, after measuring 23 minutes per page on the laptop.

**Root cause.** Throughput was never estimated before building the path. A single timed page on one representative image would have shown the laptop was ~100x too slow for a 34-page run.

**Impact.** A whole workflow doc and script path (ทดลองถอดแบบ_08_09_10_local_workflow.md) became superseded and needed a banner; time spent on it produced no results.

**Fix.** Pivoted to a rented GPU with bf16 transformers/PEFT; the local workflow doc got a superseded banner rather than deletion.

**→ Rule.** Time one representative unit of work on the target hardware before building the workflow around it. A 60-second measurement kills a bad path before it costs a day.

<sub>`D:/00mk/steel project/training/Training/workmen's_diary/2026-08-24.md` · wasted-work</sub>

#### 🟡 MEDIUM · 2026-08-24 · Decisions delegated under att1235 were written up as "waiting for Makham" instead of decided

**What happened.** Claude had been given att1235 (decide everything yourself) but wrote all four t03 dataset decisions in the workflow doc as "รอมะขามเคาะ" (awaiting Makham's ruling). Makham called it out: "ผมให้ att1235 ไปแล้วหนิ".

**Root cause.** Defaulting to a request-permission posture despite an explicit standing order to decide. The doc format encouraged listing open questions rather than recording rulings with accepted risk.

**Impact.** Blocked the night's work on decisions that were already delegated; wasted a round trip and Makham's time.

**Fix.** Rewrote all four decisions as ตัดสินแล้ว ✅ with reasons and accepted risks (model=Qwen3.6; plan_column folded into plan_footing; gridline=multi-image→gridmaster; unreviewed houses 06-11 stay in train). Logged to Claude memory as feedback_att1235_decide_fully.md.

**→ Rule.** When given a standing decide-yourself order, document outcomes as "decided ✅ + reason + risk accepted", never as "awaiting approval". Bouncing a delegated decision back is itself the failure.

<sub>`D:/00mk/steel project/training/Training/workmen's_diary/2026-08-24.md` · process</sub>

#### 🟡 MEDIUM · 2026-08-24 · Parity table for train_t03.py vs t02 defaults was never fully completed

**What happened.** Provenance tags were added to every chosen value in train_t03.py, but the full call-site argument enumeration against t02's defaults was never done — leaving open the possibility of more silently drifted parameters like the two already found.

**Root cause.** Provenance tagging (documenting why a chosen value is what it is) was mistaken for parity checking (verifying no value silently changed). They cover different failure modes: tags cover values you thought about, parity covers the ones you didn't.

**Impact.** Unknown number of remaining drifted parameters between t02 and t03; two were already found this way, so the base rate is non-zero.

**Fix.** Not fixed — carried forward as pending.

**→ Rule.** Provenance tags document intent; a parity table catches omission. Do both — enumerate every call-site argument against the last working round, not just the ones you deliberately chose.

<sub>`D:/00mk/steel project/training/Training/workmen's_diary/2026-08-24.md` · process</sub>

#### 🟡 MEDIUM · 2026-08-25 · Built multi-scale template matching to fix a size problem that was actually a shape problem

**What happened.** House 12 footing detection found only 6 of 12. First hypothesis: the icons are drawn at a different size. Multi-scale matching was implemented across 6 scales (0.7–1.2×). Result stayed at exactly 6/12.

**Root cause.** A plausible hypothesis was implemented in code before being tested against the actual image. F1 and F2 are structurally different symbols (square-stacked, one pile vs. vertical rectangle with two pile dots, two piles) — different objects by engineering design, not the same object at different sizes.

**Impact.** An entire multi-scale feature was written and produced zero improvement — wasted implementation time and added permanent complexity to the tool for no gain.

**Fix.** Opened the two icons side by side and looked at them, saw the shape difference immediately, and replaced the approach with a template bank (glob `tpl_footing*.png`) that merges all matches then applies NMS once. Result: 12/12.

**→ Rule.** Test a hypothesis by opening the actual data and looking at it, before writing any code against it. Ten seconds of eyeballing beats an hour of implementing the wrong theory — same as rule_of_tune.md lesson 14.

<sub>`D:/00mk/steel project/training/Training/workmen's_diary/2026-08-25(teach mk).md` · debugging/diagnosis</sub>

#### 🟡 MEDIUM · 2026-08-25 · Pixtral-Large was evaluated before its license was checked — commercial use is disallowed

**What happened.** Pixtral-Large was carried through weight-size and framework evaluation before a license check revealed it is under the Mistral Research License, which explicitly disallows commercial use without a separate paid license, ruling it out outright.

**Root cause.** License was checked last in the filter chain instead of first, so effort was spent on candidates that could never pass.

**Impact.** Wasted evaluation effort on a candidate that was disqualified on a criterion checkable in seconds.

**Fix.** License check applied as one of the three filters; Pixtral-Large eliminated.

**→ Rule.** Put the cheapest hard filter first. License and commercial-use terms take seconds to check and eliminate candidates before you spend time on weight sizes and framework support.

<sub>`D:/00mk/steel project/training/Training/workmen's_diary/2026-08-25.md` · process-order</sub>

#### 🟡 MEDIUM · 2026-08-25 · Claude misunderstood pass3 as "discard" when it is a real extraction stage with 8 subtasks

**What happened.** During the pass 0.5 / 1.5 architecture discussion, Claude was working from the belief that pass3 means discarding pages. Makham corrected it: pass3 is the extraction of the not-strictly-necessary pages and has its own `extract.md` with 8 subtasks.

**Root cause.** A pipeline stage's purpose was inferred from context rather than read from its own specification document, and the wrong understanding persisted long enough to shape an architecture conversation.

**Impact.** Architecture proposals were being made against a wrong model of the pipeline; if uncorrected, downstream work would have treated real extraction output as throwaway.

**Fix.** Corrected on the spot by Makham and recorded in the diary.

**→ Rule.** Read a pipeline stage's own spec before reasoning about it. Write down the corrected understanding immediately — an unrecorded correction gets re-made by the next session.

<sub>`D:/00mk/steel project/training/Training/workmen's_diary/2026-08-25.md` · misunderstanding</sub>

#### 🟡 MEDIUM · 2026-08-25 · The training set was rebuilt AFTER the TEST_STEPS sanity check ran, so the recorded check described data that no longer existed

**What happened.** t03_workflow.md row 7 recorded "ภาพจริง 2339×1654 ต่ำกว่า cap 5,120 อยู่แล้ว = ไม่ย่อเลย" from a TEST_STEPS run at 22:00, but train.jsonl on disk is timestamped 22:13 — the dataset was rebuilt 13 minutes after the check. No image of the recorded size exists in the current train set, and the old 3,778-token figure cannot be proven or disproven.

**Root cause.** A verification result was recorded as a durable fact without pinning it to the dataset version it measured; the rebuild step does not invalidate or re-trigger the checks that ran against the previous build.

**Impact.** A recorded, quoted measurement in the workflow doc became unverifiable — it could not be confirmed as a past error or a still-true fact, so it had to be written down as "do not trust" rather than corrected.

**Fix.** Recorded honestly as "re-read what the assert prints next run; do not trust the old 3,778 figure" instead of asserting a past error; the assert itself was fixed to print the configured cap alongside the measured value.

**→ Rule.** Stamp every recorded measurement with the dataset build it came from, and re-run the sanity checks after any rebuild — otherwise a rebuild silently orphans every number recorded before it.

<sub>`D:/00mk/steel project/training/Training/workmen's_diary/2026-08-25.md` · process</sub>

#### 🟡 MEDIUM · 2026-08-26 · House 42 deleted locally (uncommitted) while origin held newer teammate edits — merge conflict

**What happened.** Makham deleted house 42 (`42บ้าน_เล็ก_2ชั้น_18`) from his local working tree without committing, while origin still had the house with newer edits from a teammate. This produced a diverged-branch merge conflict on main.

**Root cause.** An uncommitted local deletion is invisible to everyone else, so a teammate kept editing a house that was already considered dead locally. No coordination signal existed for "this house is being dropped".

**Impact.** Merge conflict requiring manual resolution; risk of destroying a teammate's fresh work if the deletion had simply won the merge.

**Fix.** Parked the house in `wait_for_ทิ้ง/42บ้าน_เล็ก_2ชั้น_18/` instead of hard-deleting, so nothing is lost. Its final fate is still undecided.

**→ Rule.** Never resolve a deletion-vs-edit conflict by deleting. Park the disputed data in a holding area and decide later — and announce a house's removal before deleting it locally.

<sub>`D:/00mk/steel project/training/Training/workmen's_diary/2026-08-26.md` · process</sub>

#### 🟡 MEDIUM · 2026-08-26 · None of the GPU-research recommendations were acted on

**What happened.** A long GPU/model-selection research session produced concrete recommendations — split plan_beam into per-grid-zone sub-answers, try FINETUNE_VISION=1, run a zero-shot Thai-read test before committing to GLM-4.6V or Llama-4-Scout — and none of them had been executed.

**Root cause.** Research output landed in a diary entry and a PDF rather than in a task list with owners. Recommendations with no ticket decay into notes.

**Impact.** The plan_beam bottleneck — the round's headline failure — remained unaddressed while other work proceeded.

**Fix.** Not fixed; recorded as pending with a pointer to the original reasoning in 2026-08-25's [19:30-01:30] entry.

**→ Rule.** Convert every research recommendation into a concrete next action with a cost estimate the same session, or it will not happen. A recommendation buried in prose is a recommendation not made.

<sub>`D:/00mk/steel project/training/Training/workmen's_diary/2026-08-26.md` · process</sub>

#### 🟡 MEDIUM · 2026-08-26 · train/val/test.jsonl regenerated — the previous set is gone with no snapshot

**What happened.** Adding the glossary triggered a full regenerate of train/val/test.jsonl. The old jsonl set no longer exists. The new build also folded in `strip_assigned` and GT edits made under att1235.

**Root cause.** The dataset builder writes in place with no versioning or archive of the previous build. Reproducibility depends entirely on the GT and builder both being at the right commit.

**Impact.** Any result produced against the previous jsonl cannot be exactly reproduced unless the exact GT + builder commit is recovered. Multiple changes (glossary + strip_assigned + GT edits) landed in the same regenerate, so their effects cannot be separated.

**Fix.** Not fixed — noted that jsonl can always be rebuilt from GT, so this is not deletion. But the old bytes are gone.

**→ Rule.** Stamp each dataset build with a hash/version and keep the manifest, so any result can be tied to an exact dataset. Do not bundle multiple independent changes into one regenerate — you lose the ability to attribute a metric change to a cause.

<sub>`D:/00mk/steel project/training/Training/workmen's_diary/2026-08-26.md` · process</sub>

#### 🟡 MEDIUM · 2026-08-26 · GT correction commits say only "final"/a house number — reasoning is unrecoverable

**What happened.** Seven GT-correction commits across houses 01, 28, 29, 30, 34, 35, 36, 43, 44 carried messages like "บ้าน 34 final", "29", "แก้ระบบ", "แก้แบบ". The diary entry had to be reconstructed from git log alone, and the reasoning behind each individual fix is not captured anywhere.

**Root cause.** Commits were made during focused solo GT work with no session transcript and no per-fix note. The commit message was treated as a checkpoint marker rather than a record.

**Impact.** Nobody can later tell why a specific rebar count or grid line was changed, or whether it was a genuine drawing re-read or a mistake. GT provenance is lost for 9 houses' worth of corrections.

**Fix.** Not fixable retroactively — the diary notes to ask makham directly if detail is needed.

**→ Rule.** A GT data correction commit must name what changed and why (which drawing, which value, what it was before). "final" tells a future reader nothing and destroys the audit trail on data that feeds a model.

<sub>`D:/00mk/steel project/training/Training/workmen's_diary/2026-08-26.md` · process</sub>

#### 🟡 MEDIUM · 2026-08-27 · A 156-line GT page deleted from house 37 with no recorded reason

**What happened.** Commit `1d01d98` "บ้าน 37 final" deleted `หน้า26_section_slab_stair.json` (156 lines). The diary can only speculate: "likely folded into another page or found invalid".

**Root cause.** Same as the commit-message problem — a data deletion was bundled into a batch "final" commit with no note explaining whether the page was merged elsewhere or judged invalid.

**Impact.** 156 lines of extracted GT are gone with no record of whether they were duplicated elsewhere or genuinely wrong. If it was a mistake, nobody will know.

**Fix.** Not fixed — flagged as unexplained in the diary.

**→ Rule.** Deleting GT is a data decision, not a cleanup. It needs its own commit and a one-line reason, always.

<sub>`D:/00mk/steel project/training/Training/workmen's_diary/2026-08-27.md` · process</sub>

#### 🟡 MEDIUM · 2026-08-29 · The hint-block contract lives in two places (prompt.md and cv_hint_text()) with only a comment preventing drift

**What happened.** pass2.4_hint/prompt.md documents what a hint block must contain, while the code that actually generates the text is cv_hint_text() inside tools/cv_scan.py. The README explicitly notes the file exists 'กันสองที่ drift กัน' — as a contract to stop the two diverging.

**Root cause.** Specification and implementation are stored separately with no automated conformance test; the only thing keeping them aligned is a human remembering to update both.

**Impact.** No damage yet, but this is the identical structural setup that produced earlier drift incidents in this project.

**Fix.** Not fully fixed — mitigated only by documenting the relationship. No test asserts that cv_hint_text() output satisfies prompt.md's contract.

**→ Rule.** When a spec document and its implementation must agree, add an automated test that validates the implementation's output against the spec. A comment saying 'keep these in sync' is not a control.

<sub>`D:/00mk/steel project/training/Training/workmen's_diary/สอน_t04_Purson_2026-08-29.md` · process</sub>

#### 🟡 MEDIUM · 2026-08-29 · pass 4 prompts were fully written and then cancelled as unnecessary

**What happened.** pass 4 covered secondary sheets (architectural, electrical, sanitary, cover, table of contents). On 2026-08-29 Makham cancelled it outright — 'หน้าพวกนั้นไม่จำเป็น'. The prompts remain parked in t03/pass4_unused/.

**Root cause.** Scope was set before confirming which sheet types the downstream BOQ/BBS calculation actually consumes. Work was built for pages that were never required.

**Impact.** Prompt authoring effort for an entire pass wasted; the artifacts are now dead weight kept only so they are not lost.

**Fix.** Removed from the conveyor, prompts kept but marked unused.

**→ Rule.** Confirm downstream consumption before building an extraction stage. Trace which fields the final calculation actually reads, and only build passes that feed them.

<sub>`D:/00mk/steel project/training/Training/workmen's_diary/สอน_t04_Purson_2026-08-29.md` · scope</sub>

#### 🟡 MEDIUM · 2026-08-29 · Experiment arm 2.4b (numbered marked images) was built into the pipeline and then cancelled

**What happened.** The CV scan produces a numbered marked-up image per page, originally intended to be fed to the model as experiment arm 2.4b. That arm was cancelled on 2026-08-29 ('ใส่แต่ hint พอ'), leaving the marked image as a human-viewing artifact only, and apply_arm() had to be simplified back down.

**Root cause.** A third experimental arm was implemented before deciding whether three arms were affordable or necessary, so both the image-generation path and the arm-switching code carried dead complexity.

**Impact.** Wasted implementation effort on the 2.4b path plus rework to strip it out of apply_arm(); the marked-image generation now runs with no consumer other than human inspection.

**Fix.** Arm cancelled, apply_arm() reduced to two arms ('หลังตัด 2.4b แล้ว เหลือเรียบมาก').

**→ Rule.** Decide the experiment's arm count before implementing the switching machinery. Start with the control plus one treatment; add arms only when the first comparison shows they are needed.

<sub>`D:/00mk/steel project/training/Training/workmen's_diary/สอน_t04_Purson_2026-08-29.md` · scope</sub>

#### 🟡 MEDIUM · 2026-08-29 · pass 3 takeoff prompt was written in full but has never been executed, and may need a full rewrite

**What happened.** The pass 3 prompt is complete but has never been run. It is deliberately blocked pending the arm-experiment result, and the README states outright that if the model does not read hints, the entire pass 3 block must be rethought.

**Root cause.** A downstream stage was authored in full before its upstream dependency (does the model use hints at all?) was answered, so its design rests on an unvalidated assumption.

**Impact.** An entire prompt's worth of work is at risk of being discarded; meanwhile the pipeline has an untested final stage, so end-to-end capability is unknown.

**Fix.** Not fixed — status explicitly recorded as 'เขียนเต็ม ยังไม่เคยรัน' with the dependency named.

**→ Rule.** Do not fully build a stage whose design depends on an unanswered upstream question. Run the cheap experiment that resolves the assumption first, then build.

<sub>`D:/00mk/steel project/training/Training/workmen's_diary/สอน_t04_Purson_2026-08-29.md` · scope</sub>

#### 🟡 MEDIUM · 2026-08-29 · The Vast rental section of the RUNBOOK is three hard rules — cheap card first, separate venv, pull results before destroy — each written after the corresponding loss

**What happened.** RUNBOOK.md codifies GPU rental as a checklist with three non-negotiables: rent the cheap card first, use an isolated venv, download results before destroying the instance. These are stated as rules, not as suggestions, and they map one-to-one onto the three ways a rented-GPU night can be lost: debugging on an expensive card, a pip install breaking a running job in a shared environment, and an ephemeral instance destroyed with the outputs still on it.

**Root cause.** Each rule exists because the failure it prevents costs real money or unrecoverable output, and none of them is enforced by tooling — they are prose in a runbook that a tired operator reads at the start of a night and not again at the end.

**Impact.** Unquantified in this file, but each violation is a full rental night: wrong-card debugging, a corrupted environment mid-training, or a destroyed instance with no artifacts.

**Fix.** Written down in RUNBOOK.md as a pre-flight checklist. Not automated — no script blocks a destroy before a download, and no check enforces the venv.

**→ Rule.** A rule that only lives in a runbook gets skipped exactly when it matters. The destroy step in particular should refuse to run until the outputs are confirmed off the box.

<sub>`D:/00mk/steel project/training/Training/workmen's_diary/สอน_t04_Purson_2026-08-29.md` · process</sub>

#### 🟡 MEDIUM · 2026-08-29 · Moving prompts and scripts from t03 to t04_Purson broke relative paths across many files

**What happened.** Moving pass0_classify/, pass2 prompts and later the whole data_before_tune set from t03 into t04_Purson broke relative paths in the moved prompts themselves (../_common.md → ../../t03/_common.md), in build_dataset_t03.py's load_subtask_prompt, in README pointers, in assembled_example.md and in t03/README.md.

**Root cause.** Prompts and scripts referenced each other by relative path with no path constant or resolver, so any directory move breaks a scattered set of references that only a full grep can find.

**Impact.** Every move required a manual path-fix sweep and a rebuild-and-compare to prove nothing broke. The moves happened in at least three separate batches on the same day, each needing its own sweep.

**Fix.** Fixed every path, verified all resolve, and rebuilt the dataset each time confirming identical counts (989 → 989, then 987 → 1020 only from deliberate data additions) — proving the moves caused no regression. t03/README.md got a staleness note rather than a full rewrite.

**→ Rule.** Verify a directory move by rebuilding the artifact and comparing counts against the pre-move number — a passing import is not proof. Better: resolve cross-file references through a path constant so a move touches one line.

<sub>`D:/00mk/steel project/training/Training/workmen's_diary/2026-08-29.md` · process</sub>

#### 🟡 MEDIUM · 2026-08-29 · InternVL3 rejected in the 2026-08-26 catalog, then adopted three days later — the rejection reason was never actionable

**What happened.** The 2026-08-26 model catalog rejected InternVL3 because "สมองเป็น Qwen2.5-72B อยู่ดี" (the backbone is Qwen2.5-72B anyway). On 2026-08-29 Makham directed t04 to use InternVL3-78B, explicitly accepting that condition.

**Root cause.** The catalog's rejection criterion was an architectural observation, not a measured performance disadvantage. A rejection reason that nobody can act on or verify does not survive contact with a decision-maker who accepts the tradeoff.

**Impact.** Three days of downstream planning proceeded on a model catalog whose exclusion was reversed, and the reversal carried the full toolchain cost documented above.

**Fix.** Model adopted with the condition accepted; new Phase 0 workflow doc written for the toolchain rebuild.

**→ Rule.** A model rejection must cite a measured deficiency or a hard constraint (license, framework support, VRAM), not an architectural opinion. Rank candidates by testable criteria so a reversal is a data question, not a preference question.

<sub>`D:/00mk/steel project/training/Training/workmen's_diary/2026-08-29.md` · planning</sub>

#### 🟡 MEDIUM · 2026-08-29 · pass 3 prompt and merge_guard written but never run against a model — explicitly forbidden to try

**What happened.** The pass3_takeoff prompt and tools/merge_guard.py (which enforces 'never delete' via stubs and dropped_by_pass3) were written and self-checked, but pass 3 has no runner and has never been executed against a model. WORKFLOW_INTERN.md lists it as "pass 3 ห้ามลอง" (do not attempt).

**Root cause.** Deliberate sequencing — waiting for the 3-arm experiment results before building the runner. But it leaves a fully-written, entirely-unvalidated stage in the codebase.

**Impact.** An untested pipeline stage that looks complete. merge_guard's whole protection depends on JSON parsing succeeding first, which has never been verified end-to-end with real model output.

**Fix.** Not fixed by design; the gap is documented in WORKFLOW_INTERN.md alongside the other known holes (pass 0 has no runner, infer reads only jsonl, column bank missing 13 houses).

**→ Rule.** Mark unrun code as unvalidated in the place someone would run it from, not only in a workflow doc. Written-and-self-checked is not the same as ever-executed.

<sub>`D:/00mk/steel project/training/Training/workmen's_diary/2026-08-29.md` · process</sub>

#### 🟡 MEDIUM · 2026-08-29 · k-fold CV infrastructure was built after being judged not worth the GPU-hours, and has never been run

**What happened.** `--folds N` in build_dataset and `FOLD=N` in train_t03.py were implemented and verified on 5 folds, on an explicit order given despite the stated assessment that it was not worth the GPU cost. No fold has been trained.

**Root cause.** The cost objection was raised and overruled, but no decision was made about when or whether the 5× GPU spend would actually happen — so the code shipped into a waiting state.

**Impact.** Working infrastructure with a 5× cost multiplier sitting unused, in the same category as pass 4 and arm 2.4b: built, wired, never executed. And it was built against train_t03.py, which the InternVL3 switch invalidated the same day.

**Fix.** not fixed — infra complete, waiting on a human to decide to spend the GPU time

**→ Rule.** Build-on-request is fine, but attach the trigger condition at build time ('run when X'). Infra with no run condition and a 5× cost is indistinguishable from infra that will never run — and it rots when the toolchain under it changes.

<sub>`D:/00mk/steel project/training/Training/workmen's_diary/2026-08-29.md` · wasted-work</sub>

#### 🟡 MEDIUM · 2026-08-30 · Standing risk of returning only the last GPU and confusing stop with destroy (prior 2026-08-24 lesson) — this round had 4 cards

**What happened.** The workflow's card-return step was written for a single card. This round used 4 rented instances at once, so the step was expanded to require destroying all four, explicitly restating that destroy is not the same as stop (a lesson from 2026-08-24) and adding a verification step.

**Root cause.** Teardown checklists were written for the single-card case and did not scale with the number of resources; 'stop' releases nothing on vast.ai but reads as done.

**Impact.** Forgetting a single card costs a full day of burn (~$103/day at this round's rate). Ultimately all 4 were returned and verified at 0 instances, with $16.66 credit remaining.

**Fix.** Workflow item 13 rewritten with all 4 instance IDs and full commands in a table, plus the `vastai show instances` = 0 verification step.

**→ Rule.** Make the teardown checklist enumerate every resource by ID and end with a provider-side query proving zero remain — never a generic 'return the card' line.

<sub>`D:/00mk/steel project/training/Training/workmen's_diary/2026-08-30.md` · process</sub>

#### 🟡 MEDIUM · 2026-08-30 · Reported 'workflow updated' when the file had not actually been edited

**What happened.** A previous message stated the workflow doc had been updated, but the real file was never modified. Corrected later and acknowledged directly in chat.

**Root cause.** Reporting an intended action as a completed one — the write step was skipped but the status message was already composed.

**Impact.** The workflow document stayed out of sync with reality while everyone believed it was current, feeding the larger doc-drift problem found in the later audit.

**Fix.** Actually edited items 4/6 of the task sequence and admitted the error openly.

**→ Rule.** Never report a file change as done without having actually issued the write; when in doubt re-read the file and quote the changed line as evidence.

<sub>`D:/00mk/steel project/training/Training/workmen's_diary/2026-08-30.md` · process</sub>

#### 🟡 MEDIUM · 2026-08-30 · llama.cpp's GGUF converter only supports non-hf InternVL3 checkpoints, but the whole pipeline forced training on the `-hf` variant

**What happened.** Found before being asked: `convert_hf_to_gguf.py` supports InternVL3 only for 'non-hf' checkpoints, while LLaMA-Factory requires the `-hf` model. Whether a merged `-hf` adapter can be converted to GGUF at all was unverified — the same class of risk as the t01 'Day of Shame'.

**Root cause.** Two required steps of the pipeline (training framework and export format) each had their own model-variant requirement, and the compatibility between them was never checked when the framework was chosen.

**Impact.** Would have been discovered only after a full 78B training run if not caught early — potentially an unexportable model after ~$60 of training.

**Fix.** Added as Phase 0 item 14 in `t04_workflow.md` requiring a GGUF conversion test with a small InternVL3 (2B/8B) during the dry-run, before spending on the 78B. Later Makham cancelled GGUF entirely ('adapter is enough'), which removed the whole risk class from the round; the reasoning was kept in the doc, not deleted.

**→ Rule.** Verify end-to-end format compatibility (train → merge → export → serve) on the smallest possible model before committing to a large paid run — never let the export step be the last thing you test.

<sub>`D:/00mk/steel project/training/Training/workmen's_diary/2026-08-30.md` · process</sub>

#### 🟡 MEDIUM · 2026-08-30 · The plan to serve the t03 adapter via vLLM was invalid — Unsloth's MoE LoRA layout matches neither vLLM format

**What happened.** Inspecting `adapter_model.safetensors` before renting a GPU showed the MoE expert LoRA stored as `...mlp.experts.lora_A.weight` with shape [4096, 2048] — 256 experts × rank 16 flattened together, an Unsloth-specific layout. Key counting confirmed neither vLLM-accepted form was present: no `gate_up_proj/down_proj`, no per-expert indices.

**Root cause.** The serving plan assumed a de-facto standard adapter layout without inspecting the actual weight file produced by the training framework.

**Impact.** Caught before renting. Had it not been checked: rent a card → wait ~45 minutes for the model to load → fail after paying, or worse, silently produce garbage via the mis-declared vLLM path.

**Fix.** Wrote `serve_purson.py` — a FastAPI OpenAI-compatible shim that loads with Unsloth internally, lifting the load/generate/xgrammar code straight from `infer_house_t03.py`, which had already run 33 real jobs. `worker.py` needed no changes, and the vLLM path can be swapped back if the adapter is ever converted.

**→ Rule.** Inspect the actual artifact (key names, shapes) against the consumer's expected format on a local machine before renting any GPU — 'check the cheap thing before the expensive thing'.

<sub>`D:/00mk/steel project/training/Training/workmen's_diary/2026-08-30.md` · serving-architecture</sub>

#### 🟡 MEDIUM · 2026-08-30 · The whole Purson→web integration was written with none of its steps ever executed — migration unapplied, function undeployed, button never pressed against a real GPU

**What happened.** Seven new files were written wiring Purson into Constistant (queue table, Edge Function, worker, presentation script, JS client, UI button), but at that point the migration was not applied, the Edge Function not deployed, the button never clicked against a real worker+GPU, and `--model t04` (78B, TP2) had never been served even once.

**Root cause.** An entire integration was built top-to-bottom on unverified assumptions about every external boundary, with verification deferred to a single future rehearsal.

**Impact.** Any of the untested boundaries could have failed on presentation day. Subsequent sessions did close most of them (migration applied, Supabase e2e passed, real GPU test run) but the blocking-call bug and the browser-path test were still open at end of day.

**Fix.** Explicitly written down as 'ยังไม่พิสูจน์เลยสักขั้น' with the rule 'rehearse the full end-to-end round before the presentation, do not debut mid-event'. Later sessions proved the Supabase hop, the importer path, and partial model output.

**→ Rule.** For anything with a hard demo date, rehearse the complete end-to-end path at least once well before the date. Write down explicitly which steps have never executed, and treat that list as the schedule.

<sub>`D:/00mk/steel project/training/Training/workmen's_diary/2026-08-30.md` · process</sub>

#### 🟡 MEDIUM · 2026-08-30 · `test_browser_path.py` (real user JWT, not service key) never completed a run against the real model

**What happened.** The new browser-path test verified RLS behaviour with a real user JWT (upload allowed under own prefix, denied outside it; job insert relying on `auth.uid()` default; user cannot change job status), but the run against the real model never finished because the server hung and the machine had to be torn down.

**Root cause.** The test depended on the same inference server that had the blocking-event-loop bug, so the last unproven hop could not be closed.

**Impact.** There is still no evidence that a real end user can go from browser to model result end-to-end — the single most important claim for the presentation.

**Fix.** Listed as item 3 of the pre-presentation must-do list.

**→ Rule.** Sequence verification so the riskiest end-to-end claim is proven first, while the rented resource is healthy — do not leave the highest-value test until after exploratory runs that can destabilise the environment.

<sub>`D:/00mk/steel project/training/Training/workmen's_diary/2026-08-30.md` · process</sub>

#### 🟡 MEDIUM · 2026-08-30 · A full house takes ~3 hours and ~$3.2 of GPU — it cannot be run live during the presentation

**What happened.** Measured on the rented card: ~4-5 minutes per job, so a full house (~38 pass2 jobs) takes about 3 hours at ~$3.2.

**Root cause.** Per-job latency was never measured before designing a presentation flow that implied showing extraction live.

**Impact.** Would have produced a dead demo if run on stage. Caught in time.

**Fix.** Decision recorded: the extraction must be run in advance, not clicked live during the presentation.

**→ Rule.** Measure per-unit latency of any demo workload and multiply by the real workload size before designing the demo flow — anything over a couple of minutes must be pre-computed.

<sub>`D:/00mk/steel project/training/Training/workmen's_diary/2026-08-30.md` · process</sub>

#### 🟡 MEDIUM · 2026-08-30 · Advised staying on the single existing split 'to save budget for eval' without ever checking whether that split's val was contaminated

**What happened.** Before the k-fold decision, the standing recommendation was to keep training on the one existing train/val split and spend the saved money on evaluation instead. When the split was finally checked with a real script (house names pulled from image paths), all 5 val houses turned out to be in train — so the eval the budget was being saved for could never have measured generalisation. The recommendation had been given on an unverified assumption about the data.

**Root cause.** A budget/scheduling recommendation was made about a dataset whose basic property (train/val disjointness) had never been verified. The split had been inherited from t03, where the overlap was a deliberate design choice for a different purpose, and that provenance was not re-examined when the purpose changed.

**Impact.** The plan was steered toward an eval that would have produced meaningless numbers; the direction had to be reversed to k-fold, forcing new fold builds, new configs, and additional rentals.

**Fix.** Verified with a script, admitted to Makham directly, and the plan changed to k-fold on clean folds (0 shared houses, verified before spending).

**→ Rule.** Do not give budget or scheduling advice about a dataset until its split integrity has been verified — one cheap script is smaller than the plan built on top of the assumption.

<sub>`D:/00mk/steel project/training/Training/workmen's_diary/2026-08-30.md` · process/planning</sub>

#### 🟡 MEDIUM · 2026-08-31 · Manual eyeball matching of beam pages was attempted and proved physically impossible

**What happened.** The queued plan was to eyeball-match beam pages one by one. On the real pages the box numbers overlap so densely they cannot be read visually at all.

**Root cause.** The plan was made without first testing the method on the hardest real page.

**Impact.** Work was queued and started on a method that could not work, costing time before the pivot.

**Fix.** Replaced eyeballing entirely with geometry: fitted a linear metre-to-pixel mapping from column boxes sitting on named (non-dummy) grid lines, then matched beam boxes by real pixel distance. Verified by hand on page 31 (19 pairs, 100% GT match) before trusting it, plus a robust fit tested on the most complex page with residual 0.

**→ Rule.** Pilot any manual method on the single hardest real case before queueing it across a batch — and prefer a geometric/deterministic method over human inspection when coordinates already exist.

<sub>`D:/00mk/steel project/training/Training/workmen's_diary/2026-08-31.md` · process</sub>

#### 🟡 MEDIUM · 2026-08-31 · Training ETA was off by a factor of two because InternVL-78B step times were applied to Qwen 35B-A3B

**What happened.** The 13-15 hour estimate came from t04's measured 180-196s/step on InternVL3-78B. Real logs showed 82-106s/step on the much lighter Qwen 35B-A3B model.

**Root cause.** A measured constant from one model architecture was reused for a materially different one without flagging the substitution as unvalidated.

**Impact.** Budget and scheduling planning was wrong by 2x; the error was in the safe direction but it drove the whole rental sizing decision.

**Fix.** Recomputed from real per-step log values once training started.

**→ Rule.** Never carry a step-time constant across model architectures — treat it as unknown until a real dry-run on the target model produces a number.

<sub>`D:/00mk/steel project/training/Training/workmen's_diary/2026-08-31.md` · estimation</sub>

#### 🟡 MEDIUM · 2026-08-31 · Destroyed three GPUs about two minutes before the 'don't return the cards yet' message arrived

**What happened.** gpu2/3/4 were destroyed after the Day-of-Shame checklist passed; Makham's instruction not to return them arrived roughly two minutes later.

**Root cause.** An irreversible action was taken during a period when a human instruction could still be in flight.

**Impact.** No data lost (everything was on HuggingFace) but the cards could not be recovered if further work had been wanted.

**Fix.** Reported it directly and immediately; gpu1 was held per the follow-up instruction.

**→ Rule.** Treat destroy as irreversible: when a human is awake and in the loop, pause briefly before destroying — the cost of waiting minutes is far below the cost of a lost machine.

<sub>`D:/00mk/steel project/training/Training/workmen's_diary/2026-08-31.md` · process</sub>

#### 🟡 MEDIUM · 2026-08-31 · destrier (t05) test results were written under t04_Purson, making them look like results from the dead t04 arm

**What happened.** The benchmark house images had been staged under t04_Purson/test_house_new/ on 30 Aug. Scripts and result files for destrier (t05 Courser) were then added on top of them in the same folder.

**Root cause.** A shared, cross-round benchmark asset was stored under a round-specific folder, and new work followed the existing location without questioning it.

**Impact.** Results appeared to belong to the abandoned Voldemort/t04 arm — a real misattribution risk. Makham caught it.

**Fix.** Moved the scripts, prompt and first four result files to t05_Courser/destrier_test_house/ locally. The 65 page images were deliberately left in place because gpu1 was mid-run reading from that path.

**→ Rule.** Store cross-round benchmark assets in a round-neutral location from the start, and never write a new round's outputs into a previous round's folder just because the inputs happen to live there.

<sub>`D:/00mk/steel project/training/Training/workmen's_diary/2026-08-31.md` · process</sub>

#### 🟡 MEDIUM · 2026-08-31 · op04_run.py writes to fixed output filenames, so a comparison round would have destroyed the first round's results

**What happened.** The scoring runner writes the same output filenames every time. Without manually renaming the greedy run's folder first, the sampling comparison round would have overwritten it.

**Root cause.** No run identifier in the output path.

**Impact.** Nearly lost the greedy baseline that the entire greedy-vs-sampling comparison depends on; caught in time.

**Fix.** Renamed op04 to op04_greedy_run1 before the second run.

**→ Rule.** Give every experiment run its own output directory keyed by run identifier — never rely on remembering to rename before a comparison run.

<sub>`D:/00mk/steel project/training/Training/workmen's_diary/2026-08-31.md` · process</sub>

#### 🟡 MEDIUM · 2026-08-31 · The U/P proportion fallback is assigned to the VLM, which research proved cannot measure at takeoff accuracy

**What happened.** Research ordered by Makham established that VLMs cannot measure pixels at takeoff precision (MeasureBench best 30.3%; grounding scored at IoU 0.5 passes while being 25-30% off). The current design still asks the VLM to do the U/P proportion fallback — a metric job.

**Root cause.** The symbolic/metric split (VLM reads marks, CV+gridmaster does distances) was correct in pass3 rule 5 but was never applied to the proportion fallback path.

**Impact.** Any dimension the model derives via that fallback is unreliable and will flow into quantity takeoff.

**Fix.** not fixed — recorded in the dossier as a recommendation to move it to the CV layer

**→ Rule.** Every place the pipeline asks the model for a number rather than a name is a place to audit against the symbolic/metric split, not just the one path being designed at the time.

<sub>`D:/00mk/steel project/training/Training/workmen's_diary/2026-08-31.md` · architecture</sub>

#### 🟡 MEDIUM · 2026-09-01 · t44 was built on InternVL3-78B, a model the team's own catalogue had disqualified days earlier

**What happened.** The 26 Aug catalogue disqualified InternVL3-78B because it uses Qwen2.5-72B as its backbone, violating the 'not Qwen by backbone' criterion. Days later, t44 (Voldemort) was launched on exactly that model, described in the 1 Sep write-up as 'โมเดลคนละตัว'.

**Root cause.** The catalogue's findings were not treated as a binding shortlist when the next branch was launched — the research artifact and the decision that followed it were disconnected, so the disqualification reason did not carry forward.

**Impact.** Effort spent standing up a branch on a model the team had already ruled out on documented grounds; the branch then died for an unrelated reason (quantized vision encoder) before the backbone issue mattered.

**Fix.** Not addressed — the discrepancy is visible only by reading both documents together, and is not reconciled in either.

**→ Rule.** When research produces a disqualification list, make it the binding input to the next selection decision and record which shortlist entry was chosen and why. A catalogue nobody consults at decision time is wasted research.

<sub>`D:/00mk/steel project/training/Training/workmen's_diary/สอนมะขาม_ทำไม_Purson_กับ_Voldemort_พัง_2026-09-01.md` · process</sub>

#### 🟡 MEDIUM · 2026-09-01 · pass3 can now measure unresolved beam spans but was never wired into the adapter to replace the nulls

**What happened.** `span_source: 'unresolved'` in `raw-extraction-adapter.js` (beams whose endpoints are not on a named grid line) can in principle now be resolved by pass3's measurements — but the adapter was never connected to consume them, so the values stay null.

**Root cause.** A capability was built without connecting it to the consumer that needed it, leaving the original defect fully in place while appearing solved.

**Impact.** Beams with off-grid endpoints still contribute no span — and therefore no quantity — despite the measurement now existing.

**Fix.** Not fixed — recorded as pending across multiple entries.

**→ Rule.** Building the capability is half the fix. Track 'wired into the consumer' as a separate, explicit completion criterion, or the original bug survives untouched behind a solved-looking component.

<sub>`2026-09-01.md` · process</sub>

#### 🟡 MEDIUM · 2026-09-01 · Whole demo environment torn down and re-set-up a second time because the first run was not screen-recorded

**What happened.** The live-demo teardown cycle (`presentation.py down`) was run twice in one day. One of the two full down/up cycles existed only to redo the demo with screen recording turned on — i.e. a complete rented-GPU setup, tunnel, worker start and job run were repeated because the first pass produced no recording.

**Root cause.** Recording was not part of the demo start checklist, so the artifact the demo existed to produce (a recording) was missing after a successful run and the only remedy was to re-rent and re-run everything.

**Impact.** A second full GPU rental + setup cycle (~1 hour of session time on a day that already lost its demo to host failures), for zero new technical output.

**Fix.** not fixed — no checklist item added; the redo was done manually

**→ Rule.** Anything whose only purpose is to produce an artifact for someone else (recording, screenshot, exported file) must be armed and verified BEFORE the expensive run starts, not after — a GPU run cannot be replayed for free.

<sub>`D:/00mk/steel project/training/Training/workmen's_diary/2026-09-01.md` · process</sub>

#### 🟡 MEDIUM · 2026-09-01 · Codebase could not be reorganised because scripts hard-code paths, so a 115 MB duplicate copy was made instead — two sources that will drift

**What happened.** The t05 cleanup could not move any .py/.jsonl file, because the scripts reference paths directly and `onstart.sh` uploads the entire folder to the rented box. The workaround was to create `tune_ai/t05_Destrier/` as a 115 MB *copy* of everything actually in use (run_this/, prompts/, training/, merge_model/, proof/, web_integration/) while leaving the originals in place.

**Root cause.** Hard-coded relative paths across the training/serving scripts make the layout immovable, so organisation had to be achieved by duplication rather than by moving.

**Impact.** 115 MB of the most important files now exist in two places with no sync mechanism — precisely the situation that already killed the parallel `en/` diary folder (it fell out of date after 2026-07-21 and had to be deleted). A fix applied to one copy will silently not reach the other.

**Fix.** not fixed — copy shipped deliberately, originals untouched, no sync or symlink

**→ Rule.** Duplicating files to organise them creates a second source of truth that WILL drift; this repo has already deleted one such folder for that exact reason. Fix the hard-coded paths, or use a single copy plus a manifest, before copying anything again.

<sub>`D:/00mk/steel project/training/Training/workmen's_diary/2026-09-01.md` · process</sub>

#### 🟡 MEDIUM · 2026-09-02 · Truncated-JSON recovery is a manual salvage step, not real automation

**What happened.** `salvage_json.py` successfully recovered the broken pages, but it is run by hand. There is no permanent fix for dense pages — the pipeline still cannot pass such a sheet on its own; someone must crop it or salvage the output.

**Root cause.** The failure was addressed at the recovery end rather than the cause end. Salvage makes the symptom survivable and thereby removes the pressure to fix the underlying density problem.

**Impact.** Every future house with a dense multi-view sheet requires human intervention; the pipeline is not actually unattended.

**Fix.** Not fixed — explicitly recorded that cropping footing and beam apart is the likely permanent fix but has not been built.

**→ Rule.** A salvage script relieves pain but hides the defect — log it as debt with the real fix named, and do not count the pipeline as automated while a human step remains in the normal path.

<sub>`2026-09-02.md` · process</sub>

#### 🟡 MEDIUM ·  · Pushing predictions into Label Studio Repeater Choices without a small test first broke import for all 71 tasks

**What happened.** An unverified mechanism (pushing model predictions into a Repeater Choices control) was trialed directly on the full 71-task dataset instead of one record first.

**Root cause.** No small-scale test step existed before applying a new, unverified mechanism to the entire dataset at once.

**Impact.** Import broke for all 71 tasks in one shot instead of failing on a single test record.

**Fix.** Adopted a standing rule: always trial an unverified mechanism on one record before the full dataset.

**→ Rule.** Never trial an unverified mechanism on the full dataset at once — test on one record first.

<sub>`d:/00mk/steel project/training/Training/No_touch_box/docs/rule_of_tune.md` · process-rollout-discipline</sub>

#### 🟡 MEDIUM ·  · The warn-before-acting rule was found to be missing coverage for external system state, not just local files

**What happened.** It was recognized that the standing warn-before-editing rule had not been explicitly scoped to cover external system state as well (e.g. deleting all tasks in a cloud annotation tool's Data Manager) — only local file edits were being warned about.

**Root cause.** The warning rule's scope was written with local files in mind and never explicitly extended to actions on external systems that could destroy real review data.

**Impact.** Risk of deleting real review data on an external system without the same warn-first discipline applied to local raw-JSON edits.

**Fix.** Extended the warning rule's scope explicitly: always ask whether real review data exists on an external system before proposing deletion there, same as for local files.

**→ Rule.** The warn-first rule also covers external system state, not just local files — e.g. deleting all tasks in a cloud annotation tool's Data Manager. Always ask whether real review data exists there before proposing deletion.

<sub>`d:/00mk/steel project/training/Training/No_touch_box/docs/rule_of_tune.md` · process-rule-scope-gap</sub>

#### ⚪ LOW · 2026-07-05 · Pages mixing two views were a known warned-about risk that was only confirmed by a pilot read after the schema was designed

**What happened.** A pilot read of pages 1, 2, 3, 19, 21 and 58 was done to check the designed patterns against reality, and found that pages 19 and 21 really do mix 2 views together — confirming an issue the Makham's Pattern document had already warned about.

**Root cause.** A known risk was documented as a warning rather than resolved as a design decision before extraction, so it had to be validated empirically afterwards and drove the split-into-separate-files-per-pattern rule that then applied to everything.

**Impact.** Comparatively small, because the pilot read caught it before the bulk run — but this same multi-view structure sits behind several of the day's low-confidence pages, including page 19 view2 which was subsequently re-extracted twice.

**Fix.** The pilot read was done deliberately before the bulk extraction, and the decision was made to split into separate files per pattern/view within the same page rather than using a Gen 2-style views[] array.

**→ Rule.** Keep doing the pilot read — it worked here and is the cheapest possible validation. But when a spec document warns about a structural risk, resolve it as a decision before extraction rather than carrying it as a warning; a warning that survives into the run becomes a mid-run schema change.

<sub>`D:/00mk/steel project/training/Training/workmen's_diary/2026-07-05.md` · planning-gap</sub>

#### ⚪ LOW · 2026-07-05 · The spec doc was moved out of the Training repo, then quietly moved back — the cross-repo relocation was churn, not a decision that held

**What happened.** On 2026-07-05 Makham's patter of rawjson20260705.md was moved out of the Training repo into Constistant/mk's stuff/, and the entry states it 'no longer exists at its old path in the Training repo'. It was then edited from that Constistant location all through 2026-07-06 (Gen 3.1/3.2/3.3 sections). But the retroactive 2026-08-04 note in the same diary file records it being archived from No_touch_box/docs/ — a Training-repo path — so it was moved back at some point, and the diary never records the reversal or the reason.

**Root cause.** The doc was relocated on the basis of which repo it 'belonged to' rather than which repo's work it governs — it is the extraction spec for Training-repo data, so keeping it in Constistant put the governing document one repo away from every file it governs, and that split did not survive.

**Impact.** A load-bearing spec spent at least a day in a different repo from the data it governs (with a 0-byte ghost left at its old path, causing a separate scare), and moved twice in total; anyone reading the diary chronologically gets two contradictory statements about where the file lives.

**Fix.** not fixed in these entries — the return move is only visible implicitly in the 2026-08-04 archival note's path

**→ Rule.** Keep a spec in the same repo as the data it governs. If a move is reversed later, record the reversal in the diary at the point it happens, otherwise the log leaves two contradictory locations on record.

<sub>`D:/00mk/steel project/training/Training/workmen's_diary/2026-07-05.md` · process</sub>

#### ⚪ LOW · 2026-07-10 · The first condensed schema (45KB to 10KB JSON) was rejected as too short and redone

**What happened.** primary_rawjson_schema.json condensed the 45KB draft to 10KB and was rejected with 'this looks too short'. It was rewritten as an 11.8KB .md keeping every operational rule and cutting only the Gen2-vs-Makham history, and the original .json was deleted.

**Root cause.** The compression target was set by size rather than by what must survive; no criterion distinguished operational rules (must keep) from rationale (safe to cut) before the first attempt.

**Impact.** A full write-and-review cycle discarded, plus a file created and deleted.

**Fix.** Rewrote as .md against an explicit rule: keep every operational rule, cut only history and reasoning.

**→ Rule.** Before condensing a spec, write down what class of content must survive verbatim — optimising for a byte target first guarantees a second attempt.

<sub>`D:/00mk/steel project/training/Training/workmen's_diary/2026-07-10.md` · process/rework</sub>

#### ⚪ LOW · 2026-07-10 · The production folder was created without its 00 sort prefix and had to be renamed mid-move

**What happened.** The folder `00file_for_making_rawjson_from_claude/` was initially created without the `00` prefix. In the middle of moving primary_rawjson_schema into it, the rename to add the prefix was ordered, so the move target changed mid-operation. The file itself was also churned in the same window: created as .json, moved, redone as .md, and the .json then deleted.

**Root cause.** No naming convention was settled before the folder was created, even though the sibling convention (`0N<house>`) for house folders was being defined in the same session.

**Impact.** Minor — a rename plus a re-point of the move. Cost is a few minutes and one more chance for a path reference to be left pointing at the old name.

**Fix.** Folder renamed to add the 00 prefix; move completed to the new name.

**→ Rule.** Settle the naming convention for a folder before putting anything in it — renaming a directory mid-move is where stale path references get created.

<sub>`D:/00mk/steel project/training/Training/workmen's_diary/2026-07-10.md` · process</sub>

#### ⚪ LOW · 2026-07-12 · The same source-document price anomaly re-flagged as a reading error on four consecutive houses

**What happened.** House 6's row in the 10-house price table shows spread footing as more expensive than pile foundation. This was flagged as a suspected reading error on houses 2, 3, 4 and again on 5 before being accepted as real data from the original.

**Root cause.** There was no shared registry of already-adjudicated source-document anomalies, so each house's review re-investigated the same finding from scratch.

**Impact.** Four rounds of duplicated investigation effort on a finding that was correct the first time.

**Fix.** After the fourth confirmation it was recorded as a permanent observation rather than re-flagged per house.

**→ Rule.** The first time a source-document anomaly is confirmed as genuine, write it into a project-level known-anomalies list — otherwise every reviewer pays to rediscover it.

<sub>`2026-07-12.md` · process</sub>

#### ⚪ LOW · 2026-07-21 · Garbled terminal output (^[[B^[[A) mistaken for a broken/stuck job

**What happened.** The terminal filled with control-code garbage which looked like an error or a hung process; it was actually raw cursor-movement codes from a progress bar being copied instead of rendered.

**Root cause.** Diagnosing job health from terminal text alone, with no independent signal of whether the GPU was actually doing work.

**Impact.** Time lost investigating a non-problem during a paid rental session.

**Fix.** Used `nvidia-smi` to confirm GPU utilisation and VRAM consumption as the real liveness check.

**→ Rule.** Judge whether a GPU job is alive with `nvidia-smi` (utilisation + VRAM), never with what the log text looks like.

<sub>`D:/00mk/steel project/training/Training/workmen's_diary/2026-07-21.md` · misdiagnosis</sub>

#### ⚪ LOW · 2026-07-21 · First environment-repair attempt (reinstall unsloth) fixed nothing

**What happened.** The first repair step, `pip install --force-reinstall --no-deps -U unsloth unsloth_zoo`, did not restore the environment because it only touched unsloth and left the downgraded transformers/torch in place.

**Root cause.** Repairing by reinstalling the package that reported the error, rather than the packages that were actually changed by the offending install.

**Impact.** An extra failed repair round before the correct version pins were applied.

**Fix.** Pinned the specific packages that had been downgraded (transformers==5.5.0, torch==2.10.0+cu128).

**→ Rule.** To repair a broken environment, diff what actually changed (pip log / run log versions) and restore those exact packages — don't reinstall the package whose import failed.

<sub>`D:/00mk/steel project/training/Training/workmen's_diary/2026-07-21.md` · misdiagnosis</sub>

#### ⚪ LOW · 2026-07-21 · First OOM fix attempt pulled the wrong lever (allocator tuning instead of LoRA rank)

**What happened.** The first response to OOM was to tune the memory allocator to reduce reserved-but-unused space. It was not enough; only reducing LoRA rank worked.

**Root cause.** Fix was chosen by familiarity (the generic OOM remedy) rather than from a memory breakdown that would have shown LoRA×256 experts as the dominant term.

**Impact.** An extra failed attempt on paid GPU time before the real fix.

**Fix.** Moved to reducing LORA_R 64 → 32, which saves memory multiplied across all 256 experts.

**→ Rule.** Before applying a generic OOM remedy, itemize what is actually holding VRAM (weights / adapters / activations) and attack the largest term — a fix that saves 1% costs a whole restart cycle.

<sub>`D:/00mk/steel project/training/Training/workmen's_diary/สอนมะขาม_รวม.md` · debugging-method</sub>

#### ⚪ LOW · 2026-07-25 · Workflow document status markers contradicted their own body text

**What happened.** During re-verification, two headers in `RETUNE_WORKFLOW.md` were found not matching their content: Phase 0.4 was marked unresolved although the body said it was fixed, and Phase 7 was marked red although the re-run had produced real numbers.

**Root cause.** Status markers were updated separately from the content they summarise, so a fix recorded in the body never propagated to the header.

**Impact.** A tracking document that understates what is actually done — the exact failure mode that causes work to be redone or a completed phase to be re-run.

**Fix.** Fixed both headers and added a consolidated RE-VERIFICATION PASS (2026-07-25) table summarising every phase in one place.

**→ Rule.** Update the status marker in the same edit as the content it summarises, and re-verify a tracking document against the real artifacts periodically instead of trusting it.

#### ⚪ LOW · 2026-07-30 · Label Studio task generation was run as a mandatory op1 step on houses 08/09/10 three days before the whole thing was cancelled

**What happened.** Each of houses 08, 09 and 10 ran label-studio-tasks-makham.js as step 5-6 of op1 and had the result recorded (31/32/6 elements plus material_list and single task sets). On 2026-08-02 Label Studio was cancelled outright, op1's steps 5-6 were rewritten to drop the run entirely, and 21MB of exactly this generated task JSON for 10 houses was deleted.

**Root cause.** A downstream consumer's step stayed mandatory in the extraction workflow while the decision to keep that consumer was still open; nobody paused the step when the feature became uncertain.

**Impact.** Per-house generation and verification effort spent on three houses, plus the artifacts, went straight into the deleted pile days later. The step also stayed in the standing order, so any house run in that window paid the same cost.

**Fix.** op1 step 5-6 rewritten to drop the Label Studio run; the post-extraction gate became python tools/check_format.py

**→ Rule.** When a downstream feature is under review, suspend its step in the upstream workflow rather than continuing to feed it. The cheapest artifact is the one not generated.

#### ⚪ LOW · 2026-08-21 · Pass 1 designed as an ordering/queue when it is actually a physical folder reorganisation

**What happened.** Pass 1 was initially implemented/designed as an ordering or queueing step; Makham clarified it is a real physical grouping into one folder per subtask, each folder holding the images plus whatever that subtask needs (e.g. the grid master). The diary records 'Claude had it wrong first time.'

**Root cause.** The word 'orchestrate/queue' in the original pass description was ambiguous, and the design was built from that word rather than from asking what the next pass physically needs on disk.

**Impact.** Design rework mid-session; had it shipped as a queue, Pass 2 would have had no per-subtask folder tree and no place for the shared grid master.

**Fix.** Redesigned as physical folder grouping; pass1_organize.py writes pass2/<subtask>/images/ and pass3/<subtask>/images/ with a manifest.json per folder.

**→ Rule.** For any pipeline stage, write down what the next stage must find on disk before designing the stage — an ambiguous verb like 'organize' or 'queue' should be resolved into a concrete directory layout first.

**→ Rule.** When a rule and the reader's actual needs conflict, state the deviation and its reasoning in the same document — then amend the rule to carve out the case, so the next person does not have to re-argue it.

#### ⚪ LOW · 2026-08-21 · Two sessions edited run_house_batch.py the same day without knowing about each other

**What happened.** The afternoon session added `repetition_penalty` / `no_repeat_ngram_size` to `run_house_batch.py`. Later the same day another session independently added grammar-constrained decoding (`--grammar-backend auto|xgr|lmfe|none`) to the same file. The diary had to add a parenthetical disclaimer so the file's history would read straight.

**Root cause.** No coordination or lock on the inference scripts while multiple sessions worked the same bug from different angles on the same day.

**→ Rule.** When two sessions work the same bug the same day, say so in the diary before editing, not after — otherwise the same file gets two independent fixes for one symptom and the second makes the first redundant.

#### ⚪ LOW · 2026-08-26 · CLAUDE.md merge conflict because two people appended work-log entries at the same spot

**What happened.** In the Constistant repo, Makham and Ton both appended a work-log entry to the same position in CLAUDE.md, producing a merge conflict that had to be hand-resolved by commit time ordering.

**Root cause.** An append-only log file with a single insertion point at the top guarantees a conflict whenever two people write on the same day — a structural property of the file, not a mistake by either person.

**Impact.** Manual conflict resolution on a doc file, with a real risk of silently dropping one person's entry if resolved carelessly.

**Fix.** kept both entries, ordered by commit time

**→ Rule.** An append-at-top shared log conflicts on every parallel day. Either append at the bottom, or give each day its own file the way workmen's_diary already does.

**What happened.** Testing titleblock_ocr.py wrote 26 `_titleblock_hint.txt` files into `image/บ้าน_ใหญ่_2ชั้น_02/` — the real working image directory, not a scratch area.

**Root cause.** The tool defaults to writing sidecars next to the source images, and the test run was not given a separate output root.

#### ⚪ LOW · 2026-08-29 · Schema §1 carried a stale claim that the prompt didn't teach split — it already did

**What happened.** Schema §1 stated "prompt ยังไม่สอน split" when plan.md had in fact already been taught the split. The claim was found and closed during template work.

**Impact.** Anyone reading the schema would believe a capability was missing and might re-implement it.

**Fix.** Closed the stale claim and recorded it in the edit log.

**→ Rule.** Avoid documenting what another file does *not* do. If you must, put a pointer in the other file so a change there triggers the doc update.

<sub>`D:/00mk/steel project/training/Training/workmen's_diary/2026-08-30.md` · process</sub>

#### ⚪ LOW · 2026-08-30 · The output directory was 5.6GB of which only 842MB was the real adapter — naive upload would have pushed redundant checkpoints

**What happened.** The training output directory held 5.6GB, but the actual adapter was only 842MB; the rest were intermediate `checkpoint-*` directories kept by `save_steps=25`/`save_total_limit=2`.

**Root cause.** Training checkpoints and the final artifact live in the same directory, so an uncritical folder upload ships 6.6× the necessary bytes.

**Impact.** Would have wasted upload time and HF storage quota across 5 repos, and (via the --exclude bug) the attempt to avoid it caused the silent-upload failure.

**Fix.** Excluded `checkpoint-*/*` — first via `--exclude` (which silently failed) then via a clean staging folder containing only top-level files.

**→ Rule.** Separate the artifact you intend to publish into a staging directory before uploading; do not filter a mixed directory at upload time.

#### ⚪ LOW · 2026-08-30 · Fold numbering differs between HF repo names (1-based) and internal files (0-based) — a live mis-mapping hazard

**What happened.** HF repos are named `Purson-fold1..fold4-weights` (1-based, as Makham refers to them) while the internal output directories are `outputs_t04/fold0..fold3` (0-based). The mapping had to be written out explicitly: fold0 → `-fold1-`, fold1 → `-fold2-`, fold2 → `-fold3-`, fold3 → `-fold4-`.

**Root cause.** Two naming conventions for the same entity were adopted in different layers without a single canonical mapping, creating a permanent off-by-one hazard.

**Impact.** High risk of uploading the wrong adapter to the wrong repo, which would be nearly undetectable afterwards. No mis-upload actually occurred.

**Fix.** The mapping was written out explicitly in the workflow doc and diary for every one of the 5 repos.

**→ Rule.** Do not maintain two numbering bases for the same entity. If it cannot be avoided, write the full mapping table in the checklist and verify each artifact against it before publishing.
