**What happened.** The service key was first placed under `PURSON_GPU_KEY` instead of the correct field, and the pasted value was missing its leading character.

**Root cause.** Manual copy-paste of an opaque secret into a config file with no validation of field name or value format.

**Impact.** Auth failures that look like permission problems and cost debugging time to distinguish from real RLS behaviour.

**Fix.** Moved to the correct field and the missing character restored; `worker_config.json` confirmed git-ignored.

**→ Rule.** Validate secrets at load time — assert the expected prefix (`sb_secret_`) and reject unknown config keys loudly, so a mis-pasted or misplaced value fails with a clear message instead of an auth error.

<sub>`D:/00mk/steel project/training/Training/workmen's_diary/2026-08-30.md` · process</sub>

#### ⚪ LOW · 2026-08-30 · 146 template candidates stuck in staging awaiting human review — the bottleneck is people, not tooling, and auto-promotion is forbidden by a prior lesson

**What happened.** `harvest_templates.py` finished its job (118 further candidates deduped to retired_dupes), leaving 146 candidates in `templates/staging/` that must be reviewed by eye. Auto-promotion is explicitly forbidden by the earlier F1/F2 lesson.

**Root cause.** The pipeline automates generation but not acceptance, and no review tooling existed, so the queue grew without a way to drain it.

**Impact.** CV template coverage stayed frozen while a completed harvest sat unused.

**Fix.** Wrote `tools/review_staging.py` generating a self-contained `staging_review.html` (base64-embedded, opens from file) showing all 146 images at once with tick + type selection producing a `--promote ... --kind ...` command to paste into the terminal. The web page deliberately never moves files itself — a human still runs the command. Verified: 146 images / 37 houses / 0.2 MB.

**→ Rule.** When a step must stay manual for correctness, build tooling that makes the manual step fast rather than letting the queue grow — and keep the tool advisory (it produces a command) rather than actuating.

<sub>`D:/00mk/steel project/training/Training/workmen's_diary/2026-08-30.md` · process</sub>

#### ⚪ LOW · 2026-08-31 · Vast.ai credit balance was recorded as $16.66 when it was actually $84.82

**What happened.** Planning notes said the $40-57 two-arm budget could not be covered because credit was $16.66, requiring a top-up before renting. The real balance checked before renting was $84.82.

**Root cause.** A misread of the balance figure that was then written into planning docs and treated as fact.

**Impact.** Planning was blocked on a non-existent funding problem and a top-up was nearly requested unnecessarily.

**Fix.** Checked the real balance directly before renting and proceeded with four instances.

**→ Rule.** Re-check the live account balance from the provider at the moment of the spend decision — never plan against a number copied from an earlier note.

<sub>`D:/00mk/steel project/training/Training/workmen's_diary/2026-08-31.md` · process</sub>

#### ⚪ LOW · 2026-08-31 · Benchmark house images remain under t04_Purson — carried over as unfinished for a second day

**What happened.** The 65 page images for the cross-round benchmark house were left under t04_Purson both locally and on gpu1, because moving them mid-run would break the running queue. It remained on the pending list at the end of the day.

**Root cause.** Deferred cleanup during an active run, then not completed once the run finished.

**Impact.** Ongoing misattribution risk and a second consecutive day carrying the same open item.

**Fix.** Not fixed — planned move to a round-neutral location such as tune_ai/benchmark_house_new/ with script and doc path updates.

**→ Rule.** When cleanup is deferred because a job is running, schedule it to the job's completion rather than to a generic to-do list, or it rolls over indefinitely.

<sub>`D:/00mk/steel project/training/Training/workmen's_diary/2026-08-31.md` · process</sub>

#### ⚪ LOW · 2026-08-31 · Epoch count was changed in both arms' configs before the verification research had returned

**What happened.** Makham asked for epochs 3->2 and also asked that the reasoning be double-checked online first. The configs in both arms were changed immediately while the research agent was still running in the background.

**Root cause.** Two parts of the instruction (change it / verify it first) were sequenced in the convenient rather than the stated order.

**Impact.** Configs were committed on unverified reasoning; the change happened to be correct and also aligned with the later overfit finding (loss 0.10-0.13).

**Fix.** The research was still dispatched and reported separately; the change was documented in both workflow docs.

**→ Rule.** When an instruction pairs a change with a verification step, complete the verification before committing the change unless the instruction explicitly says otherwise.

<sub>`D:/00mk/steel project/training/Training/workmen's_diary/2026-08-31.md` · process</sub>

#### ⚪ LOW · 2026-08-31 · The CV batch was estimated at 70s per page from a cold-start first page; the real rate was ~13s

**What happened.** The per-page throughput estimate for the 159-page CV batch was taken from the first page, which included cold-start overhead. The real steady-state rate was about 13 seconds per page.

**Root cause.** Extrapolating a rate from the first sample, which carries one-time initialization cost.

**Impact.** A ~5x overestimate of batch duration that affected scheduling decisions for the night.

**Fix.** Corrected once real throughput was observed across 159 pages.

**→ Rule.** Discard the first sample when estimating a throughput rate — measure steady state across several items before projecting a batch duration.

<sub>`D:/00mk/steel project/training/Training/workmen's_diary/2026-08-31.md` · estimation</sub>

#### ⚪ LOW · 2026-08-31 · Suspected the rasterizer was producing inconsistent DPI; measurement showed DPI was fine and the variance came from one house

**What happened.** Image-size variance across the corpus was initially attributed to a rasterizer problem. Actually measuring the 884 images showed DPI is consistent — the outliers are 122 images at 4631x3473 (16 MP) all from a single house, and 151 images exceeding the pixel cap by only 0.13%.

**Root cause.** A distribution was judged from its outliers before it was measured.

**Impact.** Would have sent effort at re-rasterising the whole corpus for a non-existent problem; instead the real finding (151 images downscaled for a 0.13% overage) surfaced.

**Fix.** measured the real size distribution before acting; no rasterizer work done

**→ Rule.** Measure the distribution before naming a cause — "the sizes vary" and "the tool is broken" are different claims.

<sub>`D:/00mk/steel project/training/Training/workmen's_diary/2026-08-31.md` · misdiagnosis</sub>

#### ⚪ LOW · 2026-08-31 · Renaming t05_Asclepius to t05_Courser invalidated both datasets because paths were baked into the generated JSON

**What happened.** A folder rename required sweeping every script and then rebuilding both the Unsloth and LLaMA-Factory datasets from scratch, because image and script paths were embedded inside the generated JSON rather than resolved at load time.

**Root cause.** Generated data files carry absolute/repo-relative paths, so any move of the producing folder makes them wrong; hand-editing them with sed was rejected as too risky.

**Impact.** A full dataset rebuild plus a sweep of 6+ scripts, purely for a rename.

**Fix.** rebuilt both datasets from the new location instead of patching JSON by hand; only two historical mentions of the old name kept deliberately

**→ Rule.** Keep paths out of generated data — resolve them at load time from a single root — or a rename becomes a rebuild.

<sub>`D:/00mk/steel project/training/Training/workmen's_diary/2026-08-31.md` · process</sub>

#### ⚪ LOW · 2026-08-31 · Opening the worker window is the step most often forgotten when starting the demo by hand

**What happened.** The manual start sequence has a step — opening the worker window — that is repeatedly missed, so the system looks up but no job is ever claimed. It was folded into GO.bat menu item 1 specifically because of this.

**Root cause.** A multi-window manual startup with no check that every process is actually running.

**Impact.** A silently non-functional demo: jobs sit unclaimed with no visible error.

**Fix.** GO.bat menu item 1 now opens the worker window automatically

**→ Rule.** A startup step that is easy to skip and silent when skipped should be automated or asserted, not documented.

<sub>`D:/00mk/steel project/training/Training/workmen's_diary/2026-08-31.md` · process</sub>

#### ⚪ LOW · 2026-09-01 · pass2.5 self-harvest output written to results with no consumer anywhere

**What happened.** pass2.5's self-harvest output was saved into result files, but nothing consumes it — pass3 (takeoff) has no runner on the server side.

**Root cause.** A producer stage was built ahead of its consumer, so the data flows to disk and stops. Speculative capability built before the thing that needs it exists.

**Impact.** Compute and code maintained for output nobody reads; risk that someone later assumes the data is being used.

**Fix.** Not fixed — recorded honestly in code comments and warnings rather than hidden.

**→ Rule.** Do not ship a producer stage before its consumer exists. If you must, mark it loudly in code and in the diary so nobody mistakes 'the file exists' for 'the feature works'.

<sub>`2026-09-01.md` · process/yagni</sub>

#### ⚪ LOW · 2026-09-01 · An entire greedy-decoding experiment round failed and had to be archived as a dead result

**What happened.** During the results cleanup, the 7 result folders were renamed by actual chronology: folder 01 is the usable result, folder 02 is the greedy round that failed.

**Root cause.** Recorded only as a failed experiment round; the cause is not detailed in this entry. The folders were also originally named so ambiguously that a cleanup pass was needed just to tell which result was usable.

**Impact.** One full experiment round's compute wasted, plus later confusion about which results were valid until the renaming pass.

**Fix.** Renamed all 7 folders in real execution order with a Thai README explaining each.

**→ Rule.** Name experiment output folders with their outcome and order at creation time (`01_usable`, `02_failed_greedy`), not afterwards — an ambiguous results directory costs a cleanup pass and risks someone quoting a dead run.

<sub>`2026-09-01.md` · process</sub>

#### ⚪ LOW · 2026-09-01 · INVENTORY.csv was 70 rows behind reality — six whole categories of work were untracked

**What happened.** The artifact inventory went from 261 to 331 rows in one catch-up pass, adding categories 12 (t04 Purson), 13 (t44 Voldemort), 14 (t05), 15 (soup), 16 (test results) and 17 (t05_Destrier) — i.e. several complete model-training efforts and their outputs had never been entered.

**Root cause.** The inventory is updated as a separate housekeeping task rather than as part of finishing each piece of work, so it drifts behind by however long it is between cleanups.

**Impact.** For an unknown stretch, nobody could tell from the inventory what models, folds and result sets existed — the same period in which a t04 data fold was nearly reused for a different model.

**Fix.** Backfilled 70 rows across 6 new categories in one pass

**→ Rule.** An inventory updated in batches is an inventory that is wrong most of the time; a new model/fold/result set should get its row when it is created, not at the next cleanup.

<sub>`D:/00mk/steel project/training/Training/workmen's_diary/2026-09-01.md` · process</sub>

#### ⚪ LOW · 2026-09-02 · npm test was skipped for the session on the reasoning that only an untested file changed

**What happened.** `npm test` was not run for this round, justified by the fact that the only change was to `serve_purson.py`, which has no test coverage.

**Root cause.** Test coverage gap used as a reason to skip the suite entirely, rather than as a reason to add coverage. The suite also serves as a regression check against changes made earlier in the day.

**Impact.** No regression signal for the session; the file that caused the day's biggest failure remains untested.

**Fix.** Not fixed — noted honestly.

**→ Rule.** 'This file has no tests' is a reason to add one, not to skip the suite. Run the suite anyway — it is cheap and it guards the rest of the day's work.
